rationale.rationale: Management framed the separation as the final step of a structure-simplification project begun in 2022, when the India crop protection business was carved into UPL Sustainable Agri Solutions (UPL SAS) while the international crop protection business sat under UPL Crop Protection Holdings (UPL Cayman, 77.78% UPL-owned). The Feb 20, 2026 Composite Scheme does three things in order: merges UPL SAS into UPL Limited (1,000 UPL shares for every 48 UPL SAS shares), demerges the India Crop Protection business into UPL Global Sustainable Agri Solutions (UPL 2) on a 1:1 entitlement, and merges UPL Cayman into UPL 2 (1,000 UPL 2 shares for every 213 UPL Cayman shares) — leaving UPL Limited as a diversified agro/specialty-chemicals platform (SUPERFORM, Advanta, new verticals) and UPL 2 as what Mike Frank called the world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform, present in 140+ countries. The stated problems it solves: a conglomerate discount (Bikash Prasad: the market applies 'a single conglomerate multiple' and sum-of-parts is unclear), value trapped at platform level (Toshan Tamhane said the KKR and Alpha Wave private valuations were not flowing through to UPL Limited), a complex holding structure, and the fact that crop protection and seeds have fundamentally different cash-flow and capital-allocation needs — explicitly citing Corteva's announced crop-protection/seeds split as precedent. Separation is meant to give each entity its own capital structure, governance and board focus so each can raise capital independently and attract a different investor, lender and strategic-partner set; Jai Shroff said these businesses 'need an independent life' and claimed they can grow 3x-4x faster than peers. Management said the precondition was deleveraging, which it declared done at the May 2026 CMD: gross debt down from $3.8bn (FY24) to $2.3bn (-40%), net debt $3.1bn to $1.6bn (-48%), gearing 4.6x to below 1.6x, after repaying $400m perpetuals and $500m of loans and extending another $400m to March 2029 — Shroff said leverage 'was an issue which kept the multiple of the company. That is I'm sure gone away now.' The push came from several directions: analysts and rating agencies (five explicit feedback items Prasad catalogued, including the ~INR5,000 crore of below-EBITDA line items and short-term liquidity), platform investors KKR and Alpha Wave seeking value realisation (Advanta's Jan 19, 2026 DRHP is an offer-for-sale with KKR selling 2.2% and UPL Limited 7.8%, proceeds 'largely for deleveraging of the group balance sheet'), and the Upswing Trust, an existing 5% UPL SAS investor that swapped 22.21% of UPL Corp Cayman into UPL Cayman (completed July 31, 2026) and ends with 16.78% of UPL 2 plus one board nomination right. Notably, at least one large holder pushed back: Old Bridge's Tarang Agarwal called the announced structure 'fairly detrimental to the current shareholders' and likely to trigger 'a significant HoldCo discount,' and Prasad said the feedback tracker would go 'unfiltered to the board' within a month or two, while noting at least 10 structures had already been evaluated.
rationale.evolution: On the Aug 1, 2025 Q1 FY26 call the idea surfaced only as a line in Jai Shroff's press release: Bikash Prasad said advisors were just being engaged 'to explore unlocking value across all platforms,' with no structure chosen and deleveraging framed as the near-term priority; by the Nov 6, 2025 Q2 call it had hardened into 'restructuring or strategic fundraising, potential liquidity events like IPO' across platforms, alongside the DECCO-into-Advanta integration, and was explicitly linked to funding the FY27 $900m maturities. On the Feb 2, 2026 Q3 call the first concrete step landed — Advanta's DRHP filed Jan 19, 2026 — with management guiding to 'IPO and restructuring within a period of 1 to 3 years' and Toshan Tamhane giving the industrial logic (crop protection vs seeds cash flows, the Corteva split, Advanta's 'destiny of its own'), while Tarang Agarwal already questioned whether UPL shareholders gained anything. The Scheme itself was approved by the board on Feb 20, 2026 and by the May 11, 2026 Capital Markets Day the debate had shifted from whether to separate to how: Agarwal attacked the chosen structure as HoldCo-discount-creating and asked for alternatives, Shroff and Prasad defended it while promising to take investor feedback to the board, and the process then moved through CCI approval (June 2-3, 2026), BSE/NSE observation letters (July 29, 2026) and completion of the Cayman swap and ESOP swap (July 31, 2026), with Nov 2, 2026 results confirming no accounting effect yet pending NCLT and shareholder approvals.

points.point: First acknowledgement: advisors only just being engaged, no structure decided, timeline unknown; purpose stated as unlocking value across platforms, tied to deleveraging the balance sheet over one to two years.
points.quote: The idea behind engaging advisors is to explore unlocking value across all platforms.

points.point: Prasad linked the strategic options directly to balance-sheet repair rather than to growth at that stage.
points.quote: However, as we continue to evaluate various strategic options to unlock value across the platform, our focus will be to significantly deleverage our balance sheet over the next year or two.

points.point: The option set was named for the first time — restructuring, strategic fundraising, IPO — across all platforms, after DECCO was folded into Advanta in September 2025.
points.quote: UPL continues to evaluate various strategic opportunities to unlock shareholders' value across platforms, including restructuring or strategic fundraising, potential liquidity events like IPO.

points.point: Asked how the ~$900m of FY27 maturities would be met, Prasad made the value-unlock actions part of the funding answer.
points.quote: We had indicated during Q1 earnings call and press release that we are looking at various options to unlock shareholders' value. And if some of those we decide to take, that would also help in terms of deleveraging the balance sheet.

points.point: Advanta DRHP filed 19 Jan 2026 as the first concrete corporate action, with a stated 1-3 year window for IPOs and restructuring across all platforms.
points.quote: As we have communicated earlier, we remain focused in evaluating various corporate actions for all our platforms, including IPO and restructuring within a period of 1 to 3 years.

points.point: The Advanta IPO is an offer for sale, not primary: KKR selling 2.2% and UPL Limited 7.8%, with proceeds going to the group, chiefly to cut debt.
points.quote: But it will come to the group largely for deleveraging of the group balance sheet.

points.point: Tamhane gave the industrial rationale — crop protection and seeds need different capital and cash-flow profiles — and cited Corteva's split as the global precedent, calling Advanta the eighth largest seeds player.
points.quote: we believe that the needs of crop protection in terms of the cash flows, capital allocation are very different from that of the seeds business.

points.point: Management conceded that the private-round valuations of platform stakes (KKR, Alpha Wave) were not being reflected in UPL Limited's own price — the trapped-value argument.
points.quote: Because , if you look at the valuation that KKR and subsequently Alpha Wave came in at , at least we feel that the full value of that is no t flowing through to UPL Limited.

points.point: The 20 Feb 2026 Composite Scheme consolidates UPL SAS (India crop protection) and UPL Cayman (global crop protection) into UPL 2 to create a pure-play crop protection platform with its own management.
points.quote: The Scheme proposes to consolidate  the India Crop Protection Business held in UPL SAS and Global Crop Protection Business held in UPL Cayman, under a single entity, creating a focused, pure -play crop protection platform.

points.point: Independent capital raising and capital-structure optimisation for each of the two listed entities is given as a core benefit, alongside a wider investor, lender and partner base and sharper board focus.
points.quote: The Scheme will allow UPL 1 and UPL 2 to raise capital independently, allowing each entity to optimize its capital structure and pursue business opportunities more efficiently and effectively.

points.point: Mechanics and ratios: UPL SAS merges into UPL at 1,000:48, India crop protection demerges into UPL 2 at 1:1, UPL Cayman merges into UPL 2 at 1,000:213; no cash consideration; UPL 2 ends 71.56% promoter / 28.44% public with Upswing Trust at 16.78%, and promoters locked in for 18 months.
points.quote: 1 (One)  equity share of UPL 2 of INR 2 each fully paid -up for every 1 (One)  equity share of UPL 1 of INR 2 each fully paid -up.

points.point: Scale claim and leadership: Mike Frank, CEO of UPL Corp, becomes CEO of UPL Global, which management says will be the second largest listed pure-play crop protection company, in 140+ countries with 9 R&D centres and 25 formulation sites.
points.quote: Bringing our crop protection businesses under one platform creates the world's second largest  listed pure- play crop protection platform.

points.point: Shroff's rationale: the brand/IP-led, high-growth platforms need autonomy to grow at multiples of peers, and SUPERFORM stays inside UPL Limited as the manufacturing platform.
points.quote: All these businesses need long-term need a kind of independent life, right?

points.point: Prasad named the valuation problem explicitly — a single conglomerate multiple and an opaque sum of the parts — and said separation gives each platform its own capital and governance structure.
points.quote: You know that even today market is valuing us using a single conglomerate multiple, they are applying on us.

points.point: Shroff argued the pre-condition had been met: leverage, which he said had capped the multiple, is no longer an issue after FY26 deleveraging (gross debt -40% to $2.3bn, net debt -48% to $1.6bn, gearing below 1.6x).
points.quote: We've also made sure that the as in the past leverage was an issue for which kept the multiple of the company. That is I'm sure gone away now, and I think we will see the unlocking of shareholder value

points.point: A large shareholder (Old Bridge) publicly opposed the chosen structure as HoldCo-discount-creating and dilutive to existing holders, and pressed for alternatives.
points.quote: But the challenge is that the manner in which that the current s tructure has been announced, it's likely to trigger a significant HoldCo discount .

points.point: Prasad said feedback from two months of investor meetings would be put unfiltered to the board within a month or two, while defending the design as the best of at least ten structures reviewed with advisors.
points.quote: By going to a structure, and before we come to conclusion on this structure, it has been discussed, reviewed by our advisors, and we have looked at least 10 different structures to come up to this structure.

rationale.what_management_expects: UPL Limited: a diversified agro and specialty-chemicals platform (SUPERFORM, Advanta, new verticals), lower debt, better ROE. UPL 2: a pure-play crop protection platform with its own capital structure, governance and board focus, manufacturing/R&D/market-access synergies, independent fundraising, a wider investor and lender base, and growth management claims at 3x-4x peers. For holders: clearer sum-of-parts, removing the conglomerate discount.
rationale.gaps: No quantified synergies, no debt/cost split between the two entities, no SUPERFORM-to-UPL 2 supply pricing, no resolution of the HoldCo-discount objection, no Advanta IPO interaction.

For Q2/H1 FY27 the deck also gives EBIT (Q2FY27 ₹203 cr, 22.0% margin; H1FY27 ₹532 cr, 25.8%). No PBT or PAT is disclosed for this platform at any period.

rationale.rationale: Management frames the separation as a strategic re-alignment of a company that had grown into two very different businesses: Radar Electronics, Electronic Warfare and Telemetry on one side, and Space, Meteorology and Hydrology on the other, the latter being carved into Astra Space Technologies Private Limited (ASTPL), a wholly owned subsidiary that will be listed separately while AMPL continues as a pure-play Defence and Aerospace company retaining its JVs (Astra Rafael Comsys) and other wholly owned subsidiaries. The stated objective is sharper strategic and operational focus, with dedicated management teams free to pursue sector-specific growth, plus enhanced governance and accountability, a simpler corporate structure, clearer investment propositions and a broader investor base. The Scheme filing is explicit that Space/Met/Hydrology 'operates in a sector with distinct industry characteristics, competitive dynamics, regulatory environment, and risk profile', so it needs a differentiated growth strategy and its own capital allocation, and that a standalone entity is better placed to attract investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders with sector-specific interests. The press release adds the capital angle bluntly: Space and Weather is a scaled-up, profitable, high-growth opportunity in satellite design/assembly and satellite data, but it is capital-intensive and execution-dependent, and the demerger 'creates the structural clarity to attract capital and talent at scale'. The numbers cited are modest but real: the demerged undertaking did roughly INR157 crores of FY26 turnover, 13.58% of AMPL's total (space plus meteorology was ~16% of FY26 revenue); cumulative ISRO orders of over INR750 crores across two decades with INR250 crores still to execute by FY28, and over INR330 crores of met/hydrology contracts with a INR285 crores book to FY28; at December 2025 the standalone order book of INR2,226 crores already contained INR249 crores of space and INR369 crores of metrology/hydrology. Consideration is a 1:1 share entitlement (one INR2 ASTPL share for every INR2 AMPL share), no cash, so ASTPL's shareholding mirrors AMPL's (promoters indicatively 6.45%, public 93.55%), with listing sought on BSE and NSE and completion targeted by Q1 FY28. Leadership was split to match: Managing Director S. Gurunatha Reddy stepped down on 30 September 2026 to oversee the demerger and join ASTPL as a Director, Dr M. V. Reddy became MD of AMPL from 1 October 2026, and CFO Rahul Rungta had already moved to ASTPL in February 2026. The texts name no investor, lender or partner as having demanded the split; it is presented throughout as board-initiated, with the benefit framed as 'unlocking the value of the Demerged Undertaking for the shareholders of the Demerged Company'.
rationale.evolution: The idea surfaces obliquely as a valuation argument: on 14 Aug 2025 Atim Kabra says the separately incorporated space subsidiary is 'very, very valuable' given how thinly-revenued space peers are priced, and on 13 Nov 2025 he extrapolates space alone to near AMPL's whole market capitalisation while flagging heavy space investment and Astra SAT-1; on 13 Feb 2026 he turns to financing, saying the balance sheet must be 'creative' so blue-sky projects are not starved, and teases 'a few very interesting options'. Structurally it moves fast after that: CFO Rahul Rungta is shifted to ASTPL on 11-12 Feb 2026, the Board grants in-principle approval on 27 Feb 2026 with a same-day press release (revised the same day), and SGR announces it on the 27 May 2026 call. The Board approved the full Scheme of Arrangement on 10 June 2026 with the 1:1 ratio and the INR157 crores / 13.58% disclosure, SGR's exit as MD was confirmed on 10 Aug 2026 effective 30 Sep 2026, and BSE/NSE observation letters with no adverse observations/no objection arrived on 29 Oct 2026.

points.point: A year before the demerger was announced, management had already carved space into a separate wholly owned subsidiary (Astra Space Technologies Private Limited) with its own hiring and Bangalore clean rooms, and Atim Kabra pitched it as undervalued inside AMPL on a space order book of about INR230-239 crores.
points.quote: And given where companies with very limited indigenous capabilities are valued, you might find that our space business is actually very, very valuable.

points.point: Kabra sharpened the hidden-value argument, saying space peers with almost no revenue were being valued at $750-800 million and that extrapolating Astra's space business alone approached AMPL's entire market capitalisation.
points.quote: Companies are raising money at like $750 million, $800 million valuation with hardly any revenue numbers to their credit.

points.point: Two weeks before the Board's in-principle approval, Kabra devoted his remarks to the criticality of adequate financing for development and 'blue sky' projects and hinted at structural options to come, while the standalone order book of INR2,226 crores contained INR249 crores of space and INR369 crores of metrology and hydrology.
points.quote: So watch the space. There are a few very interesting options as they crystallize, we'll be letting you know.

points.point: S. G. Reddy announced the Board's in-principle approval of the demerger of the space, meteorology and hydrology business and listed the objectives: dedicated management teams, better governance, a simpler structure and clearer investment propositions, with the formal scheme to follow within weeks; space and meteorology were ~16% of FY26 revenue of INR1,157 crores.
points.quote: The objective of this move is to create sharper strategic and operational focus for business segments.

points.point: Management tied the restructuring to global as well as Indian opportunity and to capital allocation and efficiency over the medium to long term, alongside FY27 guidance of 15-20% growth and FY26 operating cash flow of INR370 crores versus minus INR99 crores.
points.quote: Furthermore, this restructuring will position us to capitalize on emerging opportunities both in India and globally.

points.point: The 27 Feb 2026 press release states the purpose as unlocking shareholder value and creating two focused listed platforms - AMPL for Defence and Aerospace, ASTPL for Space, Meteorology and Hydrology - and lists broader investor base, better oversight and less structural complexity as benefits.
points.quote: The proposed demerger is aimed at unlocking shareholder value and enhancing strategic focus across business verticals.

points.point: The same release argues the space and weather business is profitable and high-growth but capital-hungry and execution-dependent, and that the separation is what makes it possible to raise capital and hire for it at scale, on a 20-year base of over INR750 crores of cumulative ISRO orders and over INR330 crores of met/hydrology contracts.
points.quote: The Indian and global markets are opening simultaneously, India's geopolitical positioning is aligned with this opportunity, and the demerger of ASTPL creates the structural clarity required to attract capital and talent at scale.

points.point: The 10 June 2026 Scheme of Arrangement filing gives the formal rationale, including that the segment faces a different regulatory and risk environment and needs its own strategy, and that a standalone entity is better placed to attract investors, strategic partners and lenders.
points.quote: The Space, Meteorology and Hydrology business operates in a sector with distinct industry characteristics, competitive dynamics, regulatory environment, and risk profile, necessitating a differentiated growth strategy aligned with its specific market opportunities.

points.point: The filing sizes the demerged undertaking and sets the terms: no cash consideration, a 1:1 share entitlement ratio so ASTPL's shareholding mirrors AMPL's (promoters 6.45%, public 93.55% indicatively), transfer on a going-concern basis, and listing on BSE and NSE targeted by Q1 FY28.
points.quote: The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking of the Company for the financial year ended 31st March 2026 was approximately INR. 157 Crores, representing 13.58% of the total turnover of the Demerged Company for the said year.

points.point: Management was reorganised around the split: CFO Rahul Rungta moved to ASTPL in February 2026, MD S. Gurunatha Reddy resigned effective 30 September 2026 to oversee the demerger and join ASTPL's board, and Dr M. V. Reddy was elevated to MD of AMPL from 1 October 2026; BSE and NSE issued no-adverse-observation/no-objection letters on 29 October 2026.
points.quote: In continuation to my earlier letter dated 03/04/2026 informing my resignation from the post of Managing Director wish to inform you that I am resigning from the position Directorship also with effect from the close of business hours on 30th September, 2026, to oversee the ongoing demerger of the Space and Meteorology business pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement.

rationale.what_management_expects: AMPL: a pure-play defence/aerospace company keeping JVs and subsidiaries, with simpler structure, focused management and better capital allocation. ASTPL: an independently listed, profitable, high-growth space-and-weather platform spanning upstream hardware, integration and data, able to attract sector-specific investors, partners, lenders and talent. Both: sharper focus, improved operational efficiency, clearer investment propositions and unlocked shareholder value over the medium to long term.
rationale.gaps: No valuation basis, standalone ASTPL financials, margins, capex, debt or working-capital split, transaction costs, or who initiated it; calls never field demerger questions.

rationale.rationale: Management framed the demerger as splitting one company that had been doing two businesses with two different investor bases: an asset-heavy business that designs, develops, finances and owns hotels (pension funds, insurance companies betting on inflation, repricing and annuity yield) and an asset-light business that monetises brand, management, loyalty, distribution and technology with almost no capital intensity. Keswani said Lemon Tree had only built hotels in 2004-2007 because owners would not hand their hotels to an unknown brand, and that with the brand now widely recognised (MakeMyTrip's CEO told him 20-25% of occupancy comes from them the moment a Lemon Tree opens) there was no reason to keep owning assets rather than monetise the brand — explicitly the Marriott/Host Hotels and Hilton/Park Hotels playbook. Mechanically (Composite Scheme approved 9 Jan 2026, appointed date 1 April 2026): Carnation Hotels and Hamstede Living merge into LTH; Oriole Dr. Fresh, Canary, Sukhsagar and Manakin merge into Fleur against shares to LTH; and the Demerged Undertaking — 11 operating hotels plus Aurika Shimla under construction, the investment in Arum (Aurika Shillong, 165 rooms) and the entire development capability/team with exclusivity on all future ownership, leasing and development — demerges into Fleur, with 20 Fleur shares for every 311 LTH shares (demerged division turnover Rs 23,037.34 lakh, 59.90% of LTH standalone turnover; 1,563 operating rooms across 15 hotels per the presentation, 1,820 keys/17 hotels per the press release). A second stated problem was conflict of interest: development capability was moved to Fleur with 'Chinese firewalls' so Fleur shareholders could never feel Lemon Tree was cherry-picking the best assets for itself, and Lemon Tree must refer new acquisition/development opportunities to Fleur. All group debt (about Rs 1,300 crore at demerger, Rs 1,500 crore total borrowings at FY26-end, cost of debt 7.42%) goes to Fleur, leaving Lemon Tree debt-free with only technology and marketing spend, forcing the Board to frame a dividend/shareholder-reward policy. Warburg Pincus (Coastal Cedar Investments B.V.) bought APG's entire 41.09% of Fleur and committed up to Rs 960 crore of primary equity, giving Fleur roughly Rs 3,000 crore of deployable capital at 1:1 debt-equity against 2,500+ rooms under active discussion and Aurika Nehru Place (572 rooms, ~Rs 700 crore); post-scheme LTH shareholders own ~74% of Fleur (32.96% direct plus ~41% through LTH) versus the 59% LTH owns today, and Fleur lists separately for 'transparent price discovery and market-driven valuation of the asset-heavy business'.
rationale.evolution: The idea was first visible as a Fleur listing aspiration in the Nov 2024 call, where Keswani said debt-freedom would come sooner 'if we list Fleur before that' and put an IPO 'within the next 2-3 years at most'; in the Aug 2025 call he disclosed that committees of directors had been set up in both Lemon Tree and Fleur to evaluate transferring LTH's assets into Fleur via a demerger and listing it, alongside splitting the management teams (Neelendra Singh for LTH from 1 October, Saurabh Shatdal for Fleur), with listing hoped for end-CY2026. In the Nov 2025 call it was 'in process' with a Board subcommittee and a promise of 'some other even more exciting stuff' within three months; the scheme, the Warburg/APG transactions and the 74%/26% shareholding math were announced in the Jan 2026 (15 January) dedicated call with a 12-15 month path to listing. By the Feb 2026 call Keswani confirmed the scheme was effective from 1 April and, responding to Ashish Kumar's request, promised pro forma financials for both entities; those pro formas appeared with the Jun 2026 (29 May) results, where CCI approval (April 2026), Warburg's completed purchase of APG's stake and a longer 12-18 month NCLT-dependent timeline were given, followed by NSE/BSE observation letters on 22 September 2026.

points.point: Asked directly by Kunal Lakhan (CLSA) what was wrong with the old structure, Keswani said the hotel business has two subsets with two different investor types — developers/owners wanting chunky yield and inflation-linked annuity returns versus asset-light investors betting on brand and management — and Lemon Tree was a combination of both.
points.quote: We have actually separated 2 types of businesses. One is asset heavy, long -term appreciating asset, capital intensive. It has a different kind of investor, and this business has a very different kind of investor, and we wanted to actually attract both types of investors.

points.point: He explained the historical accident being corrected: hotels were built only to establish the brand, and with the brand now established the company should monetise it instead of owning assets.
points.quote: We were forced to build hotels to build our brand. But once we build our brand, technically, we do not need hotels because now it is time for Lemon Tree to monetize its brand, which is enormous recall.

points.point: The transfer of the development capability and exclusive development mandate to Fleur was driven by a conflict-of-interest problem — Fleur minorities fearing Lemon Tree would keep the best projects for itself — and was solved with firewalls.
points.quote: Development capability was an issue which was raised in order to maximize Fleur's growth, we did not want shareholders of Fleur to ever feel that Lemon Tree when it recommends any assets was cherry -picking, which means Lemon Tree would say, I have got this very nice asset in Delhi, why should I offer it to Fleur.

points.point: All of Lemon Tree's debt moves to Fleur: Fleur carries roughly Rs 1,300 crore of debt against a ~Rs 900 crore net EBITDA and can borrow another ~Rs 1,300 crore, while Lemon Tree goes to zero debt.
points.quote: Firstly, when this demerger happens, all the debt, including the Lemon Tree's debt, after adjustment is being transferred to Fleur. Fleur will have 100% of our debt and Lemon Tree will have zero debt.

points.point: Keswani justified keeping a ~41% indirect stake in Fleur (challenged by Jinesh Joshi on hold-co discount) as Lemon Tree retaining 'skin in the game' as Fleur's manager, with natural dilution as Fleur raises capital; he quantified that Rs 1,000 crore deployed by Fleur generates ~Rs 350 crore of turnover, Rs 170-180 crore EBITDA and ~Rs 30 crore of fees for Lemon Tree.
points.quote: We felt it was prudent to have significant skin in the game at this stage, which means that going forward, it is very possible that Lemon Tree may dilute or even increase its stake over time; this will obviously be a Board decision .

points.point: Warburg's Rs 960 crore primary commitment plus Fleur's own cash and 1:1 debt gives roughly Rs 3,000 crore to deploy pre-listing against 2,500 rooms in active discussion; Keswani guided Fleur to over Rs 1,000 crore net EBITDA by FY28 and Lemon Tree to 80% EBITDA margin / 60% PAT margin.
points.quote: We have potentially about Rs 3,000 crores available to deploy in this growth before we list.

points.point: Opening the call with pro forma financials for both entities, Keswani described the transaction as simple — Warburg has bought APG's Fleur stake, Lemon Tree transfers 17 hotels and development capabilities in exchange for Fleur shares to LTH shareholders, and Fleur lists.
points.quote: This scheme will result in 2 distinct financially sound businesses.

points.point: He restated the economic outcome for each entity: Lemon Tree debt-free, high-margin, high-ROCE and fee/brand-driven; Fleur the consolidated owner of a fully renovated portfolio, post-scheme India's largest hotel platform by inventory at 5,600 rooms and 39 operational hotels.
points.quote: Post the reorganization , Lemon Tree will emerge as a debt -free, high-margin, high ROCE company generating strong free cash flows from fees and brand -related income.

points.point: Shareholder arithmetic: LTH shareholders end up with close to 74% of Fleur (33% direct, ~41% through Lemon Tree) versus the 59% Lemon Tree directly owns in Fleur today, before Warburg's primary infusion; Keswani also said he will cease to be executive at Lemon Tree from March 2027 and focus on Fleur as Executive Chair.
points.quote: Post reorganization , Lemon Tree shareholders will effectively own close to 74% of Fleur Hotels, 33% directly and about 41% indirectly through Lemon Tree.

points.point: Answering Achal Kumar, Keswani confirmed Fleur will be brand-agnostic post-demerger and may hand assets to other operators — Lemon Tree has no automatic right to Fleur's hotels and must earn them on results.
points.quote: Yes. But Lemon Tree must be able to deliver best results to get it . Just because Lemon Tree has skin in the game with Fleur does not mean that it has an automatic right to any asset that Fleur develops.

points.point: On capital allocation after the split, Lemon Tree is expected to need almost no capital and move to distributing profits, while Fleur will retain capital for growth rather than pay dividends.
points.quote: Lemon Tree will not need any significant capital other than potentially investments in technology or in marketing and so on. It will be essentially a zero -debt cash accretive company.

points.point: Keswani confirmed the scheme is effective from 1 April and that Lemon Tree becomes debt-free from next year, with all assets and debt going to Fleur and fee income becoming free cash; the Board must decide a dividend policy within six months.
points.quote: What will happen is in the scheme of demerger, all the assets of Lemon Tree, including its debt will be transferred to Fleur. Lemon Tree will immediately effectively be a debt -free company from next year.

points.point: Investors pushed for separate reporting: Ashish Kumar of Infinity Alternatives asked for pro forma financials of both businesses while awaiting the listing, and management agreed to publish them from the next quarter.
points.quote: Now that we have decided on the split of the 2 businesses, what might be helpful is if we can add pro forma financials for both of the assets as they look like so that while we are waiting for the l isting, we do get a good sense of what the numbers are looking like.

points.point: Keswani positioned the asset-light entity as a first in India, with fee income from hotels signed three years earlier only now flowing, and Fleur guided to ~Rs 1,000 crore EBITDA by FY28, its first year as a listed company.
points.quote: And keep in mind that Lemon Tree will be the first fully asset -light brand owning tech and distribution and management company in India, the first.

points.point: The demerger was still with Board subcommittees of both Lemon Tree and Fleur, with management hinting that more than the demerger was being negotiated (the Warburg/APG transactions announced two months later).
points.quote: It is not only the demerger of Fleur, but some other even more exciting stuff, but we will talk about it when the time is right.

points.point: First formal disclosure of the structure: committees of directors in both companies to evaluate transferring LTH's assets into Fleur via demerger and then list Fleur, with Lemon Tree becoming asset-light and focused on management, brand and technology — described as the global trend in the space.
points.quote: You may have also seen that we have said that a committee of directors has been set up in Lemon Tree and in Fleur to evaluate how we can possibly look at a transfer of assets from Lemon Tree into Fleur through a demerger scheme and then automatically look at how we can list Fleur.

points.point: The separation of management was done first and explicitly for this purpose — Neelendra Singh to run asset-light Lemon Tree from 1 October and Saurabh Shatdal to drive Fleur's asset-heavy growth, with Keswani handholding and moving to strategic oversight.
points.quote: The intent of the leadership change was to get 2 very good people who would then run these two companies independently on a day -to-day basis.

points.point: Keswani drew a hard line on mandates — Fleur builds, buys and leases, Lemon Tree only manages or franchises — and noted that the more Fleur dilutes and raises capital, the more Lemon Tree's economic interest rises via fees (Rs 100+ crore this year, potentially Rs 300-400 crore from Fleur in three years).
points.quote: Fleur's mandate will be to focus on, at the right value, building, buying, or leasing hotels. Lemon Tree's will only be to manage or franchise. Lemon Tree will not lease hotels once the Fleur demerger happens.

points.point: The earliest trace in these calls: a Fleur listing was already seen as the accelerator of deleveraging, with Keswani putting an IPO within 2-3 years at most when asked by Prashant Biyani.
points.quote: I think we are sticking to our guidance that in the next 3 - 3.5 years, we should be debt free , but if we list Fleur before that then we will be debt free that much earlier.

points.point: The 9 Jan 2026 filing states the Board reviewed the business with a view to segregating the asset-heavy ownership/development undertaking from the asset-light management/brand platform, and that the demerged business is self-sustaining and better housed in Fleur; the demerged division's turnover was Rs 23,037.34 lakh, 59.90% of LTH standalone turnover.
points.quote: Therefore, to achieve operational focus, greater flexibility for capital deployment, and clearer alignment of business objectives, it is proposed under this Scheme to (i) amalgamate Transferor Company 3, Transferor Company 4, Transferor Company 5 and Transferor Company 6 with the Transferee Company; and (ii) demerge and vest the Demerged Undertaking (comprising the Demerged Hotel Properties and the Development Capabilities together with the related undertakings, as defined hereinafter) into the Transferee C ompany, while the Company will continue to focus on the asset -light hotel management support, brand and operations including management support of the hotels transferred to the Transferee Company and other properties.

points.point: A stated purpose is market-driven valuation: Fleur ceases to be LTH's subsidiary and lists, so LTH shareholders participate directly in the asset-heavy business through listed shares rather than through a subsidiary.
points.quote: Following the implementation of the Scheme, the Transferee Company will cease to be a subsidiary of the Company , and its shares will be listed on the Stock Exchanges, enabling transparent price discovery and market -driven valuation of the asset -heavy business.

points.point: The filing also sets out structural clean-up and partner-flexibility objectives: merging two wholly owned subsidiaries into LTH to remove layering and cost, and creating a structure that lets Fleur bring in investors or co-development partners per project without touching LTH's brand operations.
points.quote: To create a flexible structure enabling the Transferee Company to attract investors or co -development partners for specific hotel projects, without affecting Company's brand operations or control over strategic decisions.

points.point: Continuity is contractually locked: every hotel amalgamated into or demerged to Fleur stays under Lemon Tree Hotel Operating Agreements (existing ones amended/restated and extended from the Appointed Date), and LTH must refer new acquisition/development opportunities to Fleur and drop them if Fleur declines.
points.quote: Further, all the hotels amalgamated with or demerged into the Transferee Company will continue to be managed and operated by the Company under Hotel Operating Agreements and, the existing Hotel Operating Agreements with the Transferee Company and its subsidiaries shall be amended and/or restated, inter alia, to reflect the revised terms as detailed in the Scheme, and the Company shall refer new hotel acquisition or development opportunities to the Transferee Company and shall not pursue them if declined, except for hotel operations/franchise arran gements through third parties.

points.point: The Shareholders' Agreement with Warburg gives Fleur the exclusive global right to own, lease and develop hospitality assets, Investor/LTH affirmative consent on reserved matters, up to 3 Investor and 3 LTH directors with Keswani as non-retiring executive chairman, and the right to inject up to Rs 960 crore of primary capital.
points.quote: The Agreement provides Fleur t he exclusive right to own, lease and develop hospitality assets globally, with LTHL being entitled to undertake key money arrangements, in the manner as mutually agreed.

points.point: The 22 Sept 2026 filing records receipt of NSE 'no objection' and BSE 'no adverse observation' letters under Regulation 37, valid six months, with NCLT, shareholder and creditor approvals still pending — the gating item management had flagged as the timing risk.
points.quote: In this regard, we wish to inform you that the Company has received the Observation Letter s with 'no objection ' from the NSE and 'no adverse observations' from the BSE on September 22, 2026 vide their respective letters , pursuant to Regulation 37 of the Listing Regulations , in relation to the Scheme .

rationale.what_management_expects: Lemon Tree: debt-free, fee/brand/tech-only, EBITDA margin from ~60% pro forma to 70-80% steady state, ~60% PAT margin, high ROCE, free cash funding dividends. Fleur: India's largest owner (5,600 rooms, 39 hotels), net EBITDA Rs 850 crore FY27 and Rs 1,000+ crore FY28, ~48%+ post-fee margins, Warburg-backed capital for 2,500+ rooms, capital growth not dividends, and separately listed for market valuation.
rationale.gaps: Absolute valuation of the demerged undertaking and Warburg's price for APG's stake, Fleur's issue price, hold-co discount size, post-demerger ROE, and fate of the two retained leases.

judge.what_is_spun: Agrochemicals (Crop Health Sciences) division — pesticides, insecticides, herbicides, biostimulants — demerged into Natco Crop Health Sciences Limited
judge.reason: Risk and reward of the pharmaceutical and agrochemicals verticals differ; segregation enables focused growth, operational efficiency, independent capital allocation, different investor sets, and is expected to unlock the value of the business verticals.
judge.insiders: Promoter and Promoter Group hold 8,84,65,126 of 17,91,09,870 shares (~49%); 1:1 entitlement carries that stake into the Resulting Company. Demerged Company retains 20% post-listing; director P.S.R.K. Prasad sits on Natco Crop Health Sciences' board.
judge.hidden_value: Demerged turnover was only ₹60.62 crore, 1.48% of total; FY25 agro segment result was a ₹1,458 million loss. Management says it reached ~₹140 crore sales and roughly EBITDA breakeven. Separation removes a loss-maker from pharma and exposes an early-growth agro business.
judge.selling_pressure_why: Tiny (1.48% of turnover), loss-making, different industry; 4,22,879 pharma shareholders receive 1:1 agrochemical shares, with parent holding 20%.
judge.listing_timeline: Not stated as a listing date. Board (March 24, 2026): Appointed Date 1st October 2026 and "Subsequent to the Scheme coming into effect, the Resulting Company /Transferee Company shall apply for the listing of its equity shares over Stock Exchanges in accordance with the Scheme." On the Feb 12, 2026 call management said "roughly, we're thinking by October, November" and "we should be able to do it in the next 8, 9 months"; on Nov 14, 2025 "we are targeting that for the year 2026." On September 9, 2026 the Company said it "has not filed the Scheme and related applications with the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal" and will file a revised Scheme after the Rights Issue.
judge.read_next: The revised Scheme to be filed with Stock Exchanges post Rights Issue — check the share swap ratio and agro segment numbers.
judge.quote: The segregation is also expected to unlock the value of the business verticals of the Demerged Company.

rationale.rationale: NATCO is demerging its Crop Health Sciences (Agrochemicals) division into Natco Crop Health Sciences Limited, leaving the listed parent as a pure pharmaceutical company (FDFs, APIs, oncology-led branded/complex generics). Management's stated reason is that the two verticals carry different risk-reward profiles and serve entirely different customers — Rajesh Chebiyam said the demerger "gives a more focused approach because the business, ultimately, the customers are quite different" — so a dedicated management, channel and product strategy (differentiated, patent-controlled, limited-competition molecules like the fungicide GLANZ and CTPR combinations) can be run without competing for attention inside a much larger pharma P&L. The second reason is valuation and capital: agro turnover was only INR 60.62 crore in FY25, i.e. 1.48% of total turnover, against FY25 group revenue of INR 4,784 crore and PAT of INR 1,883.4 crore, and Rajeev Nannapaneni said shareholders "will get another business which is not being valued in our system because it is of a very tiny business and a very large business in pharma"; separately listed, "it can raise its own capital and grow by itself." The timing was deliberately set after the division approached breakeven — segment loss of about INR 150 crore in FY25 (including a INR 50 crore non-cash PP&E impairment taken in Q4 FY25), narrowing to a INR 3.2 crore loss in Q1 FY26 on INR 34.7 crore of sales, EBITDA-positive at INR 52.4 crore of sales in Q2 FY26, and roughly INR 140 crore of FY26 sales versus INR 60 crore the prior year, against the INR 150–170 crore management had said was needed for EBITDA breakeven. The Scheme adds the corporate-finance logic: focused growth, operational rationalisation, optimum use of resources, and the ability for each business to "address independent business opportunities, pursue efficient capital allocation and attract different sets of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders," plus unlocking the value of the verticals. Shareholders get 1 share of the resulting company for every 1 NATCO share, with NATCO retaining 20% of the post-listing equity to keep supporting a business "still at its early growth stages" — so holders retain 100% of the ultimate economic interest (80% direct, 20% through NATCO). The push came from public-market shareholders, not lenders or partners: an investor on the Nov 14, 2025 call asked directly about "value unlocking for the shareholders," and management separately cited shareholder feedback that NATCO's profit base was too concentrated. Agro is almost entirely domestic ("predominantly domestic" sales, with 25–30% input cost inflation flagged in 2026), which management contrasts with the export-weighted pharma business.
rationale.evolution: On the Feb 13, 2025 and May 29, 2025 calls there was no demerger talk — only agro losses, the INR 50 crore impairment and a INR 120–170 crore breakeven target; the Aug 13, 2025 call reported the loss down to INR 3.2 crore with still no mention. The board gave in-principle approval to evaluate the demerger on Sep 25, 2025, and Rajeev first discussed it publicly on the Nov 14, 2025 call ("demerge this business from the main company and list it separately... targeting that for the year 2026"), framing it as value unlocking plus the ability to raise its own capital; the board approved incorporating the wholly-owned resulting company on Nov 14, 2025. On Feb 12, 2026 the timeline was guided to "October, November" 2026 (8–9 months), and the Scheme itself was approved on Mar 24, 2026 with a 1:1 share entitlement, appointed date Oct 1, 2026 and 20% retained by NATCO; the May 29, 2026 call reiterated focus and different customers as the primary reason. By Sep 9, 2026 the Scheme had stock-exchange observation letters but had not been filed with the NCLT, because the INR 1,279.36 crore rights issue at INR 750/share (allotted Oct 23, 2026) changes the capital structure — the board decided to re-cut and re-file the Scheme after the rights issue while keeping the same swap ratio.

points.point: First public confirmation of the plan: demerge Crop Health Sciences out of the parent and list it separately, targeted for 2026, disclosed alongside the division reaching roughly EBITDA breakeven at INR 52.4 crore of quarterly sales.
points.quote: I think we have announced earlier that we will demerge this business from the main company and list it separately and we are targeting that for the year 2026.

points.point: Rajeev defines the value-unlock logic in response to an investor question: separate listing gives the business special focus and the ability to raise its own capital and grow independently, now that it is breaking even.
points.quote: Value unlocking means I think what we see is this business now is about breaking even now. So, we will list it separately and then we will have special focus on this and it can raise its own capital and grow by itself.

points.point: The core valuation argument: the agro business is too small to be valued inside a pharma company of NATCO's size, and shareholders will get a complete see-through into both businesses.
points.quote: I think you will get another business which is not being valued in our system because it is of a very tiny business and a very large business in pharma.

points.point: Timeline guidance: the process has started, with an internal goal of completing in the next 8–9 months (around October–November 2026), but no firm date committed.
points.quote: I think we have started the process. So , I think roughly, we're thinking by October, November, but I don't want to say any definite time lines, but this is our, what should I say, goal to do.

points.point: Management's clearest operating rationale, from the head of Crop Health Sciences: a focused approach is needed because the agro customer base is entirely different from pharma, with FY26 agro sales of about INR 140 crore versus INR 60 crore the year before.
points.quote: So, as you're aware, so we're in the process of demerging the business. And one of the primary reasons we felt also it gives a more focused approach because the business, ultimately, the customers are quite different.

points.point: Growth plans — new differentiated, patent-controlled, limited-competition products, more channel partners and more people — are tied directly back to the demerger as the reason for sharper focus.
points.quote: So I think we're fairly confident going forward. And that's also one of the main reasons for demerging and having more focus on the business.

points.point: The Mar 24, 2026 Scheme of Arrangement grounds the demerger in differing risk-reward profiles of the pharmaceutical and agrochemicals verticals; agro turnover was INR 60.62 crore in FY25, 1.48% of total company turnover.
points.quote: The Board of Directors of the Demerged Company believe that the risk and reward associated with each of the aforesaid business verticals are different.

points.point: The Scheme's capital-markets rationale: each business can chase its own opportunities, allocate capital efficiently and attract its own investor and lender base, alongside focused growth, operational rationalisation and value unlocking.
points.quote: Each business would be able to address independent business opportunities, pursue efficient capital allocation and attract different sets of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders.

points.point: NATCO keeps 20% of the post-listing equity of the resulting company so it can keep funding and strategically supporting an early-stage business; shareholders get 1 new share for every 1 NATCO share, retaining 100% of the ultimate economic interest (80% direct plus 20% indirect).
points.quote: Further, the Demerged Company intends to retain the current shareholding in the Resulting Company (20% of post listing shareholding) in order to continue to offer support to the Agrochemicals Business which is still at its early growth stages and help in monitoring the progress and providing strategic support.

points.point: The Nov 14, 2025 board filing states the purpose as unlocking value in the core pharmaceutical business while giving each entity operational flexibility, dedicated management and separate brand positioning.
points.quote: To demerge the Agro business of the Company into a separate entity, the move shall enable value unlocking of the core business (pharmaceuticals) and enhance long -term growth.

points.point: Pre-demerger baseline for why the division was a drag: a INR 50 crore non-cash impairment on agro property, plant and machinery in Q4 FY25, FY25 agro revenue of about INR 60 crore, and INR 160–170 crore needed just to be EBITDA positive.
points.quote: So, I think this year, we feel we are going to hit that critical mass where we'll start breaking even. We are doing about INR60 crores net revenue last year. So, I think we need to hit about INR160 crores to INR170 crores at least to have that EBITDA positive.

points.point: The Sep 9, 2026 board update: the Scheme had received observation letters from both exchanges but was not filed with the NCLT because the INR 1,300 crore rights issue changes the capital structure, so the Scheme will be amended and re-filed post-issue with the swap ratio unchanged.
points.quote: The fund raising by way of a Rights Issue proposed at the meeting of the board of directors held on September 09, 2026 is expected to result in change to the Company's capital structure and shareholding pattern and consequently would require necessary changes to the Scheme.

rationale.what_management_expects: Agro: dedicated management focus, its own capital raising, differentiated limited-competition products, growth past breakeven from roughly INR 140 crore sales. Pharma: a cleaner, focused oncology/complex-generics entity. For shareholders: value unlocked in a business "not being valued in our system," a complete see-through into both, operational efficiency, efficient capital allocation, and distinct investor/lender bases.
rationale.gaps: No standalone agro financials, debt/asset split, valuation or swap-ratio basis; no post-demerger profitability, capital needs, board/management, listing date, or revised Scheme terms.

segments.measure_notes: Profit line is the Ind AS 108 'Segment results' from consolidated segment reporting — a pre-finance-cost, pre-tax result (total segment result less finance cost = consolidated PBT), i.e. effectively segment EBIT including the FY2025 ₹500 mn PP&E impairment charged to this segment. Revenue is 'Segment revenue' which sums exactly to consolidated total revenue from operations; no inter-segment revenue is separately disclosed, so it is treated as external. Quarterly presentations report a 'Crop Health Sciences' revenue line only (FY25 598 / FY26 1,382 vs segment-note 606 / 1,382) with no segment-level profit.

judge.what_is_spun: Merchant Power Undertaking — Vedanta's merchant thermal power generation business (Athena, Meenakshi), demerged into Talwandi Sabo Power Limited
judge.reason: Creation of five independent sector-specific pure-play companies, allowing each to chart its own growth trajectory and attract thematic investors; unlocking hidden value by enabling each business to be valued independently, with improved transparency
judge.insiders: Each Resulting Company issued 1 share for every 1 Vedanta share, so promoter group (Vedanta Resources, 54.72% of VEDL as on June 30, 2026) carried over pro rata; promoters excluded from VEDL ESOS/ESPP 2026
judge.hidden_value: Separation reveals leverage: Vedanta Power's net debt/EBITDA 4.7x, highest of the five, though debt is mostly structural long-term PFC/REC with 7-10 year maturities; residual Vedanta sits at 0.30x with AA+/stable
judge.selling_pressure_why: 1:1 shares pushed to every Vedanta holder; thermal power unrelated to parent's metals/mining mandate; most levered of the five entities
judge.listing_timeline: On April 29, 2026: effective and record date set for May 1st, with shares of the resulting companies 'expected to list and commence trading by mid-June'; the July 30, 2026 presentation states '4 new entities listed on NSE & BSE on 15th June'

On the demerger, we are at the final stage. We remain confident of completing our demerger by end of this fiscal, unlocking focused value acros s our five verticals. In summary, we remain encouraged about our commodity macro fundamentals, operational momentum and strengthened balance sheet. With several growth projects coming online and a stronger expected run rate in H2, we are confident in achieving an annual EBITDA of more than $6 billion in FY '26 at Vedanta India consol level, surpassing previous records and supporting Vedanta's transformation into a global leader in critical minerals, energy transition and technology. rationale.rationale: Management framed the separation as the core of "Vedanta 2.0": breaking one monolithic diversified natural-resources company into five independent, sector-specific pure-play listed companies — Vedanta Limited (residual: Zinc India/HZL, Zinc International, Copper, Ferrochrome/FACOR, Nickel), Vedanta Aluminium Metal Ltd, Vedanta Power/Talwandi Sabo Power (merchant power), Vedanta Oil & Gas/Malco Energy (Cairn), and Vedanta Iron & Steel — so that each could "chart out their own growth trajectory and attract respective thematic investors" rather than being valued as a conglomerate (Apr 2026, Apr 2025: "pure-play entities that will enhance strategic focus and operational flexibility"). The stated problem was that a single balance sheet and single capital-allocation process blurred very different businesses: Zinc India at 56% EBITDA margin and $959/t COP, aluminium at 38% margin, versus a Copper trading business running ~1% margin, and a power business that wants to add 10–12 GW. The fix was a capital structure "architected with precision… aligning debt with earning strength and growth stage of each resulting company": of $5.5bn net debt (group leverage 0.95x), $3.5bn goes to Aluminium (1.3x), Power sits at 4.7x on long-dated PFC/REC paper, Vedanta Limited keeps ~$1bn (0.4x), while Oil & Gas is nil-debt and Iron & Steel carries no more than $0.2bn. Specific frictions the split removes: the Copper brand fee drops from 3% to 0.75% on ~$3.1–3.2bn of revenue (~$65m, +2.25% to EBITDA), taking Copper margin from ~1% toward at least 5% in FY27; the dividend policy moves from "prescriptive" to "descriptive", from rule-based (minimum 30% of profit) to principle-based, and the mandate to upstream Hindustan Zinc dividends within six months falls away; Ajay Goel also called it "an opportunity… from taxation viewpoint" via recast balance sheets, accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation. Third parties shaped the terms: lenders demanded debt allocation be "broadly aligned with the bankers as a precondition for granting NOC"; the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas objected at NCLT over ~$512–520m of disputed dues and was satisfied only by a Vedanta corporate guarantee covering the full alleged claims, with any arbitration outcome ring-fenced to Oil & Gas; creditor SEPCO was settled in full for ₹660 crore "as part of demerger proceedings… paving the way for a proposed demerger process", and a ₹1,248 crore cash-backed bank guarantee was lodged with NCLAT over the TSPL power demerger. Management also pointed to equity-side demand — "many anchor investors domestically and globally are very keen to come in the cap table" of the de-merged entities as a fresh deleveraging avenue for VRL's remaining $4.7bn. Three months after listing, the Board extended the same logic to a second, vertical separation: ~2,264 acres and ~53,185 sq ft of surplus real estate (22 assets, only ₹1.26 crore of FY26 turnover, 0.001% of standalone revenue) into Vedanta Property Platforms Ltd at 1 share for every 20, because the portfolio was "historically subject to limited focused utilisation, resulting in sub-optimal visibility… and value realization."
rationale.evolution: The demerger was already a live execution item by the Feb 2025 call (Jan 31, 2025), where Ajay Goel flagged the Feb 18 shareholder/creditor meetings as "the important stage of execution"; on the Apr 2025 call (Apr 30, 2025) Deshnee Naidoo recast it as creating "pure-play entities" under Vedanta 2.0 with completion guided for September 2025. It then slipped repeatedly on legal and stakeholder hurdles — Aug 2025 (Jul 31, 2025) disclosed the NCLT second-motion part-hearing of July 2 with the next date Aug 20, an NCLAT interim stay on the TSPL power order, and the MoPNG objection; Nov 2025 (Oct 31, 2025) resolved SEPCO for ₹660 crore and MoPNG via a Vedanta corporate guarantee, guiding to a final Nov 12 hearing and five listings by FY26-end. Jan 2026 (Jan 29, 2026) reported NCLT approval on Dec 16, 2025 (power on Jan 9, 2026) and shifted the detail toward mechanics — bank NOCs conditioned on debt allocation, recast balance sheets, tax structuring — targeting Apr 1 effectiveness; Apr 2026 (Apr 29, 2026) set the record date at May 1 with mid-June listing, 4 extra shares per share, and added two new rationales not previously spelled out: the Copper brand-fee cut to 0.75% and five independent dividend policies. By the Jul 30, 2026 filings the plan had extended beyond the original five, with a sixth vertical split of surplus real estate into Vedanta Property Platforms Ltd at 1:20.

points.point: The demerger was already at the shareholder/creditor-vote stage, pitched purely as investor value unlock, with no operational rationale given on this call.
points.quote: On the demerger front, we are in the important stage of execution , the shareholders and the creditors meeting scheduled on Feb 18th. This transformative step is poised to unlock significant value for our investors.

points.point: First explicit statement of the design goal — pure-play entities for strategic focus and operational flexibility — inside the Vedanta 2.0 ambition of a $100bn critical minerals, energy and technology powerhouse; completion then guided for September 2025.
points.quote: We are making good progress with our demerger plan, aiming to create pure-play entities that will enhance strategic focus and operational flexibility.

points.point: A shareholder (Ashish Kejriwal, Nuvama) pressed that mining leases — Sijimali bauxite and the coal blocks held under Vedanta Limited — must first be transferred to Vedanta Aluminium before the split can complete; management confirmed a parallel approvals plan.
points.quote: Ashish, you are right. This is part of the overall approvals that we have in our sight.

points.point: Execution stalled in two forums at once: the NCLT second-motion petition was part-heard on July 2 with the next date Aug 20, and NCLAT granted an interim stay on the TSPL power demerger order, backed by a ₹1,248 crore fully cash-backed bank guarantee over the SEPCO creditor matter.
points.quote: Separately, the NCL AT has granted an interim stay on TSPL, our power demerger order by NCLT, with the next hearing scheduled on 4th August.

points.point: The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas objected at NCLT, questioning whether the demerged, standalone Cairn oil & gas P&L could absorb disputed dues if arbitration went against Vedanta — i.e. a regulator worrying that separation strips a weaker entity of parent support.
points.quote: In the last NCLT hearing, they did express concern about the payments of any of the disputed dues that may become payable by Cairn in case the ongoing arbitration ruling, as we have all learned now, comes in their favor.

points.point: A long-standing SEPCO creditor dispute was settled in full for ₹660 crore (part of ₹1,547 crore of net exceptional items that quarter) explicitly to clear the path for the scheme.
points.quote: As part of demerger proceedings, a full and final settlement of Rs. 660 Cr has been done with SEPCO , thereby resolving a long -standing dispute, paving the way for a proposed demerger process.

points.point: MoPNG's objection — over roughly $512–520m of alleged claims — was resolved not by cash but by a Vedanta corporate guarantee covering the full extent of the claims, so the demerged oil & gas entity would not carry the obligation.
points.quote: Their concern has been taken care of by us providing a corporate guarantee from Vedanta.

points.point: Five simultaneous listings by FY26-end were framed as the vehicle for sharper strategic focus, with Goel adding that it unlocks "focused value across our five verticals".
points.quote: This will set the stage for the listing of all five demerge d entities by the end of FY '26, enabling greater strategic focus and enhanced value creation for all stakeholders.

points.point: After NCLT approval on Dec 16, 2025 (power order Jan 9, 2026), the rationale was stated as three things at once — sharper strategy, stronger standalone balance sheets, faster growth — with Q3 results already reported under Ind AS 105 demerger accounting.
points.quote: This marks a defining moment in our journey, one that empowers our businesses to sharpen the strategies, strengthen the balance sheets and accelerate growth with the aim of unlocking shareholder value.

points.point: Lenders drove the capital-structure design: debt allocation across the five entities had to be agreed with banks before they would issue no-objection certificates, with $6.7bn of Vedanta India consol net debt split by asset ratio and each entity's own cash-generation and debt-servicing capability.
points.quote: When we went to the banker seeking NOC, in that case, debt allocation was broadly aligned with the bankers as a precondition for granting NOC for demerger approval.

points.point: Goel named taxation and deleveraging as further gains — recast balance sheets, accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation per entity — alongside the intent to make oil & gas and iron & steel debt-free, funded partly by the ₹3,000 crore HZL OFS.
points.quote: One thing I can confirm to the entire audience and to the stakeholders at large, that demerger in fact, becomes an opportunity across the areas.

points.point: Final articulation: five sector-specific pure-play companies whose purpose is independent growth paths and dedicated thematic investor bases; record date May 1, 2026, one Vedanta share yielding four additional shares, listing targeted by Q1 FY27 (mid-June).
points.quote: This will entail creation of five independent sector -specific pure -play companies, allowing each company to chart out their own growth trajectory and attract respective thematic investors.

points.point: Debt was matched to each business's earnings power and growth stage rather than split pro-rata: Oil & Gas nil debt, Iron & Steel under $0.2bn, Aluminium $3.5bn at 1.3x, Power 4.7x on 7–10 year PFC/REC paper, Vedanta Limited ~$1bn at 0.4x, against group leverage of 0.95x.
points.quote: The de -merger has been architected with precision on capital structure, aligning debt with earning strength and growth stage of each resulting company.

points.point: A concrete economic benefit of unbundling: the brand fee was re-benchmarked per entity, cutting Copper's rate from 3% to 0.75% on ~$3.1–3.2bn of revenue (~$65m), lifting Copper margin from roughly 1% to at least 5% in FY27, while the other entities stay at 3% (fixed to FY29).
points.quote: So the brand fee for copper from the current 3% will go down to 0.75% and that alone from India's viewpoint means higher EBITDA by 2.25%.

points.point: Each of the five boards gets its own dividend policy; Vedanta's shifts from rule-based (minimum 30% of profit) to principle-based, and the obligation to pass through Hindustan Zinc dividends within six months is removed.
points.quote: Currently, Vedanta's policy on dividend is more prescriptive; it will become more descriptive.

points.point: Separation creates a new deleveraging route for VRL's remaining $4.7bn: differentiated capital structures that anchor investors can enter at the entity level, on top of the ~$400m brand fee and 4–5% dividend.
points.quote: Now as we de -merge all the five companies, additionally we'll have the optionality of a differentiated capital structure and in that case, many anchor investors domestically and globally are very keen to come in the cap table , and that will be additional avenue for de -leveraging.

points.point: M&A governance was redrawn around the split: each CEO is mandated to grow organically on their own 2x/3x plans, with cross-sector or out-of-portfolio acquisitions sitting at a new holdco with its own M&A team and the Chairman.
points.quote: Holdco will be set up to make sure there is some visibility of capital allocation across all 5 businesses, but also with its own M&A team to start looking at some of these opportunities.

points.point: The May 16, 2026 cost-apportionment filing fixes the five resulting entities and their relative weights: Vedanta Limited 52.34%, Vedanta Aluminium Metal 7.15%, Talwandi Sabo Power 12.23%, Malco Energy (oil & gas) 21.49%, Vedanta Iron and Steel 6.79% — one share of each per Vedanta share, effective/appointed date May 1, 2026.

points.point: On July 30, 2026 the Board approved a sixth, vertical separation — surplus real estate (22 assets, ~2,264 acres and ~53,185 sq ft, just ₹1.26 crore of FY26 turnover, 0.001% of standalone revenue) into Vedanta Property Platforms Ltd at 1 share per 20 — because the assets sat embedded in the operating business and were under-utilised.
points.quote: The real estate business is currently embedded within the operating business and the real estate portfolio has been historically subject to limited focused utilisation, resulting in sub -optimal visibility of the real estate business segment and value realization.

points.point: The real estate scheme's stated aim mirrors the five-way logic — a pure-play platform with its own management, capital structure and investor base, potentially consolidating real estate from other group companies (Meenakshi Energy, Incab) and claiming a value-creation opportunity of over ₹30,000 crore on ~130mn sq ft.
points.quote: To unlock the inherent value of the Real Estate Business, enable focused development, exploit the growth potential of the Real Estate Business and attract a distinct set of investors and strategic partners aligned with real estate and infrastructure development, it is proposed to consolidate the Real Estate Business of the Demerged Company under an independent, dedicated entity.

points.point: The Q1 FY27 filings present the completed demerger as having validated the thesis: combined market cap of the resulting companies up over ₹71,000 crore in one quarter, and ₹225.50 at announcement (Sep 29, 2023) versus ₹932.05 combined on listing day (June 15, 2026).

rationale.rationale: Astral's board approved a Composite Scheme on 25 June 2026 that would (i) demerge the Chemicals Business Undertaking — adhesives, sealants, polyvinyl acetate, cyanoacrylates, solvent cements, silicone sealants, epoxy resins, construction chemicals, putties and specialty chemicals added 'through recent strategic acquisitions of DSS' — out of Astral Limited into its wholly-owned subsidiary Astral Chemie Limited (formerly Astral Coatings Pvt Ltd), which already holds the Paints & Coatings (Gem/Astral Paints) business, and (ii) amalgamate another wholly-owned subsidiary, Al-Aziz Plastics Pvt Ltd (electrofusion/compression fittings, saddles; FY26 turnover ₹373 mn, net worth ₹215 mn), back into Astral alongside Plumbing. The chemicals undertaking was ₹12,663 mn of FY26 turnover, 21% of Astral's ₹59,076 mn standalone revenue (net worth ₹41,058 mn); in the 20 May 2026 analyst meet management described the same mix as 'piping 72%, paint and adhesive 28%' of consolidated sales. The stated reasons: the two verticals have different products, customers, operating models, capital requirements, risk profiles, regulatory frameworks and growth opportunities, so each needs a dedicated leadership team and a specialised board instead of 'overlapping boardroom priorities'; combining all chemical verticals (adhesive, paint, specialty chemicals) under one umbrella was said to yield 'huge cost saving in Plants, Warehousing, Marketing and R&D' from shared labs, machinery and technical staff; capital deployment discipline — eliminating 'internal capital allocation conflicts', letting each vertical set its own capex, working capital and funding, and explicitly helping 'Bathware business in capital allocation discipline' while 'liberating the existing management to focus exclusively on the core plumbing business'; and value unlocking — the Scheme 'eliminates any conglomerate discount', lets global investors, institutions and shareholders back either vertical, and gives 'credit rating agencies, lenders, and research analysts … a clean, unbundled view of each Business vertical's financial and operating metrics'. The Al-Aziz merger was justified on the opposite logic: its fittings and Astral's pipes are interdependent ('their standalone utility is limited'), so merging internalises the supply chain, adds PAN-India plants/depots/field staff, centralises overlapping HDPE, specialty polymer and metallic insert buying for bulk discounts, and removes a separate legal entity's compliance and duplicate roles. Consideration was non-cash: 1 Astral Chemie share of ₹1 for every 1 Astral share held (1:1), Astral Chemie's pre-scheme capital cancelled, so its shareholding mirrored Astral's (promoters 54.22%, public 45.78%) with NSE/BSE listing to be sought; Al-Aziz shares simply extinguished with no new issue. No lender, partner or named investor is recorded as having asked for the split — the only requesters cited are 'various stakeholders, including shareholders, investors and other market participants', and their post-announcement feedback is what stopped it: on 5 July 2026 the board ordered a comprehensive independent review by 'any one of the big four or equivalent firm' (report within 30 days), and on 29 July 2026 that Independent Consultant 'recommended not to proceed … in the present form in light of the current scale of the Chemical Business'. The board withdrew the Scheme entirely, saying it 'may not be in the best interests of the Company and its shareholders' at this stage and that the chemicals demerger 'may be considered once it achieves scale and has financial strength to fund its organic and inorganic growth' — consistent with the chemicals segment's own May 2026 commentary that it was only now ready to scale (adhesives India targeting ₹2,000 cr and paints ₹1,000 cr in 3-4 years, paints still EBITDA-negative with a ₹6 cr Q4 loss).
rationale.evolution: The separation does not appear in any earnings call in the record: the 12 Aug 2025 (Q1 FY26), 6 Nov 2025 (Q2 FY26) and 20 May 2026 analyst-meet transcripts discuss only CPVC backward integration, the Al-Aziz and Nexelon acquisitions, UK/paint turnarounds and ROE pressure, and the 5 Feb 2026 'call' is only an exchange letter with an audio link, no transcript. What the calls do show is mounting investor pressure on the diversification (Sujit Jain on falling ROE and 2x capex overruns in Aug 2025; Sudeep Jain asking for per-acquisition sales/margin/cash-conversion/ROCE disclosure; questions in May 2025 on whether Astral would exit the UK), against management saying the opposite — 'we are not looking to exit any business' (Aug 2025) and 'we also are not looking at any other segments now than whatever the four segments we are in' (20 May 2026). The idea surfaces fully formed in the 25 June 2026 board filing and press release, is put under big-four independent review on 5 July 2026 after 'feedback from various stakeholders post the announcement', and is withdrawn on 29 July 2026 on the consultant's advice, with the demerger deferred until the chemicals business has scale.

points.point: The 25 June 2026 board approved a composite two-part restructuring: demerge the Chemicals Business (adhesives, sealants, construction chemicals, specialty chemicals from the DSS acquisitions) into wholly-owned Astral Chemie (which holds paints and coatings), and merge Al-Aziz Plastics back into Astral with Plumbing.
