points.quote: We believe these businesses have now reached a stage where dedicated leadership, greater accountability, sharper strategic focus and independent capital allocation can meaningfully accelerate their next phase of growth.

points.point: The Al-Aziz leg used the reverse argument — integration rather than separation — because its fittings need Astral's pipes to be sellable, plus HDPE/polymer procurement scale, PAN-India depots and fewer duplicate compliances.
points.quote: Given that the Transferee Company's fittings cannot function independently and inherently require specific piping systems manufactured by the Transferor Company, their standalone utility is limited.

points.point: Ten days after announcing it, the board put the whole Scheme under a big-four independent review because of shareholder/investor/market feedback, with recommendations due in 30 days.
points.quote: the management has received feedback from various stakeholders post the announcement of the Scheme. In view of the feedback received, the Board has decided to undertake a comprehensive independent review of the Scheme.

points.point: On 29 July 2026 the Scheme was withdrawn outright: the independent consultant judged the chemicals business too small to stand alone in that form.
points.quote: The Independent Consultant has recommended not to proceed with the Composite Scheme of Arrangement in the present form in light of the current scale of the Chemical Business.

points.point: The demerger was deferred rather than abandoned in principle, conditional on the chemicals business reaching scale and being able to self-fund growth and acquisitions.
points.quote: the demerger of the Chemical Business may be considered once it achieves scale and has financial strength to fund its organic and inorganic growth.

points.point: Six weeks before the announcement, management still presented the chemicals division as an in-house platform just reaching its scaling phase, with adhesives India targeting ₹2,000 crore and paints ₹1,000 crore in 3-4 years and paints not yet EBITDA-positive (₹6 crore Q4 loss) — the very scale shortfall later cited for withdrawal.
points.quote: The vision is to touch 2000 as fast as we can and we are sure that in next 3 to four years we'll be touching 2000 plus in Indian revenue not UK will be separate.

points.point: Hiranand Savlani framed the company's history as plumbing then chemical diversification, with the chemical platform 'ready' to scale under Astral — no hint of hiving it off.
points.quote: 1996 to 2014 was the plumbing era where the focus was on the plumbing side of the business.

points.point: The segment mix disclosed on the call (72% piping / 28% paint+adhesive consolidated) is the economic basis of the later split, though the Scheme's 21% is on standalone turnover, which excludes the UK adhesive business.
points.quote: This is basically piping is contributing 72% and paint and adhesive is contributing 28%.

points.point: Sandeep Engineer spent his opening remarks defending the diversification against persistent investor questions ('Why paint? Why adhesive?') and ruled out any further portfolio change — the opposite of a separation signal.
points.quote: at the same time we also are not looking at any other segments now than whatever the four segments we are in

points.point: The February 2026 earnings call is in the record only as an exchange intimation with an audio link, so no management commentary from that quarter is available on the question.
points.quote: Please find below web-link of Audio Recordings of "Earnings Call" held on 05th February, 2026.

points.point: Management's answer to the 70/30 plumbing-versus-chemicals mix question was that both verticals would keep growing inside one company, with only a mild shift from the low chemicals base — not a structural separation.
points.quote: No. It is not like that. Both vertical will keep growing.

points.point: Investors were pressing on the consequences of diversification — ₹1,500 crore of capex, falling ROE, acquisitions in 'WIP mode' — and the CFO conceded the return-ratio problem, which is the pressure the later demerger rationale answers.
points.quote: Question was continued pressure on ROE, yes, definitely you are absolutely right. We are also very worried about that thing also.

points.point: An investor asked for standardised per-acquisition accountability (growth, margin, cash conversion, ROCE) on each acquired business, i.e. the 'unbundled view' the Scheme later promised through separate listing; management agreed to create the format.
points.quote: a clear guidance for each acquisition in terms of sales growth, margin, cash conversion and ROC and progress on that quarter-after-quarter

points.point: Kairav Engineer explicitly denied any intent to separate or exit businesses, framing Astral as a permanent multi-segment owner.
points.quote: We are not thinking of any short term gain, we are not looking to exit any business, we are always here for long term

points.point: The earliest portfolio-separation pressure in the record concerns the loss-making UK adhesive business, which analysts asked Astral to exit; management refused and promised a turnaround instead.
points.quote: Many questions were asked today about what we would do with the UK and whether we're thinking of exiting the UK.

points.point: Management's stated logic for owning paints was its synergy with adhesives and construction chemicals — the same complementarity later used to justify putting them together in Astral Chemie, away from plumbing.
points.quote: paint was specifically acquired to increase the adhesive business, to be in the paint business, and also in the industrial paint and construction chemical business.

points.point: Two years earlier the chemicals/paints verticals were explicitly run as part of one Astral — systems, SAP, credit cycles and an Astral-brand launch managed centrally, with the adhesive integration playbook applied to paints.
points.quote: It is recalling this adhesive story when in 2014 we acquired adhesive also couple of years were like that only because we have to correct a lot of system and that is exactly happening right now also.

rationale.what_management_expects: Chemicals (adhesives, sealants, construction chemicals plus Gem/Astral paints) gains dedicated leadership, shared R&D/plant/warehouse/marketing cost savings, its own capex and funding decisions, and separately listed equity; Astral keeps plumbing and absorbs Al-Aziz fittings for procurement scale and fewer compliances. Both get ring-fenced capital allocation, unbundled metrics for lenders and analysts, no conglomerate discount, specialised boards.
rationale.gaps: No margin, cost-saving or valuation numbers quantified; DSS acquisition unexplained; Astral Chemie standalone financials, advisor identity, and which stakeholders objected never disclosed; calls never mentioned the demerger.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is AHEL's omnichannel pharmacy and digital health vertical — Apollo HealthCo, comprising the ~7,500-store Apollo Pharmacy retail/front-end network and the Apollo 24/7 digital platform (46mn users, INR 528 cr quarterly platform GMV) — which is being demerged into Apollo Healthtech Ltd, with Apollo Healthco Ltd and the promoter-linked distributor Keimed Private Limited (which supplies ~60,000 pharmacy stores) amalgamated into the same vehicle, which is then renamed Apollo Healthco Limited and listed; hospital-based pharmacies stay inside Healthcare Services, since as A. Krishnan put it in Aug 2025, 'what we are spinning out is only the retail pharmacies and the online.' The Scheme's own rationale states the problem plainly: the Identified Business Undertaking is 'distinct from other businesses undertaken by the Demerged Company' and 'necessitates a differentiated strategy aligned to its industry specific risks, market dynamics, and growth trajectory', so separation lets hospitals and retail/digital each focus on 'their respective businesses, efficient management, and control', consolidates HealthCo's and Keimed's distribution 'in an independent company focusing exclusively on digital health and pharmacy distribution', and lets the new entity 'build a wider capital and financial base, by attracting a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and stakeholders' — plus supply-chain integration, wider assortment, 'improved transparency in the supply chain preventing the entry of counterfeit or substandard medicines', administrative efficiency, board/managerial rationalisation and economies of scale. The financial case management repeated for six straight quarters is scale plus margin convergence: pro-forma combined revenue of INR 4,430 cr in Q1 FY26 (~INR 17,000 cr run-rate, INR 19,000 cr for FY26) becoming a INR 25,000 cr run-rate at 7% EBITDA by Q4 FY27; Sanjiv Gupta's arithmetic was that a 3.2% blended FY25 margin is already 6.4% once Apollo 24/7's losses and the accelerated ESOP charge are stripped out, with offline pharmacy going 7.4%→8-9% on private label (15.5% of pharmacy sales) and Keimed 3.1%→3.5%. The loss drag has in fact collapsed — digital cash losses fell from INR 111 cr (Q4 FY24) and INR 101 cr (Q2 FY25) to INR 29 cr in Q3 FY26 and INR 16 cr in Q4 FY26, with breakeven ex-ESOP guided to Q1 FY27 and including ESOP (~INR 50 cr FY27) by Q3 FY27 — and Apollo HealthCo crossed INR 10,000 cr of annual revenue in FY26, making it listable on its own. Keimed's merger was justified on concrete synergies: shared technology, data, people and product categories, cheaper dark stores (22 today) to push beyond the top six metros to the next ten cities, and private-label penetration across Keimed's franchise base. The push is not purely internal: Rasmeli Limited, the investor holding Class A/B compulsorily convertible preference shares in Apollo Healthco, receives a nominee director in the Resultant Company and signed a June 30, 2025 Upside Agreement sharing up to 9% of its own upside (only above 4x MOIC) with Ms. Shobana Kamineni — proposed Executive Chairperson — and identified employees; after shareholder and proxy-adviser pushback the Company issued clarifications on June 15 and June 19, 2026 adding 10% fall-away thresholds on nomination rights, tiered caps on promoter nominees, an individual 5% waiver, six independent directors and a Lead Independent Director. A second, separate separation was announced in May 2026: AHLL's Apollo Cradle and fertility verticals (INR 450 cr FY26 revenue, INR 45 cr IGAAP EBITDA) were combined with Cloudnine at INR 1,550 cr — 35x EBITDA — for cash plus a 9.9% stake, with the INR 750 cr of cash redeployed into primary care and diagnostics, which management called the funnel into Apollo.
rationale.evolution: The idea surfaced before this window as the 'strategic intent' for Apollo HealthCo (Aug 14, 2024 call) and was tracked through Feb 11, 2025 and the May 31, 2025 (Jun 2025) call purely as the Keimed merger 'progressing well', with a ~15-month timeline and Sanjiv Gupta's 3.2%→7% FY27 margin bridge; the composite Scheme itself was board-approved and filed on June 30, 2025. On the Aug 13, 2025 call management first spelled out the full shape — Apollo HealthCo as it stands gets demerged and separately listed by Q4 FY27, all steps within 18-21 months, only retail plus online moving out, Keimed folded in for technology/data/people/product synergies. Nov 7, 2025 and Feb 11, 2026 were process updates (statutory steps on track; CCI and SEBI approvals obtained, NSE no-objection Dec 23, 2025, NCLT filed and hearings begun, Keimed's subsidiaries consolidated to 100%), and the May 21, 2026 call set the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting for June 24, 2026 with completion still Q4 FY27. In the final stretch the plan changed on governance rather than structure: clarifications dated June 15 and June 19, 2026 added nomination-right fall-away thresholds in response to shareholder feedback, and on June 24, 2026 the Scheme passed with 90.44% of all votes and 85.71% of public votes in favour, but 14.31% of institutional votes against.

points.point: First explicit statement on a call of the demerger and separate listing, with the 18-21 month timetable and the INR 25,000 crore / 7% EBITDA end-state for the scheme concluding by FY27.
points.quote: The strategic reorganization of our omni -channel pharmacy and digital health business is proceeding as planned , and we expect to complete all steps within 18 to 21 months, a timeline that we had earlier announced.

points.point: A. Krishnan confirmed the mechanics in answer to an investor: HealthCo in its current form is the entity being demerged and listed by Q4 FY27, by which time Keimed's NCLT merger will also have happened.
points.quote: What will happen is Apollo HealthCo., as you are seeing in the current form, is what is going to be demerged and will be listed separately by Q4 of FY27.

points.point: Scope limit made explicit — hospital-based pharmacies stay with Healthcare Services; only the ~6,500-store retail chain and the online business leave, alongside Keimed, which supplies about 60,000 third-party pharmacy stores.
points.quote: The hospital -based pharmacies continues as part of hospitals, which I am sure you know, but it is something that , remember, what we are spinning out is only the retail pharmacies and the online out of that.

points.point: Madhivanan Balakrishnan listed the Keimed synergies: shared technology, data and people, cheaper dark stores (22 at the time) enabling expansion from the top 6 cities to the next 10 and beyond, and private label (then 14.6% of sales) pushed across Keimed's franchises.
points.quote: So , technology, data, people, and product categories , all the four synergies should start playing out as this merger comes in place.

points.point: Process update framing the combination as the way to capture scale benefits inside HealthCo; separately Madhivanan said merging Keimed, Apollo Pharmacy and the digital business would release further cost synergies from the next financial year.
points.quote: The statutory processes for the restructuring within Apollo HealthCo and the Keimed merger continue to proceed as per plan, and we remain well positioned to capture the full benefit of scale within Apollo HealthCo.

points.point: Regulatory progress is reported and the combined-entity target is restated verbatim as INR 25,000 crore run-rate revenue with 7% EBITDA.
points.quote: We have also made progress with respect to the regulatory integration process for the com posite scheme of Keimed merger and demerger of Apollo HealthCo and remain well positioned to capture the full benefits of scale with the combined entity to achieve a run rate of INR 25,000 crore in combined revenues with 7% EBITDA.

points.point: Obul Reddy itemised the approvals obtained (CCI, SEBI) and the NCLT filing, and confirmed Keimed had been cleaned up so that its subsidiaries are 100% owned before the merger.
points.quote: We have obtained Competition Commission approval and SEBI approval. We have filed with NCLT.

points.point: The purpose is stated in value terms for the first time in opening remarks — sharpening focus and unlocking long-term value across the integrated platform — in the same breath as HealthCo crossing INR 10,000 crore of annual revenue.
points.quote: During the year, we also announced a strategic restructuring of the omnichannel pharmacy and digital health business, an important step towards sharpening focus on unlocking long -term value across our integrated health care platform.

points.point: Timeline and end-state confirmed: NCLT-convened shareholder meeting on June 24, 2026, listing of Apollo Healthtech around end-December/early Q4 FY27, annualised revenue of INR 25,000 crore at listing.
points.quote: And hopefully, by Q4 FY27, end of December or early Q4 FY27 is when Apollo Healthtech should get demerged and listed.

points.point: A second, separate disposal: AHLL's Cradle and fertility verticals (INR 450 cr revenue, INR 45 cr EBITDA) go into a Cloudnine-combined platform at INR 1,550 crore — 35x EBITDA — for cash plus a 9.9% stake, with INR 750 crore of cash redeployed into primary care and diagnostics.
points.quote: One is the valuation, which is clearly key to get a valuation of INR 1,500 for EBITDA at a multiple of 35 in this market is something that you cannot ignore.

points.point: The Scheme's stated core problem: the pharmacy/digital undertaking is a different business from hospitals and needs its own strategy, risk posture and growth path; separation gives each side focus, management and control.
points.quote: The Scheme would enable carving-out of the Identified Business Undertaking, which is distinct from other businesses undertaken by the Demerged Company, necessitates a differentiated strategy aligned to its industry specific risks, market dynamics, and growth trajectory.

points.point: Capital-markets rationale: the separated entity is expected to attract its own investors, partners and lenders — i.e. a funding base hospitals cannot supply.
points.quote: The Scheme is expected to enable Resultant Company to build a wider capital and financial base, by attracting a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and stakeholders, as well as promoting overall business growth;

points.point: The Keimed leg is justified as consolidating pharmacy distribution into a single pure-play vehicle, with the Scheme also citing supply-chain integration, wider assortment, counterfeit prevention, administrative efficiency and board rationalisation.
points.quote: The Scheme would also result in consolidation of pharmacy distribution business of Transferor Company 1 and Transferor Company 2, in an independent company focusing exclusively on digital health and pharmacy distribution, enabling synergies;

points.point: Governance package embedded in the Scheme: a 12-member board with 6 independents, the AHL Promoter as Executive Chairperson, three promoter nominees, one AHEL nominee and one nominee for investor Rasmeli Limited, plus the Rasmeli-funded upside-sharing arrangement with Ms. Shobana Kamineni and identified employees.
points.quote: reconstitution of the board of directors of Resultant Company as follows: (i) AHL Promoter (as defined in the Scheme); (ii) 3 (three) directors nominated by the Resultant Company Promoters (as defined in the Scheme); (iii) 1 (one) director nominated by the Demerged Company; (iv) 1 (one) director nominated by Rasmeli Limited; and (v) 6 (six) independent directors;

points.point: June 15, 2026 clarification issued in response to shareholder feedback: the Upside Agreement is investor-funded with no cash outflow from Apollo Healthtech, capped and conditional on a 4x MOIC hurdle, and Rasmeli plus the promoter group will waive nomination rights below 10% shareholding.
points.quote: No minimum amount is guaranteed, with a maximum of 9% of the upside delivered to Rasmeli for achievin g at least 4x MOIC.

points.point: June 19, 2026 follow-up added a sliding scale of promoter nominee caps (nil below 10%, up to 5 at 35%+), an individual 5% waiver per promoter entity, half the board independent while there is an executive chairperson, and a Lead Independent Director.
points.quote: Apollo Hospitals now further clarifies that the promoter and promoter gro up are committ ed to waiving their rights to nominate directors in excess of the maximum numbers set out below, by reference to their aggregate shareholding.

points.point: Shareholder vote on June 24, 2026 passed the Scheme (90.44% of votes polled in favour; 85.71% of public votes), but institutional public shareholders split 85.69% for / 14.31% against — the clearest sign of residual investor discomfort, which no earnings call addressed.
points.quote: the public shareholders of the Demerged Company have approved the Scheme the votes cast in favour of the Scheme are more than the votes cast against the Scheme.

rationale.what_management_expects: Apollo Healthtech becomes a pure-play pharmacy and digital health company: INR 25,000 cr run-rate revenue at 6.5-7% EBITDA by Q4 FY27 (FY26 exit 4.3%), digital at breakeven, Keimed 3.1%-to-3.5%, offline pharmacy 8-9% on private label, its own investors, lenders and board. AHEL keeps hospitals and AHLL at 25.4% ROCE, redeploying cash into beds, primary care and diagnostics.
rationale.gaps: Calls never discussed the share entitlement ratio, debt/cash split, AHEL's residual stake, Keimed's purchase valuation or related-party pricing, the 14.31% institutional dissent, or the Upside Agreement.

judge.what_is_spun: HUL's Ice Cream business undertaking, demerged into Kwality Wall's (India) Limited on a going-concern basis
judge.reason: "Creation of a leading listed ice cream company in India with focused management having greater flexibility to deploy strategies suited to the Ice Cream businesses' distinctive operating model and market dynamics, to realise its full potential"
judge.insiders: Promoter stake in KWIL not stated; HUL's own shareholding in KWIL was reduced and cancelled and KWIL ceased to be a subsidiary. KWIL has a dedicated management team (Chitrank Goel, Deputy MD; Prashant Premrajka, CFO) drawn from HUL.
judge.hidden_value: Cost apportionment puts KWIL at only 1.91% of HUL's value versus 98.09%, set on net assets as at 30 November 2025 — a small, separately listed ice-cream pure-play, 2,34,95,91,262 shares of Re 1, with Kwality Wall's, Cornetto and Magnum.
judge.selling_pressure_why: Very small relative size (1.91% of pre-demerger cost basis) distributed 1:1 to every HUL holder; a separate ice-cream company versus a large FMCG parent.
judge.listing_timeline: FAQ dated 29th November 2025: "the statutory timeline for the listing and commencement of trading of shares of KWIL is within a period of 60 days from the receipt of the certified copy of the order of the NCLT sanctioning the Scheme (in or around Q4 of FY26)"; filing dated 13th February 2026 confirms listing and trading approval received 12th February 2026 for 2,34,95,91,262 equity shares with "Date of Commencement of Trading: ... 16th February, 2026"
judge.read_next: KWIL's first standalone results and balance sheet — the net assets behind the 1.91% cost apportionment.
judge.quote: The Scheme has come into effect on 1st December , 2025, being the Effective Date (as defined under the Scheme ).

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is HUL's Ice Cream business — the Kwality Wall's, Cornetto and Magnum brands — demerged into a new listed entity, Kwality Wall's (India) Limited (KWIL), under a Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai (orders dated 30 October 2025 and 6 November 2025), effective 1 December 2025, with KWIL listing on 16 February 2026. The Scheme's stated benefit is the 'creation of a leading listed ice cream company in India with focused management having greater flexibility to deploy strategies suited to the Ice Cream business's distinctive operating model and market dynamics, to realise its full potential' — i.e. the structural argument is that ice cream does not fit HUL's FMCG operating model. The financial case management gave on the calls is size and dilution: Ice Cream is 'roughly 3-odd percentage of our business' and 'makes low single-digit margin', below the HUL average, so CFO Ritesh Tiwari guided that removing it adds 50–60bps to reported EBITDA margin on top of the 22–23% guidance (later restated by Niranjan Gupta as a 50bps benefit, giving an implied 22.5–23.5% band). FY26 also showed the category's volatility — Ice Cream 'declined year on year, impacted by extended monsoon in addition to GST transition' in the September quarter — reinforcing the seasonality/operating-model argument. Mechanically it was a two-step process: demerger completed in the December quarter with Ice Cream reported as a discontinued business, then listing in Q4 FY26; shareholders received 1 KWIL share of Re.1 for every 1 HUL share (2,34,95,91,262 shares allotted on 1:1), with cost of acquisition apportioned 98.09% HUL / 1.91% KWIL. The December quarter reported PAT of Rs. 6,603 crores (up 121%) included a 'one-time non-cash gain arising from Ice Cream demerger', and HUL flagged it would lose PLI benefits that had flowed through the P&L via Ice Cream. By May 2026 Priya Nair framed it as portfolio rotation — 'strategic actions such as the demerger of Ice Cream, along with the investments at OZiva and Minimalist, are already enhancing the growth mix of the portfolio' — while explicitly keeping Foods (Tea, Coffee, Horlicks/Boost, Kissan) 'outside the perimeter of the Unilever transaction that we have done'.
rationale.evolution: In the Apr 2025 call (24 April 2025, FY25 results) it was already an in-flight action — 'progressing on track with regulatory requirements', completion expected by end of FY26 — the original announcement rationale sitting in earlier calls not included here. By the Oct 2025 call (23 October 2025) the plan was firmed and quantified: demerger in the December quarter with Ice Cream shown as a discontinued business, listing in Q4 FY26, ~3% of business at low single-digit margin, 50–60bps reported-margin accretion, plus the admission that Ice Cream had declined on extended monsoon and GST transition. In the Feb 2026 call (12 February 2026) it was done — demerger completed in December, KWIL listing announced for 16 February 2026, a one-time non-cash demerger gain in reported PAT, and the guided EBITDA band reset to an implied 22.5–23.5%. By the May 2026 call (30 April 2026) it was cited retrospectively as one of the portfolio actions improving HUL's growth mix, alongside Minimalist and OZiva.

judge.what_is_spun: The Industrial business (Demerged Undertaking) — bearings for infrastructure, manufacturing, railways, energy — into SKF India (Industrial) Limited
judge.reason: Both businesses have different market dynamics, distinct customer needs; demerger enables focused capital allocation, faster decision making and independent growth strategies, giving strategic clarity to sharpen priorities and unlock greater value for all stakeholders
judge.insiders: Mirror-image demerger: 1 SKF Industrial share per SKF India share; Resulting Company's shareholding pattern mirrors the parent on the record date, so no valuation was carried out. Management incentives in the new entity not stated
judge.hidden_value: Industrial carries 53.12% of the cost base versus 46.88% automotive, so the spun half is larger. Retained automotive guides only 11-12% PBT, 15.3% EBITDA, below Schaeffler/Timken ~20%; management says industrial is a little higher margin business than automotive
judge.selling_pressure_why: New separate listing of the larger half; every automotive-focused shareholder automatically received industrial shares in a different end-market
judge.listing_timeline: NCLT Mumbai sanctioned the Scheme by Order dated 26th September 2025; per NSE observation 18, SKF India (Industrial) Limited "shall ensure that steps for listing of specified securities are completed and trading in securities commences within sixty days of receipt of the order of the Hon'ble High Court/NCLT", which the Company said it "shall endeavour to comply" with (letter dated November 28, 2025); Information Memorandum advertisement published 27 November 2025, and by the 6 February 2026 press release the restructuring "has resulted in two independently focused entities"

rationale.rationale: SKF India separated its Industrial bearings business out of the listed company into SKF India (Industrial) Limited, leaving SKF India Ltd as a pure-play Automotive bearings company (management called it a "reverse carve-out" mirroring SKF AB's global split of Automotive, ~30% of group revenue versus 34-35% in India). Management's stated logic rested on three pillars: fundamentally different macro drivers (Automotive: EV/CAFE and BS-VII emission norms, 30% EV penetration target by 2030, premiumization/SUVs, last-mile commercial vehicles; Industrial: infrastructure spend, Make in India/NIP/PLI, China-Plus-One, railways/metro/Vande Bharat, wind and renewables doubling by 2030); different customer needs (a few large auto OEMs needing application-specific, longer-cycle engineered products — 60-65% engineered order in Auto versus ~25-30% in Industrial — against hundreds of industrial verticals wanting uptime, condition monitoring and remanufacturing); and a different manufacturing philosophy (Auto = large batch, small/medium bearings, automation and cycle-time efficiency; Industrial = wide assortment, small/large sizes, flexible lines with fast changeover plus a large traded component). The problems they said this solves: management attention split across two unlike businesses, capital allocation that could not be tailored (Auto was short of capacity, Industrial needed a brand-new Pune plant and localization from ~30-35% toward 70%), slow decision-making and launches, mismatched innovation cycles, and poor financial visibility for investors in a combined P&L. Operationally the split was defined down to the line: Bangalore 10 lines (7 Auto, 3 Industrial, with those 3 moving to Pune so Bangalore becomes 100% Auto), Pune 22 lines (12 Auto, 10 Industrial), Haridwar 4 lines all Auto; land 85:15 in Bangalore, 52:48 in Pune, 100% Auto in Haridwar; manpower 55-60% Auto versus 40-45% Industrial; cash allocated on the two businesses' last three years of profits. Shareholders received one SKF Industrial share of Rs 10 for every SKF India share held (PwC Business Consulting share entitlement report dated 24 December 2024; Saffron Capital fairness opinion 25 December 2024), with pre-demerger cost of acquisition apportioned 46.88% to SKF India and 53.12% to SKF Industrial. Pro forma FY24 economics shown to investors were Auto ~18% EBITDA and Industrial ~17%, both ~16% PBT, off a combined FY24 revenue of INR 45.7 billion; FY25 combined revenue was INR 4,919.9 crore (+7.65%) with PBT INR 763.1 crore (+3.71%). Nobody external demanded the separation — it was a group-level decision, with investors on the calls supportive (one explicitly "wholeheartedly supported" it) while pressing for structural clarity given SKF would still have three Indian entities including the unlisted SKF Engineering & Lubrication (Ahmedabad plant, global technical centre, lubrication and sealing factories); no lender or partner requirement was ever cited.
rationale.evolution: The demerger was announced in Q4 CY2024 and first explained in detail on a dedicated update call on 9 April 2025, which laid out the three macro/customer/manufacturing drivers, the six enablers (management focus, manufacturing efficiency, tailored capital, agility, innovation, investor visibility), pro forma FY24 carve-out financials and a 12-15 month timeline, plus an aspiration of "2 to 3 more points" of EBITDA. By the 19 May 2025 Q4 call the plant allocation had firmed up (Haridwar 100% Auto, Bangalore ~80-85% Auto, a new Industrial factory beside the Pune plant), and the 30 June 2025 investor meet added line-by-line, land and manpower splits, segment revenue mixes from FY22-FY25, three-year guidance (Auto 10-12%, Industrial 8-10% to FY28, margins held at 17-19%) and a step-up in capex from ~INR 150 crore to roughly INR 350-400 crore a year (INR 450-500 crore Pune industrial plant by 2028, INR 500-600 crore Auto capex to 2030); the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting on 14 July 2025 approved the 1:1 scheme, and the 6-7 August 2025 AGM and Q1 FY26 call quantified the cost for the first time (INR 184 million in Q1, mostly SAP/IT separation and consultants, 1.5-2% margin drag running into H1 FY27, plus stamp duty on asset transfer) while conceding the businesses were "so deeply integrated" that separation was complex. After NCLT sanction on 26 September 2025, effectiveness on 1 October 2025 and a 15 October 2025 record date, the story changed tone: the 21 May 2026 call presented SKF India as a standalone automotive company guiding to only 11-12% PBT margin (FY26 EBITDA 15.3%) with investors complaining that disclosure had "dropped substantially" post-demerger and that margins were far below what was promised in the run-up to the demerger vote, management answering that royalty was unchanged and this was a transition.

points.point: The stated purpose: two independent, fit-for-purpose companies that each accelerate growth and profitability, driven by three differences — industry dynamics, customer needs and manufacturing philosophy.
points.quote: The intention of this demerger is to create 2 fit-for-purposes independent companies, which will accelerate both growth and profitability of both companies.

points.point: Management summarised the rationale as three separate axes of difference, with manufacturing efficiency and customer service as the payoff.
points.quote: So to summarize, macro drivers are different. Customer drivers and innovation is different; and third, the manufacturing itself, the process of manufacturing itself is very different, what will make us most efficient and help us serve the customer needs.

points.point: Manufacturing philosophy was the concrete operating problem: Auto runs large batches of small/medium bearings for few OEMs with automation and economies of scale, while Industrial needs flexible lines, customised solutions and a large traded/regional component.
points.quote: Automotive has a large batch sizes with small and medium-sized bearings.

points.point: Margin ambition attached to the separation: 2-3 percentage points of EBITDA upside in both businesses, from more efficient manufacturing, procurement and value-based pricing of premium products such as ceramic and energy-efficient bearings.
points.quote: So I would say while the margins are typically relatively thin, we would hope that we can get at least 2 to 3 more points on our EBITDA going forward.

points.point: Shareholders were told the split was economically neutral — a mirror shareholding with a 1:1 share issue and listing of SKF Industrial on both exchanges.
points.quote: The new company will mirror the shareholding of the existing listed company with each shareholder of SKF India receiving one share of SKF Industrial as a consideration of the demerger.

points.point: Investor visibility into the two businesses' separate performance was explicitly listed as one of the demerger benefits, alongside tailored capital deployment and two different manufacturing philosophies.
points.quote: and finally, just more visibility for the -- our investors, all of you, to be able to see the performance of the 2 entities independently.

points.point: Pro forma FY24 carve-out economics given to investors: Automotive ~18% EBITDA, Industrial ~17%, both around 16% PBT, with capex set to double from INR 130-150 crore as a new Industrial plant is built next to the existing Pune site.
points.quote: So if you look at FY '24, our EBITDA margins for automotive was around 18%. And industrial was around 17%.

points.point: The asset split was disclosed line by line — Bangalore 10 lines 70:30 with three lines moving to Pune so Bangalore becomes 100% Automotive, Pune 52:48 land, Haridwar 100% Automotive, manpower roughly 55:45.
points.quote: There are three main plants, as we said, Bangalore, Pune and Haridwar. Bangalore, today there are 10 lines that will be split in the ratio of 70 to 30.

points.point: Three-year guidance for the two entities: Automotive 10-12% growth, Industrial 8-10% (held back until the new Pune plant and localization land in FY27-28), with margins maintained at 17-19% and upside beyond FY28.
points.quote: Next 3 years till '28, we expect growth in automotive to be in the 10 % to 12% range, industrial to be a little lower, 8% to 10% range.

points.point: Capital allocation was the hard constraint being fixed: a brand-new Industrial-only Pune plant (DGBB, TRB, unitised bearings) costing INR 450-500 crore by 2028 plus INR 350-450 crore of additional lines, on top of INR 500-600 crore of Automotive capex to 2030.
points.quote: Pune, we will be setting up a new plant, fully industrial, for industrial, making primarily DGBBs, which are deep groove ball bearings, tapered roller bearings, and unitized bearings, which are UCs.

points.point: At the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting, management conceded the separation was complex precisely because the two businesses were deeply intertwined, and said the total demerger cost was still being accumulated.
points.quote: As you know, it's a complex project primarily because the businesses both automotive and industrial, they are so deeply integrated that having two independent businesses is a complex process.

points.point: An existing institutional shareholder (Ravi Purohit) publicly backed the demerger while asking why India would still be left with three SKF entities when the group was simplifying structures; management said no merger of entities was contemplated until the demerger completed.
points.quote: And first of all, we'd like to congratulate and have wholeheartedly supported this demerger initiative that SKF Group is undertaking.

points.point: First quantification of the cost: INR 184 million in Q1 FY26, mainly SAP and separate data infrastructure plus compliance consultants, with a 1.5-2% margin drag expected to run to H1 FY27 and extra stamp duty/registration cost on asset transfer in the Industrial entity.
points.quote: So if you look at our current quarter, cost of demerger was around INR184 million.

points.point: At the FY25 AGM the Chairman framed the demerger as strategic repositioning to sharpen focus, improve execution agility and deepen customer alignment, with manufacturing roadmaps diverging (Automotive automation-led high throughput; Industrial modular and demand-responsive).
points.quote: The announcement of our demerger, which is separating the automotive and industrial businesses into two focused publicly listed entities was a significant milestone.

points.point: Post-demerger, management clarified the direction of the carve-out — Industrial was hived off and the listed SKF India Limited is the automotive division, a reverse of the group-level split.
points.quote: But in India, it is a reverse carve -out where industrial has gone out. So SKF India Limited remains as automotive division.

points.point: The promised margin uplift did not appear: FY26 PBT fell 694 bps, EBITDA was 15.3%, and guidance was reset to 11-12% PBT, with Auto still buying medium DGBB and tapered roller bearings from SKF Industrial because of its own capacity shortage.
points.quote: Now talking about the sustainable margin, we could be looking at 11 -12% kind of margin in the near future, while obviously in long term, the focus would be on improving it further, but the sustainable margin will be that.

points.point: A long-term shareholder attacked the post-demerger communication gap, noting pre-demerger guidance of 16-19% (even 18-19%) EBITDA for a 95%-localised Auto business and a 50-70% valuation discount to Schaeffler and Timken; management replied royalty was unchanged and there is now no pure-play comparable.
points.quote: Increasingly, our post demerger, what we are realizing is that the investor communication and the disclosures have dropped substantially.

points.point: Management's closing framing still rested on focus and agility as the value-unlock, with restructuring costs described as a temporary hit.
points.quote: The demerger positions us to unlock greater value by enabling sharper focus and agility in our business.

points.point: The scheme transferred the Industrial business as a going concern into SKF India (Industrial) Limited under Sections 230-232, effective 1 October 2025 (NCLT order 26 September 2025, record date 15 October 2025), with pre-demerger cost of acquisition apportioned 46.88% to SKF India and 53.12% to SKF Industrial — i.e. Industrial was the larger half.
points.quote: The Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench, vide its Order dated 26th September, 2025, sanctioned the Scheme of Arrangement between SKF India Limited ("the Company" or "Demerged Company") and SKF India (Industrial) Limited ("SKF Industrial" or "Resulting Company") and their respective shareholders and creditors under Sections 230 to 232 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 ("Scheme"), providing for the demerger of the Company's Industrial Business (Demerged Undertaking as defined in the Scheme ) into SKF Industrial on a going concern basis

points.point: The post-completion press release restated the purpose as two focused entities with independent boards and governance, and attached separate investment plans — Industrial INR 8,000-9,500 million by 2030 including a new Pune facility by 2028, Automotive INR 4,100-5,100 million by 2030 across EV, two-wheeler and wheel-end capacity in Haridwar, Pune and Bangalore.
points.quote: The demerger, sanctioned by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) and approved by shareholders earlier this year, has formally separated SKF India's business into two focused entities — SKF Industrial and SKF Automotive — each equipped with independent boards and governance structures.

points.point: The FY26 AGM presentation codified the five official reasons for the separation and rebranded the automotive entity as SKF Vertevo, reporting FY26 revenue of INR 21,295 million, 15% EBITDA margin and EPS of INR 23.7.
points.quote: Why the Demerger? Different Market Dynamics Distinct Customer Needs Focused Capital Allocation Faster Decision Making Independent Growth Strategies

rationale.what_management_expects: Two fit-for-purpose entities growing faster and more profitably: automotive 10-12% and industrial 8-10% growth to FY28, both holding 17-19% EBITDA with 2-3 points of upside later; sharper management focus, tailored capital deployment and manufacturing efficiency, plus separate financial visibility attracting more aligned investors.
rationale.gaps: Never quantified: total demerger cost, dis-synergies, inter-entity trading/rent/service charges, or why post-demerger margins (11-12% PBT) fall far below the 16-19% promised pre-demerger.

judge.insiders: Tata Sons Private Limited is Promoter; promoter group held 1,565,402,703 of 3,682,582,902 shares (~42.5%), mirrored 1:1 in the resulting company. P B Balaji (4,93,186 shares) is a director of the CV entity.
judge.hidden_value: Separation leaves the parent as cars/SUVs plus JLR: India PV net cash ~Rs.7,000 Cr with 15% FY26 volume growth, over 40% EV share, while JLR carries Rs.33,000 Cr net debt and 0.7% EBIT; CV took 31.15% of cost base.
judge.selling_pressure_why: Every PV holder received 1:1 shares in a smaller, different-industry commercial-vehicle entity (31.15% of apportioned cost); index effects not stated.

rationale.rationale: The separation at issue is the demerger of the Commercial Vehicles business out of the old Tata Motors Limited into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited, executed together with the amalgamation of the PV subsidiary back into the listed parent, under one Composite Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai (orders of August 25, 2025 and a rectification order of September 10, 2025), with an appointed date of July 1, 2025 and effective date of October 1, 2025. The Scheme states only two objectives in these texts: to transfer the Commercial Vehicles undertaking to the Resulting Company 'on a going concern basis' in compliance with Section 2(19AA) of the Income-tax Act, and to amalgamate Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited into TML 'with an objective of consolidating the Passenger Vehicles Business with TML', after which TML was renamed Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited and TMLCVL renamed Tata Motors Limited (w.e.f. October 13, 2025). The result is that, as the postal ballot puts it, 'the Commercial Vehicle and Passenger Vehicle businesses of the Company are housed in two separate entities', each with its own reconstituted board and KMP (Shailesh Chandra as MD & CEO of TMPV from October 1, 2025; P B Balaji moved from Group CFO to CEO of Jaguar Land Rover from November 17, 2025), and TMPV left reporting one automotive segment of JLR plus Tata Passenger Vehicles, 'other than CV segment moving out'. Shareholders were handed direct ownership of both: 1 TMLCVL share for every 1 TML share held on the October 14, 2025 record date, with historical cost apportioned 31.15% to the CV entity and 68.85% to TMPV, and the new CV shares listed from November 12, 2025. Management's only economic framing on the calls is accounting and capital: a notional demerger gain of ~Rs. 83,000 Cr (CV business valued at ~Rs. 94,000 Cr by third-party agencies against ~Rs. 11,000 Cr book value of net assets transferred), fully offset by a contra deemed-dividend entry so there is 'absolutely no impact on either distributable reserves or on our net worth'; an India PV business that is net cash (~Rs. 5,000 Cr at Q3 FY26, ~Rs. 7,000 Cr at FY26-end) which 'gives a lot of flex to fund the rich product investment cycle'; and the two entities now declaring dividends separately (Rs. 3 at TMPV plus Rs. 4 at TMLCV, 'a total dividend of Rs. 7 in the year when the demerger was undertaken' versus Rs. 6 before). Costs disclosed are stamp duty: a Rs. 400 Cr provision in Q3 FY26, included within about Rs. 4,100 Cr of FY26 exceptionals. No investor, lender or partner is named anywhere in these texts as having asked for the separation; the only stakeholder input recorded is the shareholder vote, which management described as 'overwhelming votes in our favor', and the nine AGM resolutions passed in July 2026.
rationale.evolution: On the Feb 2025 call (Q3 FY25, January 29, 2025) the demerger was already a filed corporate action awaiting exchange/SEBI NOC, with appointed date July 1 and effective date around October 1, 2025; by the Jun 2025 call (Q4 FY25, May 13, 2025) the shareholder vote had passed overwhelmingly and both dates were reconfirmed, and on the Aug 2025 call (Q1 FY26, August 8, 2025) the NCLT final hearing had concluded that same day with judgment reserved and the October 1 effective date 'on plan'. The Nov 2025 call (Q2 FY26, November 14, 2025) was the first set of results reported post-separation, where management walked through the demerger accounting entries, the Rs. 83,000 Cr notional gain and contra deemed dividend, and the new segment structure. Thereafter the subject narrows to residuals and costs: the Feb 2026 call (February 5, 2026) notes CV is out of the segments and books a Rs. 400 Cr stamp duty provision, and the Jun 2026 call (May 14, 2026) folds stamp duty into FY26 exceptionals and frames the two separate dividends as Rs. 7 combined; the strategic 'why' is never revisited on any of these six calls.

points.point: The Scheme bundles two steps: hiving off the Commercial Vehicles undertaking into TMLCVL on a going concern basis (structured to qualify under Section 2(19AA) of the Income-tax Act), and amalgamating the PV subsidiary into the listed parent — the only explicit objective language in any document supplied.
points.quote: Amalgamation of TMLPV with TML with an objective of consolidating the Passenger Vehicles Business with TML and consequent dissolution of TMLPV without being wound up.

points.point: The November 2025 postal ballot explains the consequence the separation was meant to produce — two self-standing entities — and uses it as the reason to rebuild both boards, appointing Shailesh Chandra MD & CEO of TMPV from October 1, 2025 and P B Balaji as a non-executive director while he became CEO of Jaguar Land Rover from November 17, 2025.
points.quote: In view of the above, it was proposed to reconstitute the Board of Directors of both  the entities .

points.point: Shareholders were given direct ownership of both businesses rather than cash, at a strict 1:1 entitlement on the October 14, 2025 record date, with historical cost of acquisition apportioned 31.15% to the CV entity and 68.85% to TMPV; the CV shares were approved for listing and trading from November 12, 2025.
points.quote: 1 (one) share of the Resulting Company (face value of INR 2/- each fully paid up), for every 1 (one) share of the Demerged Company (face value of INR 2/- each fully paid up) of the same class of shares outstanding and as held by such shareholder in the Demerged Company, without any further application, act or deed (‘Share Entitlement Ratio’).

points.point: At the 81st AGM (July 8, 2026) the Chairman and the MD & CEO presented the demerger as completed and as the platform for TMPV's own roadmap, pairing it with JLR's new Panapakkam, Tamil Nadu production and with long-term growth aspirations to FY31 on a consolidated basis.
points.quote: He highlighted the demerger of Commercial Vehicles business into a separate legal entity and commencement of commercial production by JLR at Panapakkam, Tamil Nadu reflecting the synergy between the Company and JLR.

points.point: The demerger was presented purely as a corporate action on track — filings with the exchanges and SEBI complete, operational carve-out work advanced, appointed date July 1 and effective date around October 1, 2025 — alongside the parallel Tata Motors Finance merger into Tata Capital.
points.quote: Operational activities are in an advanced stage and progressing as per plan.

points.point: Management reported that shareholders had backed the Scheme decisively and that both the appointed and effective dates were intact; asked about asset allocation, Balaji confirmed the Tata Capital stake would sit with the CV business after separation.
points.quote: we had overwhelming votes in our favor and therefore we are on track for an appointed date of July 1st

points.point: The NCLT final hearing concluded on the day of the call with judgment reserved, which management said would let them complete the demerger within the quarter for an October 1 effective date; the same slide carried the CV side's Iveco acquisition, i.e. each business already pursuing its own agenda.
points.quote: Hot of the press is the demerger.

points.point: First results after separation: the demerger produced a ~Rs. 83,000 Cr book gain on disposal of the CV undertaking (CV valued at ~Rs. 94,000 Cr by third-party agencies versus ~Rs. 11,000 Cr book value of net assets transferred), but it is entirely notional with no effect on net worth or distributable reserves.
points.quote: But this is only a notional gain as there is a contra entry of ~Rs. 83,000 Cr as a deemed dividend.

points.point: Reporting was simplified to one automotive segment comprising JLR and Tata Passenger Vehicles plus 'others' (mainly Tata Technologies and Tata Motors Holdings Pte Singapore); prior-period income statements were restated to TMPV only, while prior balance sheets still include CV and are not comparable.
points.quote: The automotive segment will now comprise of JLR and Tata Passenger Vehicles business.

points.point: Capital framing of the standalone PV entity: the India business is net cash, which management said gives flexibility to fund its heavy product investment cycle; one residual link to CV remains — the Rs. 6,500 Cr PLI cap still applies to PV and CV together because the original 2021 application was made as a Group.
points.quote: We had applied originally in 2021 as a Group.

points.point: CV is confirmed out of the reporting perimeter with nothing else changed, and the first demerger cost is booked — a Rs. 400 Cr stamp duty provision within Rs. 1,600 Cr of quarterly exceptionals alongside JLR cyber and India wage-bill charges.
points.quote: Commercial vehicle business is out I think last quarter post the demerger , everything else is the same.

points.point: FY26 exceptionals of about Rs. 4,100 Cr include demerger stamp duty; separately, the two entities now set dividends independently — Rs. 3 per share at TMPV (about Rs. 1,100 Cr outflow) plus Rs. 4 at TMLCV — which management framed as more total distribution than the pre-demerger company paid.
points.quote: So this actually represents a total dividend of Rs. 7 in the year when the demerger was undertaken and an increase over the Rs. 6 that we have paid for the last two years.

rationale.what_management_expects: Stated only indirectly: CV and PV housed in two separate listed entities, each with its own board, leadership and dividend (Rs. 3 + Rs. 4 vs Rs. 6 before); TMPV consolidating PV, EV and JLR under one automotive segment, with a net-cash India business (Rs. 7,000 Cr) giving flexibility to fund its product investment cycle while JLR carries Rs. 33,000 Cr net debt.
rationale.gaps: No value-unlock, focus, valuation or synergy argument; no demerger costs/benefits beyond stamp duty; no dis-synergies, debt-allocation logic, or any investor, lender or partner request.

judge.what_is_spun: The Data Centre and Cloud Services business of ARL and ARCPL, vested in Ashok Cloud Private Limited
judge.reason: Consolidate the entire Data Centre Business in one entity and create two dedicated listed companies, enabling independent market recognition and valuation, dedicated management focus and sector-specific funding.
judge.insiders: ARL promoters hold 57.42% of ARL; post-scheme ACPL is 28.14% promoters directly plus 51% held by ARL (79.14% total), public 20.86%. Promoter-group Anish Sarin oversees data-centre rollout.
judge.hidden_value: Demerged Undertaking turnover Rs 145.90 cr is only 8.96% of Rs 1,627.72 cr; management cites ~75% data-centre EBITDA margin, 357 MW planned capacity, Rs 20,000 cr capex, net-cash parent with Rs 4,471.64 cr net worth.
judge.selling_pressure_why: Small (8.96% of turnover), only 20.86% public float in ACPL, and a digital-infrastructure business alien to real-estate holders.
judge.listing_timeline: not stated — the July 21, 2026 filings say only that ACPL's demerger shares and ARL's existing ACPL shares "shall be listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited by seeking exemption under Rule 19(7)", subject to NCLT, SEBI, exchange, shareholder and creditor approvals; no date given
judge.read_next: The full Composite Scheme: asset/liability split and valuation of the Demerged Undertaking versus ACPL's Rs 74.86 cr rights issue.
judge.quote: The Data Centre Business has evolved significantly over the years and is well poised to chart its own growth path and operate as a separate listed entity focused on the rapidly growing Data Centre Business whilst continuing to leverage ARL's institutional strengths, strong brand equity and goodwill.

listing.text: NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

rationale.rationale: Management says Anant Raj Ltd today runs two unlike businesses under one roof — the legacy real estate/infrastructure business (residential townships, luxury housing, commercial leasing, hospitality) and a data centre & cloud services business — and that the Data Centre Business is itself split across two entities, Anant Raj Limited and its wholly owned Anant Raj Cloud Private Limited (ARCPL), with assets, employees, investments and operations housed in both. The Composite Scheme therefore first amalgamates ARCPL into ARL and then demerges the whole Data Centre Business out of ARL into Ashok Cloud Private Limited (ACPL), so all of it sits in one dedicated, separately listed company. The stated problems it solves: the two verticals differ 'significantly in their nature, risk profile, competitive dynamics, and capital requirements', and the Board recorded on May 11, 2026 that keeping both in one company 'does not adequately reflect the true potential and intrinsic value of each business segment, thereby impacting stakeholder returns'; the split is meant to give independent market-driven valuation of a pure-play digital infrastructure asset, dedicated management focus, a simpler ownership structure with intra-group arrangements cancelled/rationalised, and the ability to attract sector-specific capital, strategic investors and partnerships. The numbers cited: the Demerged Undertaking did ₹145.90 cr turnover in FY26 versus ₹1,627.72 cr aggregated (8.96%); ARCPL turnover ₹136.20 cr and net worth ₹49.45 cr versus ARL's ₹1,491.52 cr turnover and ₹4,471.64 cr net worth; ACPL had nil turnover and ₹0.04 cr net worth and was capitalised days earlier via a ₹74.86 cr rights issue (37,43,22,553 shares at ₹2). Scale is the driver: the Board noted an MOU with the Govt. of Andhra Pradesh for 50 MW IT load taking total planned capacity to 357 MW IT load, requiring about ₹20,000 cr of investment — against a real estate business management repeatedly said should carry as little debt as possible. Mechanically, ARL shareholders get 1 ACPL share of ₹2 for every 1 ARL share of ₹2, giving them 49% of ACPL directly (promoters 28.14%, public 20.86%) while ARL retains 51%, so ACPL stays a subsidiary and ARL holders keep 100% of the ultimate economic interest; ACPL will be listed on BSE and NSE under the Rule 19(7) exemption. The ask came from the equity market side — an investor asked about a demerger as early as the Apr 2024 call, and analysts kept pressing for separate real estate vs data centre reporting — not from lenders or partners, who are never cited as requesting it.
rationale.evolution: On the Apr 25, 2024 call Arpit Shah of Stallion Asset asked outright whether there were plans to demerge the business and Amit Sarin refused — 'too soon', focus on execution — while describing the cloud venture as a half-megawatt pilot with TCIL. By the Oct 30, 2024 call (Q2 FY25) management was framing the group as 'two full-fledged divisions' (real estate plus a technology division) with a ₹2,100 cr fundraise earmarked purely for data centre/cloud, and Raj Sarraf pushed for separate data centre revenue disclosure; on the Nov 12, 2025 call (Q2/H1 FY26) the CFO called the company 'at an important inflection point' with a 'legacy real estate business' alongside the data centre/cloud 'future ready platform', the ₹1,100 cr QIP was done, and analysts again asked for a separate segment/EBITDA breakup, which management declined on the 10%-of-revenue threshold. The demerger itself was never discussed on any of the three calls: it surfaced in the May 11, 2026 board note (which recorded the need for merger/demerger and set up a committee of Amit Sarin, Ashim Sarin, Manoj Goyal and Pankaj Gupta to frame a scheme), then was executed as the ACPL rights-issue funding on July 20, 2026 and the Composite Scheme approved on July 21, 2026.

points.point: An investor (Arpit Shah, Stallion Asset) directly asked about demerging the data centre business; management declined to engage, calling the business too young and prioritising execution toward the 300 MW mark in four years.
points.quote: We are too soon to say anything on that. Let's focus on execution, Arpit.

points.point: Management set out the different capital philosophies that later justify separation: real estate was to be net debt-free by December 2024 and the only debt acceptable would be lease rental discounting, including against long 10-15 year data centre leases.
points.quote: And the only debt which Anant Raj is open to taking is LRD and this is one of the best items for LRD because you have long-term leases and good clients.

points.point: Management began describing the group as two separate divisions — the historic real estate 'bread and butter' and a new technology division of colocation and cloud — the same two-vertical framing the Scheme later uses.
points.quote: So Anant Raj Limited will now have two full-fledged divisions. Real estate division which is the historical, the division of the company, the bread and butter of the company as of now and plus the technology division, in which we will be data center, co-location infrastructure and cloud.

points.point: The ₹2,100 cr fundraise (₹100 cr promoters, ₹2,000 cr market) was ring-fenced entirely for the data centre/cloud build-out, with real estate funded from internal accruals — distinct funding requirements per vertical, with cloud capex cited at ~₹100 cr per MW on top of ₹26 cr colocation capex.
points.quote: This is purely data center, sir. This fund is going to be purely for data centers. For our real estate, we are completely funded with our internal sources.

points.point: An analyst (Raj Sarraf of Finvestors) asked for data centre revenue to be reported separately from real estate because it would become the major contributor; management conceded the point.
points.quote: Sir, both the revenues are going to be substantial and we will be breaking them up, sir . We will do that definitely.

points.point: The CFO positioned the company at an 'inflection point' with a legacy real estate business and a separate future-ready data centre/cloud platform — H1 FY26 revenue ₹1,223.2 cr of which data centre only ₹58.42 cr, ₹1,100 cr QIP completed, net cash positive, ~₹700 cr capital employed in data centres at 75% EBITDA margin.
points.quote: Our legacy real estate business continues to deliver a consistent growth and strengthen our leadership in high demanding markets. At the same time, our Data Center and Cloud initiatives are shaping up the future ready platform that positions us as a diversified resilient enterprise s.

points.point: Investors (Sri Gopal of StockHifi, Ashwani Sharma of Emkay) again pressed for separate real estate vs data centre revenue and EBITDA reporting; management said formal segment disclosure was not yet triggered because data centre revenue was under 10% of the total.
points.quote: In this, you have to give segmental breakup once you do 10%.

points.point: Asked whether the company should lever up to scale data centres faster, management refused on the grounds that real estate is the backbone and must stay low-debt — a tension a separately funded data centre entity resolves. Capacity plans were 63 MW by Dec 2026, 117 MW by FY28 and 307 MW by FY31-32.
points.quote: And as it is, we feel that our backbone is still real estate, which will always be. And we feel that real estate should be as low on debt as possible.

points.point: The May 11, 2026 board note first records the need for a merger/demerger, citing differing nature, risk profile, competitive dynamics and capital requirements, plus the 357 MW IT load plan (after the 50 MW Andhra Pradesh MOU) needing about ₹20,000 cr; a committee of Amit Sarin, Ashim Sarin, Manoj Goyal and Pankaj Gupta was formed to design it.
points.quote: The Board of Directors have considered that the Company is presently engaged in two distinct business undertakings, namely Real Estate Development and Data Center Services, which differ significantly in their nature, risk profile, competitive dynamics, and capital requirements and continuing both businesses under a single corporate does not adequately reflect the true potential and intrinsic value of each business segment, thereby impacting stakeholder returns.

points.point: The July 21, 2026 Scheme explains the data centre business is split across ARL and ARCPL, so ARCPL is first merged into ARL and the combined Data Centre Business then demerged into Ashok Cloud — consolidating it in one entity and creating two focused listed companies.
points.quote: The Data Centre Business is presently conducted through ARL and ARCPL, with various assets, employees, investments and business operations pertaining to the Data Centre Business being housed across both entities.

points.point: Stated benefit one: independent market recognition and valuation of the data centre business given its distinct operating profile, growth trajectory, risk-return characteristics and funding needs; demerged undertaking turnover was ₹145.90 cr, 8.96% of ₹1,627.72 cr for FY26.
points.quote: the segregation of the Data Centre Business into a separately listed company would facilitate independent market recognition and valuation of the Data Centre Business, having regard to its distinct operating profile, growth trajectory, risk-return characteristics and funding requirements;

points.point: Stated benefit two: a distinct legal entity lets Ashok Cloud attract sector-specific capital, investors, acquisitions and partnerships, with simpler ownership and intra-group arrangements cancelled or rationalised.
points.quote: the separation of the Data Centre Business into a distinct legal entity will enable Ashok Cloud to effectively attract sector specific resources for its growth requirements and pursue strategic investments, partnerships, thereby unlocking greater value for its shareholders;

points.point: Consideration is 1 ACPL share of ₹2 for every 1 ARL share of ₹2; ARL holders get 49% of ACPL directly (promoters 28.14%, public 20.86%) while ARL keeps 51%, so ACPL remains a subsidiary and ARL holders retain 100% of the ultimate economic interest; listing on BSE and NSE via the Rule 19(7) exemption.
points.quote: Overall, the shareholders of ARL will hold 100% of the ultimate beneficial economic interest in the Resultant Company, ACPL ( direct holding of 49% and indirect holding of 51% throughARL).

points.point: Days before the Scheme, the Finance and Investment Committee funded the shell resultant company: a ₹74,86,45,106 rights issue of 37,43,22,553 ₹2 shares in ACPL (incorporated Oct 11, 2021; nil turnover in FY24, FY25 and FY26) to meet data centre and cloud development funding.
points.quote: ACPL proposes to raise the fund to meet the funding requirement for development of its data centres and cloud business.

points.point: The press release frames the outcome as two independent platforms — ARL in real estate/infrastructure and Ashok Cloud in data centres, sovereign public cloud, AI-ready cloud infrastructure and DC/DR services — citing separate growth trajectories, operational priorities and capital needs.
points.quote: "Our real estate, infrastructure business and Data Centre & Cloud Services Business have evolved into two distinct platforms, each with its own growth trajectory, operational priorities, and capital needs.

rationale.what_management_expects: Ashok Cloud: pure-play digital-infrastructure valuation and independent market recognition, sector-specific growth capital, partnerships and acquisitions, dedicated leadership, consolidated ownership (75% EBITDA-margin colocation/cloud, 357 MW plan, ~₹20,000 cr capex). Anant Raj: sharper focus on real estate, infrastructure and hospitality, low debt, continued execution. Both: operational efficiency, agility, faster decision-making, transparency, unlocked shareholder value, with holders participating directly in each.
rationale.gaps: Calls never mention the demerger; no appointed date, debt/cash/asset split, valuation or swap basis, why ARL keeps 51%, how ₹20,000 cr capex gets funded, or listing timeline.

judge.what_is_spun: Dalmia Bharat Refractories' Tyre Business — designing, manufacturing and development of all types of tyre and tyre products
demerged_business_names: Himadri Birla Tyre Manufacturer Private Limited
judge.reason: Strategic forward-integration: integrate the Tyre Business with HSCL's carbon black and advanced carbon materials business, giving direct ownership, sourcing/manufacturing/distribution synergies, focused ownership, investment flexibility and long-term value creation
judge.insiders: HSCL Promoter & Promoter Group 26,48,59,302 shares, 52.49% pre-Scheme to 52.47% post; DBRL promoters stay 74.99%, unchanged. HSCL has 53,896 outstanding exercisable employee stock options
judge.hidden_value: A ₹149.31 crore-turnover tyre business (3.39% of HSCL turnover) moves in for only 1,76,462 new shares — promoter stake dilutes just 0.02pp. Management targets ₹3,000 crore Birla Tyres top line in 4-5 years; EBITDA breakeven not yet reached
judge.selling_pressure_why: Only 1,76,462 new shares on 50.45 crore base; 1-for-260 entitlement leaves most DBRL holders fractions pooled with a trustee
judge.listing_timeline: Stated 21 September 2026: HSCL equity 'already listed on BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited'; the new shares 'shall be listed and/or admitted to trading' on both, subject to requisite approvals; no date given. Appointed Date 1 October 2026
judge.read_next: The Scheme on www.himadri.com — Demerged Undertaking's assets, liabilities and Birla Tyres' standalone profitability
judge.quote: The Demerger will enable the Resulting Company to integrate the Tyre Business with its existing carbon black and advanced carbon materials business, thereby strengthening its presence across the tyre value chain.

listing.text: NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: Stated 21 September 2026: HSCL equity 'already listed on BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited'; the new shares 'shall be listed and/or admitted to trading' on both, subject to requisite approvals; no date given. Appointed Date 1 October 2026

rationale.rationale: Read against the documents, HSCL is not separating a business of its own — it is the receiving side of a separation: the 21 September 2026 Scheme demerges the Tyre Business (Birla Tyres, Balasore) out of Dalmia Bharat Refractories Limited (DBRL, the Demerged Company) and vests it in HSCL (the Resulting Company) as a going concern on an as-is-where-is basis with appointed date 1 October 2026, with no cash consideration — only 1 new HSCL share of Re 1 for every 260 DBRL shares of Rs 10, which adds just 1,76,462 shares and moves promoter holding from 52.49% to 52.47% (50,45,74,175 to 50,47,50,637 shares). The Board's stated reasons are: strategic forward integration of tyres with HSCL's existing carbon black and advanced carbon materials business; leveraging HSCL's material expertise, R&D, manufacturing and customer relationships for tyre product customisation; synergies across raw material sourcing, product development, manufacturing, logistics, distribution, market development, shared services and customer engagement; direct ownership and control to coordinate capacity utilisation, modernisation and product expansion; and greater strategic and financial flexibility to align investment, funding and capacity expansion — plus 'more focused ownership and a robust operating structure' so each company can direct management attention and capital to its own strengths. The business being moved is small and loss-making for now: turnover of the Demerged Undertaking was INR 149.31 crores at 31 March 2026, just 3.39% of HSCL's turnover (management separately cited Birla Tyres FY26 topline of INR 187 crores, INR 60+ crores in Q3FY26, INR 26 crores in Q2FY26, INR 5 crores in Q1FY26 and INR 127 crores in Q1FY27), with commercial operations only from 29 May 2025, EBITDA breakeven/cash-positive guided 'in this financial year' (FY27), and a target of INR 3,000 crores topline in 4-5 years. The problem it solves, as the calls make plain, is the awkward interim structure: tyres were manufactured on DBRL's balance sheet and merely bought and resold by wholly-owned Himadri Clean Energy, so HSCL booked tyre revenue but no tyre profit — 'we don't have any positive or negative impact as such as of now' (Jan 2026), 'we have not consolidated' (Apr 2026), and 'once it becomes part of Himadri, then the numbers will come' (Jul 2026). Direct ownership also lines up with the heavy spend already running through tyres — roughly INR 250-300 crores of additional capex in FY26 continuing for three years, and INR 500 crores of the ~INR 2,000 crores FY27-28 capex earmarked for Birla Tyres to convert Truck & Bus Bias capacity to OTR/OHT and commission a PCR line by FY28 for EV/SUV tyres. Notably, nobody on these calls says investors, lenders or partners demanded the step: analysts repeatedly pushed for tyre consolidation and segment numbers (Sanjesh Jain, Jul 2025; Dhruvin Kadakia, Apr 2026; Bhavin Chheda, Jul 2026) and Bharat Shah of ASK questioned whether a B2C tyre business was a distraction from speciality chemicals, but the Scheme is presented purely as a Board decision backed by a valuation report and a fairness opinion, with no lender or JV-partner request disclosed.
rationale.evolution: Through FY26 management framed Birla Tyres as deliberately arm's-length: on the Jul 18, 2025 call it was 'a standalone business' with its own P&L, HSCL explicitly selling it no carbon black, and when asked when the manufacturing entity would come inside HSCL the answer was flat — 'there is no intention as such now as of date.' The Oct 24, 2025 and Jan 21, 2026 calls kept the trading structure (Himadri Clean Energy buying from DBRL and reselling, so tyre margin landed nowhere in HSCL), while distributors grew 20 → 29 → 36; by Apr 27, 2026 the line was 'we have not consolidated — once we consolidate, then we can discuss this,' and on Jul 16, 2026 the CMD said tyres still sit on Dalmia Refractory's balance sheet and 'once it becomes part of Himadri, then the numbers will come,' alongside a INR 500 crore tyre capex plan. The Board then gave notice on 18 September 2026 and approved the demerger Scheme on 21 September 2026 (valuation and fairness opinion both dated 20 September 2026), with 1 October 2026 as the appointed date.

points.point: At the outset the tyre entry was positioned as deliberately non-integrated: Himadri would not supply carbon black to Birla Tyres because it could sell the same black at a premium elsewhere, and each business kept its own P&L.
points.quote: However, it is important to note that Himadri will not be selling any carbon black to Birla Tyres.

points.point: Asked directly when the tyre manufacturing entity would be brought inside Himadri, management ruled it out at the time, calling Birla Tyres a standalone business acquired for about INR 300 crores against assets worth INR 3,400 crores.
points.quote: No, there is no intention as such now as of date of its coming into Himadri.

points.point: Bharat Shah of ASK Investment Managers challenged the fit of a B2C tyre business inside a B2B speciality chemicals company; the CMD defended it as the ready-made launching pad into B2C with a 40-year brand, run by a separate vertical head.
points.quote: See, today or tomorrow I have to go into B2C.

points.point: Six months into operations tyre sales were immaterial (INR 26 crores in Q2FY26 against INR 5 crores in Q1FY26), with 29 distributors and over 350 dealers and the year treated as a start-up phase.
points.quote: So, this year is like a start-up. To be very frank, we are not considering this as any revenue.

points.point: The interim structure was spelled out: tyres were made under the Dalmia Bharat Refractories partnership and merely bought and resold by Himadri Clean Energy, so no tyre profit or loss reached HSCL on INR 60+ crores of quarterly tyre revenue.
points.quote: So in Himadri, in Himadri Clean Energy, we are buying from Dalmia Refractory and selling the Birla Tyres. So we don't have any positive or negative impact as such as of now.

points.point: Asked for tyre volumes and realisation, management refused on the ground that tyres were not consolidated — only clubbed into an 'others' segment with mining — while disclosing FY26 tyre topline of INR 187 crores and a INR 3,000 crore ambition in four years.
points.quote: Tyre still now, we have not consolidated. Once we consolidate, then we can discuss this.

points.point: On Bhavin Chheda's question whether the INR 127 crore quarterly tyre revenue was EBITDA positive, the CMD said not yet and tied the missing profit disclosure explicitly to the business sitting on DBRL's balance sheet pending transfer into Himadri.
points.quote: So now Birla Tyres is reflected on Dalmia Refractory balance sheet. So once it becomes part of Himadri, then the numbers will come.

points.point: The capital case for direct ownership: INR 500 crores of the ~INR 2,000 crore FY27-FY28 capex is for Birla Tyres, funding phased TBB-to-OTR conversion, modernisation/automation, 400+ new SKUs and a PCR line by FY28, with breakeven guided for FY27.
points.quote: We reach EBITDA breakeven in this financial year only. We will be cash positive.

points.point: The Board's first stated benefit is forward integration — folding the tyre business into HSCL's carbon black and advanced carbon materials platform to own more of the tyre value chain, reversing the earlier 'separate P&Ls, no internal carbon black sales' stance.
points.quote: The Demerger will enable the Resulting Company to integrate the Tyre Business with its existing carbon black and advanced carbon materials business, thereby strengthening its presence across the tyre value chain.

points.point: Control and funding flexibility are cited as the operating rationale: direct ownership lets HSCL coordinate capacity utilisation, modernisation, product expansion and distribution, and align tyre investment and funding with group strategy.
points.quote: Direct ownership will enable the Resulting Company to align investment, funding, capacity expansion and growth priorities of the Tyre Business with its broader business strategy.

points.point: Scale of what moves: the Demerged Undertaking (all assets, liabilities, contracts, employees, brands, trademarks, licences of DBRL's tyre business) had turnover of INR 149.31 crores at 31 March 2026, only 3.39% of HSCL's turnover.
points.quote: Turnover of the Demerged Undertaking as on 31 March 2026, was INR 149.31 crores, which constitutes 3.39% of total turnover of Resulting Company in the immediately preceding financial year / based on financials of last financial year (i.e. for year ended 31 March 2026).

points.point: Consideration is non-cash and barely dilutive: 1 HSCL share per 260 DBRL shares, based on a 20 September 2026 valuation by SSPA & Co and CA Manish Gadia with a fairness opinion from Jajodia Equity Advisors; promoter holding moves 52.49% to 52.47%.
points.quote: 1 (One) fully paid-up equity shares of face value of INR 1 (one) each of the Resulting Company shall be issued and allotted for every 260 (Two Hundred Sixty) fully paid-up equity shares of face value of INR 10 (ten) each held in the Demerged Company

points.point: The Board also frames it as cleaner ownership for both sides, letting DBRL and HSCL each direct management attention, capital and resources to businesses matching their own strategic capabilities.
points.quote: the proposed Demerger would provide a more focused ownership and robust operating structure for the Demerged Undertaking, while enabling each of the Companies to deploy its management attention, capital and resources towards businesses aligned with its respective strategic capabilities and long-term objectives.

rationale.what_management_expects: For HSCL: forward integration across the tyre value chain, synergies in sourcing, product development, logistics, distribution and shared services, direct control over capacity utilisation, modernisation, OTR/PCR expansion, and flexibility to fund it — tyres reaching EBITDA breakeven in FY27 and INR 3,000 crores topline in 4-5 years. For DBRL: focused ownership, with management attention and capital redirected to its own strategic businesses.
rationale.gaps: No reason given for DBRL exiting or for reversing the Jul 2025 'no intention' stance; no tyre EBITDA, debt, or treatment of HSCL's INR 300 crore stake, NCDs or HBTMPL 49%.
