rationale.rationale: Two distinct things are going on, and only one of them is explained in detail. The hard, documented action is a composite scheme of arrangement approved by SAMIL's board on 07.02.2025 and sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 26.10.2026, with an Appointed Date of 01.04.2024: the 'Automotive Manufacturing and Services Business' (the Demerged Undertaking) is carved out of wholly owned subsidiary Samvardhana Motherson Innovative Solutions Limited (SMISL) and vested in listed parent Samvardhana Motherson International Limited (SAMIL), while SMISL's 'Remaining Business' stays behind; alongside it, Samvardhana Motherson Auto System Private Limited (SMAS) amalgamates into SAMIL and Motherson Machinery and Automations Limited (MMAL) amalgamates into SMISL, both amalgamating companies dissolving without winding up and their share capital simply cancelled. Management's stated reasons for the demerger are focused management attention and leadership, independence and flexibility over each business's cash flows so projects can be run 'more consistently and advantageously', a leaner and more focused organisation, a reduction in layers of investments producing a simpler structure, more transparent shareholding with better visibility and accountability, and enhanced shareholder value. The merger legs are justified separately as eliminating multiple group entities, pooling financial, human, technological and managerial resources, cutting duplicated administrative expenses and overheads and compliances, better day-to-day coordination, and unlocking synergies across products, customers, technology and manufacturing. No valuation, ratio or cash changes hands: because SMISL is a 100% subsidiary, 'no shares will be issued by the Resulting Company', and SMAS/MMAL shareholders likewise get nothing — the scheme is pure structural plumbing within wholly owned entities. Separately and far more loudly, the Sep 2025 investor meet framed a different kind of separation as a Vision 2030 deliverable: having 'successfully took out MSWIL', management said many businesses are 'ripe to now leave the SAMIL fold and be independently listed on their own', explicitly flagging aerospace (grown 550x in five years, ~USD 250mn revenue, >USD 1bn order book then, USD 1.6bn by May 2026) as 'probably ripe for the independence'. Nobody outside management — no investor, lender, customer or JV partner — is cited as asking for either; the RD, ROC and Official Liquidator raised only process points (SMAS's negative net worth, protection of creditors, BEN-2 filings, Income Tax scrutiny), and the Petitioners answered that nothing in the Companies Act bars merging a negative-net-worth company and that both demerged and resulting net worth are positive.
rationale.evolution: The idea first appears as corporate action on 07.02.2025 (board approval, intimated to exchanges 28.02.2025), then NCLT first motion on 30.05.2025 and further service affidavits through 18.09.2025; the earnings calls never mention it. The only management articulation comes at the Sep 2025 investor meet, where Vaaman Sehgal makes 'independent companies from SAMIL' a Vision 2030 target, citing the MSWIL precedent and naming aerospace as the likeliest candidate. The Aug 2025, Nov 2025, Feb 2026 and May 2026 calls say nothing about any separation — they stay on European restructuring, consumer electronics GF1/GF2/GF3, aerospace order book and acquisitions (Atsumitec, Yutaka Giken, Nexans Autoelectric). Final NCLT sanction landed 26.10.2026, binding from the 01.04.2024 Appointed Date, with SMAS and MMAL dissolved.

points.point: Vaaman Sehgal makes separation an explicit Vision 2030 deliverable, citing the already-completed MSWIL (Motherson Sumi Wiring India) carve-out as the template for more businesses leaving the SAMIL fold as separately listed companies.
points.quote: We successfully took out MSWIL, which has been extremely successful for us. And we believe that many companies are ripe to now leave the SAMIL fold and be independently listed on their own.

points.point: He frames the purpose as value unlocking for shareholders from businesses incubated inside SAMIL that can now stand alone, and says it will go beyond divisions to multiple independent companies.
points.quote: We're going to create a lot more independent companies from SAMIL, which they have been incubated and stand on their own feet and unlock a tremendous amount of value for all our shareholders.

points.point: Aerospace is singled out as the most likely candidate for independence, right after Kunal Bajaj's segment reporting 550x growth in five years, ~USD 250mn revenue and over USD 1bn order book from a standing start.
points.quote: Ladies and gentlemen, one of the most exciting verticals, probably ripe for the independence that I spoke about, and a lot of things are going to happen in this vertical.

points.point: Clause 3.1(i): the core stated reason for hiving the Automotive Manufacturing and Services Business out of SMISL and into SAMIL is focused management attention and leadership.
points.quote: To ensure focused management attention and leadership it is proposed to segregate the Demerged Undertaking from the Demerged Company into the Resulting Company.

points.point: Clause 3.1(ii): the separation is justified as giving each business independent control over its own cash flows and project funding decisions.
points.quote: The structure post Demerger will provide independence and flexibility to the management in decisions regarding the use of their respective cash flow under various projects.

points.point: Clause 3.1(iii)–(iv): efficiency and shareholder-value arguments — a leaner, focused organisation and a focused operating strategy in the interest of shareholders, employees and other stakeholders.
points.quote: Overall, Demerger would enhance operational efficiency and effectiveness by creating leaner and focused organisation.

points.point: Clause 3.1(v)–(vi): the structural problems being solved are stacked investment layers and opaque shareholding inside the group holding chain.
points.quote: The Demerger will facilitate a reduction of layers of investments, leading to a simpler structure.

points.point: Clause 3.2: the two amalgamation legs (SMAS into SAMIL, MMAL into SMISL) are justified on entity-count reduction, resource pooling and removal of duplicated administrative expenses, overheads and compliances.
points.quote: Simplification of the corporate structure by elimination of multiple entities in the group.

points.point: Clause 3.2(v): the mergers are also expected to unlock cross-business synergies, the same language used across Motherson's acquisition rationales.
points.quote: Unlocking potential synergies across  products, customers, technology and manufacturing excellence.

points.point: Clauses 14.1, 25.1–25.2 and 37.1: no consideration, no share issuance and no ratio — all participating entities are wholly owned, so SMAS's and MMAL's capital is simply cancelled on the Effective Date and both dissolve without winding up.
points.quote: Since the Demerged Company is 100% (one hundred percent) subsidiary of the Resulting Company, no shares will be issued by the Resulting Company.

points.point: The Registrar of Companies flagged that SMAS carried a negative net worth as at 31.03.2025; the Petitioners answered that nothing in the Companies Act bars merging such a company and that both Demerged and Resulting Company net worth is positive post-arrangement.
points.quote: From the Financials of the Amalgamating  Company 1 i.e. Samvardhana Motherson  Auto System P rivate Limited  as at  31.03.2025, it is observed that the  company is having negative net worth.

points.point: The scheme is backdated: the Appointed Date is 01.04.2024, with the First Motion application filed 06.03.2025 to stay inside the one-year window under section 232(6), and NCLT sanction only arriving 26.10.2026.
points.quote: The Appointed Date  fixed under the proposed Scheme of A rrangement  is 01.04.2024.

Per Sep 2025: independently listed companies unlocking shareholder value, aerospace first.

rationale.rationale: Pricol's board, on 27 June 2026, approved demerging the Driver Information & Connected Vehicle Solutions (DICVS) undertaking — connected/electronic/mechanical/electro-mechanical instrument clusters, infotainment, e-cockpit, telematics, battery management systems and some sensors — into a newly incorporated wholly-owned company, Pricol Autotech Limited, leaving Pricol Limited with Actuation, Control & Fluid Management Systems (ACFMS) and the Precision Products polymer business (P3L, acquired from Sundaram Auto Components on 1 February 2025). DICVS was not a small tail: its FY26 turnover was INR 2,424.63 crores, 61.17% of the INR 3,963.85 crore consolidated revenue, and on the 15 May 2026 call management put the mix at roughly 60% DICVS, 20% ACFMS, 20% P3L. The stated problem is that the two halves had drifted apart on "differing customer needs, competitive dynamics, capital allocation and risk profiles" while both had reached "sufficient scale and maturity to function more effectively as focused standalone businesses" — an innovation-led electronics platform (software, display/chip partnerships like the exclusive BOE MOU, 4.5% of revenue on R&D, semiconductor and technology-disruption risk) versus a scale-led manufacturing platform (capacity, automation, tooling, commodity cost and cyclicality risk). The calls show the underlying economics the split addresses: DICVS at INR 2,100–2,200 crores with 12.5–13% EBITDA, ACFMS at ~INR 600 crores targeting 30–35% growth, and polymer at INR 850–900 crores at ~9.5%, a business management said "will never have a 13 to 15% EBITDA because it is a component company" — plus competing claims on one balance sheet, with INR 680–700 crores of capex planned for FY27 alone. The filing says the separation will give each entity financial flexibility for its own investment decisions, reduce operational complexity and speed decision-making, provide "independent and dedicated management teams," let each tailor processes, systems and governance, and deliver "clear market recognition and appropriate valuation benchmarks for each business, free from conglomerate discount," improving the ability to attract strategic and financial investors. Shareholders get 1 new Pricol Autotech share per Pricol share (1:1, INR 1 face value), so the 38.51% promoter / 61.49% public pattern is mirrored, with no cash consideration and listing sought on NSE and BSE. Notably, no investor, lender, customer or partner is named anywhere as having asked for the separation: it is presented as a board-initiated strategic decision, supported by Veda Corporate Advisors, Khaitan & Co, Ramani & Shankar, PwC, SSPA & Co (share entitlement ratio) and Saffron Capital (fairness opinion).
rationale.evolution: Across all eleven calls from 9 November 2023 to 15 May 2026 the separation is never mentioned — what evolves is the three-vertical structure that makes it possible: DICVS/ACFMS running at ~69:31 in May 2024, the TVS-group plastics acquisition announced on the 30 January 2025 call and closed 1 February 2025, and by 7 November 2025 three verticals with explicitly divergent profiles (DICVS INR 2,100–2,200 cr at 12.5–13%, ACFMS ~INR 600 cr growing 30–35%, polymer INR 850–900 cr at 9.5%). The only visible pre-announcement trace is the 30 January 2026 call, where a question about a newly incorporated subsidiary was answered as flexibility for technology partnerships and the BOE MOU, not as a carve-out vehicle; the 15 May 2026 call likewise discussed only capex, headwinds and polymer value-addition. The plan surfaces fully formed in the 27 June 2026 board filing, media note and presentation, and is then carried as a one-line note in the 30 July 2026 and 4 November 2026 results, with Pricol Autotech Limited, Coimbatore appearing in the consolidated subsidiary list and approvals from the exchanges, NCLT, shareholders and creditors still pending.

points.point: The core stated problem: the DICVS undertaking and the remaining ACFMS/P3L business had come to differ on customers, competition, capital allocation and risk, and each had grown big enough to stand alone.
points.quote: The Demerged Undertaking and the Remaining Business of the Demerged Company currently operates with differing customer needs, competitive dynamics, capital allocation and risk profiles.

points.point: Scale of what is leaving: DICVS turnover of INR 2,424.63 crores in FY26, i.e. 61.17% of consolidated turnover — the majority of the company, not a tail business.
points.quote: The turnover of the DICVS Business for the financial year ending March 31, 2026, stood at INR 2,424.63 crores. This represents 61.17% of the total consolidated turnover of the Company for the financial year ending March 31, 2026.

points.point: Valuation is an explicit objective — the presentation names the conglomerate discount as the thing being removed by giving each business its own benchmark.
points.quote: Clear market recognition and appropriate valuation benchmarks for each business, free from conglomerate discount

points.point: Capital allocation is framed as structurally incompatible: Autotech's money goes to talent, software, global R&D centres and overseas acquisitions, while Pricol Ltd's goes to plants, automation and domestic acquisitions.
points.quote: Talent, product development, software, global R&D centres, tech investments & overseas acquisitions

points.point: The two entities are also said to carry different risk books — technology/semiconductor risk on one side, cyclicality and commodity/execution risk on the other.
points.quote: Technology disruption, product innovation cycles & semiconductor ecosystem risks

points.point: Operational benefits claimed: dedicated management teams, faster decisions, and the ability to tailor processes, policies, systems and governance per business.
points.quote: This demerger will provide each of the businesses with independent and dedicated management teams enabling clear market access and a clean operating model, allowing them to better leverage growth opportunities in the domestic and international markets

points.point: Consideration and ownership: no cash, a 1:1 share entitlement so Pricol Autotech mirrors the 38.51% promoter / 61.49% public pattern, with listing to be sought on NSE and BSE.
points.quote: Shareholders of Pricol Limited will receive one fully paid-up equity share of Pricol Autotech Limited for every one fully paid-up equity share held in Pricol Limited (1:1 share entitlement ratio), resulting in the shareholding of Pricol Autotech Limited mirroring the shareholding of Pricol Limited, subject to the Scheme becoming effective.

points.point: Vikram Mohan's framing of timing — the businesses have become differentiated enough that independence, not scale, is now the constraint.
points.quote: We believe this is the right time for each business to operate independently with dedicated leadership, sharper strategic focus and greater operational agility.

points.point: The only pre-announcement trace on any call: a newly incorporated subsidiary (Pricol Autotech was later the resulting company) was explained purely as flexibility for technology partnerships such as the BOE MOU, with no mention of a carve-out.
points.quote: Considering all these aspects, we wanted to have the flexibility and have a company in place.

points.point: One month before the board approval, management sized the three verticals that the scheme then split 60:40 — DICVS against ACFMS plus P3L.
points.quote: On the DICVS our revenue is about 60% of our total revenue, and ACFMS is about 20% and P3L would be about 20%.

points.point: The divergent financial profiles the split formalises were laid out on this call: DICVS at INR 2,100–2,200 crores and 12.5–13% margin, ACFMS at ~INR 600 crores targeting 30–35% growth, polymer at INR 850–900 crores at ~9.5%.
points.quote: And the DICVS vertical will be at around INR 2,100 crores to INR 2,200 crores, and the margin is likely to be at around 12.5% to 13%.

points.point: Management stated the structural margin ceiling difference between the electronics business and the newly acquired polymer component business — the economic gap that later justifies separate valuation frameworks.
points.quote: Pricol Precision Products will never have a 13 to 15% EBITDA because it is a component company.

points.point: DICVS spending that earns no revenue of its own — the BOE display/optical-bonding backward integration — illustrates the technology-capex intensity of the demerged business versus the manufacturing capex of the retained one.
points.quote: Is it going to give any revenue? No, because it is a backward integration project to make it more self-reliant and to give us cost arbitrage.

points.point: Competing claims on one balance sheet: a fresh INR 680–700 crore capex cycle spanning ACFMS, polymer and DICVS simultaneously, funded with debt kept to 0.5–0.6x equity.
points.quote: In fact, this year, in itself, we have planned for about between INR 680 crore to INR 700 crores of CAPEX to cater to all of our new businesses that we have won, new plants, new machines, so on and so forth, which will keep propelling us forward and to maintain this growth momentum.

points.point: The retained polymer business was being repositioned up the value chain with a centre of excellence and forward hiring, accepting ~10% margins for two years — a different value-creation model from DICVS technology investment.
points.quote: We stay committed to our mid-to-long term projections, our investments, and our recommitment to technology, and in the polymer business, we are going to be investing in technology and converting it from a component maker to a value-added polymer player, and we do hope that those will also pay dividends, like in our other divisions in the years to come.

rationale.what_management_expects: Pricol Autotech: an innovation-led electronics platform funded for talent, software, global R&D and overseas M&A, with higher content per vehicle. Pricol Limited: scale-led ACFMS plus polymer, funded for capacity, automation and domestic M&A, riding exports and disc-brake/ABS mandates. For both: separate valuation benchmarks free of conglomerate discount, tailored capital allocation, dedicated leadership, faster decisions, and easier access to strategic and financial investors.
rationale.gaps: No explanation of who asked, debt/asset split, Autotech's standalone P&L or margin targets, dis-synergies and duplicated costs, listing timeline, or named management teams; no earnings call ever discussed it.

rationale.rationale: Religare is demerging its entire financial services business — SME/MSME lending (Religare Finvest), retail broking plus e-governance (Religare Broking and its subsidiary Religare Digital Solutions), affordable housing finance (Religare Housing Development Finance, already an RFL subsidiary), and the related investment and ancillary/support activities — out of the listed holdco REL into RFL, which will itself be listed, leaving REL as a pure-play holder of its 63.2% stake in Care Health Insurance; REL shareholders get 1 RFL share for every REL share, and RFL's pre-scheme capital held by REL is cancelled so RFL's shareholding mirrors REL's. Management framed it as three converging conditions rather than a reaction to distress: the Burman Group's completed takeover as promoters (open offer concluded Feb 2025, board reconstituted July 2025, promoters at 29.75% fully diluted in Feb 2026 and ~30.3% by May 2026 after ~4% of open-market buying, heading to ~34% on warrant conversion), the INR1,500 crore preferential warrant raise subscribed 50:50 by the Burmans and marquee investors (earmarked INR600 crore to Care, INR250 crore to housing finance, INR200 crore to broking, INR75 crore to repay REL's own debt and INR375 crore general corporate purpose), and the fact that the businesses had reached an inflection point where "each business also operates with different capital requirements, risk frameworks, manpower talent and growth trajectories." The stated problems it solves are a conglomerate structure in which insurance (FY26 GWP INR11,417 crore, PBT INR539 crore on 'n' basis, 19.7% retail SAHI share) drowns out a tiny financial services segment (FY25 demerged-undertaking turnover of only INR457.29 crore, 6.2% of consolidated revenue), investors who cannot value the two halves, and management bandwidth: the scheme's four pillars are streamlined focus/simplified structure, value unlocking plus targeted capital raising through a separate RFL listing, dedicated leadership with sector-specific talent and performance-linked rewards, and risk/compliance frameworks tailored to each segment. The financial services side is being restarted from a cleaned-up base — RFL is debt-free with all legacy promoter-era diversion issues provided or written off (including the full INR750 crore Lakshmi Vilas Bank FD), RBI's Corrective Action Plan lifted in July 2025 and bank fraud tags removed, leaving ~INR591 crore cash, ~INR900 crore net worth, 261% CRAR, NOF of INR821 crore and only a ~INR60 crore core SME book — so Arjun Lamba tied the demerger directly to scaling: "Our intent is to scale all of these business to make them meaningful and sizable and part of this demerger is on account of this." Who asked for it: shareholders and analysts had been pressing since the first call back in Nov 2025 (Vikas Shrivastav on demerging Care and removing the holdco discount, Dixit Doshi on IPO vs demerger of Care), and after the announcement nearly every questioner — Umang Shah, Adarsh, Hitaindra Pradhan, Ravi Purohit, Niharika Karnani, Sarvesh Gupta — argued the value sits in Care and demanded a reverse merger giving direct Care shares, citing the Max Financial precedent. Management conceded the point but said IRDAI's 25–26% promoter requirement cannot be met while the Burmans' look-through stake in Care is only ~18–19%, so this was "the first step in that direction," done after evaluating structural alternatives with leading advisors; Lamba refused to amend the scheme and would not commit to a timeline for a second one. Execution has since run into the regulator: exchanges gave no-objection/no-adverse-observation letters on 7 July 2026, but on 6–7 August 2026 RBI informed REL and RFL that their application for no-objection/prior approval "has not been acceded to," and the companies said they would engage further with the regulator.
rationale.evolution: On the Nov 2025 call (Q2/H1 FY26, the first investor call after the Burman takeover) there was no plan — Vikas Shrivastav asked directly what the structure would look like in two years and whether Care would be demerged from the holdco, and CFO Pratul Gupta would only say the board was evaluating options and wanted to make the businesses "larger, better, stronger" before any capital-market action, while Dixit Doshi asked whether Care would be IPO'd or demerged. A Moneycontrol report on 3 Feb 2026 that REL would demerge and list Care drew an exchange query, which REL denied as a disclosable event; eleven days later, on 14 Feb 2026, the REL and RFL boards approved the scheme — and the Feb 2026 call (16 Feb) was where Gupta laid out the full rationale, the four pillars, the 1:1 ratio, the 15–18 month timetable and a Q1 FY28 RFL listing, while every analyst pushed back that Care, not financial services, should have been separated. By the May 2026 call (13 May, Q4/FY26) the framing had shifted from Gupta's structural logic to Executive Director Arjun Lamba's: separating FS from insurance was "number one," the promoters had bought ~4% more stock toward the IRDAI threshold, and he declined to amend the scheme while leaving a later reverse merger of Care open "at an appropriate stage." The 7 July 2026 exchange observation letters cleared the way, but the 7 Aug 2026 filings disclosed RBI had refused to accede to the application, leaving the scheme stalled pending further engagement.

points.point: Asked outright about demerging Care and the other subsidiaries from the holdco and about removing the holdco discount, Pratul Gupta said nothing was decided — the board was weighing options and wanted to strengthen the businesses first, after the INR1,500 crore raise, before any capital-market action.
points.quote: On the second question about how the structure will look like in some future time, what I can very clearly assure you is that the management and the Board is evaluating various options which can add value to the shareholders.

points.point: Investors were already framing the choice as Care IPO versus demerger; Dixit Doshi asked it explicitly alongside questions on NBFC yields, showing the separation idea originated with shareholders rather than management.
points.quote: And in terms of your initial comments on the value unlocking, if you can just touch upon whether we will be looking for an IPO for the care health business or we will be better off with the de -merger of the business?

points.point: Gupta presented the demerger as a strategic imperative rather than a housekeeping exercise, announced two days after the REL and RFL boards approved it on 14 Feb 2026.
points.quote: It is a strategic imperati ve step designed to unlock shareholder value, create business clarity and position the resulting entities for sustained long -term growth.

points.point: The trigger was three converging conditions — the Burman takeover as promoters, the INR1,500 crore warrant raise covering funding needs for the foreseeable future, and the businesses reaching a scale that demands specialised focus.
points.quote: Each business also operates with different capital requirements, risk frameworks, manpower talent and growth trajectories.

points.point: Mechanics: lending, broking and ancillary support services move from REL to RFL on a going-concern basis, the Care stake stays in REL, RFL issues one share per REL share and then lists, with a 15–18 month process ending in Q1 FY28.
points.quote: The lending, broking and ancillary support services held under REL shall be demer ged into RFL on a going concern basis. The investment in CARE shall continue to be retained in REL.

points.point: A separate RFL listing is meant to unlock value, widen investor participation and let that business raise its own capital — the second of four stated pillars.
points.quote: The independent listing of RFL is expected to unlock shareholder value and enhance investor participation.

points.point: Analysts attacked the design immediately: Umang Shah argued demerging Care directly would have removed the holdco discount on the asset that carries most of the value.
points.quote: I'm a bit puzzled why we chose to demerge financial services and not CARE directly?

points.point: Gupta positioned this as stage one of a longer restructuring, with a Care reverse merger possible later once unspecified milestones and minimum-shareholding thresholds are met.
points.quote: Well, I think this is -- as I mentioned, this is the first step in that direction.

points.point: The binding constraint on a Care reverse merger is the IRDAI promoter-shareholding rule against a Burman look-through stake in Care of only ~18–19%, which Gupta confirmed when Vikas Srivastava spelled out the law.
points.quote: So you are right in terms of the fact that the look - through shareholding of the promoter group today in CARE is at around 18% to 19%.

points.point: Management said the structure was chosen after a full review of alternatives with external advisors, and promised no operational, customer or employee disruption during implementation.
points.quote: This has resulted after comprehensive evalu ation of various structural alternatives which were discussed with leading advisors.

points.point: Arjun Lamba restated the core purpose as separating financial services from insurance to give shareholders a clean, understandable structure and management a single focus, while acknowledging the holdco-discount complaint.
points.quote: And for us, number one has been to separate the FS business from the insurance business and to provide a clean structure so that the shareholders can understand, th e management can be very focused in doing what they have to do.

points.point: Lamba linked the demerger to the capital allocation plan — INR600 crore to Care, INR250 crore to housing finance, INR200 crore to broking, ~INR375 crore general corporate purpose, with RFL needing none given ~INR900–1,000 crore net worth and ~INR600 crore cash.
points.quote: Our intent is to scale all of these business to make them meaningful and sizable and part of this demerger is on account of this.

points.point: Pressed by Vikas Srivastava on whether the scheme could be amended to fold Care in once the promoters reach 26%, Lamba ruled out amending it but left a subsequent scheme open.
points.quote: No, I'll answer your last question first. We don't want to amend the scheme.

points.point: Lamba conceded the value is concentrated in Care and said the separation is intended to create value in the other entity too, as promoters moved from ~26% toward ~34% diluted.
points.quote: Yes, we understand that the value is in Care. We are cognizant of that. That's why we are separating the entities, creating clear paths, and we hope to create value in the other entity as well

points.point: The 14 Feb 2026 filing states the demerged undertaking is all of REL's financial services activity — lending, broking, investment and ancillary/support services — explicitly excluding the retained insurance business, i.e. the Care Health shareholding.
points.quote: Provided that, the Demerged Undertaking shall exclude the Remaining Business ( as defined in the Scheme ) compris ing of all the units, divisions, undertakings, assets and liabilities in relation to the Demerged Company’s insurance business, comprising of its investment and shareholding in Care Health Insurance Limited .

points.point: The scheme quantifies how small the demerged half is: FY25 turnover of INR457.29 crore on a consolidated basis, just 6.2% of REL's consolidated turnover.
points.quote: The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the year ended 31  March , 202 5 was INR 457.29 Crores on a consolidated basis  representing 6.2% of the total consolidated turnover of the Company for the year ended 31 March , 202 5.

points.point: Stated rationale includes that the two businesses face different competition and attract different investors, partners and lenders, and that a separately listed vehicle enables sector-focused talent and growth opportunities.
points.quote: The nature and competition involved in the businesses comprising of the Demerged Undertaking is distinct from the other businesses and it is capable of attracting a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders.

points.point: The press release lists four objectives — streamlining businesses, listing financial services, focused management with performance mapped to each business, and segment-tailored risk and compliance frameworks — with 1:1 mirror shareholding in RFL and listing targeted for Q1 FY28.
points.quote: Focused management attention:  Enable mapping of employee p erformance and rewards to respective business outcomes, and facilitate attraction and retention of sector -specific talent and resources.

points.point: SEBI's comments routed through the NSE observation letter of 7 July 2026 require REL to disclose the need for the demerger, cost-benefit analysis, risks and the RBI approval position to shareholders — i.e. the rationale was not yet fully documented for them.
points.quote: Need for demerger, rationale of the scheme, synergies of  business of the entities involved in the scheme, impact of the scheme on the shareholders and cost benefit analysis of the s cheme.

points.point: Execution setback: after exchange no-objections on 7 July 2026, RBI declined the no-objection/prior-approval applications of both REL and RFL in letters dated 6 and 7 August 2026, and the companies said they would go back to the regulator.
points.quote: The Company has received a letter dated August 6, 2026 , from the RBI, conveying that the application has been examined and that the request has not been acceded to .

rationale.what_management_expects: REL becomes a pure-play health insurance holdco around Care (GWP INR11,417 crore, PBT INR539 crore 'n' basis, combined ratio heading from 101.4% to ~100% in two years on operating leverage, 18–24% growth). RFL becomes an integrated, separately listed financial services platform — debt-free, ~INR900 crore net worth, ~INR591 crore cash, 261% CRAR — able to leverage to industry norms, raise targeted capital, hire sector-specific leadership on performance-linked rewards, run tailored risk frameworks, and unlock value via mirror 1:1 listing.
rationale.gaps: No cost-benefit or synergy quantification, no RFL valuation or AUM/ROE targets, no holdco-discount fix or Care reverse-merger timeline, no stated path to IRDAI's 26%, and no RBI-rejection reasoning.

rationale.rationale: The separation is the demerger of the Industrial undertaking of SKF India Limited (automotive remaining with SKF India Ltd.) into SKF India (Industrial) Limited, a company incorporated 17 December 2024 purely to receive it, sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 26 September 2025 with appointed/effective date 1 October 2025, a 1:1 share exchange (49,437,963 shares to SKF India holders on the 15 October 2025 record date) and listing on BSE/NSE from 5 December 2025. Management's stated reason is sector focus: the Q3 FY25-26 release frames it as 'SKF's demerger into two sector-focused, strategically independent organizations, enabling sharper market orientation, faster decision-making, and enhanced long-term value creation for shareholders,' a 'pivotal step in SKF's 102-year India journey,' with the industrial entity 'more agile and focused,' able to 'respond faster to market needs' and 'tailor it's manufacturing capabilities' for manufacturing, railways, renewables, cement and heavy engineering. On the 13 May 2026 call the operating logic is spelled out as the ACES strategy to 2028 (accelerate localization, commercial excellence, disciplined execution, one SKF) plus the point that industrial economics differ structurally from automotive — 'industrial business is all about flexibility in the channels... because the lot size, unlike automotive, is smaller' — and that localization lets it re-enter segments it had exited (wind, freight railways, agricultural tractors). Dedicated capacity is the second half of the logic: the Board approved a new Pune factory on 3 February 2026, part of INR 800 crore+ capex to FY29-30 (including INR 350-400 crore of DGBB/TRB channel additions), commissioning end-CY2028, because the business is 'running out of capacity' and currently relies on SKF India job work. The cost of separating was explicit: INR 1,800.8 million of exceptional demerger charges in Q3 FY26 (IT, professional fees, large stamp duty/transfer premium on the land transferred from SKF India), INR 1,961 million for nine months, and a further INR 183 million of demerger IT cost in Q4, which turned reported Q3 PBT to negative INR 671.4 million against INR 1,129.4 million before exceptionals. Management's payoff case is margin recovery to ~13% once demerger costs lapse by end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 and an aspiration of 16-18%, on 8%+ growth; interim performance cited was Q4 FY26 sales INR 9,457.2 million (+9.8% QoQ, +31% YoY), PBT 9.5% reported and 11.5% ex-one-offs, net working capital down 2.8% to 18.7% of sales, then Q1 FY27 revenue INR 9,707.7 million (+18.3% YoY) at 9.0% PBT.
rationale.evolution: These texts contain no pre-demerger call, so the origin of the idea is not on record here; the earliest document is the Scheme itself (NCLT order 26 September 2025, effective 1 October 2025, listing 5 December 2025). The 4 February 2026 press release, reporting the first post-demerger quarter, carries the only explicit rationale statement (two sector-focused independent organizations, sharper orientation, faster decisions, shareholder value) alongside INR 1,800.8 million of separation costs, and the same Board meeting on 3 February 2026 approved the new Pune factory — converting the rationale into standalone capacity. By the 13 May 2026 Q4/FY26 call the framing had shifted from justification to execution: the ACES strategy 'as we are now a separate listed entity,' INR 800 crore+ capex, re-entry into previously exited wind/railway/tractor business, and a margin path of 13% near term to 15% by FY29-30. The 12 August 2026 Q1 FY27 release continues the 'focused, independent business' framing with 18.3% YoY growth at 9% PBT.

points.point: The Scheme of Arrangement between SKF India Limited (Demerged Company) and SKF India (Industrial) Limited (Resulting Company) transferred the Industrial Undertaking on a going-concern basis at carrying values, with the difference credited to Capital Reserve; NCLT order dated 26 September 2025, appointed and effective date 1 October 2025.
points.quote: The Scheme, among other provisions, entails the demerger of the Demerged Undertaking from the Demerged Company into the Resulting Company on a going concern basis.

points.point: The only explicit statement of purpose in the filings: two sector-focused, independent organizations for sharper market orientation, faster decision-making and shareholder value, after 102 years of SKF in India.
points.quote: The results come against the backdrop of SKF's demerger into two sector-focused, strategically independent organizations, enabling sharper market orientation, faster decision-making, and enhanced long-term value creation for shareholders, marking a pivotal step in SKF's 102-year India journey.

points.point: MD Mukund Vasudevan's rationale in the 4 February 2026 Q3 FY25-26 release: agility, speed of response and manufacturing tailored to industrial customers, serving manufacturing, railways, renewables, cement and heavy engineering.
points.quote: As a more agile and focused industrial entity, SKF India (Industrial) is well-positioned to respond faster to market needs, tailor it's manufacturing capabilities, and support India's accelerating infrastructure and manufacturing build-out.

points.point: Separation cost quantified as exceptional items: INR 1,800.8 million in Q3 FY26 and INR 1,961 million for nine months for IT cost, professional services and stamp duty including transfer premium on land acquired under the Scheme — which pushed reported Q3 PBT to negative INR 671.4 million versus INR 1,129.4 million before exceptionals.
points.quote: During the quarter and nine months ended 31 December 2025, the Company accounted certain demerger expenses for IT Cost, professional services and stamp duty, including estimated transfer premium payable to statutory authorities to effect transfer of registration of land acquired under the Scheme, aggregating to Rs. 1,800.8 million and Rs. 1,961 million, respectively, which have been included under "Exceptional items".

points.point: The Board meeting of 3 February 2026 — the same meeting that approved the first post-demerger results — approved a new standalone factory at Pune, the capacity leg of the separation.
points.quote: We wish to inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting held today, i.e. on February 03, 2026, has approved the setting up of a new factory /plant at Pune, Maharashtra.

points.point: Management re-stated the ACES strategy (accelerate localization, commercial excellence, disciplined execution, one SKF, defined through 2028) explicitly because the company is now separately listed and needs its own growth and profitability narrative.
points.quote: I thought it's important to reiterate our strategy as we are now a separate listed entity as SKF India (Industrial) and I think it helps to kind of say what are we trying to do and how are we trying to grow and make our business more profitable.

points.point: The structural case for separate industrial management: industrial runs on small lot sizes and channel flexibility unlike automotive — the Pune TRB example raised capacity from 600,000 to 886,000 pieces, cut cost ~18% and improved changeover/flexibility 20% and new-product lead time 35%.
points.quote: Flexibility, which is key, which is industrial business is all about flexibility in the channels, which means we can switch between one product and another because the lot size, unlike automotive, is smaller.

points.point: A concrete problem the focused, localized entity solves: segments previously abandoned on cost/margin grounds — wind, freight railways, agricultural tractors — are being re-entered via localization, including a 32.5 crore tractor OEM win and ZF/Suzlon wind orders that drove 91% QoQ wind growth.
points.quote: The reason you are right, we did exit wind business . Because of localization we are now getting back into it.

points.point: Residual entanglement with the automotive entity persists: SKF India (Industrial) manufactures for SKF India Automotive (~4% of FY26 sales), pays royalty/trademark (up ~INR 60 million QoQ) and a transfer-pricing margin on services, and SKF India job-works for it until the new plant starts.
points.quote: We are , till that new plant comes up , comes about, we are continuing to do some our SKF India entity is continuing to manufacture some for us on a job work basis.

points.point: The one-off separation charges continued into Q4 FY26 at INR 183 million, so reported PBT of 9.5% was 11.5% adjusted (versus 13.1% adjusted in Q3), with the remaining gap blamed on OEM mix (OEM up from 46% to 50%) and full bonus accrual.
points.quote: In this quarter, we again had demerger -related IT costs, primarily that, totalling up to INR 183 million.

points.point: Margin roadmap post-separation: back to ~13% once demerger costs end around end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 through localization, operational efficiency and S&A leverage, with 16-18% only an aspiration held back by OEM mix, competition and depreciation from the new plant.
points.quote: So given the recent demerger expenses, right, by we would say towards the end of this calendar year, we see that mostly normalizing. We should get back to a little more around 13%.

points.point: Standalone capital plan: INR 800 crore+ capex FY26-27 to FY29-30, a large part for the new Pune plant plus DGBB and TRB channel additions (the INR 350-400 crore earlier flagged), operational mid-2028 and fully ramped by end-CY2028, with growth of ~8% in the interim.
points.quote: So, on capex, the overall plan for the between FY 26, FY27 to FY 29, FY30, we are looking at doing a capex spend of around INR 800 crores plus, which includes a significant chunk of investment on the new Pune plant which we are in the process of setting up.

points.point: Q1 FY27 (12 August 2026) validates the focused-entity framing: revenue INR 9,707.7 million, up 18.3% YoY, PBT INR 869.2 million at 9.0%, with growth in Wind, General Machinery and Agriculture (Tractors) despite currency and residual demerger costs.
points.quote: In our 3rd quarter as a focused, independent business, SKF India (Industrial) delivered 18.3% year-on-year Sales growth, while maintaining a healthy 9% PBT (in spite of headwinds from currency and demerger-related expenses).

rationale.what_management_expects: For SKF India (Industrial): sharper market orientation, faster decisions, agility and manufacturing tailored to industrial lot sizes; ~8% growth with PBT recovering to ~13% by end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 (16-18% aspiration); net working capital 19-20% of sales; INR 800 crore+ own capex and a new Pune plant replacing SKF India job work; shareholder value via two independent listed entities.
rationale.gaps: No pre-demerger call rationale; no named requester (investors, lenders, partners); no synergy loss, standalone-cost, tax or valuation quantification; nothing on the automotive entity's economics or arm's-length agreement terms.

rationale.rationale: Management presents the separation as a Composite Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230–232, sanctioned by the NCLT Mumbai Bench amongst Tata Motors Limited (the demerged company, now Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited), TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (the resulting company) and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (amalgamated into the demerged entity), effective 1 October 2025; the resulting company was renamed Tata Motors Limited on 29 October 2025 and its shares listed on BSE/NSE (ticker TMCV) on 12 November 2025, with outstanding PSUs replaced one-for-one under a new scheme covering up to 23,07,647 shares (0.062% dilution). The stated problem the split solves is a reporting and identity one: 'Historically, we reported a CV segment. It was an internal construct that carved out CV operations from within the erstwhile combined entity. That was a practical necessity then' — from Q4 FY26 the company reports standalone financials including the Tata Cummins joint operation as its primary lens, giving 'a cleaner, more complete, and more directly comparable picture'. The separation cost ₹960 crore of one-time demerger expense booked in Q3 FY26 (part of ₹1,500 crore standalone / ₹1,600 crore consolidated exceptionals, alongside ₹603 crore of new labour code and ₹82 crore of Iveco acquisition cost). The pure-play case is argued with numbers: FY26 revenue ₹77,000 crore (vs ₹66,000 crore FY23), EBITDA margin up from 7.8% (FY23) to 13.2% (FY26) — ~550bps of 'structural improvement' — EBITDA doubled from ₹5,100 crore to ₹10,200 crore, PBT before exceptionals ₹8,700 crore, first-ever double-digit EBIT at 11% (the CV segment first crossed it at 10.6% in Q3 FY26), FCF ₹9,200 crore or 12% of revenue, Auto ROCE 72%, cash conversion cycle of negative 31 days, net cash ₹7,500 crore standalone and ₹13,700 crore consolidated, and a maiden final dividend of ₹4/share (~₹1,500 crore outflow). Cyclicality is the second problem: non-cyclical revenue (parts & service, Fleet Edge digital subscriptions, Smart City e-bus operations) is compounding at 2.7x the cyclical CAGR, 'deliberately building this mix', and Q4 working-capital sinks historically concentrated in Q4 have been spread through the year. Third, the standalone CV entity became the acquisition vehicle: its own balance sheet and a committed EUR 3.825 billion bridge from Morgan Stanley and MUFG funded an all-cash voluntary totalitarian tender offer for Iveco Group N.V. at EUR 14.10 (raised to EUR 14.40), valuing Iveco at ~EUR 3.82 billion, creating ~EUR 21 billion (INR 2,28,000 crore+) of combined revenue and ~590k units with Europe ~46%/India ~32%/South America ~8%/RoW ~14% and 'substantially no overlap' — expected to 'drive better operating leverage by spreading its capital investments over larger volumes, generating operating efficiencies and reducing the cash flow volatility inherent in the commercial vehicles sector', plus enhancing Iveco's FPT powertrain business. Structural simplification continues inside the CV entity: TMF Holdings Limited and TMF Business Services Limited (wholly owned subsidiaries) are being amalgamated into it, and Tata Motor Finance had already been folded into Tata Capital (whose October 2025 IPO priced 20–25% below the merger valuation, forcing a ₹2,000 crore mark-to-market loss in Q2 FY26 and a ₹295 crore write-back in Q3).
rationale.evolution: In the Nov 2025 call (Q2 FY26, 13 November 2025) management reported the split as done rather than argued for it — demerger effective 1 October, CV listing completed as TMCV 'as committed previously', Iveco approvals underway and the bridge loan secured. In the Feb 2026 call (Q3 FY26, 29 January 2026) the cost showed up as a ₹960 crore one-time demerger exceptional while the CV segment hit a double-digit EBIT margin (10.6%) for the first time and Iveco approvals were guided to end-March. In the May 2026 call (Q4 FY26, 13 May 2026) the framing shifted decisively: 'Tata Motors is now a pure play commercial vehicle company... a defining shift', the old carved-out CV segment was retired in favour of standalone reporting, three-year pure-play metrics were laid out, and Iveco closure slipped to Q2 FY27 pending French and Spanish financial-regulator approvals. Filings then show execution: offer launched 4 September 2026, 89.42% tendered by 27 October 2026, 96.29% after the reopening on 6 November 2026, triggering the Dutch legal squeeze-out, alongside the TMF Holdings/TMF Business Services amalgamation notices.

points.point: The problem the split solves, as stated: the CV business was previously visible only as an internal carve-out construct inside the combined entity.
points.quote: Historically, we reported a CV segment. It was an internal construct that carved out CV operations from within the erstwhile combined entity. That was a practical necessity then.

points.point: Post-demerger reporting switched to standalone financials including the Tata Cummins joint operation as the primary lens, for transparency and comparability.
points.quote: This gives you a cleaner, more complete, and more directly comparable picture of the business going forward.

points.point: The margin record cited as structural rather than cyclical: 7.8% to 13.2% EBITDA over three years, with EBITDA doubling from ₹5,100 crore to ₹10,200 crore and FY26 EBIT at 11%.
points.quote: EBITDA margins have expanded from 7.8% in FY23 to 13.2% in FY26. That's nearly 550 bps of structural improvement over three years.

points.point: Capital-efficiency case for the standalone entity: ₹9,200 crore FCF (12% of revenue), ₹2,800 crore reinvested, Auto ROCE of 72%, negative 31-day cash conversion cycle, net cash ₹7,500 crore standalone and ₹13,700 crore consolidated.
points.quote: Finally, the Auto ROCE stands at 72% is an industry-leading number, when EBIT doubles, capital discipline holds, returns follow.

points.point: Deliberate de-cyclicalisation of the standalone business via parts & service, Fleet Edge digital and Smart City e-buses, growing far faster than the cyclical truck business.
points.quote: Over the period, non-cyclical CAGR is running at 2.7x the cyclical CAGR. We've been deliberately building this mix, and this is now showing up meaningfully in the numbers.

points.point: Mechanics of the separation as disclosed in every filing: NCLT Mumbai-sanctioned Composite Scheme of Arrangement amongst Tata Motors Limited, TML Commercial Vehicles Limited and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited, with the resulting company renamed and listed.
points.quote: As per the Composite Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by the Hon’ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench—amongst Tata Motors Limited, TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (the Company) and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited—the Company’s name was changed to Tata Motors Limited from TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (effective 29 October 2025), and its equity shares are listed on the BSE Ltd and the NSE Ltd.

points.point: Employee incentives were carried across the split one-for-one: outstanding PSUs of the demerged company entitle holders to a matching PSU from the CV entity, implemented via a new scheme for up to 23,07,647 shares (0.062% dilution).
points.quote: the unexercised performance share units (“PSUs”) (whether vested or unvested) granted to participants under the Demerged Company’s Incentive Scheme(s) and remaining outstanding as on the record date shall entitle such participants to receive one (1) corresponding PSU to be granted by the Resulting Company under a new incentive scheme.

points.point: The separated CV entity's strategic use of its independence — the Iveco combination is justified on scale, no overlap, operating leverage and dampening CV cash-flow volatility; ~EUR 21 billion combined revenue, ~590k units, Europe 46%/India 32%.
points.quote: The new company will be able to drive better operating leverage by spreading its capital investments over larger volumes, generating operating efficiencies and reducing the cash flow volatility inherent in the commercial vehicles sector.

points.point: Iveco was pursued as an all-cash EUR 14.10 (later EUR 14.40) offer valuing Iveco at ~EUR 3.82 billion, funded by a committed EUR 3.825 billion bridge from Morgan Stanley and MUFG, with Exor (27.06% of shares, 43.19% of votes) irrevocably committed.
points.quote: TML CV HS signed a debt commitment letter with Morgan Stanley Bank, N.A., Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, Inc. and MUFG Bank, Ltd. for fully committed bridge financing to be used in connection with the Transaction, which was subsequently implemented through a facility agreement entered into by the Offeror for an aggregate amount of up to EUR 3,825,000,000.00.

points.point: Structural simplification continued after the demerger: the CV entity is absorbing its own wholly owned financing subsidiaries TMF Holdings and TMF Business Services under a further NCLT scheme.
points.quote: The Scheme provides for the merger of Amalgamating Company 1 and Amalgamating Company 2 (being direct and indirect wholly owned subsidiaries of the Company respectively) with the Company.

rationale.what_management_expects: Pure-play CV: cleaner, comparable standalone reporting including Tata Cummins joint operations; teens (not mid-teens) EBITDA guidance, double-digit EBIT, capex 2–4% of revenue, FCF ~12% of revenue, 72% ROCE, net cash ₹7,500cr standalone/₹13,700cr consolidated funding a ₹4 dividend and the Iveco bid; with Iveco, ~EUR21bn revenue, operating leverage over larger volumes, less cash-flow volatility. No PV-entity commentary.
rationale.gaps: Why separate at all — no pre-demerger call is in the record: no stated valuation-unlock, synergy or capital-allocation rationale, no investor, lender or partner named as requesting it, no entitlement ratio.

judge.what_is_spun: The Bio Pharma (Biopharma) Undertaking — bio-pharma and bio-polymers businesses, plant-based APIs, nutraceuticals and nicotine derivatives
demerged_business_names: Ennature Biopharma division of India Glycols Limited
Ennature Bio Pharma Private Limited (former name)
judge.reason: "The demerger will result in the creation of three separate companies, each with a clear business focus," giving each dedicated management oversight and capital, investments and resources managed to its own business requirements.
judge.insiders: Promoter family controls it: Pragya Bhartia Barwale Managing Director 5 years (ran the division to Rs 200 crore revenue); father U.S. Bhartia and sister Pooja Jhaver non-executive directors; promoters held 3,99,67,854 of 6,70,26,765 IGL shares, voted 100% in favour.
judge.hidden_value: Tax cost apportionment assigns Ennature 20.61% of value on only ~2% of group revenue (FY26 segment revenue Rs 207.77 crore, EBIT Rs 7.23 crore, 3.5%, down from 20.76 crore EBIT in FY25), with segment assets Rs 426.42 crore versus liabilities Rs 92.49 crore — a depressed-margin, asset-heavy business management says is being rebuilt into branded nutraceuticals.
judge.selling_pressure_why: Smallest of three entities, only 2,23,42,255 shares on a 1-for-3 ratio creating odd lots; pharma/nutraceuticals unrelated to chemicals or spirits holders bought.
judge.listing_timeline: Per EBPL's letter dated 2 November 2026: listing and trading approvals received from BSE and NSE on November 02, 2026 for 2,23,42,255 equity shares of Rs 5/- each, with "Date of Commencement of Trading: November 04, 2026"; earlier, the 1 September 2026 news release said only that "The management of Ennature Bio Pharma Limited will apply to BSE and NSE for listing of its shares on the respective bourses."
judge.read_next: Ennature Bio Pharma's Information Memorandum (board-approved 8 September 2026) — standalone balance sheet, debt allocation and segment margin trend.
judge.quote: Ennature Bio Pharma Limited will house the bio-pharma and bio-polymers businesses.

rationale.rationale: Management presented the separation as a focus-and-investor-base argument, not a rescue: India Glycols was running four structurally different businesses under one listing — Bio-based Specialties & Performance Chemicals (BSPC, including the 49% Clariant IGL Specialty Chemicals JV into which IGL sells ethylene oxide), Potable Spirits (country liquor/IMIL plus IMFL, with the Amrut and Bacardi tie-ups), Bio-Fuel/ethanol-ENA sold at government-administered prices to OMCs, and Ennature Biopharma (thiocolchicoside, nicotine, nutraceuticals) with biopolymers. On 4 February 2025 the board approved splitting these into India Glycols (chemicals, glycols, bio-glycols, new specialties, industrial gases, plus the Clariant JV), IGL Spirits (spirits + bio-fuel/ENA) and Ennature Bio Pharma (biopharma + biopolymers), all three to be listed via the NCLT route. CEO Rupark Sarswat said the purpose was to run the companies differently with much more focus and to allow potential investments in different businesses because different investors have different appetites; CFO Anand Singhal listed the benefits as independent growth for each business, reducing the risk of one business affecting the others, unlocking value by drawing focused investors, and clearer focus leading to improved management and resource allocation — while insisting the structure would not unduly increase the cost base. Scale was quantified with 9MFY25 numbers: chemicals Rs 1,079 cr at 13.6% EBITDA margin, IGL Spirits Rs 1,628 cr net at 14.4%, Ennature Bio Pharma Rs 178 cr at 14.9% (against FY24 BSPC Rs 1,626 cr, Bio-Fuel Rs 512 cr, Potable Spirits Rs 5,575 cr gross). Capital allocation was the hard constraint: big capex was frozen until after the demerger, long-term debt was pre-allocated with the SBI-led consortium (about Rs 500 cr chemicals / Rs 700 cr liquor out of Rs 1,200 cr in May 2025, restated to Rs 600 cr / Rs 800 cr out of about Rs 1,400 cr in November 2025), the Rs 467 cr preferential allotment at Rs 915/share in November 2025 went entirely into prepaying debt, and the credit rating was parked on watch-list with no upgrade possible until the demerger completed. Management simultaneously defended keeping bio-fuel with spirits rather than with chemicals, arguing captive multi-feedstock ethanol/ENA gives backward integration, quality control, scale and resilience even if it dilutes percentage margin, and that plant proximity and the EO-to-JV link preserve synergies. By FY26 the residual chemicals business was pitched as under-earning for want of focus and in-house cost streamlining, with the contracted sale of a further 24% of the Clariant JV in FY29 expected to make the chemicals entity debt-free. The scheme was sanctioned by NCLT Allahabad on 17 July 2026, became effective 1 September 2026 (appointed date 1 April 2026), with IGL Spirits and Ennature Bio Pharma listing and trading from 2–4 November 2026.
rationale.evolution: First disclosed on the 6 February 2025 call as a composite scheme that also folded promoter holding company Kashipur Holdings into IGL so promoters would hold IGL directly; by the 21 May 2025 call it was accompanied by a Rs 500 cr/Rs 700 cr debt split, and the board on 16 May 2025 dropped the KHL amalgamation to pursue the demerger alone. The 11 August 2025 and 18 November 2025 calls hardened the mechanics — three named entities, capex deferred to the post-demerger companies, debt restated to Rs 600 cr/Rs 800 cr, and a Rs 467 cr promoter-and-associates preferential issue to cut debt — while an investor on the August call openly questioned demerging a unit in degrowth. The 12 February 2026 call added that the credit rating would stay on watch-list and no sizeable capex would be sanctioned until completion, and the 18 May 2026 call was spent waiting on the NCLT hearing of 21 May. Shareholders (4,42,48,625 of 4,42,48,626 votes) and unsecured creditors (100% by value) approved on 24 March 2026; NCLT sanctioned on 17 July 2026, effective 1 September 2026, record date 2 September 2026, with trading in both new entities from 4 November 2026.

points.point: Rupark Sarswat first unveiled the three-way restructuring, initially to sit inside the IGL group before listing.
points.quote: So, essentially what we are trying to do is to restructure these businesses into three separate companies, for the time being within the IGL group.

points.point: The core stated reason: different businesses need different strategies and attract different pools of capital.
points.quote: And also, to allow potential investments in different businesses because different investors tend to have a different focus for investments.

points.point: CFO Anand Singhal framed one benefit as ring-fencing contagion between segments (relevant given Ennature's margin collapse and the chemicals/EO price squeeze).
points.quote: Separating the business will reduce the risk of one business affecting the others.

points.point: Anand gave the pro-forma 9MFY25 size and margins of each proposed entity — chemicals Rs 1,079 cr at 13.6%, spirits+biofuel Rs 1,628 cr at 14.4%, Ennature Rs 178 cr at 14.9%.
points.quote: IGL Spirits, which is proposed to be the other Company which will be having the Liquor business and the Bio-Fuel business, is having 9MFY25 turnover of Rs. 1,628, this is on net basis with 14.4% EBITDA margin.

points.point: Anand confirmed the NCLT route, a 12-15 month timetable, 1 April 2026 appointed date and listing of all three entities.
points.quote: So, this demerger will be effective from 1st April, 26 and all the three companies will be listed on the stock exchange.

points.point: Investors pushed on listing of the biggest piece, noting over 75% of the business would sit in IGL Spirits.
points.quote: Sir, my first question regarding post restructuring, more than 75% of business comes from IGL Spirits. Is there any plan to list that entity?

points.point: Lender involvement: working capital and term loan allocation across the three companies had to be negotiated with the SBI-led consortium and was not yet confirmed.
points.quote: Rohit, regarding the working capital allocation to each Company and the term loan allocation, we are talking to the term lender, mainly the State Bank of India, who is the leader in our consortium banking.

points.point: Rupark stressed the split must not create duplicate overheads; corporate resources would stay shared with an allocation mechanism.
points.quote: The principle of demerger to start with is to continue to run the businesses under one umbrella, but differently as in separately from a strategic perspective, but not unduly increasing the cost base.

points.point: Asked by Saket Kapoor whether clubbing government-priced bio-fuel with liquor would dilute the IMFL valuation, Rupark defended it as backward integration, quality control and scale.
points.quote: Well, percentage margin is one factor, but the overall profitability and resilience of the business also improves.

points.point: First debt allocation disclosed: Rs 1,200 cr long-term debt split roughly Rs 500 cr to chemicals and Rs 700 cr to liquor, with annual repayments of Rs 150-160 cr (spirits) and Rs 90 cr (chemicals).
points.quote: Just to brief you as of now position, we are having about INR 1,200 crores long-term debt in the books of the company, out of which about INR 500 crores will go to the Chemical division and INR 700 crores will go to the liquor division.

points.point: Rupark restated the rationale and the exact clustering — spirits with ethanol/bio-fuel into IGL Spirits, chemicals with the Clariant JV, Ennature with biopolymers.
points.quote: The idea is that different investors have different appetites for different kind of businesses.

points.point: Growth capex was explicitly deferred to the post-demerger entities; FY26 limited to rollover and Rs 40-50 cr maintenance capex.
points.quote: And after the demerger, the separate companies will think over the CapEx.

points.point: Investor pushback: a long-term shareholder challenged unlocking value by demerging a unit whose net margin had fallen from ~33% (2021) to ~2.4%.
points.quote: We are planning to unlock shareholder value by demerging our business units when there is extreme degrowth in that business.

points.point: Entity-level debt restated: of about Rs 1,400 cr long-term debt, Rs 600 cr to India Glycols and Rs 800 cr to IGL Spirits, with the Rs 467 cr raise plus Rs 180 cr scheduled repayment cutting both proportionately.
points.quote: INR 600 crores in India Glycols and INR 800 crores in IGL Spirits.

points.point: The Rs 467 cr preferential issue at Rs 915/share to promoters, friends and relatives was earmarked entirely for debt reduction ahead of the split.
points.quote: So, this is the update, and the money which whatever we will receive out of this preferential will be utilized for the reduction of the term loan.

points.point: Rupark tied the restructuring to the broader strategy of focusing on bio-based ingredients and consumer/lifestyle value capture.
points.quote: And one of the outcomes of that is in the last few years and now once again, how we've been reorganizing and restructuring our businesses to bring the necessary focus.

points.point: Rating agencies had placed IGL on watch-list because of the demerger; no upgrade (and hence no full benefit of the Rs 582 cr debt reduction) until completion.
points.quote: So, you will not find the rating improvement till our demerger happens.

points.point: Capex remained gated on the demerger even after the Rs 467 cr raise and planned FY26 closing term debt of about Rs 1,100 cr.
points.quote: Apart from this, we are not having any big size capex. And any capex will be undertaken only after the demerger.

points.point: Rupark argued the chemicals business (FY26 net revenue Rs 1,203 cr, down 10.4%, EBIT Rs 141 cr, margin 11.7%) is understated and needs in-house cost streamlining and dedicated focus.
points.quote: Now, there is, if you look at EBITDA without adjusting the other income and probably some streamlining that is required in-house, we will start to see that the quality of the Chemicals business is probably going to be better than this going forward.

points.point: Anand said the contracted sale of a further 24% of the Clariant JV in FY29 would fund term-loan repayment and leave the chemicals entity debt-free.
points.quote: So, in '28-'29, I'm hopeful that the Chemical business will be totally debt-free.

points.point: Investors were tracking the NCLT timetable; management expected the sanction order around 21 May/early June 2026, then ROC filing.
points.quote: 21st May, we are hopeful that we will get the order for the demerger of the division.

points.point: Plan change: the board on 16 May 2025 dropped the amalgamation of promoter vehicle Kashipur Holdings Limited and pursued the demerger alone, with appointed date 1 April 2026.
points.quote: The earlier proposal for the amalgamation of KHL into the Company will no longer form part of the Scheme being pursued.

points.point: The 1 September 2026 news release stated the benefit as dedicated focus and better oversight and resource allocation for each of the three companies.
points.quote: Each company will have a dedicated focus, enabling improved management oversight and more efficient allocation of resources towards growth.

points.point: The release made the capital-allocation argument explicit — each entity sizing its own capital and investment needs.
points.quote: In addition, each company will be able to manage its capital, investments and resources based on its specific business requirements, thereby enabling more efficient utilisation of capital.

points.point: Share entitlement: 1 IGL Spirits share for every 1 IGL share, and 1 Ennature Bio Pharma share for every 3 IGL shares (6,70,26,765 and 2,23,42,255 shares of Rs 5 allotted on 8 September 2026).
points.quote: Resulting Company 2 shall issue 1 (One) Equity Share having face value of INR 5 (Indian Rupees Five) each, to the shareholders of Demerged Company holding 1 (One) Equity Share of INR 5 (Indian Rupees Five) each.

points.point: Near-unanimous stakeholder approval at the 24 March 2026 court-convened meetings; the secured creditors' meeting was dispensed with on 95.46% consent, and unsecured creditors voted 36/36, 100% by value.
points.quote: it appearing from the said reports that the Scheme of Arrangement has been approved by the requisite majority of Equity Shareholders (4,42,48,625 votes in favour out of 4,42,48,626, with 1 vote against)

points.point: Completion: ROC filing on 1 September 2026 made the scheme effective, Q1 FY27 pro-forma net revenues being India Glycols Rs 345 cr, IGL Spirits Rs 694 cr and Ennature Bio Pharma Rs 90 cr; both new entities began trading 4 November 2026.
points.quote: Accordingly, in terms of the provisions of the Clause 24 of the Scheme, the “Effective Date” of the Scheme is 1st September, 2026 and the Scheme contemplating the Demerger has now become effective and the Resulting Companies have ceased to be the subsidiaries of the Company.

rationale.what_management_expects: Chemicals: cost streamlining, higher-value performance chemicals, improving EBIT (11.7% FY26), JV stake sale funding a debt-free unit by FY29. IGL Spirits: premiumisation toward ~22% EBIT margins on captive ENA, geographic and CSD expansion. Ennature: branded nutraceuticals margin recovery. All three: dedicated focus, own capital allocation, focused investors, value unlock.
rationale.gaps: Never quantified: value unlock, standalone corporate costs, inter-company ENA/EO transfer pricing, shared Kashipur utilities, debt-covenant consents; no investor, lender or partner was named as having requested it.

judge.what_is_spun: Power Evacuation Business (substation/evacuation infrastructure) demerged from Inox Green into Inox Renewable Solutions Limited
demerged_business_names: Resco Global Wind Services Limited (formerly name of resulting company)
judge.reason: Segregation of distinct business verticals with different risks, investors and lenders; consolidation of Power Evacuation into IRSL to unlock value; establish IGESL as pure-play O&M player; two focused listed entities
judge.insiders: Inox Wind Limited, promoter/holding company, directly holds 51.13% of Inox Green and receives mirror IRSL shares; directors/KMP hold only token stakes (Bindu Saxena 12,640; Sanjeev Jain 3,362). No separate incentive disclosed.
judge.hidden_value: Demerger strips ~Rs 1,000 crore gross block and Rs 50-55 crore annual depreciation from Inox Green, lifting profit, ROE/ROCE; parent keeps ~50%-margin O&M with Rs 700 crore tax shield. IRSL carries listed NCDs, secured/unsecured debt and a Rs 96.80 crore tax demand.
judge.selling_pressure_why: Only 122 IRSL shares per 1,000 held: tiny 4,89,82,030-share float, newly listed EPC/evacuation business in a different line from O&M
judge.listing_timeline: On 24th August 2026 IRSL allotted 4,89,82,030 shares and "is taking necessary steps ... for obtaining the listing and trading approvals for the said equity shares from the Stock Exchanges"; on 29 May 2026 management said "IRSL will be automatically listed on the stock exchange post receipt of all the approvals"; on 13 February 2026 they said post-NCLT approval "it is 1 to 1-1/2 month process for the listing of the company".
judge.read_next: IRSL listing/trading approval and its balance sheet: Rs 96.80 crore AY2023-24 tax demand, secured/unsecured debt, accumulated losses
judge.quote: 122 equity shares of IRSL (face value Rs. 10/- each) shall be issued for every 1,000 equity shares (face value Rs. 10/- each) held in Inox Green Energy Services Limited.
