rationale.rationale: Triveni Engineering & Industries (TEIL) is carving out its Power Transmission Business (PTB) — the Mysuru high-speed/turbo gearbox and incubating defence-products business — into Triveni Power Transmission Ltd (TPTL), a then-wholly-owned subsidiary, via a composite scheme that also amalgamates the 61.77%-owned listed subsidiary Sir Shadi Lal Enterprises (SSEL) into TEIL; management's stated purpose, repeated almost verbatim across calls, is 'value unlocking' and later 'to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies'. The implicit problem is the conglomerate mix: PTB is the one segment with predictable, high-quality economics (FY25 turnover +27%, PBIT ₹126.8 crore, +18.4%, PBIT margin >34%; H1 FY26 PBIT ~36%, one quarter at 41%; Suresh Taneja in Jun 2026: 'we have been maintaining about 35% PBIT'), while sugar and distillery are price- and policy-regulated commodity businesses whose margins collapsed in FY25 on a 69 bps gross-recovery fall, red rot/pest damage, ₹300/MT UP cane-price increases and frozen ethanol prices — exactly the asymmetry investor Bharat Shah (ASK) pressed management on in Feb 2025. Separation also funds and showcases PTB's own growth programme: board-approved capex in three tranches totalling ₹340 crore (₹231 crore spent to 31 Mar 2026, of which ₹78 crore on the defence facility), lifting gears capacity from ~₹400 crore to ~₹700 crore of output by September 2026, against a global high-speed/turbo gear market management sized at '$650-$700-odd million', a Swiss subsidiary (Triveni Power Transmission GmbH, bought by TPTL in FY26), AVL qualifications with global OEMs, and exports targeted at 'more than half' of original-equipment sales; Tarun Sawhney said TPTL is 'armed with sufficient cash flows and a balance sheet to be able to incur all of this CapEx and OpEx and more'. Crucially, TEIL deliberately retains ~30% of TPTL rather than a clean split — investor Resham Jain (DSP) challenged this as re-importing a holdco discount — because, per Sawhney, the defence business is being incubated and 'in establishing pre-qualifications (PQs) and the ability to be able to quote, there are balance sheet considerations that even from a Group perspective that are very, very important', plus the view that the earlier Triveni Turbine separation 'was actually quite a positive one'. Preparation was operational as well as legal: systems, CRM, SAP HANA/ERP migration, digital-twin and smart-factory work so TPTL could 'hit the ground sprinting' as a standalone, with separate board meetings and separate earnings calls promised for TEIL and TPTL from Q1 FY27. The scheme was approved by shareholders/creditors in December 2025, sanctioned by NCLT Allahabad (orders 7 and 18 May 2026), effective 19 May 2026, with scheme appointed date 1 April 2025 and demerger appointed date 1 April 2026; shareholders receive 1 TPTL share of ₹2 for every 3 TEIL shares of ₹1, and ICRA reaffirmed TEIL at AA+ Stable, 'lifting it from its previous under watch status'. Water/wastewater, sugar, distillery and IMIL/IMFL stay with TEIL, which keeps the residual cash flows the board said it would run workshops on to evaluate deployment options.
rationale.evolution: The composite scheme was approved by TEIL's board on 10 December 2024 and first discussed on the Feb 5, 2025 call, where Sawhney framed it purely as 'value unlocking', defended the ~30% retained stake on defence pre-qualification/balance-sheet grounds against Resham Jain's holdco-discount objection, and guided to NCLT approval 'by the end of this calendar year'. Through May 28, 2025 and Jul 30, 2025 the plan was unchanged but stuck at SEBI ('following up continuously with SEBI', possibly '+30-odd days'), with separation still expected in Q4 FY26/early CY2026, while Resham Jain asked for granular PTB disclosure 'given that this is going to get separately listed' and the board began workshops on what residual TEIL would do with its cash. By Nov 7, 2025 the stock exchanges had issued observation letters (BSE 7 Aug, NSE 11 Aug 2025), NCLT-convened stakeholder meetings were set for late November/early December, and TPTL had acquired the Swiss entity; on Feb 2, 2026 management added the second rationale — 'to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies' — reported December 2025 shareholder/creditor approval, a February NCLT hearing, and said 'the next time we speak in all probability, this will be two separate companies'. On Jun 4, 2026 Sawhney confirmed NCLT approval (19 May 2026 effective date), the two record dates, restored AA+ rating and guided to TPTL listing 'by the end of August' with separate calls for both entities; in fact the demerger record date was 22 July 2026 and TPTL's 10,47,54,338 shares only began trading on BSE/NSE on 12 October 2026, with cost of acquisition split 86.60% TEIL / 13.40% TPTL.

points.point: First call after the 10 December 2024 announcement; the scheme is presented as two linked steps — amalgamating the 61.77%-held listed subsidiary SSEL into TEIL and vesting the Power Transmission Business undertaking into wholly-owned Triveni Power Transmission Ltd — with value unlocking as the stated board motive.
points.quote: I also wanted to provide an update on the Scheme, as you're all aware, this is in conjunction with value unlocking that the Board of Directors has felt very important.

points.point: Resham Jain (DSP) objected that TEIL retaining ~30% of TPTL recreates the Triveni Turbines-style holdco discount and is not a clean value unlock — the clearest instance of an investor shaping the debate on structure.
points.quote: It seems that Triveni Engineering will still be holding 30% stake even after demerger. So why such structure, if the value unlocking has to happen, it should have been a clean structure where Triveni would not be holding anything otherwise, the same Holdco discount will be applicable to the Power Transmission business once it gets demerged.

points.point: Sawhney justified the retained stake on two grounds: the Triveni Turbines precedent was positive, and the co-located defence business needs group balance-sheet backing to win pre-qualifications and bid — i.e. a clean split would handicap defence.
points.quote: The second and very, very important is because we are incubating a Defence business, which we have large aspirations for. In establishing pre-qualifications (PQs) and the ability to be able to quote, there are balance sheet considerations that even from a Group perspective that are very, very important to allow us to be in contention.

points.point: Bharat Shah (ASK Investment Managers) framed the underlying investor problem the separation addresses: PTB is the one predictable, compounding business while the rest of the portfolio produces erratic outcomes, making long-term valuation of the whole impossible.
points.quote: If you look at the composition of various businesses that we are in, barring the Power Transmission business, which is relatively more robust, predictable economics and predictable outcomes over a period of time, brick-by-brick being built.

points.point: The same board meeting approved an incremental ₹60 crore capex to lift gears capacity from ~₹400 crore to ₹700 crore by September 2026, sized against a global high-speed/turbo gear market of roughly $650-700 million — the growth case the separate listing is meant to fund and surface.
points.quote: The Board has confidence that we need ₹700 crore worth of capacity as we start off 2026-27.

points.point: PTB's FY25 numbers were the evidence for separate valuation: turnover +27%, PBIT ₹126.8 crore (+18.4%), PBIT margin above 34%, order booking over ₹475 crore and record Q4 revenue of almost ₹140 crore — growth without margin dilution.
points.quote: And the PBIT grew by 18.4% to ₹126.8 crore with PBIT margins in excess of 34%, which is a very much in line with our long-term average.

points.point: Resham Jain asked for far more granular PTB disclosure — customers, industry mix — explicitly because it will be separately listed; management accepted, showing investor demand driving pre-separation transparency.
points.quote: So I would request maybe if you can start giving more colour on the Power Transmission business from like what kind of customers you are targeting ?

points.point: The plan was unchanged in substance but stalled at SEBI, with timing guided to Q1 of the next calendar year / Q4 FY26 and possible slippage of about 30 days; separately the board said it would run workshops on how residual TEIL would deploy its cash flows post-demerger.
points.quote: We are still awaiting regulatory approvals. We're following up continuously with SEBI.

points.point: Stock-exchange approvals were in hand and the NCLT process had begun with stakeholder meetings scheduled for late November/early December 2025; in parallel TPTL acquired 100% of Triveni Power Transmission GmbH (Switzerland), building the export engine inside the entity being demerged.
points.quote: The proposed scheme has been approved by the stock exchanges, and the process is obtaining approval of NCLT.

points.point: Management for the first time stated both objectives together — unlocking value and driving operational efficiencies — and confirmed December 2025 shareholder/creditor approval with a further NCLT hearing in February 2026.
points.quote: Lastly, with respect to the proposed scheme of amalgamation of SSEL and the demerger of the Power Transmission business to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies, the scheme has been approved by shareholders of creditors, this was in December of 2025.

points.point: Standalone readiness was being built deliberately — skills, systems, CRM, smart factory and SAP HANA migration — so TPTL could run as an independent company with TEIL-level efficiency from day one.
points.quote: A lot of systems work is being done as we speak to let them hit the ground sprinting, frankly speaking, and have the same kind of efficiencies that we've had at Triveni Engineering and any of the other businesses that the company has run.

points.point: Scheme effective 19 May 2026 after NCLT approval; appointed date 1 April 2025 for the scheme and 1 April 2026 for the demerger, with the SSEL record date on 3 June 2026 and TPTL listing then guided for end-August 2026.
points.quote: I'm delighted to inform you that the composite scheme of arrangement is effective from the 19th of May, 2026 after the approval of the NCLT.

points.point: A lender/rating-agency consequence: ICRA removed the rating watch tied to the scheme and reaffirmed TEIL at AA+ Stable, which management called a return to Triveni Engineering's historically highest rating.
points.quote: I am very proud to announce that post the scheme having been approved, ICRA has reaffirmed our long-term credit rating as AA+ Stable, lifting it from its previous under watch status.

points.point: TPTL carries its own funding capacity for the ₹340 crore capex programme (₹231 crore incurred to 31 March 2026, ₹78 crore of it on the defence facility; ~₹109 crore left, ~40% of it defence), which supports ~₹700 crore of gears output excluding defence.
points.quote: Of course, as power transmission migrates into Triveni Power Transmission Limited, the company is armed with sufficient cash flows and a balance sheet to be able to incur all of this CapEx and OpEx and more.

points.point: Independent listing is now named as the explicit strategic objective of the Power Transmission segment, alongside export-led growth, the Swiss subsidiary, oil-and-gas pump/compressor qualifications and compressor test rigs.
points.quote: Within the Power Transmission Business, our strategic push to clearly move towards, of course, the independent listing of TPTL.

points.point: Post-separation governance was spelled out: separate Q1 FY27 board meetings, separate published results and separate earnings calls for TEIL and TPTL — the disclosure separation investors had asked for since mid-2025.
points.quote: I do want to assure all those on this call and other investors of Triveni Engineering that the end of August 2026 will probably be after our Q1 board meetings for TEIL as well as TPTL, and we fully intend on publishing our results in the papers and on our web pages and holding earnings conference calls for both companies so that our shareholders are fully knowledgeable about the progress that the businesses have made in Q1 of FY27.

points.point: Asked directly whether demerger changes PTB margins, Group CFO Suresh Taneja pointed to continuity of the ~35% PBIT profile, with FY26 order book just under ₹500 crore (+25%) and aftermarket at ~40% of gears sales supporting it.

rationale.rationale: On the evidence supplied, Poly Medicure is not separating a business — nothing in the seven earnings/acquisition call transcripts or the one filing announces or discusses a demerger, spin-off, slump sale, hive-off or carve-out of any division, and no scheme of arrangement is on record. The structural direction management describes is the exact opposite: inbound acquisition and consolidation into one entity. In FY26 the company bought PendraCare (Netherlands, interventional cardiology guiding/diagnostic catheters; CY24 revenue €9.9m, EBITDA €1.4m, 74% gross margin; 90% stake for €11m equity plus €3.2m intra-group loans, ~1.8x EV/revenue and 13x EV/EBITDA, remaining 10% to be bought in 2030 off CY29 EBITDA), Citieffe (Bologna, Italy, trauma and extremities orthopaedics; CY24 revenue €17.3m, EBITDA €3.1m, ~90% gross margin; €18.8m equity plus €4.2m shareholder loan plus €8m debt = ~€31m EV, ~10x EBITDA) and Medyneo in Brazil (a shell with ANVISA and import licences, ~$40,000, bought to save 18–24 months of registration time). Himanshu Baid's framing on 25 May 2026 was explicitly integrative — 'in 1 or 2 years, we'll make these 3 businesses into a single global platform' — with cross-selling both ways, Indian R&D supporting Europe, some manufacturing eventually shifted to India, and subsidiary EBITDA guided from 12–14% to 18–20% over 2–3 years. The core Infusion Therapy business is being de-weighted in mix (65% historically, 57% of Q4 FY25, 50% of Q4 FY26, with Renal ~11%) but is expressly retained and used to fund the new verticals: 'this doesn't mean that we are not focusing on our core infusion business, which is generating significant profits, enabling us to invest into these new high-growth areas.' The only deliberate exit described is channel-level, not structural — shrinking government/tender business from ~10–12% of domestic revenue to a target 6–7% because of L1 pricing and state payment delays — and the only facility decision reversed was dropping the planned Jaipur plant in favour of land at YEIDA. The single filing (5 Nov 2026) is a routine board-approved refresh of five governance policies; 'demerger' appears in it only as a generic Schedule III disclosure category, not as a transaction. Financial context given: FY26 standalone revenue ₹1,662 crore (+4%), consolidated ₹1,875 crore (+12.3%), standalone EBITDA ₹446 crore at 26.8%, consolidated cash ₹842 crore, FY26 capex ₹296 crore, FY27 guidance ₹1,900–1,950 crore standalone and ₹2,300–2,400 crore consolidated; no part of that guidance is attributed to any separation.
rationale.evolution: Across the window the corporate-structure thread runs only one way — toward acquiring and absorbing. On 7 May 2025 management said only that it was on a 'constant lookout' for technology M&A and refused to name a vertical; on 8 Aug 2025 it added a wholly owned Brazil subsidiary and two CDMO contracts; the dedicated calls of 4 Sep 2025 (PendraCare) and 25 Sep 2025 (Citieffe) set out the two acquisitions, closed 23 Sep and 6 Nov 2025 respectively and reported in the 10 Nov 2025 call as adding ~₹280 crore of annualised revenue. By 6 Feb 2026 the language was integration and 'a fundamental upgrade of our business model' (not a split), and by 25 May 2026 it was explicit consolidation of three businesses into one platform plus the Medyneo bolt-on. At no point — including the 5 Nov 2026 filing — does any separation, demerger or divestment of a Polymed business appear.

points.point: Management's stated structural intent is to merge, not separate: Polymed standalone plus PendraCare plus Citieffe are to be run as one global platform, with cross-selling, shared R&D and procurement synergies.
points.quote: I think in 1 or 2 years, we'll make these 3 businesses into a single global platform for growth.

points.point: Despite Infusion Therapy falling from 57% of Q4 FY25 revenue to 50% in Q4 FY26, Baid insists it stays in-house at ~50% of mix, citing ~11% global IV-catheter share — i.e. no carve-out of the legacy business.
points.quote: Again, that is our core, core, core business.

points.point: The acquired entities are to be margin-upgraded inside the group (12–14% EBITDA now, 18–20% in 2–3 years) through Indian engineering, global supply chain and partial manufacturing transfer — the opposite of separating them out.
points.quote: All that will help us in the long run will help us to -- see, currently, these companies will operate, let's say, around 12% to 14% margin.

points.point: The 'transition' repeatedly described is a product/technology mix shift from low-tech to cardiology, critical care and orthopaedics — explicitly funded by the retained infusion business, not a legal separation of either part.
points.quote: Having said that, this doesn't mean that we are not focusing on our core infusion business, which is generating significant profits, enabling us to invest into these new high-growth areas.

points.point: The only business management says it is deliberately exiting is the government/tender channel (~10–12% of domestic revenue, degrowth of 18% in Q3 FY26, target 6–7%) on price and receivables grounds — a channel de-emphasis, not a separation.
points.quote: And deliberately, we are reducing our government business exposure as the prices are lower in government business.

points.point: The two European deals were presented as additive to the existing business, adding roughly ₹280 crore of annualised revenue, with integration already begun — no mention of any offsetting disposal.
points.quote: With these two acquisitions, we will add around close to Rs. 280 crores of revenue to our existing business on an annual basis.

points.point: On the Citieffe call, the stated M&A doctrine is to stay inside medical devices and its adjacencies and to pause and absorb — Citieffe adds orthopaedics on top of cardiology, critical care and renal, with no suggestion of separating any vertical.
points.quote: I think on the M&A strategy, which we have said in the past that we want to obviously stick to the medical devices and we'll stick to the adjacencies of the medical devices.

points.point: Even manufacturing is kept where it is: Rahul Gautam rejects moving Citieffe's Bologna production to India because customers value Made-in-Europe, limiting change to outsourcing parts of processes.
points.quote: We have currently no such plans.

points.point: PendraCare was framed as a bolt-on platform to globalise Polymed's own cardiology products (DES clinical registry of 2,000 patients, EU/FDA approvals), targeting €3–4m of incremental group EBITDA synergies and ~€25m revenue by 2030.
points.quote: This is very much part of our core strategy to grow into cardiology, something which we have been doing over the last 12 to 18 months.

points.point: At the start of the window the only structural plan disclosed was inorganic expansion funded by the Aug-2024 QIP cash (~₹1,100 crore liquidity, ~₹500 crore earmarked for organic capex); no divestment or demerger was contemplated.
points.quote: Of course, we are looking at some new opportunities in M&A side and as soon as we finalize something, we will definitely get back to you with proper details.

points.point: There is no scheme of arrangement in the record. The sole filing (5 Nov 2026) is a board-approved refresh of five governance policies; 'demerger' appears in it only inside the boilerplate Schedule III list of disclosable event categories.
points.quote: Acquisition(s) (including agreement to acquire), Scheme of Arrangement (amalgamation/ merger/ demerger/restructuring), sale or disposal of any unit(s), division(s), whole or substantially the whole of the undertaking(s) or subsidiary of the listed entity, sale of stake in the associate company of the listed entity or any other restructuring.

rationale.what_management_expects: Nothing — no separation was proposed. The only structural expectations stated are for acquisitions: PendraCare and Citieffe moving from 12–14% to 18–20% EBITDA over 2–3 years, €3–4 million of group synergy EBITDA, Citieffe revenue doubling in five years, standalone EBITDA 25–27% versus consolidated 23–25%, and three businesses run as one global platform.
rationale.gaps: No call or filing mentions a demerger, spin-off, slump sale or carve-out, so no rationale, perimeter, swap ratio, or investor/lender/partner demand for one is explained.

segments.measure_notes: The pages carry only segment-wise Total Operating Revenue (sales) by product segment — Infusion Therapy, Orthopaedics, Renal, Cardiology, Others, Export/Other Operating Revenue. No profit line of any kind (segment result / EBIT / EBITDA / PBT / PAT) is disclosed per segment. Revenue appears to be external sales; inter-segment treatment is not stated, and the presentations note 'Reclassification have been made where considered necessary'. The annual report (Annual Report 2023 — page 174) explicitly states the Group has NO reportable segments under Ind AS 108, so no segment assets, results or margins exist in the financial statements. Because the business being separated is not identified in any of these pages, no segment's figures can be attributed to it; the only totals available (e.g. FY26 1,875.3; Q2 FY27 580.5) are consolidated company figures, not the separating business.

rationale.rationale: The separation is the demerger of the power-evacuation / substation (common infrastructure) business out of Inox Wind's listed O&M subsidiary Inox Green Energy Services Ltd (IGESL, ~56% held by IWL, later diluted to 54.78%) and its merger into Inox Renewable Solutions Ltd (IRSL, formerly Resco Global Wind Services, ~88.84% held by IWL), IWL's EPC arm, after which IRSL is automatically listed and Inox Green's shareholders receive 122 IRSL shares for every 1,000 Inox Green shares. The problem management says it fixes: Inox Green's balance sheet carried roughly Rs 1,000 crore of gross block of substations/evacuation assets (84 substations pan-India) that produced only about Rs 10 crore of revenue but around Rs 50-55 crore of annual depreciation, depressing PBT, ROE and ROCE and burying the asset-light ~50%-EBITDA-margin O&M business. Post-demerger Inox Green has virtually no depreciation and negligible finance cost, so PBT equals EBITDA equals cash profit — FY27 EBITDA guided above Rs 600 crore, 'broadly everything' converting to operating cash profit, helped by a ~Rs 700 crore accumulated-loss tax shield. The infrastructure instead lands in IRSL, where the group's EPC capability, in-housed cranes, transformer manufacturing and multi-gigawatt project/land pipeline already sit, and whose value rose after the Sept-2025 CERC amendment allowing hybridisation of existing wind evacuation with solar above 50 MW — giving access to what Devansh Jain called almost 10 GW of plug-and-play infrastructure. Akhil Jindal framed the intent as shareholder choice: investors can hold the O&M business, the infrastructure business, or the whole value chain through Inox Wind, and he said no further corporate action is therefore needed (explicitly refusing to demerge Green or IRSL out of IWL). Value-unlocking is the other stated driver: IRSL raised Rs 175 crore in Sept 2025 at a valuation of ~Rs 7,400 crore, and IWL has since sold small IRSL stakes to group parties (91.90%→88.84% for Rs 173.5 crore; then →87.98% for ~Rs 50 crore). Investors and analysts (Vishal Singh, Pradyumna Choudhary, Hansal Thakker, Prit Nagersheth, Pradeep Motwani) repeatedly pressed on timing and on whether minority shareholders would see value unlocked; the scheme also required and received approval from equity shareholders, warrant holders and secured and unsecured creditors (1 Nov 2025) — no lender or partner demand was cited as the trigger.
rationale.evolution: IGESL's board approved the scheme on 13 Nov 2024; the earliest discussion in these transcripts is the Feb 2025 call (31 Jan 2025), where Manish Garg confirmed board approval and filing with NSE/BSE after an investor asked when 'the demerger of that EPC subsidiary' would happen. By the Sep 2025 call (1 Sep 2025) exchange no-objections were in, the scheme was filed at NCLT Ahmedabad with approval guided in 2-3 quarters, IRSL had raised Rs 175 crore at ~Rs 7,400 crore, and Akhil Jindal reframed the logic as giving shareholders a choice of which business to own while ruling out any further demerger out of IWL. On the Nov 2025 call (14 Nov 2025) shareholder and creditor approvals were announced and Devansh Jain said the demerger and IRSL listing would 'unlock substantial value'; on the Feb 2026 call (13 Feb 2026) it was in final NCLT hearings with the impact quantified (only ~Rs 10 crore revenue out, ~Rs 50 crore depreciation out, 84 substations to be merged). NCLT sanctioned it on 12 March 2026, effective 4 May 2026, and on the Jun 2026 call (29 May 2026) management confirmed the Rs 1,000 crore gross block and Rs 50-55 crore depreciation were eliminated, with listing 1-2 months away, while declining to give IRSL's financials until it is demerged.

points.point: First disclosure in these calls: the IGESL board had approved demerging the substation business and the scheme was filed with NSE/BSE, to be followed by an NCLT filing; an investor had asked when the 'EPC subsidiary' demerger would happen.
points.quote: So the Board approval for a demerger of the substation business from Inox Green has already been taken in the last Board meeting, the scheme has been filed with NSE and BSE, and we are waiting for their approval.

points.point: Akhil Jindal explained the mechanics — infrastructure and connectivity assets move out of Inox Green into Resco/IRSL, which then lists automatically, with Inox Green shareholders receiving IRSL shares.
points.quote: Under that, there would have been an automatic listing of Resco. And to that extent, the shareholders of INOX Green would be getting the shares of INOX Resco also.

points.point: Asked whether IGESL and IRSL would later be demerged to IWL shareholders, Jindal said the point of separating these businesses was to let shareholders pick which business to own, so no further corporate action is needed.
points.quote: As management, we have provided enough window for a shareholder to be present where he wants to be. And I think that was the intention of separating these businesses.

points.point: The balance-sheet rationale quantified: ~Rs 1,000 crore gross block leaves Inox Green and ~Rs 50-55 crore of annual depreciation is eliminated, lifting PBT and improving ROE/ROCE.
points.quote: Once the scheme is approved by the NCLT, the gross block of around INR1,000 crores will be off our balance sheet and subsequently the depreciation of approximately INR50 crores to INR55 crores annually will be eliminated, thereby increasing the PBT by that amount.

points.point: IRSL was independently valued shortly before the demerger, and the CERC hybridisation amendment (allowing existing wind evacuation infra to be shared with solar above 50 MW) multiplied the value of the infrastructure being moved into it.
points.quote: We have recently raised INR175 crores at Inox Renewable Solutions at a valuation of approximately INR7,400 crores.

points.point: Devansh Jain sized the infrastructure asset that IRSL will house post-hybridisation as near-unique in India.
points.quote: I think it gives us access to almost 10 gigawatts of plug and play infrastructure across wind and solar , which is huge.

points.point: On receiving shareholder and creditor approvals, Sanjeev Agarwal set out the two-sided benefit: IRSL lists as Inox Wind's EPC arm, Inox Green sheds the depreciation on the demerged asset blocks.
points.quote: This will add value for both Inox Wind, with subsequent listing of Inox Renewable solution as an EPC arm of Inox Wind, and Inox Green with elimination of depreciation on demergers of the asset blocks

points.point: Devansh Jain stated the headline objective as value unlocking for both listed entities.
points.quote: I believe that the de-merger and subsequent listing of Inox Renewable Solutions will unlock substantial value for both Inox Wind and Inox Green.

points.point: Management quantified the asymmetry that makes the separation accretive for Inox Green: barely any revenue leaves, but the depreciation does.
points.quote: So post the demerger, as we have clarified on the multiple cores, there would be a very limited amount of revenue in the range of INR 10 odd crore will get out of the balance sheet. And around INR 50 odd crores of depreciation will go out from the balance sheet.

points.point: Mathusudhana described the scale of the infrastructure being consolidated — 84 substations pan-India — and claimed further unquantified synergy value plus a connectivity advantage no competitor has.
points.quote: And like merging 84 substations across India, it will be a huge exercise. And that will unlock synergy value, which we will reveal in the future.

points.point: Post-NCLT confirmation that the benefit has crystallised in Inox Green's accounts, with the residual step being administrative before IRSL's automatic listing (guided at 1-2 months).
points.quote: With this gross block of approximately INR1,000 crores has been eliminated from Inox Green's balance sheet. And subsequently, the annual depreciation of approximately INR50 crores to INR55 crores has been eliminated, thereby increasing the profitability.

points.point: Devansh Jain placed the IRSL demerger in a sequence of value-creating separations, after the Inox Green spin-off, while shrugging off the share-price criticism from minority holders.
points.quote: We've spun off Inox Green, which has created tremendous value. We're on the verge of demerging Inox Renewable Solutions, which we hope will create tremendous value.

points.point: Management refused to give any top-line or EBITDA profile for the business being separated until the demerger is complete.
points.quote: We cannot say at this point in time. I think once that demerged, we'll elucidate more plans. At this point in time, it's part and parcel of Inox Wind.

points.point: Post-demerger Inox Green is positioned as a near-pure cash generator: no depreciation, no finance cost and a ~Rs 700 crore loss tax shield, with FY27 EBITDA guided above Rs 600 crore.
points.quote: Out of INR600 crore fees, broadly everything will be converted into the operating cash flow. As such, there will be no depreciation, no finance cost, and we have a tax shield up to INR700 crore of losses.

points.point: The filings record the legal path: IGESL board approval 13 Nov 2024 for demerger of the Power Evacuation business into IRSL under sections 230-232; approval by equity shareholders, warrant holders and secured and unsecured creditors on 1 Nov 2025; NCLT Ahmedabad sanction on 12 March 2026; effective 4 May 2026.
points.quote: On March, 12, 2026, Hon'ble National Company law Tribunal, Ahmedabad (NCLT) sanctioned the Scheme.

points.point: Consideration mechanics and the dilution of IWL's stake in the resulting company are specified in the filings.
points.quote: Pursuant to the Scheme, 122 equity share in the Resulting company for every 1000 share held in the demerged company to be issued to the shareholders as on the record date.

points.point: The demerger itself reduces Inox Wind's holding in IRSL, though control is retained under Ind AS 110.
points.quote: Furhter, due to effect of the demerger scheme between the lnox Renewable Solutions Limited and lnox Green Energy Services Limited as approved by NCLT vide order dated 13 March 2026, the Company shareholding in IRSL is expected to reduced from 88.41% to 79.75%.

rationale.what_management_expects: Inox Green: ~Rs 1,000 cr gross block and ~Rs 50-55 cr annual depreciation gone, higher PBT, sharply better ROE/ROCE, a pure-play ~50%-margin asset-light O&M business whose FY27 EBITDA (>Rs 600 cr) converts almost fully to cash. IRSL: a separately listed EPC/infrastructure arm of Inox Wind holding evacuation infra, cranes, transformers and hybridisation-ready plug-and-play sites. Both: substantial value unlocking.
rationale.gaps: No IRSL standalone revenue, EBITDA, debt or valuation basis disclosed; no explanation of the 122:1,000 share ratio, tax treatment, IRSL's post-listing capital needs, or any lender requirement.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is SBI Funds Management Limited (SBIFM) — SBI Mutual Fund, the bank's asset-management joint venture with Amundi — which SBI is partially separating by listing it, not by demerging it; management repeatedly framed the purpose as "value unlocking" and, in Chairman C.S. Setty's words, "more importantly, value recognition for the industry" (Nov 2025), with SBI General Insurance named alongside AMC as the other listing candidate. The driver management gave was that SBI's own stock does not reflect the conglomerate's worth: Setty called SBI's valuation "a conundrum, considering our return on equity and growth metrics" (Nov 2025, with ROE 19.7%–20.68% and ROA >1% through FY26), and the same theme runs through the hidden-value argument on strategic holdings — of the group's ~7.3% NSE stake he said "the moment NSE gets listed, the whole shareholding by SBI will be available as reserve to us to mark to market" (May 2026). Explicitly NOT a capital-need story at first: in Nov 2025 Setty said "these two companies do not require capital at this juncture. Neither the parent requires because we just raised Rs. 25,000 crores" (the July 2025 QIP, India's largest, 4.5x oversubscribed on a >Rs. 1.1 trillion book, >60% cross-border), which is why timing was left to "respective boards"; by May 2026 the rationale had hardened into a capital one — the listing "will result in capital augmentation, CET-1" on top of CAR already up 115bps to 15.4%. The structure confirms it is monetisation, not a fix for the business: the IPO is a pure offer for sale (no fresh issue), SBI offering 6.3007% and JV partner Amundi India Holding 3.7006%, total up to 10.0013% / 203,709,239 shares at Rs. 1 face value, so no money reaches SBIFM itself. Management stressed that separation does not break the franchise link — SBIFM stays the country's largest AMC inside the "One SBI" cross-sell engine (a special dividend of ~Rs. 2,200 crore came up to the bank in Q3FY26, cross-sell/CVE income targeted at $1 billion, YONO "deep integration with subsidiary production"), and Setty was explicit that "Mutual fund, we are not fully exiting. So we still have potential to monetize further when market improves" (Feb 2026). The push came from the sell side and retail investors — Sushil Choksey (Indus Equity), Manoj Alimchandani and Kunal Shah (Citigroup) raised monetisation/value-unlocking on four of the five calls, Alimchandani even arguing in Feb 2026 that delaying the IPO five years could fetch three times the market cap — rather than from lenders or regulators; the only regulator-linked nudge cited was the SEBI chairman on NSE's listing. No problem with SBIFM's performance was ever offered as a reason: it was described only as "the largest AMC in the country," contributing Rs. 4,969.09 crore of FY26 total income, just 0.70% of group income.
rationale.evolution: May 2025 had no separation plan at all — only "we will continue to nurture these subsidiaries," while the bank instead took an enabling resolution for Rs. 25,000 crore of its own equity. By Aug 2025 Setty conceded "a couple of candidates for listing, but… there is no sense of urgency," and in Nov 2025 he named them — SBI AMC and SBI General — as the right candidates for "value unlocking" and "value recognition," with boards to set timing; the SBIFM stake-sale approval for 6.3007% followed on 6 Nov 2025 and the DRHP on 19 Mar 2026 (share count restated to 128,334,397 after a bonus issue and ESOP exercises). Feb 2026 added the retained-upside caveat ("we are not fully exiting") and May 2026 re-cast the deal as CET-1 capital augmentation to be completed within FY27. The plan then changed in execution in July 2026: a pre-IPO placement of 28,832,748 shares (1.4156%) to 30 investors at Rs. 574 for Rs. 1,655 crore on 9–10 July cut SBI's offer-for-sale from 6.3007% to 4.8851% (total offer 8.3933%), priced at Rs. 574 with allotment expected 18 July 2026.

points.point: No separation on the table: subsidiaries framed purely as value creators to be retained, while the bank instead took an enabling resolution to raise Rs. 25,000 crore of its own equity.
points.quote: Our subsidiaries are consistently performing well and continue to create significant value for all the stakeholders. We will continue to nurture these subsidiaries and maintain leadership position in the respective businesses.

points.point: First acknowledgement of listing candidates, asked for by Sushil Choksey (Indus Equity Advisors); Setty explicitly de-prioritised it because the Rs. 25,000 crore QIP had just closed.
points.quote: No, as we mentioned that we definitely have a couple of candidates for listing, but the timing is not very… there is no sense of urgency there, I believe.

points.point: The rationale stated in full for the first time, in answer to Choksey on the group's underperforming consolidated value: SBI AMC and SBI General named, with value unlocking and industry recognition of value as the purpose.
points.quote: But among these four major subsidiaries, we definitely would be looking at, as I mentioned several times, SBI AMC and SBI General are right candidates for listing in our stable. It also provides some value unlocking and, more importantly, value recognition for the industry.

points.point: Answering Kunal Shah (Citigroup) on what would trigger the decision, Setty ruled capital need out as a motive for either the subsidiaries or the parent, leaving timing and quantum to the subsidiary boards.
points.quote: I think we need to just look at, see, one is, as I mentioned earlier also, that these two companies do not require capital at this juncture.

points.point: The underlying grievance the separation is meant to address — SBI's own market valuation not tracking its ROE and growth — stated in the Chairman's opening remarks; Ashok Ajmera had quantified it as a Rs. 8.82 lakh crore market cap on Rs. 100 trillion of business versus Rs. 15.14 lakh crore for a Rs. 57 trillion peer.
points.quote: Although the current valuations of SBI are a conundrum, considering our return on equity and growth metrics, we are confident that they will eventually align with our fundamental and operational metrics, the institutionalized nature of our business and our market leadership in the coming years.

points.point: Retained-stake logic: asked by Manoj Alimchandani whether delaying the IPO five years could treble the market cap, Setty defended a partial sale that keeps future upside with SBI.
points.quote: Mutual fund, we are not fully exiting. So we still have potential to monetize further when market improves.

points.point: Why the AMC is worth separating while staying attached: it is already the country's largest AMC, upstreamed a Rs. 2,200 crore special dividend into SBI's Q3FY26 profit, and feeds a cross-sell income stream management targets at $1 billion.
points.quote: If I have to talk about one-off, I think the one item which is a special dividend we have received, around Rs. 2,200 crores from SBI Mutual Fund.

points.point: The rationale shifts to capital: with the AMC listing under way, Setty tied it to CET-1 augmentation supporting credit growth (the bank could already fund ~Rs. 12 trillion of growth, CAR 15.4%, up 115bps YoY).
points.quote: We are also seriously, as you are aware, we have embarked on listing SBI AMC and hopefully in this financial year we will be able to complete, which will result in capital augmentation, CET-1.

points.point: Same hidden-value argument applied to the group's ~7.3% NSE holding, which is not marked to market today — listing is the mechanism that converts unrecognised strategic stakes into reported reserves.
points.quote: But as you mentioned, I think the moment NSE gets listed, the whole shareholding by SBI will be available as reserve to us to mark to market.

points.point: 6 Nov 2025 board approval, restated in the 19 Mar 2026 DRHP filing: a pure offer for sale of up to 10.0013% (203,709,239 shares of Rs. 1 each) — SBI 6.3007% (128,334,397 shares) and JV partner Amundi India Holding 3.7006% (75,374,842 shares). No fresh issue, so no proceeds go to SBIFM.
points.quote: The IPO comprises an offer for sale of up to 128,334,397 Equity Shares (amounting to 6.3007% of the paid-up equity share capital of SBIFML) by State Bank of India, and of up to 75,374,842 Equity Shares (amounting to 3.7006% of the paid-up equity share capital of SBIFML) by Amundi India Holding.

points.point: Plan changed in execution: a pre-IPO secondary placement on 9–10 July 2026 moved 1.4156% of pre-offer capital to 30 investors at the eventual Rs. 574 offer price, raising Rs. 1,655 crore for SBI ahead of the book build.
points.quote: State Bank of India had entered into share purchase agreements each dated July 9, 2026 to sell, in aggregate, 2,88,32,748 equity shares of SBIFM of face value Rs. 1 (one) each ("Equity Shares"), being equivalent to 1.4156% of pre-Offer share capital of SBIFM, to a total of 30 (thirty) investors at Rs. 574.00 per Equity Share, for an aggregate consideration of Rs. 1,655.00 crores.

points.point: The 11 July 2026 addendum cut SBI's offer-for-sale by exactly the pre-IPO quantum, to 4.8851% (total offer 8.3933%); the offer was priced at Rs. 574 on 16 July with a Rs. 54 employee discount and allotment expected on or about 18 July 2026.
points.quote: The size of the offer for sale by the State Bank of India in the IPO has been revised from up to 128,334,397 Equity Shares (amounting to 6.3007% of the paid-up equity share capital of SBIFM) to up to 99,501,649 Equity Shares (amounting to 4.8851% of the paid-up equity share capital of SBIFM).

points.point: Materiality disclosed for the separated business: SBIFM's FY2026 total income of Rs. 4,969.09 crore is 0.70% of group income and its reserves 0.59% of group reserves — the separation is about price discovery, not size.
points.quote: Total income: Rs. 4,969.09 crores (0.70% of Total Income of SBI Group)

rationale.what_management_expects: For SBIFM: a listed market price that recognises India's largest AMC, with SBI retaining control, banca distribution and future monetisation upside. For SBI: value unlocking and "value recognition," CET-1 capital augmentation supporting 13-15% credit growth, hidden reserves surfaced (as with NSE), and valuation converging on >1% ROA and 15%+ through-cycle ROE. No margin or focus benefit was claimed.
rationale.gaps: No valuation target, expected proceeds, CET-1 basis points, or use of funds; no reason the offer was trimmed; Amundi's motive, SBI General's timeline, and post-listing distribution/royalty terms unexplained.

judge.hidden_value: A large NBFC enters a near-empty listed shell: NDL turnover only ₹489.37 lakhs (FY26) versus HLF AUM ~₹59,000 crores and PAT ₹491 crores, HHF ~₹16,000 crores AUM. Official Liquidator flagged overdue loans, near-term repayments and FVTOCI loan valuations.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is Ashok Leyland's vehicle- and housing-finance arm — Hinduja Leyland Finance Ltd (HLFL), together with its subsidiary Hinduja Housing Finance (HHF) — which is being taken out of the Ashok Leyland consolidated structure and given its own listing via a reverse merger (merger by absorption) of HLFL into the already-listed NDL Ventures Ltd (formerly NXTDIGITAL), a near-empty vehicle with FY26 turnover of only ₹489.37 lakhs whose objects were amended to permit NBFC business. Management's first stated reason is valuation: Shenu Agarwal said on the May 2025 call that 'our share price of Ashok Leyland actually does not fully reflect the value that we have in our subsidiaries', and Dheeraj Hinduja closed the same call saying HLF and HHF 'do not really figure as we see it showing a true value in Ashok Leyland shares today, but it will through the listing process unlock this' — 'value unlocking from subsidiaries' was one of the six stated medium-term goals alongside mid-teen EBITDA and 35% MHCV share. The second reason is capital: the finance books were compounding 15–26% a year (HLFL standalone AUM ₹42,000cr on+off book in Nov 2023, ₹44,400cr Dec-24, ₹48,000cr Mar-25, ₹50,430cr Jun-25, ₹52,635cr Sep-25, ₹56,470cr Dec-25, ~₹59,000cr Mar-26; HHF ₹13,400cr to ~₹16,000cr), and Balaji repeatedly said growth was being throttled by capital — 'their business opportunities are restricted with the availability of the cash... the Tier-1 capital is also pretty low where RBI has been insisting on the requirement of more investment in Hinduja Leyland Finance' (Nov 2025), and again in Feb 2026 and Jun 2026 that 'Tier 1 capital sometimes is low compared to the peers.' Ashok Leyland had been plugging that gap itself — ₹200cr into HLFL in Q4 FY25 to meet RBI capital adequacy, with carrying value rising from ~₹60 to ~₹64 per AL share — so a listed platform lets HLFL raise its own growth equity instead: the Scheme rationale says HLFL 'will need growth capital to accelerate growth' and that listing 'will increase the avenues for raising growth capital both from public and interested investors', giving 'greater efficiency in capital raising by the merged entity, and unfettered access to both cash flow generated by the business and external capital raising.' The Scheme adds housekeeping benefits: avoidance of duplicated administrative functions, 'reduction in multiplicity of legal and regulatory compliances and cost', an increase in the transferee's net worth, and 'higher level of corporate governance as required by listed entity.' It is being done as a reverse merger rather than an IPO (swap of 25 NDL shares of ₹10 for every 10 HLFL shares of ₹10), which dilutes Ashok Leyland from 61.12% in HLFL to 59.64% in NDL, with NDL becoming the material listed subsidiary and HLFL dissolved without winding up; metrics cited alongside were PAT ₹160cr/qtr (Q1 FY26) rising to ₹220cr (Q3 FY26), FY26 HLF PAT ₹491cr (+20%) and HHF PAT ₹387cr (+4%), CAR 18.2%, GNPA 3.5%/NNPA 2.1% (FY25) improving to consolidated NNPA ~1.4%.
rationale.evolution: The listing was already in train by the Nov 2023 call, when Gopal Mahadevan said HLFL expected it 'sometime in Q4' and flagged that 'it's a reverse merger, there are a lot of compliance that are to be done additionally other than a standard DRHP'; by Feb 2025 it was 'on track... likely to be concluded by the end of Q1 FY26.' In May 2025 the rationale was reframed explicitly as value unlocking after repeated analyst prodding (Raghunandhan, Pramod Kumar), with management conceding delay pending approvals; Aug 2025 brought RBI's final clearance to merge with NXT Digital and Balaji's long list of remaining steps (valuers, swap ratio, RBI/exchange intimation, ROC, SEBI, EGM, NCLT) with a 'minimum of 2, 3 quarters' guide, while simultaneously disclosing RBI pressure on Tier-1 capital. Nov 2025 said it was 'progressing as per plan', the boards of HLFL and NDL approved the Scheme on 25 November 2025 (appointed date 1 April 2026) — prompting a 27 November 2025 rumour-verification filing correcting a report that Ashok Leyland's own board had approved it — then Feb 2026 admitted 'some initial delays' with approvals now in place, and the Jun 2026 call (Q4 FY26) said it 'should get consummated within this or the next quarter'; shareholders and unsecured creditors approved on 30 July 2026 (100% of HLFL equity by value, 99.99% of unsecured creditors) and NCLT Mumbai sanctioned it on 3 November 2026.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is Cyient's global semiconductor arm, carved out effective 1 April 2025 into Cyient Semiconductors Private Limited (plus Singapore, US, UK, Germany, India and Cayman step-downs) with its own CEO (Suman Narayan), CFO (Ramya Mohan) and board, and reported from Q1 FY26 as a fourth segment alongside DET, DLM and Others, with DET restated to exclude it. Management's stated reason is twofold: the semiconductor model is capital-hungry in a way the engineering-services parent is not — Krishna Bodanapu drew an explicit parallel to Cyient DLM, saying 'the way semiconductor business works is more like a DLM kind of a structure where you do have a higher capital investment, you have design, which takes upfront capital' — and the losses from that investment were being punished inside the listed parent. The numbers they cited: semiconductor FY26 revenue of only $25.7M (Q4 $7.2M, +5% QoQ, fourth straight sequential rise) against a Q4 EBIT loss of $2.8M; group EBIT margin contracted 254bps YoY to 9.5% 'primarily reflecting strategic investments in the semiconductor business'; stated maximum organic investment of $15M, later a committed envelope of 'up to $100 million' of which ~$30M was deployed and ~$70M remained; breakeven slipping from FY27 to 'late FY27, early FY28' to FY28. The problem they said separation solves is valuation: Bodanapu argued the market ascribes 'marginal, if not negative' value to the unit because an EV/EBIT multiple on a loss-making business goes negative, that Cyient shareholders were 'getting penalized' for it, and that continuing to fund it from the parent without establishing its value was 'unfair to shareholders'; against that, turnkey ASIC companies 'have commanded valuation multiples nearly 3x those of semiconductor services firms', rising further with owned IP. The chosen mechanism was an independent capital structure rather than a demerger: Kinetic Technologies ($85M, 82.9% stake, ~250 products, 100+ patents, doubling addressable market to ~$8.5bn) was funded by ~$80M of low-cost Singapore-entity debt on the semiconductor balance sheet, and in May 2026 the unit signed its first external round with EAAA Alternatives (ex-Edelweiss Alternatives) — INR 300 crore as INR 200 crore debt plus INR 100 crore equity at an INR 4,650 crore / $500M post-money equity valuation, roughly 6–7x revenue — closed in Q1 FY27 as $30M of fresh capital. CFO Ramya Mohan framed the structure as giving 'a dedicated capital base', 'real operational discipline and financial separation from the parent', and 'its own long-term optionality that includes potentially a future spin-off path', with debt deliberately preferred over a large equity issue 'to protect it against dilution'. Management was explicit that a comparable clean demerger of Cyient DLM is not contemplated, because of engineering/manufacturing interdependence, and that an own capital structure is itself the value-unlock avenue.
rationale.evolution: The idea surfaced as a structural carve-out announced complete on the 24 Jul 2025 Q1 FY26 call (new four-segment reporting, DET restated ex-semis, start-up framing), and on 16 Oct 2025 Bodanapu first attached a valuation thesis to it — 'create a DLM like story for Cyient's shareholders' plus the 3x ASIC-vs-services multiple argument — while capping organic investment at $15M and promising EBIT-neutrality in FY27. Through 18 Dec 2025 (Kinetic signing) and 22 Jan 2026 the rationale shifted from services to an IP/product company needing sustained R&D, and Kinetic was financed on the subsidiary's own Singapore-entity debt rather than parent cash. On 23 Apr 2026 the Board agreed in principle to explore an external debt-and-equity raise 'for the semiconductor business, which is a stand-alone business and the step-down subsidiary', with Bodanapu naming the real driver — the market ascribes marginal-to-negative value and Cyient shareholders are being penalised — and guiding to only 10–12% initial dilution; by 26 May 2026 the EAAA deal was signed at a $500M post-money valuation with a 'potentially a future spin-off path' named for the first time, and on 23 Jul 2026 the $30M round was reported closed while a clean DLM demerger was declined on the same call.

points.point: Carve-out of the semiconductor business into a separate wholly owned subsidiary with its own leadership and reporting segment is announced as complete, with DET restated to exclude it and the unit framed as a start-up investment.
points.quote: Coming to the highlights for this quarter , It is my pleasure to announce that the Semiconductor business carve out process is completed as planned.

points.point: The unit is described as a separate subsidiary with its own leaders, management and structure, reported under a new four-segment structure (DET, DLM, Semiconductor, Others) precisely because its strategic plans differ.
points.quote: The reason why we've split it out as such is it has very different strategic plans.

points.point: Bodanapu gives the first explicit value-unlock rationale: replicate for shareholders what the separately capitalised, listed Cyient DLM did, including the stated $15M cap on organic investment and FY27 EBIT-neutrality.
points.quote: The opportunity here is to create a DLM like story for Cyient's shareholders through Cyient semiconductors.

points.point: The valuation arbitrage is quantified: turnkey ASIC and IP-owning businesses trade at multiples far above semiconductor services, which is why the unit must be valued on its own.
points.quote: Historically, turnkey ASIC companies have commanded valuation multiples nearly 3x those of semiconductor services firms, and as we gain ownership and control over IP, these multiples increase even further.

points.point: The Kinetic Technologies majority stake (~250 ASSP products, 100+ patents, doubling addressable market to $8.5bn) is justified by the need for sustained R&D and owned IP — the capital-intensity argument for a separate balance sheet.
points.quote: True product differentiation, scalable and profitable growth, and long -term shareholde r value in a semiconductor business is created through sustained investment in R&D, control of the semiconductor ecosystem for cost reduction, and the ownership of intellectual property and patents.

points.point: The Board agrees in principle to an external debt-and-equity fundraise, expressly ring-fenced to the stand-alone step-down subsidiary and driven by its growth and working-capital needs, alongside a INR 720 crore buyback at the parent.
points.quote: I just want to repeat that this is for the semiconductor business, which is a stand -alone business and the step -down subsidiary of Cyient Limited.

points.point: Asked to reconcile a parent buyback with a subsidiary fundraise, Bodanapu states the core problem the separation solves: Cyient shareholders are being penalised for semiconductor losses, so an independent valuation and capital structure is needed.
points.quote: So we want to make sure that the Cyient shareholders are not getting penalized for the performance of Cyient Semiconductor by establishing an independent valuation and an independent capital structure.

points.point: He quantifies the mispricing: on an EV/EBIT basis a loss-making unit carries marginal or negative value inside the listed parent, and funding it from Cyient without establishing value is unfair to shareholders (FY26 semi revenue $25.7M, Q4 EBIT -$2.8M).
points.quote: Now in terms of what percentage of Cyient's market cap now that's for our invest ors to determine, which as I understand it, the value that's attributed to Cyient Semiconductor is marginal, if not negative, because if we just do a simple EBIT multiple, EV to EBIT multiple, then it actually becomes negative because it's a money -losing business.

points.point: On the 26 May 2026 semiconductor financing call, CFO Ramya Mohan answers 'why raise external debt when there is cash with the parent' by naming financial separation, governance and a possible future spin-off as the goal — the clearest statement of intent on the separation.
points.quote: Our goal is to build Cyient Semiconduct ors as a stand -alone business with its own governance, its own accountability and its own long -term optionality that includes potentially a future spin -off path.

points.point: Bodanapu draws the explicit DLM parallel on capital intensity — upfront design capital — as the reason the unit needs its own capital structure and its own investor base, while keeping Cyient's up-to-$100M commitment ($30M already in, ~$70M available) intact.
points.quote: So, we think it's better that Cyient Semiconductor has its own independent capital structure with the kind of investors that want to participate in that capital structure, and we thought this was a good starting point.

points.point: The round is announced as INR 300 crore (INR 200 crore debt plus INR 100 crore equity) at an INR 4,650 crore / $500M post-money equity valuation from EAAA Alternatives, roughly 6–7x revenue, after inbound interest from global funds and strategics; debt was chosen over a large equity issue to limit dilution.
points.quote: But we made a deliberate choice not to issue a large amount of equity at this stage to protect it against dilution and preserve the shareholder value we are working to create.

points.point: The round is confirmed closed at $30M of fresh debt-and-equity capital at the $500M post-money valuation, framed as balance-sheet strength to fund the high-power ASSP development that is depressing operating profitability (breakeven now FY28, with ~$3M/quarter Kinetic amortisation).
points.quote: I am pleased to announce that we have closed this round $30 million of fresh capital raised through a combination of debt and equity is in place.

points.point: Asked by ChrysCapital for a clean DLM demerger to unlock value, Bodanapu declines on grounds of engineering/manufacturing interdependence and says the separate capital structure is itself the value-unlock avenue — defining the limits of the separation strategy.
points.quote: So we believe that the intent of establishing its own capital structure was to provide an avenue towards value unlock.

points.point: The FY26 audited results segment note records the legal restructuring: the global semiconductor business was reorganised under Cyient Semiconductors Private Limited effective 1 April 2025 and pulled out of the DET segment because that is how the CODM now reviews it.
points.quote: Effective April 01, 2025, the Group has reorganised its business structure by restructuring Its global semiconductor business under Cyient Semiconductors Private Limited, Its subsidiaries and an associate.

points.point: The Q2 FY27 filing shows the EAAA instruments landing on the subsidiary: Cyient Semiconductors Singapore issued INR 2,000Mn of 3-year NCDs and INR 1,000Mn of CCPS whose investor exit right forces liability (not equity) classification — evidence of an investor-protected, separable capital structure.
points.quote: The CCPS have fixed conversion terms and exit right on the Company if certain events do not occur within the stipulated period.

rationale.what_management_expects: For Cyient Semiconductors: dedicated long-cycle R&D capital, operational discipline and financial separation, ASSP gross margins of 50–60% versus services, EBIT breakeven in FY28, ASSP rising to 50–55% of mix, and an IP-led valuation (6–7x revenue, $500M) with optionality including a future spin-off. For Cyient: DET margins no longer dragged by semiconductor losses (group EBIT fell 254bps to 9.5%), no shareholder penalty, and value unlock via an independent, separately-funded structure.
rationale.gaps: No scheme of arrangement, demerger mechanics, record date, share-entitlement ratio, listing route or timetable for the stated spin-off path; no stranded-cost, tax or regulatory detail.

rationale.rationale: The separation at issue is the demerger of Siemens Limited's Energy Business into Siemens Energy India Limited (SEIL), under a Scheme approved by both boards on 14 May 2024, sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 25 March 2025 (effective 25 March 2025, appointed date 1 March 2025), with 356,120,505 shares issued 1:1 to Siemens Limited shareholders on 14 April 2025 and listing on BSE/NSE on 19 June 2025. The only explicit rationale management gives is in the Q4 FY25 press release: the demerger 'created a pure play energy technology company in India that operates across the entire energy value chain, offering customers greater focus and agility, while unlocking shareholder value' — i.e. focus/agility for customers plus value unlock for shareholders, mirroring the global carve-out of Siemens' energy business into Siemens Energy. Management frames the problem it solves as capturing a step-change in Indian energy demand that a conglomerate structure would serve less sharply: generation doubling from ~500 GW to ~1,000 GW, 500 GW renewables by 2030 ('two Germany's in the next seven to 10 years'), per-capita consumption of ~1,400 kWh versus one-third of the global average, NITI Aayog's $9–14 trillion to 2070, and CEA's upgraded 2030–36 plan adding 200+ GW of generation and ~800 GVA of transformation. The separated entity is a two-segment, eight-factory, ~4,500-person business — Power Transmission (transformers, GIS/switchgear, HVDC VSC, STATCOM/SynCon, services) and Power Generation (industrial and up-to-250 MW steam turbines, gas/steam service, ER&D 'local for global') — explicitly excluding coal plant additions, solar, wind and compressors. The post-separation entity has moved fast on capital: ₹7.4 billion of brownfield expansion (Kalwa transformers doubling 15,000→30,000 MVA; Sambhajinagar switchgear) and a ₹20.6 billion / ₹2,060 crore greenfield 30,000 MVA power transformer plant funded from internal accruals, rationale filed as 'very high and increasing demand for large power transformers', operating FY2030–32. Numbers cited around the separation: FY25 revenue ₹78 billion (+25%), orders +49% to ₹13,114 crore, backlog ₹162 billion (+47% to ₹16,205 crore), profit from operations 18.0% FY25 / 19.3% per the deck (18% ex 1.3% one-offs); H1 FY26 backlog ₹150→184 billion (+22.2%), revenue ₹34→43 billion (+27%), PFO 19.1%→20.7% (underlying 17.2%→18.9%), book-to-bill 1.5, exports +500 bps, and a maiden ₹4/share (200%) dividend. Separation costs and limits were disclosed rather than argued away: a ₹546 million stamp duty/transfer-fee provision, ~1.9% of H1 profit from 'accrual releases and stamp duty charges associated with demerger', the entity remaining legally separate from Siemens Energy AG with sales rights only for South Asia (India, Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Maldives) so that exports happen only when Siemens Energy requests them, and compressors (Siemens Energy Industrial Turbomachinery India, Baroda) plus wind (Siemens Gamesa, Chennai) still sitting in separate Indian companies outside SEIL. Crucially, in these texts nobody is named as having asked for the separation — no investor, lender, customer or partner demand is cited; it is presented as a promoter/parent-led structural decision, and the related question of Siemens Energy AG buying Siemens AG's stake was declined as 'between the two parents or the promoters'.
rationale.evolution: The idea pre-dates these transcripts: the filings record board approval of the Scheme on 14 May 2024, NCLT sanction on 25 March 2025, allotment on 14 April 2025 and listing on 19 June 2025, with the 24 November 2025 FY25 press release supplying the only stated rationale (pure play, focus and agility, unlocking shareholder value) and the Q4 margin drag from mix plus a ₹546 million stamp duty provision. At the first analyst and investor meet on 10 December 2025, management presented SEIL as 'an independent listed entity' and 'pure play energy leader', restated FY23–FY24 using Siemens Limited's Energy segment for comparability under Ind AS 103, and conceded the carve-out is partial — compressors and wind remain in separate Indian companies and any integration 'depend[s] very much on the headquarters strategy'. On 13 February 2026 the board turned the standalone balance sheet into capex, approving ₹2,060 crore for a new 30,000 MVA transformer factory from internal accruals. By the 15 May 2026 Q2/H1 FY26 call the framing had shifted from rationale to consequences: demerger stamp duty and accrual releases were still a ~1.9% one-off in H1 profit, management stressed SEIL and Siemens Energy 'are still today different companies' with South Asia-only sales rights, and the pending parent-to-parent stake transfer was left unanswered.

points.point: The FY25 results press release gives the only explicit purpose statement for the separation: a pure-play energy technology company spanning the whole value chain, with customer focus/agility and shareholder value unlock.
points.quote: This created a pure play energy technology company in India that operates across the entire energy value chain, offering customers greater focus and agility, while unlocking shareholder value.

points.point: The legal mechanism and timeline: boards approved the Scheme on 14 May 2024 for the demerger of Siemens Limited's Energy Business under Sections 230–232, NCLT sanctioned it on 25 March 2025 with appointed date 1 March 2025.
points.quote: The Scheme of Arrangement between the Company and Siemens Limited and their respective shareholders and creditors, was approved by the Board of Directors of the Company and Siemens Limited on 14 May 2024, at their respective meetings, providing for the demerger of Siemens Limited's Energy Business to the Company in compliance with Sections 230 to 232 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 (the "Scheme").

points.point: Consideration was a mirror 1:1 share entitlement to Siemens Limited shareholders on the 7 April 2025 record date — 356,120,505 shares allotted 14 April 2025, listed 19 June 2025 — i.e. a value-unlock demerger, not a cash sale.
points.quote: in the ratio of 1 (One) fully paid-up equity share of the Company having face value of Rs. 2 (Rupees Two) each for every 1 (One) fully paid-up equity share of Rs. 2 (Rupees Two) each held in Siemens Limited

points.point: The direct frictional cost of the separation disclosed in the accounts: a Rs. 546 million provision for stamp duty, transfer fees and registration charges on moving property titles from Siemens Limited.
points.quote: During the year ended 30 September 2025, pursuant to the Scheme and applicable laws of India, stamp duty, transfer fees and other registration charges are payable by the Company on the transfer of the title of immovable properties / leasehold land from Siemens Limited to the Company. Accordingly, the Company had recorded a provision of Rs. 546 million towards these expenses.

points.point: Four months post-listing the standalone board committed Rs. 2,060 crore of internal accruals to a ~30,000 MVA greenfield transformer plant (FY2030–32), justified purely by transformer demand — the clearest evidence of the focused entity deploying its own capital.
points.quote: Domestic and global trend for energy transition and electrification has resulted in a very high and increasing demand for large power transformers.

points.point: The December 10, 2025 meet was staged as the debut of a standalone company, positioning SEIL as a pure-play energy leader setting its own course after the demerger.
points.quote: A company built on a legacy of innovation, now charting its own course as a pure play energy leader .

points.point: Mendonca grounded the pure-play logic in whole-value-chain coverage against niche competitors — generation, transmission and industrial consumption in one entity.
points.quote:
So we are a company that only focus on the power sector and differently from other competitors
Siemens Energy goes through the entire value chain .

points.point: Harish explained the comparability problem the separation created: FY23/FY24 had to be shown as Siemens Limited's Energy segment, with Ind AS 103 forcing an 8-month versus 12-month comparison from incorporation on 7 February 2024.
points.quote: Because this is a first year and you would know for a new entity it's a bit different in terms of how do we compare numbers and to Consistency and comparability what we've done is we've also taken the Energy segment which was reported hitherto in Siemens limited as a segment in the past two years .

points.point: The carve-out is deliberately incomplete: compressors sit in Siemens Energy Industrial Turbomachinery India (Baroda) and wind in Siemens Gamesa (Chennai), so SEIL is not the full parent portfolio in India.
points.quote:
The portfolio that we do in SEIL is everything but compressors and wind, but we are
serving the country as a whole.

points.point: Asked whether the missing compressor business would be folded in to align SEIL with the parent portfolio, management said the decision is not theirs.
points.quote: If you ask me about integr ation. This is something that I cannot answer you because we are depend very much on the headquarters strategy when they want to do that.

points.point: A structural limit of the separated entity: the export leg is controlled by the parent's global factory network, so SEIL can plan only the domestic market.
points.quote: But when is about export actually the headquarters side. Because it's their responsibility to decide for a given country for a given customer what is the most suitable factory to supply

points.point: Mendonca spelled out the post-separation relationship: SEIL and Siemens Energy are still distinct companies, Siemens Energy is only a shareholder, and SEIL's own sales rights cover India plus Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Maldives.
points.quote:
We have to bear in mind that SEIL
and Siemens Energy, they are still today different companies, right? So, Siemens Energy is a shareholder in our
company and the SEIL has the sales rights and the responsibility to make business in the South Asia, as we call it.

points.point: Demerger costs were still distorting reported profit a year after listing: accrual releases and stamp duty charges worth about 1.9% of H1 profit, with underlying margin given as 17.2%→18.9%.
points.quote:
So, when we look at the profit,
it's important that in H1 there were one -time impacts of about 1.9% owing to accrual releases and stamp duty
charges associated with demerger, which were disclosed back then.

points.point: The unfinished promoter-level step — Siemens Energy AG acquiring Siemens AG's stake in SEIL, and any resulting stock supply — was explicitly refused, with SEIL calling itself 'the object' of the transaction.
points.quote:
On the stake pickup, we can't actually comment on that because this is something which is between the two
parents or the promoters.

points.point: The standalone entity's performance case: backlog up 22.2% to ₹184 billion, revenue up ~27% to ₹43 billion, and profit from operations up 160 bps to 20.7% on operating leverage and higher exports.
points.quote:
As regards profitability, our profit from operations as a percentage of revenue improved from 19.1% in H1FY25
to 20.7% in H1FY26, an improvement of 160 basis points.

rationale.what_management_expects: A focused, agile pure-play covering the whole energy value chain, with shareholder value unlocked via the 1:1 listing. Standalone capital goes into transformer/switchgear capacity (₹7.4bn brownfield, ₹20.6bn greenfield, internal accruals). Margins to rise on operating leverage and export mix (H1FY26 20.7%; PG 17.7%→21.3%), funding a ₹4/share dividend. Siemens Limited's post-demerger prospects are never discussed.
rationale.gaps: No stated initiator, no synergy/dis-synergy or valuation quantification, no royalty/trademark economics, nothing on Siemens Limited's residual company, why now, or why compressors and wind were excluded.
