rationale.rationale: On the documents supplied, Lloyds Engineering Works Ltd. (LEWL) is NOT separating a business — it is doing the opposite: a Scheme of Merger by Absorption approved by all four boards on 29 December 2025 that folds three group entities INTO the listed company, with Appointed Date 1 April 2025. The transferors are Lloyds Infrastructure & Construction Ltd. (LICL, an unlisted associate in which LEWL holds ~24.20%, EPC/roads, bridges, railways, industrial civil, slurry pipelines, BOOT/BOO/BOLT/PPP), Metalfab Hightech Pvt. Ltd. (MHPL, 76% subsidiary, heavy fabrication for steel, railways and infrastructure) and Techno Industries Pvt. Ltd. (TIPL, wholly owned, elevators, escalators, motors and pumps); LEWL itself makes process plant equipment for hydrocarbon, steel, captive power, marine, ports and nuclear heat exchangers. The headline number management cites repeatedly is LICL's 'robust order book of over ₹4,500 crores', which combined with LEWL's manufacturing and execution capability is said to create one 'unified engineering and infrastructure company' able to bid for larger, multidisciplinary contracts; the merging businesses are described as having 'complementary capabilities, overlapping customer base and shared execution requirements'. The stated problems it solves are structural and financial: duplicated/redundant functions, fragmented management, scattered technical and financial resources, a complex multi-entity shareholding that burdens the 'ever-evolving regulatory compliance framework' and governance/transparency, and a smaller balance sheet with costlier borrowing — hence 'improved borrowing capabilities and reduced borrowing costs' and 'unfettered access to cash flow generated by the combined businesses'. Scale being consolidated: LICL FY26 revenue ₹1,902.25 cr / PAT ₹173.81 cr / EBITDA ₹280.01 cr (vs ₹1,060.98 cr / ₹66.66 cr in FY25 and ₹395.14 cr / ₹22.10 cr in FY24), MHPL ₹173.36 cr / ₹33.47 cr, TIPL ₹185.74 cr / ₹5.20 cr, against LEWL's own ₹1,052.22 cr / ₹118.27 cr / ₹188.12 cr; assets/liabilities transferred are LICL ₹1,315.93 cr/₹1,012.61 cr, MHPL ₹321.60 cr/₹269.67 cr, TIPL ₹240.83 cr/₹158.55 cr. Consideration is 1,798 LEWL shares per 1,500 LICL shares (Streamland Estate LLP gets 36,19,97,330 shares, Pravriddhi Trust 59,93,333, all classified Public) and 94 LEWL shares per 5 MHPL shares (Manan Agrawal 1,29,72,000); nothing is paid for TIPL as a wholly owned subsidiary. Who asked: no investor, lender or partner demand is recorded anywhere — it is board-driven, with lenders merely consenting (NOC from lending scheduled commercial banks/financial institutions obtained, 'no conditions imposed by the lenders'), CCI clearing it on 12 May 2026, NSE/BSE observation letters on 18/19 May 2026, NCLT ordering meetings on 19 August 2026, and on 16 October 2026 equity shareholders and unsecured creditors (758,413,241 votes, 72.54% of outstanding, 100% in favour) approving it.
rationale.evolution: No earnings-call transcripts were provided ('no transcripts on file'), so the idea cannot be traced call by call; the only record is filings. It surfaces fully formed on 29 December 2025 (simultaneous board approvals, valuation by Bansi S. Mehta Valuers LLP and fairness opinion from Mark Corporate Advisors, both dated that day), is prepared through 2026 by moving MHPL's registered office to Mumbai (20 December 2025) and TIPL's from Ahmedabad to Mumbai (Regional Director order, 27 February 2026), clears CCI (12 May 2026), the exchanges (18–19 May 2026) and NCLT (19 August 2026), and is approved by shareholders and unsecured creditors on 16 October 2026 with results filed 17 October 2026. In parallel the group consolidates further rather than separating: a 17 August 2026 preferential allotment of 7,00,42,458 shares at ₹71.25 swaps in 1,66,35,087 shares of Steel Infra Solutions Company Ltd. (SISCOL), plus 7,00,000 shares for cash; and on 6 August 2026 the board re-cut the April 2025 rights-issue objects (₹987.25 cr gross, ₹660.52 cr spent, ₹326.73 cr unutilised at 30 June 2026), cutting the Bhilai Engineering Corporation asset purchase from ₹130.25 cr to ₹71.25 cr and adding ₹86.59 cr to working capital — passed by postal ballot on 25 September 2026 (99.9948% in favour).

rationale.what_management_expects: No separated entities exist — only one survivor. For LEWL: ~₹4,500 cr added order book, FY26 combined revenue of roughly ₹3,314 cr versus ₹1,052 cr standalone, larger net worth and asset base, cost synergies from removing duplicated functions and compliance costs, unfettered access to combined cash flows, improved borrowing capacity at lower cost, simplified shareholding, better governance, and value unlocked via a larger, more diversified entity.
rationale.gaps: No earnings calls supplied; no separation/demerger exists in these texts. Filings never quantify synergies, cost savings, margin or borrowing-cost impact, dilution, or investor/lender demand.

rationale.rationale: Nothing in these texts describes a demerger, spin-off or NCLT scheme; what management actually explains are three narrower separations plus a new offshore holding vehicle. (1) The Consumer Healthcare/OTC business was carved out into a wholly-owned subsidiary of Mankind Pharma (announced on the Q2 FY25 call, first quarter of reporting as a separate segment in Q3 FY25) because OTC is a 'push' business whose channel economics and culture differ from prescription — Rajeev Juneja identified 'a mixed kind of a culture where one guy, one leader is taking care of OTC and pharma both' as the thing being fixed, alongside cutting stockist numbers from a few thousand, stopping cash-and-carry trade that was causing rate-cutting in the market, and pushing modern trade/e-commerce (9% of OTC sales in FY25 to 13% in FY26, growing 40–57%). (2) The numbers cited for OTC: INR232 cr (+20%) in Q2 FY25, INR193 cr (+30%) in Q3 FY25, INR809 cr (+15%) FY25, INR879 cr (+9%) FY26 with Q4 FY26 at INR213 cr (+20%); roughly 7% of company revenue at 18–20% EBITDA versus company guidance of 25–26%, which Abhishek Agarwal said is 'not going to contribute or significantly, you can say, dilute the overall margins.' (3) Separately, BSV's inherited TTK branded-generic prescription portfolio was separated out of BSV and slump-sold into Mankind (slump-sale notification flagged in Q1 FY26, transition effective 1 November 2025) on the logic that BSV should hold only super-specialty, high-entry-barrier biologics (Anti-D, Foligraf, HMG, ASVS, recombinants, immunoglobulins) while branded generics belong on Mankind's 'Delhi Mankind' platform, which 'understands the Rx business better.' (4) The TTK fix was quantified: three divisions collapsed into one, 600-plus field staff reduced to 440 by March 2025 and then ~325, MR productivity up from ~INR2 lakh PCPM to ~INR2.9 lakh, BSV blended PCPM 6.5 lakh versus above INR8 lakh excluding TTK, against TTK turnover that had collapsed from INR197 cr to INR104 cr (FY24 to FY25) after inventory corrections; total BSV synergies were guided at INR50–100 cr over 12–24 months, with margins 26–28% rising 50–100 bps a year toward 30% by FY30. Stamp duty on that intra-group slump sale was booked as an exceptional item in Q3 FY26, part of why reported EBITDA margin was 22.9% against adjusted 25.9%. (5) The third strand is non-core divestment to delever after the INR10,000 cr BSV debt raise: Mahananda Spa & Resorts sold for INR562 cr on 11 February 2025 (against a INR600–650 cr target for the two hospitality units), Broadway Hospitality Services approved for 100% sale to AKRK Projects LLP for INR49 cr on 11 July 2026 (FY26 revenue INR9.63 cr, 0.07% of company; net worth INR38.99 cr), BSV's surplus Hyderabad land being returned to the authorities with a INR13 cr impairment, and the dormant Sri Lanka subsidiary wound up on 13 April 2026. (6) No investor, lender or partner is recorded as asking for any of this: the demand side is management's own 'prudent financial strategy' and promoter long-termism, with shareholder-approved INR3,000 cr QIP proceeds, net debt down to INR3,932 cr and 1.1x adjusted EBITDA at Q4 FY26, and full acquisition-debt retirement targeted by FY28. (7) Forward-looking, the 11 July 2026 board also approved a Netherlands wholly-owned SPV (up to EUR 5 million) to hold R&D assets and do niche-therapy business development through JVs or strategic interests — i.e. ring-fencing innovation risk outside the operating company, alongside the Vadodara biotech plant funded via up to INR500 cr into Mankind Medicare, the manufacturing arm.
rationale.evolution: The idea surfaced on the Nov 2024 (Q2 FY25) call, where OTC was said to have been carved into a wholly-owned subsidiary for its 'next phase of growth' and, in the same breath, TTK was described as 'not a core BSV kind of a business' that 'will be separated out'; Ashutosh Dhawan simultaneously named Mahananda and Broadway as hospitality units being liquidated to retire debt. Jan 2025 reported the first post-carve-out OTC quarter (+30%) and explained the TTK shift as Mankind 'understanding the Rx business better'; May 2025 confirmed Mahananda's INR562 cr sale and framed the move as 'integration of BSV's prescription business into Mankind's platform'; Aug 2025 disclosed the formal slump-sale notification. Nov 2025 gave the field-force and PCPM metrics, Feb 2026 confirmed the 1 November 2025 transition, the stamp-duty exceptional and the Hyderabad land impairment, and May 2026 moved on to the Vadodara biotech build via Mankind Medicare. The filings then extend the same non-core logic: Sri Lanka WOS wound up 13 April 2026, and on 11 July 2026 Broadway sold for INR49 cr while a Netherlands R&D SPV was approved — so the plan migrated from fixing acquired businesses to housing new R&D risk offshore.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is NMDC's steel-making arm — the 3 MTPA NMDC Iron & Steel Plant (NISP) at Nagarnar, Chhattisgarh — which was demerged out of NMDC Limited into a separate listed company, NMDC Steel Limited (NSL), under a Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by the MCA on 6 October 2022 (effective 13 October 2022, appointed date 1 April 2021), leaving NMDC as a pure mining company and NSL as the vehicle the Government of India intends to privatise, with NMDC retaining a 10% stake. Management never presented a board-level strategic case on these calls; the reasons they did give are (a) the demerger is a government/DIPAM-driven disinvestment, run by GCOM/'Deepam' and not by NMDC — the draft SPA was shown to NMDC, which 'gave the go ahead' — and management repeatedly said it has 'no visibility' on it, (b) a deliberate corporate policy that NMDC will not build any more steel plants after Nagarnar (the reason the 2,857-acre Karnataka/KVSL land bought for a 3 MTPA plant was left stranded with ₹639.61 crores paid to KIADB and still unresolved as of Jun 2026), and (c) identity as a merchant miner rather than an end-consumer of its own ore, which management said in Aug 2024 put NMDC 'in a more comfortable, more reassuring space' than peers when the Supreme Court retrospective-royalty judgment landed. The numbers they cited for the drag steel puts on the miner are blunt: consolidated EBITDA margin fell from 42% to 33% purely because of the steel business, while standalone iron ore stayed at 42% (Jun 2026); ₹2,502.64 crores of pre-demerger expenses were incurred by NMDC on NSL's behalf (₹901.25 crores repaid, ₹1,601.39 crores still outstanding); NSL and RINL were the only two credit accounts behind receivables of about ₹7,800 crores at FY25 (NSL trade receivables ₹4,499.20 crores plus ₹167.53 crores employee costs and ₹179.83 crores HR-coil advance at Jun 2026); and these advances earn NMDC no interest at all ('No we cannot. This is not a deposit'). Post-demerger NMDC supplies NSL at arm's length — about 5 million tonnes of ore at NSL's 3 MTPA peak, roughly 10% of NMDC sales rising to ~13% of Bailadila — and management insisted the ore relationship survives any change of ownership because Bailadila, 131 km away, stays the nearest source. Separation also lets each side run its own plan: NMDC's ₹50,000–70,000 crores capex to 100 million tonnes by FY30, coal (Tokisud, Rohne), rare earths/critical minerals and overseas acquisitions; NSL as a lean, low-manpower, energy-efficient single-blast-furnace producer targeting ~25% EBITDA at ~90% utilisation.
rationale.evolution: The demerger was already done before this window (MCA sanction Oct 2022), so the calls track the privatisation and the unwinding of entanglement rather than the decision: in Nov 2023 management said multiple offers had come, the draft SPA had been discussed and cleared from NMDC's side, but progress stalled around the Chhattisgarh election and questions should go to 'Deepam'; in Feb 2024 it said the sale was 'being driven by GCOM and not by us' with 'huge amount of interest' and no visibility, and investors flagged that halted privatisation news had dented confidence. By Jun 2024 management stated the deliberate policy of no more steel plants after Nagarnar (stranding the Karnataka land) and spoke of 'a blueprint' for taking NMDC and NSL separately to the next level, while Aug 2024 and Feb 2025 handled the sale as a given — ore sourcing unaffected by ownership, the retained 10% stake monetisable only 'as and when it is proposed to the disinvestment', a 'hypothetical question'. From Jun 2025 to Jun 2026 the privatisation dropped out of the discussion entirely and the talk became operational cleanup: NSL under 'the same management', marketing routed ~60% through SAIL, HR-coil trading by NMDC as a one-off cash-flow bridge, pre-demerger dues down from ₹2,500 crores to ₹1,800 crores at ~₹100 crores a month, and the steel business shown as the sole cause of EBITDA falling from 42% to 33%.

points.point: The separation is a formal demerger of the Nagarnar steel plant (NISP) out of NMDC into NMDC Steel Limited, sanctioned by the MCA with an appointed date of 1 April 2021, under which NMDC held the undertaking in trust for NSL between appointed and effective dates.
points.quote: The Scheme of Arrangement for the demerger of NMDC Iron & Steel Plant (NISP) from NMDC Limited (NMDC) into NMDC Steel Limited (NSL), along with their respective shareholders and creditors, was sanctioned by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) on October 6, 2022.

points.point: The trust arrangement left NMDC funding NSL: ₹2,502.64 crores of pre-demerger expenses with no repayment schedule in the Scheme, of which ₹1,601.39 crores was still outstanding at 30 June 2026, on top of ₹4,499.20 crores of iron-ore trade receivables, ₹167.53 crores of employee costs and a ₹179.83 crores HR-product advance.
points.quote: As per the terms, NMDC shall act in trust for NSL and accordingly, an amount of ₹ 2,502.64 crores was incurred by NMDC on behalf of NSL with no specific repayment schedule defined in the scheme.

points.point: Asked about the divestment, management said the process belongs to the government's disinvestment department, not NMDC — it had cleared the draft SPA from its side, several offers had come, and progress stalled around the Chhattisgarh election.
points.quote: As of now we do not have a clear visibility on that issue so in fact we should be referring that to Deepam.

points.point: Management reiterated it is a government-run sale handled by GCOM, with strong bidder interest in what it called a state-of-the-art plant, while NMDC concentrated only on ramping production.
points.quote: Of course when it was being driven, it is being driven by GCOM and not by us we were aware that there is a huge amount of interest in that very special interest and rightly so it is the state of the art plant.

points.point: The underlying corporate rationale management did state: NMDC will not build any more steel plants after Nagarnar — which is why the 2,857-acre Karnataka (KVSL) land bought for a 3 MTPA plant, with ₹639.61 crores paid to KIADB, was left without a use and handed to consultants.
points.quote: So that -- now we are left with finding out alternatives.

points.point: Management framed NMDC and NSL as two separately steered companies with their own growth blueprints rather than one integrated group.
points.quote: We plan to take both the companies NMDC and NSL to the next level, and we are -- it's not an ad hoc plan.

points.point: The inter-company funding is uncompensated — the ₹2,500-2,600 crores of pre-demerger expenses plus ~₹1,300 crores of ore credit carry no interest because they are not deposits under Section 186, so the drag sat entirely on NMDC's balance sheet.
points.quote: No we cannot. This is not a deposit.

points.point: Post-demerger, ore to the steel plant is an arm's-length sale, not an internal transfer, sized at about 5 million tonnes at NSL's 3 MTPA peak — roughly 10% of NMDC's total sales and ~13% of Bailadila.
points.quote: No. It's not an internal, it's an arm length sale.

points.point: Asked directly whether selling NSL to a private buyer would hurt NMDC, management said ore sourcing is unaffected by ownership because Bailadila, 131 km away, remains the nearest source versus Odisha.
points.quote: So I don't think -- the sourcing of material irrespective of the ownership, whether it's stays with us or it doesn't stay with us irrespective of the ownership Bailadila will remain.

points.point: On the Supreme Court retrospective mining-levy judgment (~₹2,500-2,600 crores Karnataka, ₹144 crores Chhattisgarh, ₹21 crores Panna), management argued a pure merchant miner is structurally better placed than an integrated miner-consumer because levies pass through to customers.
points.quote: As I have -- hopefully I've been able to clarify that as merchant miners we are in a more comfortable, more reassuring space than maybe those -- our counterparts who are also the end consumer of what they mine.

points.point: On monetising the residual 10% NMDC holds in NSL and recovering receivables, management treated the timing as entirely the government's call and the question as hypothetical; recovery was tied only to NSL reaching breakeven at 2-2.5 rakes a day.
points.quote: The 10% equity stake is as and when it is proposed to the disinvestment on which I don't have much of idea as of now.

points.point: FY25 receivables ballooned to about ₹7,800 crores driven by just two state-owned counterparties, NSL and RINL, with ~₹50 crores of expected-credit-loss provisioning taken; NSL had begun repaying ~₹200 crores a month.
points.quote: There are only two accounts. One is RINL, the other is NSL. We don't sell on credit to any other people.

points.point: The clearest quantified cost of keeping steel attached: consolidated EBITDA margin fell from 42% to 33% solely because of the steel/HR-coil business, while standalone iron ore held at 42%.
points.quote: If you see our EBITDA, it has come down from 42% to 33%, essentially because of steel business.

points.point: NMDC had to step back in as a trader of NSL's HR coils because NSL, still under the same management with marketing routed through SAIL, hit a realisation lag and cash-flow squeeze; management called it a one-time special mechanism not expected to recur in FY27.
points.quote: Okay, so this was essentially an arrangement made for a very specific requirement of NMDC Steel where they were facing cash flows, so we stepped in and we were doing trading business with the HR coils of NMDC Steel.

points.point: Unwinding the demerger dues is on a ~16-18 month path: pre-demerger expenses cut from ~₹2,500 crores to ~₹1,800 crores at roughly ₹100 crores a month, with full liquidation of all NSL outstandings expected in 1.5-2 years as NSL turned profitable.
points.quote: If you see NSL pre -demerger expenses was around INR2,500, it has already been reduced to around INR1,800.

rationale.what_management_expects: NMDC: a pure-play miner at 42-43% EBITDA (vs 33% blended), undiluted by steel, funding ₹50,000-70,000 crores capex to 100 mt by FY30 plus coal, rare earths and overseas assets from internal accruals; receivables and ₹1,601 crores demerger dues liquidated in 1.5-2 years. NSL: a lean, energy-efficient 3 MTPA plant reaching ~25% EBITDA at ~90% utilisation, privatised by the government, with NMDC's 10% stake monetised then.
rationale.gaps: No board/government rationale, no valuation-unlock or synergy-loss math, no disinvestment timeline or price, no explanation why NMDC kept funding NSL interest-free post-demerger.

rationale.rationale: Nothing in these texts announces or explains POWERINDIA separating, demerging, spinning off or divesting a business — the premise is not supported by the seven supplied transcripts or the one AGM filing, and I am not importing anything from memory. The only 'separation' management actually describes is internal and organisational: the carve-out of Service into a standalone fifth business unit effective 1 April 2025, sitting alongside the four existing BUs (Transformers, High Voltage Products, Grid Integration, Grid Automation), mirroring a 'separate global BU Service' at Hitachi Energy — no new legal entity, no share issuance, no record date, no NCLT scheme, no listed-entity restructuring. The reasons given for that carve-out were an aging installed base (Venu cited 'Rs.60,000 crores worth of installed base in India since last 75 years' in the May 2025 call; the Feb 2025 slide said 'approximately Rs. (+80,000) crores'), the urgency of the energy transition, an 'ever evolving workforce' and the organisational shift to digitalization. The prize was sized at roughly Rs. 2,000 crores of service orders per year against a then run-rate of Rs. 500–600 crores, described as a 3-to-5-year journey; service was 7.4% of FY25 orders, 11–12% in individual quarters, and 'high single digit' thereafter, with service orders up ~60% YoY in FY25 and ~90% YoY in Q1 FY26. The problems it was said to solve were fragmented lifecycle engagement and an inconsistent customer experience ('develop service and digital proficiency and unify the customer service experience'), plus new-age customers such as data centres wanting a 'life cycle partner' rather than only equipment supply. It was also explicitly a margin lever, named by Venu alongside volume/fixed-cost leverage, exports and pricing excellence in the road map to and beyond double-digit EBITDA. Nobody asked for a separation: no investor, lender, analyst or partner in any call requests one — analysts instead pressed on margins versus peers, the ~4% royalty, admin and other expenses (Dhavan Shah even suggested cutting royalty and raising dividend instead), and management defended the royalty and promised operating leverage rather than any structural split. The single occurrence of the word 'demerger' anywhere in the record is a backward-looking administrative reference in the 31 July 2026 AGM notice to the Scheme of Arrangement that created the company, cited only to explain 1,07,421 shares allotted to the IEPF account, with no rationale attached.
rationale.evolution: The idea first surfaced on the Jan 30, 2025 call (tagged Feb 2025), where Venu said the company 'will work towards a new service business unit' as a fifth BU from 1 April 2025 and framed it against the aging installed base and digitalization. It was confirmed as launched on the May 15, 2025 call (installed base Rs. 60,000 crores, potential Rs. 2,000 crores of orders per year versus Rs. 500–600 crores today), described as 'carved out' on the Jul 30, 2025 call, and reframed on the Nov 7, 2025 call as a top-line and bottom-line margin lever. By Feb 5, 2026 it was a 'separate global BU Service including in India' with the stated aim of 'shifting center of gravity' toward export, service and digital; by May 26, 2026 service was merely a 'key pillar' and the only structural news ran the other way — Rs. 2,000 crores of additional capex (Rs. 4,000 crores cumulative) and a greenfield Karjan transformer plant, i.e. consolidation and expansion inside one entity, not separation.

points.point: First mention of any carve-out: a new Service business unit, the fifth BU, to start 1 April 2025, justified by an aging installed base of 'approximately Rs. (+80,000) crores', the energy-transition urgency, an evolving workforce and the shift to digitalization; explicitly 'the first step to develop service and digital proficiency and unify the customer service experience'. No legal separation of any business is mentioned.
points.quote: In our ambition to enhance customer experience with a strengthened and future-focused service system globally, we will work towards a new service business unit from the coming financial year of 2025-2026.

points.point: Launch confirmed as an internal business unit covering the whole asset life cycle; Venu sized the India installed base at Rs. 60,000 crores over 75 years, the annual order potential at Rs. 2,000 crores versus a current Rs. 500–600 crores, and called it a 3-to-5-year journey. Service was 7.4% of FY25 orders (up ~60% YoY). No entity separation discussed.
points.quote: Furthermore, foreseeing immense potential in service and maintenance, the company has introduced its service business unit that is the 5th business unit, from April 1st, 2025.

points.point: The word 'carved out' is used for the first and only time, and it refers to this internal service BU, not to any business being separated from the listed company; its purpose is stated as intensifying life-cycle engagement with utilities, industries and new-age customers, with all other BUs working alongside it. Service orders grew 90% YoY.
points.quote: This is also our first quarter after we carved out our new service business, effective from 1st of April, 2025, and contributed a high single digit to the overall order book.

points.point: The service BU is recast as one of the explicit margin levers — listed with growth/fixed-cost leverage, export gross margin and pricing excellence — in the stated long-term plan to reach and sustain double-digit EBITDA margins.
points.quote: We have created a dedicated service business unit, because we have a huge amount of install base, and we would like to leverage and then improve on both top line and bottom line.

points.point: The unit is described as a separate global BU Service replicated in India, tied to the ambition of 'shifting center of gravity' toward export, service and digital and to data-centre customers who want a life-cycle partner, not just equipment. Still no mention of separating, demerging or divesting any business.
points.quote: so we created the separate global BU Service including in India and we hope that the efforts of this particular team would start fetching the results over a period of time.

points.point: The most recent call contains no separation, demerger or divestment of any kind; the structural news is the opposite — Rs. 2,000 crores of fresh board-approved capex (Rs. 4,000 crores cumulative) including a greenfield large power transformer and HVDC converter transformer plant at Karjan, Vadodara, due in Q4 CY2028, plus two added power-quality lines in Bangalore, all inside the one entity.
points.quote: During our Q4FY26 Board Meeting, the Board approved an additional investment of Rs. 2,000 Crores.

points.point: The only use of 'Demerger' in the entire record is an administrative, backward-looking reference in the 31 July 2026 AGM notice, explaining shares allotted to the IEPF account under the historical Scheme of Arrangement that formed the company (incorporated 19 February 2019). No rationale, scope, business, counterparty or financial effect is described, and the notice's five agenda items are accounts, dividend, Haka's re-appointment, cost-auditor fees and the Hitachi ESPP/RSU — none of them a separation.
points.quote: Pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement (Demerger), 1,07,421 equity shares were allotted directly to the IEPF account.

rationale.what_management_expects: Only for the internal Service BU: convert a Rs. 60,000–80,000 crore installed base into roughly Rs. 2,000 crores of orders a year, lift both top line and bottom line, help sustain double-digit and then ~15% EBITDA, shift mix toward service, export and digital, and lock in life-cycle partnerships with data-centre and industrial customers. No entity-level margin, capital or valuation claims are made.
rationale.gaps: Everything about an actual separation: whether one was considered, its scope, scheme terms, standalone financials, capital allocation, valuation or re-rating case, and who wanted it.

judge.reason: Three separately listed companies "each with its own focus and its own management"; what remains is "an independent workforce, talent and technology company, with no debt", "deliberately a pure play business with a single mandate"
judge.insiders: Promoters/promoter group excluded from QSOP 2026 (52,50,000 RSUs, 3.52% of capital); CEO Lohit Bhatia holds 0.08%, gets 4,00,000 TSR-linked RSUs, CFO 1,00,000. Stake in demerged entities not stated.
judge.hidden_value: Parent is zero gross debt with ₹271 crore net cash, 20% ROE, 80% EBITDA-to-OCF; Professional Staffing (12%+ margin) and Overseas, ~14% of revenue, now give 50% of operating profit, hidden inside a 2% blended margin.
judge.selling_pressure_why: "the stock saw some weakness immediately following the demerger"; demerged entities are technology and industrial services platforms, different industries from staffing
judge.listing_timeline: At the AGM on August 25, 2026: "In FY25, we completed a three-way demerger. Where there was one company, there are now three separately listed companies: Quess Corp, Bluspring Enterprises and Digitide Solutions"; the Q3 FY26 call (January 29, 2026) dates the demerger "since 1st April 2024"

rationale.rationale: Management presented the separation as a three-way demerger of the old conglomerate Quess Corp — effective 1 April 2024 and legally completed during FY25 "well ahead of stated timeline" — into three separately listed companies: Quess Corp (pure-play workforce/staffing: General Staffing, Professional Staffing/IT staffing, Overseas staffing, digital platforms Hamara Jobs/Taskmo), Digitide Solutions (Global Technology Solutions — BPM, customer lifecycle management, platform/payroll/InsurTech, plus foundit and the Brainhunter US/Canada business), and Bluspring Enterprises (Operating Asset Maintenance — IFM, food & beverage incl. the acquired Archer business, security, and Vedang telecom infra, plus the Golden Star facility-management contracts). The stated reasons were a sharper strategic identity and unlocking shareholder value: four unlike platforms sitting in one listed entity were split so each would have "its own focus and its own management", be "agile, strategically focused" with their own boards and leadership teams (Quess's board was strengthened post-demerger; key leadership hires completed; Lohit Bhatia later made CEO from 1 Jan 2026 and ED/Group CEO from 1 June 2026, Neeraj Jain CFO from 3 Dec 2025). The demerger was explicitly used as the trigger for a portfolio clean-up: a "comprehensive review" led the Board and management to discontinue non-core, long-gestation, outcome-based projects in skilling and utilities (meter reading/bill distribution), producing a Q4 FY25 exceptional charge of INR 158 crore — INR 119 crore of accelerated expected credit loss on discontinued projects, INR 26 crore goodwill impairment (INR 7 crore Stellarslog, INR 19 crore Quess International Services, the repurposed Golden Star) and INR 13 crore of demerger costs (mainly stamp duty) — forfeiting roughly INR 300 crore of revenue at ~20% EBITDA margin from skilling, with Digitide likewise "rationalizing low-margin low-efficiency contracts" ahead of separation. Balance-sheet repair was part of the thesis: gross debt was cut (INR 224 crore at Dec 2024) to INR 12 crore by 31 March 2025 and zero later, leaving net cash of INR 255 crore (INR 271/273 crore subsequently), a new dividend policy of up to 75% of free cash flow over a rolling three-year block, and an adjusted ROE target crossing 20%. Management repeatedly conceded the cost: standalone EBITDA margin optically reset from the 2.4–2.5% the workforce division earned pre-demerger to 1.8%, because standalone corporate overheads now sit in Quess and because the high-margin skilling and Brainhunter businesses left, making history "noncomparable"; demerger expenses hit reported PAT by INR 22 crore in Q3 FY25, INR 13 crore in Q4 FY25 and INR 2 crore in Q1 FY26, and the stock "saw some weakness immediately following the demerger". Nothing in these texts says any investor, lender or partner asked for the separation — it is presented throughout as a management-and-Board decision, with shareholders and creditors merely approving it on 9 December 2024 and the NCLT sanctioning it; the only external parties named are the demerger-linked cross-sell partners (Quess selling Origint GCC-as-a-Service using Bluspring and Digitide capabilities).
rationale.evolution: On the 30 Jan 2025 call (Q3 FY25) the demerger was already in flight — first NCLT approval obtained, shareholder and creditor approvals secured on 9 December, INR 22 crore of demerger costs booked, leadership/controls being built per entity, and Digitide pre-emptively rationalizing low-margin contracts — with listing guided for Q1 FY26. By the 20 May 2025 call it was done "well ahead of stated timeline" and Quess held its "first earnings call as an independent entity", pairing the split with the INR 158 crore exceptional clean-up of skilling/utilities projects, zero-ish gross debt, net cash of INR 255 crore, the new 75%-of-FCF dividend policy, and a frank reset of margin guidance from 2.4–2.5% to 1.8% rising to 2%. Through 29 Jul 2025 ("pure-play staffing leader", residual INR 2 crore of demerger fees) and 29 Jan 2026 (the demerger invoked to explain why 4–4.5% historic margins are "noncomparable", and the Q4 FY25 ECL recalled as "the discontinued businesses as part of the demerger"), the story shifted from execution to justification; on 5 May 2026 management closed the loop by exiting the last non-conforming business — a 7,000-headcount milestone-based project worth ~INR 200 crore (1.3% of revenue) — citing the commitment made "closer to our demerger timeline". At the 25 Aug 2026 AGM the Chairman recast it retrospectively as value creation: three listed companies, ~INR 500 crore combined EBITDA, 600,000+ people, Quess debt-free, and a forward plan ("Quess 2.0") to lift dollar-linked revenue from 7% to 20% and Professional Staffing plus Overseas profit share from 50% to 65%.

points.point: Capital allocation was redefined around the separated entity: gross debt cut to INR 12 crore and net cash of INR 255 crore at 31 March 2025, a new policy to return up to 75% of free cash flow over a rolling three-year block, DSO improved 7 days to 37, and adjusted ROE guided above 20%. Asked about new geographies, management said focus came first.
points.quote: See, as part of this demerger, Siddharth, our focus is going to be on the core businesses and how much more we can do and bring in more efficiency and stay profitable.

points.point: Quess positioned itself as a pure-play staffing company, while still monetising the separation by partnering its demerged siblings: the new Origint GCC-as-a-Service line is delivered by bringing Bluspring and Digitide capabilities together on a cost-plus, asset-light basis.
points.quote: So, as we strengthen our position as a pure -play staffing leader, we remain deeply committed to operational excellence, innovation and continuously evolving our offerings to meet the dynamic needs of our clients.

points.point: Asked why margins are ~2% versus 4–5% historically, management used the demerger to explain the break in the series — Bluspring and Digitide are out, skilling was discontinued, and Brainhunter (US/Canada) moved to Digitide.
points.quote: With all of those business with high EBITDA margins, we were averaging around 4%, 4.5%, but that businesses have been discontinued and Brain hunter as part of demerger has moved into Digitide.

points.point: The INR 120 crore Q4 FY25 ECL was re-confirmed as demerger-driven, relating to the discontinued government skilling project, with collections still being pursued (delayed from Q3 to Q4 FY26 by a new RBI escrow process) and any recovery to be reported as upside.
points.quote: If you recollect, in Q4, these were the discontinued businesses as part of the demerger that we had announced to the Street, and we had taken an exceptional credit loss on that.

points.point: The portfolio-discipline promise made at the time of the demerger was carried through: a 7,000-headcount milestone-based project worth about INR 200 crore (1.3% of revenue) was fully exited in FY26, with no further such events known.
points.quote: So, as you would remember, closer to our demerger timeline, we had said any business which does not meet the financi al metrics of the company and does not yield us the cash realization , we will exit and discontinue such businesses.

points.point: One year on, management summarised the outcome as balance-sheet and execution strength in the standalone entity: FY26 revenue INR 15,305 crore, EBITDA INR 312 crore (+19%), 2.0% margin, 20% ROE, zero gross debt, net cash INR 271 crore, and INR 6 per share of final plus special dividend.
points.quote: As we said, we are foundationally strong in our 19th year and one year post our demerger.

points.point: At the 25 Aug 2026 AGM the Chairman described the end state: one company became three separately listed companies, each with its own focus and management, funded historically by INR 1,270 crore raised through the Quess IPO and IPP, now together generating about INR 500 crore of EBITDA and employing over 600,000 people.
points.quote: Where there was one company, there are now three separately listed companies: Quess Corp, Bluspring Enterprises and Digitide Solutions, each with its own focus and its own management.

points.point: What shareholders retain is deliberately single-mandate: a debt-free workforce company that will not diversify outside workforce management, with Quess 2.0 targeting dollar-linked revenue from 7% to over 20% and Professional Staffing plus Overseas profit share from 50% to about 65% in three to four years.
points.quote: We are not diversifying outside our workforce management and following the demerger  of the company is deliberately a pure play business with a single mandate.

points.point: Management acknowledged the de-rating immediately after separation and claimed subsequent recovery, while noting the demerged businesses went on to build their own technology and industrial-services platforms.
points.quote: While the stock saw some weakness immediately following the demerger, it has since recovered strongly and delivered a return of around 25% over the past year.

rationale.what_management_expects: Quess: pure-play, single-mandate staffing with sharper focus on high-margin Professional Staffing and Overseas (now 50% of profit, targeted 65%), margin from 1.8% to 2.0–2.4%, 20% ROE, zero debt, net cash, up to 75% of free cash flow returned. Digitide and Bluspring: independent technology and industrial-services platforms with their own management; three entities together about INR 500 crore EBITDA.
rationale.gaps: No sum-of-parts or valuation math, share-entitlement ratio, named investor/lender/partner demand, dis-synergy or corporate-cost allocation detail, nor any Digitide/Bluspring post-split financials.

judge.what_is_spun: The Consumer Brands (FMCG) Business Undertaking, demerged from Reliance Retail Ventures Limited into Tira Beauty Limited, renamed Reliance Consumer Products Limited
demerged_business_names: Tira Beauty Limited (to be renamed as Reliance Consumer Products Limited under the scheme)
judge.reason: Management cites a focused organizational structure: "the consumer products vertical is progressing on its accelerated growth trajectory with a focused organizational structure." No other rationale is stated in the filings.
judge.insiders: New RCPL became an 83.56% direct subsidiary of the Company; RRVL shareholders received 1 New RCPL share for every 2 RRVL shares. Promoter/management stake and incentives in the new entity: not stated.
judge.hidden_value: A fast-scaling FMCG arm: FY26 revenue Rs.22,000 crore and Q1 FY27 Rs.8,600 crore, both roughly 2x year-ago, Campa Rs.4,700 crore, yet only "breakeven on EBITDA terms" with a Rs.1 lakh crore FY2030 target; retail's reported growth and 8% margin had carried it.
judge.selling_pressure_why: Not listed; shares allotted to unlisted RRVL's shareholders, with RIL holding 83.56% directly, so no public float or index exclusion.
judge.listing_timeline: not stated
judge.read_next: RCPL's standalone EBITDA, which Reliance Retail's CFO said would only be disclosed "next quarter" (Jan 2026 call).
judge.quote: With a broad and diverse product basket ranging from classic Indian brands to new age labels, the consumer products vertical is progressing on its accelerated growth trajectory with a focused organizational structure.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is Reliance's FMCG/consumer-brands arm. Under a composite scheme of arrangement among Reliance Retail Limited, Reliance Retail Ventures Limited (RRVL), the old Reliance Consumer Products Limited (RCPL) and Tira Beauty Limited (renamed Reliance Consumer Products Limited, 'New RCPL'), the 'Consumer Brands Business Undertaking' was demerged out of RRVL effective 1 December 2025; the old RCPL stood dissolved, RRVL shareholders received 1 New RCPL share of Rs.10 for every 2 RRVL shares of Rs.10, New RCPL's pre-scheme capital held by RRVL was cancelled without consideration, and RCPL became an 83.56% DIRECT subsidiary of RIL instead of sitting under retail — confirmed on the Jan 2026 call ('RCPL became the direct subsidiary of RIL from 1st December 2025'). The only explicit rationale management gave is organisational focus and growth speed: the 16 January 2026 media release said the consumer products vertical, 'ranging from classic Indian brands to new age labels,' is 'progressing on its accelerated growth trajectory with a focused organizational structure.' Everything else they offered was scale and investment facts that imply the logic: FMCG revenue of Rs.5,000 cr in Q3 FY26 (+60% Y-o-Y), Rs.15,000 cr for 9M FY26, Rs.22,000 cr for FY26 and Rs.7,350 cr in Q4 FY26 (both ~2x), Campa at Rs.4,700 cr (4th largest CSD brand), Independence at Rs.2,600 cr, #3 water player, Rs.8,600 cr in Q1 FY27 (2x, beverages Rs.2,900 cr, daily essentials Rs.3,200 cr, #3 NARTD), 5,000+ distributors, 3 million outlets, >80% of sales through external channels, 40 export markets, 12 plants plus integrated food parks and an acquisition run (Udhaiyam, Manna, Goodness Group, Sosyo majority, Brylcreem, Toni & Guy, Badedas, Matey) — i.e. a heavy-capex, acquisitive, breakeven-EBITDA business ('yes, we are breakeven on EBITDA terms') chasing Rs.1 lakh crore by FY2030, run through third-party general trade, which fits poorly inside a ~7.9-8.0% margin omni-channel retailer. The visible consequence management kept quantifying was the drag it removes from retail's reported growth: Q4 FY26 retail growth of 11% was 'almost 14%' adjusted for the demerger, and Q1 FY27 was 7.4% reported versus 11.6% underlying. No investor, lender or partner was named as having asked for it — the scheme was presented as done, and analysts (Harit Kapoor, Vikash Jain, Percy Panthaki) only pressed afterwards for the like-for-like revenue and EBITDA impact, which Dinesh Taluja deferred ('It is a number which is going out. It is a number as well... We will have to wait for the next quarter'). Two parallel separation tracks run alongside it: the Jio Platforms IPO (fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares, DRHP 19 June 2026, SEBI observation letter 28 August 2026, RHP 14 October 2026, priced at Rs.1,119 on 24 October 2026, with Rs.2,500 cr reserved for individual/HUF RIL shareholders and Rs.500 cr for employees), and the ring-fencing of AI/data-centre capex into RIL/'Reliance Intelligence' with JPL kept asset-light ('the AI data centers are not being done in Jio Platforms Limited').
rationale.evolution: On the Oct 2024 call the consumer-brands business was still reported inside Reliance Retail as a line item ('general trade revenues are growing at 250% plus'), with no hint of a separation. By the Jan 2026 call (16 Jan 2026) it was presented as a completed fact — 'the demerger happened on 1st December' — RCPL had become a direct RIL subsidiary, got its own presenter (Ketan Mody) and its own revenue disclosure, and the same-day media release supplied the only stated reason: 'a focused organizational structure' and an 'accelerated growth trajectory.' On the Apr 2026 and Jul 2026 calls the demerger appeared only as a base adjustment to retail growth (11% reported vs ~14% adjusted; 7.4% vs 11.6%), while RCPL's own disclosure escalated to Rs.22,000 cr FY26 revenue, EBITDA breakeven and a Rs.1 lakh crore FY2030 target. In parallel, the Jio Platforms listing moved from 'imminent' and 'awaiting the new notification from the government' (Jan/Apr 2026) to DRHP on 19 June 2026 and pricing at Rs.1,119 on 24 October 2026.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is not a shipping line but SCI's non-core land and property portfolio, carved out into a separate listed-to-be entity, Shipping Corporation of India Land and Assets Limited (SCILAL), with SCI as the 'Demerged Company' and SCILAL as the 'Resulting Company'. The filings state the mechanics precisely: MCA approved the demerger scheme by order dated 22.02.2023, 192 non-core assets were transferred from SCI to SCILAL with effect from 01 April 2021, and 185 of those assets are leased back to SCI so that the shipping operations can keep using the premises they occupy. The stated reason the separation exists is the Government of India's strategic disinvestment of SCI: note 7 says the process is being run by the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) with a Transaction Advisor, that the Preliminary Information Memorandum inviting expressions of interest was released on 22.12.2020, and that the Virtual Data Room is open and being managed by the Transaction Advisor for due diligence by Qualified Interested Parties — i.e. the buyer is being sold the shipping company, and the real estate is being kept out of the sale. So the asker is the owner-seller (the Government, via DIPAM and its Transaction Advisor) and the audience is prospective strategic bidders, not lenders or JV partners; no investor on either call asked for it. The problem it solves, as the documents frame it, is that the land and buildings are 'non-core' to a shipping business and would otherwise sit inside the entity being privatised; the leaseback keeps SCI operationally whole after they leave its balance sheet. The separation is still unfinished: the leaseback is accounted for as a short-term lease only because the final lease agreement has not been executed, pending the disinvestment process, and the joint statutory auditors (D. R. Mohnot & Co and PSD & Associates) flag both note 7 and note 8 as emphasis-of-matter items in the 31.12.2025 limited review. Management itself volunteered none of this on the calls — the only live discussion was a question about a possible reverse merger of SCILAL back into SCI, which the CMD declined to answer on the ground that SCILAL is a separate legal entity and the decision rests with the Government and the Ministry.
rationale.evolution: On the Q2 FY26 call of 10 November 2025 the demerger, SCILAL and the disinvestment were not raised at all — management's entire strategic narrative was additive (the 59-vessel oil-PSU JV, the 2047 business plan, VLGC inductions), not separative. It surfaced only on the Q4 FY26 call of 11 May 2026, and then from an investor: Amitabh Vatsya of Sadhan Ventures asked about 'rumours or some news about reverse merger of SILAL with SCI', citing a signed NBCC MOU, and Capt. Tyagi answered that the NBCC MOU concerns upgrading SCI's Powai training institute and that SCILAL is a separate legal entity on which only the Government/Ministry can decide, adding 'We have no information regarding this at this stage.' Across the three filings of 06.02.2026 the language is unchanged and boilerplate — same note 7, same note 8, same auditor emphasis — so the only movement in the period is directional ambiguity (an investor floating reversal of the demerger) rather than any new company disclosure.

points.point: Note 8 of the 31.12.2025 standalone and consolidated results sets out the carve-out: MCA order dated 22.02.2023, 192 non-core assets moved from SCI to SCILAL effective 01 April 2021, and 185 of them leased back to SCI, with the leaseback treated as a short-term lease only because the final agreement is unexecuted pending disinvestment.

points.point: Note 7 names who is driving the separation and why it is still open — DIPAM with a Transaction Advisor, a PIM issued 22.12.2020, and a Virtual Data Room currently open for due diligence by Qualified Interested Parties, i.e. prospective strategic buyers of the shipping business.
points.quote: The proposed strategic disinvestment of SCI is being handled by Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) with the engagement of Transaction Advisor. In this regard, Preliminary Information Memorandum (PIM) for inviting expression of interest was released on 22.12.2020. The Virtual Data Room is open and is being managed by the Transaction Advisor for the process of due diligence by the Qualified Interested Parties.

points.point: The joint statutory auditors draw attention to the demerger and leaseback as an emphasis-of-matter in their limited review report dated 06.02.2026, expressly tying management's short-term-lease judgement to the unexecuted formal lease agreement and the disinvestment process.

points.point: An investor (Amitabh Vatsya, Sadhan Ventures) raised press reports of a reverse merger of SCILAL back into SCI, linking it to a newly signed NBCC MOU — the only time the separation was discussed live on either call.
points.quote: So, is there are some rumours or some news about reverse merger of SILAL with SCI?

points.point: Capt. B.K. Tyagi declined to give any rationale or status, treating SCILAL as outside SCI's control and the decision as the Government's/Ministry's alone, and disclaiming any information.
points.quote: As far as this SCILAL and SCI reversal is concerned, SCILAL is a separate legal entity, and this is a matter where Government, our Ministry will take decision if at all anything is there.

points.point: He redirected the question to the NBCC MOU's actual purpose — upgrading and better utilising SCI's large maritime training institute at Powai, alongside an MOU with international ship manager Synergy — not to any land-entity restructuring.
points.quote: See, number one, this NBCC MOU was signed few days back. And idea is we have got a one big training institute in Powai.

points.point: The November 2025 call contains no reference to the demerger, SCILAL, non-core assets or disinvestment; management's strategic framing was entirely about adding entities (a 50%-owned oil-PSU JV for 59 vessels, later Bharat Container Shipping Line) rather than separating existing ones.
points.quote: It will be a separate entity and where SCI will hold a shareholding up to 50%.

rationale.what_management_expects: Nothing was stated on either call — no margin, capital, valuation or focus claim for SCI or SCILAL. Only the filings imply the intent: 192 non-core land assets sit in SCILAL while SCI operates on 185 leased back, keeping property out of the shipping entity DIPAM is selling. The sole forward statement was upgrading the Powai training institute via the NBCC/Synergy MOUs.
rationale.gaps: No rationale, valuation, rent quantum, lease term, timetable, SCILAL listing/shareholding plan, or buyer status; management would not address the reverse-merger reports or confirm anything about SCILAL.

judge.listing_timeline: not stated as a listing date; appointed date 1 March 2025 and effective date 25 March 2025 (stated 14 November 2025), and at the 12 December 2025 analyst meet SEIL was described as 'now a separately listed pure play energy company'
judge.read_next: Siemens Energy India Limited's own results and the Scheme, for the Rs 37,846 million net assets and Rs 25,478 million cash transferred
judge.quote: Pursuant to receipt of necessary statutory approvals and in accordance with the Scheme, the Company has demerged the Energy business effective 25 March 2025, with appointed date being 1 March 2025, as per the Scheme.

listing.text: RECORD DATE set; the resulting company not yet listed — resulting companies have typically listed 4–10 weeks after the record date

rationale.rationale: Siemens Ltd. has separated two businesses, and the one management explained in the most detail is the Low Voltage Motors (LVM, plus geared motors and related customer service) business, sold as a going concern on a slump-sale basis to Innomotics India Private Limited for an enterprise value of INR 22 billion (INR 2,200 crore), cash-free/debt-free. The trigger was not Indian: on 1 October 2024 Siemens AG sold the global Innomotics business — and all of its intellectual property — to KPS Capital Partners, leaving the Indian unit as, in Sunil Mathur's words, a licensed sales organisation with no IP, no manufacturing (contract-manufactured to Innomotics design, ~97% of the Business's revenue) and survival dependent on an Agency & Distributorship Agreement and a Technical Cooperation & License Agreement with an entity now controlled by a private-equity owner. So the counterparty, not investors or lenders, effectively forced the decision: the Board stated the Business could not be sold to anyone else because Innomotics owns the IP, making the only alternatives selling to Innomotics India or restructuring the Business and bearing those costs. The numbers management cited were small and deteriorating: for the 12 months to 30 September 2025, revenue from operations of INR 9.67 billion (INR 967 crore) and profit from operations of INR 0.35 billion (INR 35 crore) — 6% of the company's revenue and ~2.2% of its profit from operations ex-Energy — with net capital employed of negative INR 1.38 billion, orders down 6.9% y/y in Q2 FY25, H1 EBITDA of 7.8% (down 130bps on lower price realisation and higher royalties paid to Innomotics), volumes that 'have not increased', cyclicality tied to private-sector capex and copper, and only 89 sales employees; the filing also recorded negative net worth of INR 1,175.66 million and 4.53% of revenue in FY24. Management said synergies with the rest of Siemens Ltd. were 'very limited' and framed the exit as portfolio optimisation that creates value and cash while giving customers and employees continuity. Price was set after negotiation using two independent valuations (Grant Thornton Bharat LLP and KPMG Valuation Services LLP) as at 30 September 2025, and Mathur stressed INR 22 billion was 'the same price that had been offered earlier on by the parent company' despite volumes having since declined. The earlier, larger separation was the Energy demerger into Siemens Energy India Limited (appointed date 1 March 2025, effective 25 March 2025), justified as creating two independent pure-play companies focused on their relevant markets, each with a large backlog; it transferred net assets of INR 37,846 million including INR 25,478 million of cash, cost INR 1.0 billion of demerger expenses in FY25 versus INR 0.1 billion in FY24, and under the November 2023 disclosure the promoters agreed procedures to let Siemens Energy AG acquire a majority in the new listed entity.
rationale.evolution: Dec 2024 call (20 Dec 2024): only the Energy demerger is discussed as a separation — 'on track', creating two independent companies, with LVM not yet flagged as a portfolio issue. May 2025 call (20 May 2025): after the Siemens AG–KPS Innomotics deal of October 2024 and visible margin pressure from royalties paid to Innomotics, management formally said it would 'explore options for the future' of LVM. Dec 2025 (board 8 Dec 2025; analyst meet 12 Dec 2025): the option became a signed slump-sale agreement with Innomotics India at INR 22 billion, justified by lost IP, no local manufacturing, declining volumes (6% of revenue, 2% of profit) and shareholder interest, with closing guided to mid-2026. Jun 2026 call (28 May 2026) reconfirmed completion 'on track for June 2026'; the sale closed 1 June 2026 with a provisional gain of INR 20,990 million, while in the opposite direction the Board approved amalgamating subsidiary Siemens Rail Automation into the parent (26 May 2026) and took C&S Electric to 100% via capital reduction (NCLT order 24 September 2026).

points.point: CFO Wrumnig first links LVM's fate to the parent's global divestment of Innomotics to KPS Capital Partners and to the Indian unit's technical dependence on that business, announcing an options review.
points.quote: In view of this sale and the dependency on the global Innomotics business, we will now explore options for the future of the Low Voltage Motors business.

points.point: The economics were already visibly impaired: weak orders, price pressure and royalties payable to the new KPS-owned owner of the IP compressing margins.
points.quote: Year-to-date, the business reported an EbitDA margin of 7.8%, down by 130bps due to lower price realization and higher royalties paid to Innomotics, the former global Siemens business, now owned by KPS Capital Partners.

points.point: Mathur describes what Siemens Ltd. actually owned in LVM — a licence to sell someone else's product, with outsourced manufacturing and no IP rights in India.
points.quote: It is within Siemens Limited. It is outsourced manufacturing. Revenues are cyclical, as you know, for motors.

points.point: The volume thesis that justified keeping the business had failed, tied to muted private-sector capex and copper prices.
points.quote: The expectation was that the volumes will increase. Those volumes have not increased in the country.

points.point: Board approval of the slump sale to Innomotics India at INR 22 billion, explicitly the same price the parent had offered earlier, with closing guided to mid-2026.
points.quote: And this was then finally approved by the board of Siemens Limited in terms of a sale and transfer on a slump sale basis to Innomotics India at a purchase price of 22 billion, which I will remind you was the same price that had been offered earlier on by the parent company.

points.point: Materiality and shareholder-interest framing: the business had shrunk to 6% of volumes and 2% of profits.
points.quote: Considering the fact that the volumes have declined, in the meantime, it is only 6% of the overall volume of Siemens and only 2% of Siemens profits in the meantime.

points.point: The prior, bigger separation is presented as completed and successful — Energy is now a separately listed pure-play, leaving Siemens Ltd. with DI, SI and Mobility.
points.quote: A major development during this period has been the demerger of Siemens Energy India Limited, which is now a separately listed pure play energy company.

points.point: Rationale originally given for the Energy demerger: two focused, independently capitalised companies each with large backlogs.
points.quote: Both companies are very well prepared for the future growth, focusing on their relevant markets.

points.point: Final status update before closing; the quarter also shows demerger-related expenses falling by INR 500 million as separation costs roll off.
points.quote: And third, on the portfolio topic, the sale of the low-voltage motors business is on track for completion in June 2026.

points.point: Filing of 8 Dec 2025 states the hard constraint: without Innomotics/KPS support Siemens Ltd. cannot run the business, which is why the only buyer was the counterparty itself.
points.quote: The Company itself does not have the requisite intellectual property or other capabilities to service the Business without support from Innomotics GmbH which is now owned by KPS.

points.point: Strategic-fit argument plus the stated financial benefit of exiting — portfolio optimisation generating value and cash.
points.quote: Synergies between the Business and the rest of the Company’s businesses are very limited.

points.point: Price discovery and process: negotiated against two independent valuations as at 30 September 2025, outside any scheme of arrangement and not a related-party transaction.
points.quote: The consideration for the sale and transfer of the Business has been determined after negotiation between the Company and the Buyer, taking into account two separate independent valuation reports of the Business as at 30th September 2025 pursuant to independent valuation exercises conducted by each of Grant Thornton Bharat LLP and                 KPMG Valuation Services LLP .

points.point: Completion on 1 June 2026 at INR 22 billion enterprise value, booking a provisional one-time gain of INR 20,990 million (INR 2,099 crore) in discontinued operations.
points.quote: Basis the preliminary sale consideration, a provisional gain of Rs. 20,990 million is recognized during the quarter ended 30 June 2026 and six months period ended 30 September 2026.

rationale.what_management_expects: For Siemens Ltd.: a cleaner three-business technology portfolio (DI, SI, Mobility), removal of a sub-scale, negative-capital-employed, royalty-burdened unit worth 6% of revenue but only 2% of profit, INR 22 billion of cash plus an INR 2,099 crore gain, and portfolio optimisation 'creating value and cash'. For Innomotics India: ownership aligned with the IP it already holds, continuity for LVM customers and the 89 sales staff. For Energy: an independent pure-play.
rationale.gaps: No post-sale margin, ROCE or capital-deployment guidance; no bridge from the 2024 parent offer to INR 22 billion; silent on employee transfer terms, ADA/TCLA wind-down, and buyer-selection alternatives.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is not a spirits brand but USL's wholly owned cricket subsidiary, Royal Challengers Sports Private Limited (RCSPL), which owns and operates the Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) franchises in the IPL and the Women's Premier League; USL agreed on March 24, 2026 to sell 100% of RCSPL (14,690 equity shares) to a consortium of Aditya Birla Group (Aelius Investments Pte Ltd), The Times of India Group (Times Internet Limited and Metropolitan Media Company Limited), Bolt Ventures (Bolt IPL Holdings LLC) and Blackstone's perpetual private equity strategy BXPE (Asia Investment Topco II Pte. Ltd.) for INR 166.6 bn in an all-cash transaction. The only rationale management actually gave, in MD & CEO Praveen Someshwar's press-release comment, is focus: the deal lets USL 'sharpen focus on our core beverage alcohol business to unlock its true potential with sustained growth' and continue 'long-term value creation for our stakeholders.' The second stated reason is that the asset has outgrown its owner's purpose — RCB is 'the most prominent and commercially successful franchise in the IPL and WPL' with a globally recognised brand, and 'As Sports enters a new phase of growth in India & globally, we believe this is in the best interest of the franchise and our stakeholders,' i.e. the franchise needs an owner whose business is sport. The size disclosure makes the focus argument concrete and also shows the valuation gap: RCSPL contributed revenue from operations of only INR 504 crore in FY24-25 (1.9% of USL standalone revenue) and net worth of INR 321 crore as at March 31, 2025 (4.1% of USL standalone net worth), and USL expressly notes RCSPL 'is not a material subsidiary of USL' — yet it fetched INR 166.6 bn, roughly 50x its book net worth, in cash. No operational problem, loss, capital drain, covenant, partner demand or investor campaign is cited anywhere in the supplied texts as the trigger; the stated problems solved are strategic focus and stewardship of the franchise, not fixing a weak business. Structurally the separation is a clean cash share sale rather than a demerger or scheme of arrangement (the filing marks 'Whether the sale... is outside Scheme of Arrangement' as not applicable), with USL ceasing to hold any shareholding and RCSPL ceasing to be a subsidiary on completion. Residual ties are limited and transitional: USL and its affiliates will provide certain support services to RCSPL on a transitory basis, and a co-existence arrangement will govern usage of certain brand names between USL and RCSPL, both effective only from completion. Conditions are customary plus approvals from the Board of Control for Cricket in India and the Competition Commission of India, with completion expected within six months of March 24, 2026; Citigroup India advised USL and AZB Partners was counsel.
rationale.evolution: In the only readable call, May 23, 2025, there is no separation idea at all — RCB is presented as a core strength, a 'differentiated asset' with exceptional brand equity ranking among the top five global sports teams on engagement behind only Real Madrid and FC Barcelona (the sole divestment-adjacent remark is analyst Harit Kapoor's aside that one Lower Prestige brand 'could be on the block,' which management did not address). The idea surfaces formally on November 5, 2025, the date the March 2026 filings repeatedly cite as when USL announced and 'initiated' a strategic review of RCSPL. It concludes at the board meeting of March 24, 2026 (18:09–19:00 IST), where the SPA was approved and the press release states the announcement 'concludes the strategic review of RCSPL that was initiated by USL, as announced on November 05, 2025' — i.e. the review ended in a full exit rather than a partial stake sale or demerger. The Nov 2025, Jan 2026 and May 2026 call transcripts supplied here have no extractable text, so management's call-by-call commentary between review and signing cannot be reconstructed from these documents.

points.point: RCB is framed as a core competitive asset, not a candidate for separation — management highlights its brand equity and global engagement ranking, with no mention of a review or sale.
points.quote: RCB, our differentiated asset continues to build on its strength.

points.point: The only divestment hint on a readable call is an analyst's passing reference to a Lower Prestige brand being up for sale; management's reply discussed Andhra Pradesh-driven growth and did not confirm or address any sale.
points.quote: I understand in the Lower Prestige, there's also one of the brands, which could be on the block.

points.point: USL's board approved the sale of all 14,690 equity shares of RCSPL — a 100% exit from the IPL/WPL franchise owner — for INR 166.6 bn in cash, under an SPA dated March 24, 2026.
points.quote: has inter alia approved the sale of 14,690 equity shares of Ro yal Challengers Sports Private Limited (“ RCSPL ”), a wholly owned subsidiary of USL for an aggregate consideration of INR 166.6 bn

points.point: Management's stated rationale is focus on the core alcobev business and value creation, not repair of a problem business.
points.quote: “This transaction marks an important milestone for USL as we sharpen focus on our core beverage alcohol business to unlock its true pot ential with sustained growth, and to continue delivering on long-term value creation for our  stakeholders.

points.point: The second rationale is stewardship: sport is entering a new growth phase, so new owners are better placed to take RCB forward.
points.quote: As Sports enters a new phase of growth in India & globally,  we believe this is in the best interest of the franchise and our stakeholders.

points.point: RCSPL was financially small relative to USL — FY24-25 revenue INR 504 crore (1.9% of USL standalone revenue) and net worth INR 321 crore (4.1%) — and is explicitly not a material subsidiary, underlining the valuation unlock versus book value.
points.quote: Further, it is noted that RCSPL is not a material subsidiary of USL.

points.point: The deal closes a process begun months earlier: the strategic review announced on November 5, 2025 ends in a full divestiture.
points.quote: This announcement concludes the strategic review of RCSPL that was initiated by USL, as announced on November 05, 2025.

points.point: Buyers are a four-party consortium with sport, media, brand and capital credentials — ABG, Times of India Group, Bolt Ventures and Blackstone's BXPE — none of them related to USL's promoter group, and the transaction is not a related-party transaction.

points.point: Post-completion ties are deliberately limited: transitional support services from USL and a brand-name co-existence arrangement, both effective only on completion.
points.quote: Further, the SPA contemplates, upon and on from completion of the Proposed Transaction, the provision of certain support services by USL and its relevant affiliated entities to RCSPL on a transitory basis, and a co-existence arrangement governing the usage of certain brand names as between USL and RCSPL, each of which will be entered into only upon completion of the Proposed Transaction and effective therefrom.

points.point: Closing needs BCCI and CCI clearance and is expected within six months of signing; USL will hold no shares in RCSPL thereafter.
points.quote: USL wi ll cease to hold any s hareholding in RCSPL and consequently RCSPL will cease to be a subsidiary of USL.

rationale.what_management_expects: For USL: sharper focus on the core beverage-alcohol business to 'unlock its true potential with sustained growth' and long-term stakeholder value creation, plus INR 166.6 bn of all-cash proceeds against RCSPL's INR 321 crore net worth. For RCB: growth under owners with sport, media, technology and brand-building strengths as sport enters a new global phase. No margin, capital-allocation or valuation numbers for the remaining business were given.
rationale.gaps: No use of proceeds, no EPS/margin/ROCE impact, no capital-return plan, no mention of who pushed for it, and no readable call Q&A on the review or sale.

rationale.rationale: Nothing in these three years of earnings calls or in the filings provided describes Premier Energies separating, demerging, spinning off or hiving off any business, and there is no scheme of arrangement in the record — so the premise of the question cannot be supported from these texts. The direction management describes is the opposite: consolidation and diversification into one group. Across the Nov 2025, Jan 2026 and May 2026 calls the company adds businesses rather than sheds them — a 51% stake in transformer maker Transcon Ind Limited for up to ₹5,003.00 million (₹2,500.02 million for 34.21% in Dec 2025, the balance ₹2,502.98 million in April 2026, taking Transcon and its subsidiary Neotrafo to subsidiary/step-down status), a 51% inverter JV with Syrma SGS around KSolare (FY25 revenue cited at ₹143 crores), a 6 GWh-per-phase cell-to-pack BESS line at ₹280 crores, aluminium frames at ₹260 crores, a 10 GW ingot-wafer project at about ₹5,900 crores, and a 51% stake in HeliosAnthos Energies for ₹10.45 lakh. Management's stated rationale for keeping these together is synergy, not separation: Vinay Rustagi argued 10 GVA of transformer demand per GW of renewable capacity added, with roughly 80% of installs now renewable, so transformers, inverters and BESS go to 'the same clients who we are selling our modules', 'reducing the cost of customer acquisition', and the new businesses together with BESS are expected to contribute 'approximately 30% of our revenue over time'. The only two events in the record that even resemble a separation are (a) the voluntary winding-up by strike-off of IBD Solar Powertech (Pvt.) Ltd, a Bangladesh step-down wholly owned subsidiary with nil revenue, nil turnover contribution and negative net worth of ₹2.09 lakh, where the Reg. 30 annexure marks every sale/disposal/scheme field 'Not Applicable'; and (b) the abandonment of the KSolare acquisition in Q1 FY27 — a reversal of an inbound deal, not a carve-out, with 'no financial implications arising from the same'. There is also an accounting-only split — Power Transmission & Distribution Equipment became a separate reportable segment under Ind AS 108 from the Transcon acquisition date — but that is segment disclosure, not a legal or structural separation. On these texts alone, there is no separation to explain, and no investor, lender or partner is recorded as asking for one.
rationale.evolution: The idea never surfaces: in Feb 2025 and May 2025 management frames 'Mission 2028' as a single integrated 10 GW ingot-wafer-cell-module platform plus BESS and inverters, with ₹125,000 million of capex inside one group. Jul 2025 and Nov 2025 add, not subtract — the 4.8 GW cell line is scaled to 7 GW, and the KSolare (inverter) and Transcon (transformer) acquisitions are announced as 'highly complementary and value accretive'. Jan 2026 reports the Transcon acquisition completed in Dec 2025 and KSolare closing 'in the next one month'; by May 2026 the KSolare deal is dropped for lack of agreement on final documentation while Transcon's 51% is completed, and the Aug 2026 and Sep 2026 filings record only a new reportable segment and the strike-off of the dormant Bangladesh shell. At no point in May 2025, Jul 2025, Nov 2025, Jan 2026 or May 2026 does any analyst or executive mention a demerger, spin-off, slump sale or scheme.

points.point: The only disposal-type disclosure in the filings is the strike-off of a dormant, non-operating Bangladesh step-down subsidiary — not a business separation; the Reg. 30 annexure marks turnover contribution nil, net worth negative ₹2.09 lakh, and every sale/disposal/scheme-of-arrangement field 'Not Applicable'.
points.quote: IBD, had no revenue or commercial operations and had filed an application for voluntary winding-up by way of strike off of name on 10th October, 2023 with the Office of the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms, Bangladesh.

points.point: The filings explicitly confirm no scheme of arrangement or undertaking disposal is involved in that winding-up.
points.quote: Whether the sale, lease or disposal of the undertaking is outside Scheme of Arrangement? If yes, details of the same including compliance with regulation 37A of LODR Regulations.  Not Applicable

points.point: Management's stated logic is combination, not separation: the inverter and transformer acquisitions are kept inside the group precisely because they are complementary and are expected to supply about 30% of revenue over time.
points.quote: Both these acquisitions are highly complementary and value accretive.

points.point: Rustagi quantified the cross-sell synergy that argues against separating the equipment businesses — roughly 10 GVA of transformer demand per GW of capacity added, sold to the same module customers.
points.quote: there is a, you know, 10x the 10 GVA is the demand for transformers.

points.point: Transcon is described as a future growth engine being scaled sevenfold inside the group (2.5 GVA to 16.75 GVA by July 2026) and moved up into MV/HV/EHV, with a ₹1,000 crore-plus top line targeted by FY28 — the opposite of a carve-out.
points.quote: This business is expected to become a key growth contributor for us.

points.point: The one deal that was unwound was an inbound acquisition (KSolare), dropped over documentation terms, with the inverter ambition retained in-house via the SMA/Syrma SGS JV route — again no separation of an existing Premier business.
points.quote: I think that is the reason why the transaction could not be completed.

points.point: The only 'split' in the record is an accounting one: a new reportable segment created by the Transcon acquisition under Ind AS 108, effective from the April 3, 2026 acquisition date.
points.quote: Consequently, the Company has identified Power Transmission & Distribution Equipment as a separate reportable segment in accordance with the requirements of Ind AS 108 - Operating Segments.

points.point: Forward capital plans are framed as one diversified platform funded centrally (FY27 capex ₹5,100 crores across cells, ingot-wafers, batteries and inverters; ₹5,000 crores enabling fundraise resolution), with no mention of releasing capital by separating an entity.
points.quote: FY27 is a year of large capex for us at INR5,100 crores to be deployed across cells, ingot wafers, batteries and inverters.

rationale.what_management_expects: Not applicable — no separation is described. Management's stated expectations are for the combined group: ~30% of revenue from inverters, BESS and transformers over time; Transcon margins rising toward 20-25% EBITDA as mix shifts to MV/HV/EHV with 7x-10x fixed-asset turns; cross-sell synergies lowering customer-acquisition cost; and debt/equity held near 1.0 and debt/EBITDA near 1.5 through the capex cycle.
rationale.gaps: The calls and filings never mention any demerger, spin-off, slump sale or scheme of arrangement, so no rationale, no requesting party, and no expected benefits are explained anywhere.
