rationale.rationale: Across all four transcripts (Oct 2025, Nov 2025, Feb 2026, May 2026) and both filings, Saatvik Green Energy announces NO separation, demerger, spin-off or scheme of arrangement of any business, so no management rationale for one exists in these texts; the stated strategy is the opposite — consolidating a single integrated platform. Management repeatedly describes building "entire integrated forward, backward and sideways energy company" spanning ingot/wafer, cell (scaled from 4.8 GW to 6 GW), module (8.8 GW), encapsulant (2 GW commissioned in Ambala, roadmap raised to 5 GW), inverters (UDAY series), solar pumps, EPC, BESS, transformers and components — with backward integration justified as cost competitiveness, margin sustainability and supply-chain security, worth an additional 3-5% EBITDA on self-produced cell volume. The only 'separation' language is about creating standalone business units/entities INSIDE the group, not divesting: solar pumps (INR ~2 crore FY25 revenue, targeted INR 50-80 crore in FY26, 4,000-5,000 pumps, 15,000 next year) described as "a division which has a potential of becoming a separate business unit"; encapsulant built "not only for our supply chain resilience, but also as a separate business unit" because third-party module makers "are ready to pay a premium on encapsulant" (5-10% internal saving, 7-10% of module cost); plus Saatvik Power Storage Solutions Limited launched for BESS and an 80% stake bought in Melcon Transformers and Electricals. Capacity is also being housed in separate legal vehicles — subsidiary Saatvik Solar Industries Private Limited (FY25 turnover INR 11,852.52 million) holds the new-technology capacity and carries a 15% concessional tax rate versus 25% at the parent, pulling the blended rate to 18-20% — which is corporate structuring, not a separation. Management cites capital needs that argue against breaking anything off: INR 1,850 crore Odisha capex (INR 1,300-1,350 crore cell, INR 550 crore module), INR 1,700 crore FY27 capex, INR 1,800-2,500 crore for the 6 GW ingot project in FY28, funded 70:30 debt:equity at 8.9-9%, with debt-equity to be held between 1.0x and 1.5x (0.65x in FY26 versus 1.34x in FY25). No investor, lender or partner in any of these calls asks for a separation, and no analyst question on the topic appears.
rationale.evolution: The idea never surfaces as a corporate separation in any call. Oct 10, 2025 (Q1FY26) is the first time 'separate business unit' appears, as an internal ambition for solar pumps; Nov 10, 2025 (Q2FY26) adds the subsidiary tax-rate point and Saatvik Solar Industries as the order-taking entity; Feb 5, 2026 (Q3FY26) hardens solar pumps into a targeted "standalone business unit" (then only 0.35% of revenue); May 21, 2026 (Q4FY26) extends the pattern to encapsulant as a merchant business unit, a new BESS company (Saatvik Power Storage Solutions Limited) and the Melcon transformer acquisition — all additions to the group, never a carve-out.

points.point: Solar pumps, scaling from under INR 2 crore to about INR 50 crore of revenue, is first flagged as a candidate to become its own business unit inside the group.
points.quote: So, the kind of growth which will be seen from less than INR2 crores revenue last year to about INR50 crores revenue this year and that is also a division which has a potential of becoming a separate business unit.

points.point: The strategic direction stated by the CEO is full integration across the value chain plus adjacencies, not separation of any business.
points.quote: So, all in all we are building -- we are also doing BESS projects and ultimately the target is to get into battery storage products also. So, all in all we are building entire integrated forward, backward and sideways energy company, renewable energy company especially.

points.point: Management explicitly says module capacity will be capped around 9-10 GW and growth will come from backward integration into cell and ingot-wafer, i.e. consolidation rather than divestment.
points.quote: So, our focus is not to grow our module capacities beyond 9, 10 gigawatts because that is a respectable where you can get economies of scale and we will focus on building our backward integration towards cell, towards ingot wafer and also bring in more products, you know, which are supportive to our solar module business in this industry.

points.point: The only entity-level rationale given is tax: new capacity sits in subsidiary Saatvik Solar at a 15% rate versus 25% at the parent, lowering the blended rate to 18-20%.
points.quote: So, in Saatvik Green Energy, we have normal tax rate, while in comparison , Saatvik Solar has a preferred rate at the rate of 15%. So, more revenue from Saatvik Solar Industries, the lower tax rate overall.

points.point: Solar pumps, at 0.35% of revenue, are being formalised as a standalone business unit within the company during FY26.
points.quote: This year we target to make it a business unit, a standalone business unit.

points.point: The 2 GW (now 5 GW roadmap) EPE encapsulant plant is being run as its own business unit selling to third-party module makers at a premium, on top of 5-10% internal cost savings on 7-10% of module cost.
points.quote: So initially we started this 2 gigawatt for our internal usage, but what we have found is that there are, you know, manufacturers who are not good at planning and they are not importing, they are not able to secure. So they are ready to pay a premium on encapsulant.

points.point: New activities are being placed in new legal vehicles and acquisitions rather than separated out of the company: a BESS company was launched and 80% of a transformer maker was bought.
points.quote: In parallel, we launched Saatvik Power Storage Solutions Limited, focused on battery energy storage systems.

points.point: Capital plans point to heavier consolidation, not separation: INR 1,700 crore FY27 capex and about INR 2,500 crore for the 6 GW ingot project, with gearing held at 1.0-1.5x.
points.quote: So, for FY27, our capex requirement for this expansion is about 1,700 crores.

points.point: No scheme of arrangement, demerger or spin-off is present in the filings; the only structural filing is a INR 251.60 crore rights-issue infusion into wholly owned subsidiary SSIPL for the Odisha 4 GW module plant, with no change in shareholding, alongside a postal ballot on an independent director and ESOP ratification.
points.quote: There will be no change in the percentage of shareholding of the Company in SSIPL . It will continue to remain a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.

rationale.what_management_expects: Nothing is claimed for a separation, because none is announced. For the internal business units they expect: encapsulant to add merchant sales plus 5-10% input savings; cell integration to add 3-5% EBITDA on captive volume, DCR pricing and "value unlocking"; solar pumps to scale to INR 50-80 crore then 15,000 pumps; subsidiary structure to cut blended tax to 18-20%.
rationale.gaps: Everything about a separation: no demerger, scheme, record date, entity perimeters, debt or capex allocation, valuation, listing plan, or any investor, lender or partner request for one.

rationale.rationale: No separation, demerger, spin-off, slump sale, scheme of arrangement or carve-out of any business is mentioned anywhere in the four earnings calls (Aug 2025, Nov 2025, Feb 2026, Jun 2026) or in the single filing provided (the 13 August 2026 Outcome of Board Meeting with Q1 FY27 standalone and consolidated results and limited review reports). On the contrary, management describes Travel Food Services as one integrated platform and the auditor-reviewed results state that travel QSR, lounges and related services 'comprise of only one operating segment' reviewed by the Board as the Chief Operating Decision Maker, which is the opposite of a separation narrative. The only structural changes discussed are: (1) the deconsolidation of JV entity Semolina Kitchens effective 14 October 2024, which management repeatedly frames purely as an accounting/comparability matter done 'as planned' (FY25 base restated to exclude Semolina; Q1 FY25 Semolina losses added back), not as a separation of a business with a strategic rationale; (2) the scheduled expiry on 30 September 2026 of the Delhi Terminal 3 licence held by 60:40 SPV Travel Food Services (Delhi Terminal 3) Private Limited (TFS 60%, DIAL 40%) — Varun Kapur said the SPV 'had a life tied into that concession' and that TFS would re-bid for Delhi T3 through its existing JV GMR Hospitality (GHL), with the filing noting a material uncertainty at the subsidiary level that 'does not give rise to a material uncertainty at the Group level'; and (3) new legal entities created to house growth, not to exit anything — wholly owned subsidiary Elite Assist Technology and Services (EATS) for the lounge-access tech platform, Travel Food Services Worldwide FZCO in Dubai (w.e.f. 10 July 2025) and PT Travel Food Services Indonesia (w.e.f. 23 September 2025) for international lounges. Management's stated direction across all four calls is expansion and consolidation of the same platform: 20 airports, 550+ travel QSR outlets and lounges, 145+ brands, FY26 system-wide sales of INR32.1 billion (+25.4%) and adjusted PAT of INR4.5 billion (+21.4%), zero debt with INR8.4 billion of cash, and new verticals (international lounges in Malaysia/Hong Kong/Middle East, wayside amenities on access-controlled expressways) all pursued inside the group. No investor, lender, airport partner or brand partner is recorded as asking for a separation; the only partner-related questions were about Adani/DreamFolks risk and SSP support, which Varun answered by pointing to deeper JV integration, not separation.
rationale.evolution: The idea never surfaces: across Aug 2025, Nov 2025, Feb 2026 and Jun 2026 no analyst asks about a demerger and management never raises one. The closest recurring thread is the Semolina Kitchens deconsolidation of 14 October 2024, repeated in identical accounting-comparability language in Aug 2025, Nov 2025, Feb 2026 and Jun 2026. The second thread is Delhi T3, which moves from 'contract comes up for renewal this financial year' (Nov 2025) to a six-month extension to 30 September 2026 with re-bidding intended through GHL (Feb 2026 and Jun 2026), confirmed in the 13 August 2026 filing as a licence expiry and subsidiary-level going-concern note. Entity creation runs the other way over time — EATS (Aug/Nov 2025), Dubai FZCO (July 2025) and Indonesia (September 2025) are added to pursue new business, not to separate existing business.

points.point: No scheme of arrangement, demerger or separation document exists in the material supplied; the only filing is the 13 August 2026 board outcome approving Q1 FY27 results, and its segment note affirms the group is run as a single business.
points.quote: The Group derives revenue exclusively from Travel QSR outlets, Lounge and related services. In the context of Indian Accounting Standard (Ind AS) 108 - Operating Segments, these products and service lines comprise of only one operating segment, whose operating results are regularly reviewed by the entity's Board of Directors ('Chief Operating Decision Maker') to make decisions about resources to be allocated and assess its performance.

points.point: The only entity whose life is ending is the Delhi T3 SPV, and only because its ten-year licence (with extensions) runs out on 30 September 2026 — an expiry, not a separation; the filing says the resulting uncertainty is confined to the subsidiary.
points.quote: After considering all extensions granted from time to time, the said licence agreement is scheduled to expire on 30 September 2026.

points.point: The filing explicitly ring-fences the Delhi T3 issue at subsidiary level, citing group cash flows and liquidity, and gives no separation rationale.
points.quote: Accordingly, while the above matter represents a material uncertainty at the Subsidiary level, it does not give rise to a material uncertainty at the Group level, and these Consolidated Financial Results have been prepared on a going concern basis.

points.point: The Semolina Kitchens deconsolidation is explained solely as an accounting restatement to permit like-for-like comparison of FY25 and FY26 — no strategic separation reason, no valuation or margin argument, no counterparty request.
points.quote: This entity was consolidated in our financials until October 14, 2024, and was subsequently deconsolidated.

points.point: Varun Kapur describes the Delhi T3 vehicle as a special purpose vehicle whose life was tied to the concession, and says TFS will simply re-bid through its existing JV, GHL — a contract-structure consequence rather than a business separation.
points.quote: It was operating through a special purpose vehicle, which had a life tied into that concession.

points.point: Asked about capital allocation with INR8 billion-plus of cash and zero debt, management pointed only to reinvestment in international lounges and expressway wayside amenities at ~45% ROCE — never to unlocking value via a separation.
points.quote: And as you can see, our ROCE have been at north of 40%, about 45% ROCEs.

points.point: Vikas Kapoor sets out the Delhi T3 SPV shareholding (TFS 60%, DIAL 40%) and says the renewal will go to open tender, with the winner consolidating the operations — the outcome depends on bidding, not on any planned separation.
points.quote: So our Delhi T3 is an existing joint venture as part of the SPV , when we had won that contract , wherein we hold 60% and DIAL holds 40%.

points.point: The Semolina adjustment is again framed as a planned deconsolidation for comparability only, with details in the presentation.
points.quote: Semolina Kitchens, was part of our consolidated financials for the first half and part of Q3 of FY '25 and was subsequently deconsolidated , as planned effective October 14, 2024.

points.point: The lounge-access technology business was placed in a wholly owned subsidiary, Elite Assist Technology and Services (EATS), to build a new capability inside the group — presented as integration with banks and card networks, removing aggregators, not as a carve-out.
points.quote: Additionally, at our lounges, we enable the technology platform to provide direct integration to banks and card networks for a smooth lounge access for their customers through our wholly owned subsidiary, Elite Assist Technology and Services.

points.point: Asked directly about partner concentration risk with Adani-operated airports (roughly 120 of the then 500+ units) and the DreamFolks precedent, Varun Kapur's answer was deeper joint-venture alignment with the airport operator — the opposite of separating the business.
points.quote: We already are in a joint venture with Adani Airports.

points.point: In the first post-listing call, management laid out the two commercial models (consolidated long-term contracts vs equity-accounted JVs/associates) and the reason for reporting system-wide sales; this is the structure of the business as designed, with no mention of separating any part of it.
points.quote: Long-term contracts are fully consolidated into our P&L and strategic partnerships are accounted as JVs or Associates under the equity pickup model.

points.point: The Semolina treatment is introduced as an added-back comparability adjustment for FY25 losses and FY25 profits, confirming the accounting-only character of the only 'deconsolidation' in the record.
points.quote: Accordingly, Semolina's Q1 losses for FY'25 have been added back to the results.

points.point: Growth in new verticals (international lounges, highway/expressway F&B) is explicitly described as growth 'for the TFS business' — kept within the listed entity rather than separated into a different vehicle.
points.quote: In addition, the highway F&B business in India is at a very nascent stage, and with the large public and private investments planned in the sector, coupled with the growth of access-controlled expressways, we do see that being an area of growth for the TFS business over the next decade, which we shall tap in a strategic and prudent manner.

rationale.what_management_expects: Nothing, because no separation was announced. For the group as a whole they guided to 80-83% gross margin, PAT margin of 20-22% pre-JV and 25-28% including JV share, FY27 capex of INR50-60 crore, receivables normalising to 40-45 days by H1 FY27, ~45% ROCE, zero debt, and growth from LFL plus net contract gains.
rationale.gaps: Everything about a separation: no business named, no rationale, numbers, timeline, entity structure, share ratio, requesting party, approvals, or expected benefits appears in any call or the filing.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is Amber's Electronics / EMS arm, housed in IL JIN Electronics (India) Ltd — PCB assembly (~INR2,281cr of FY26 revenue), bare PCB through Ascent Circuits (98.5% owned), Shogini Technoarts (80%) and the Ascent-K/Korea Circuit HDI JV (~INR600cr), plus Power-One Microsystems (60%, power electronics, ~15% EBITDA) and 50.4% of Israel-listed Unitronics (industrial automation, 24-25% EBITDA) — leaving Amber with the RAC/consumer-durables division (INR8,383cr FY26) and Sidwal railway/defence (INR535cr). The stated driver is funding: essentially all of the group's capex sits in electronics, with more than INR4,500cr of ECMS investment approvals (Ascent multilayer INR991cr, Ascent-K HDI INR3,200cr, Shogini INR500cr), asset turns of only 0.75-1.1x, and the 48% MeitY plus 42% UP incentives arriving 5-6 years after the spend, so FY27 capex of INR1,800-2,000cr (INR1,100-1,200cr cash) and ~INR1,400-1,500cr in FY28 must be pre-funded against a board policy never to exceed 2x debt/EBITDA and Jasbir Singh's pledge to be net-debt-free. Management said investors asked for it: private equity funds were 'chasing to invest in the electronic division', and instead of loading Amber's balance sheet they raised INR1,750cr inside ILJIN (mostly CCPS, including ChrysCapital's INR1,100cr) while Amber separately did a INR1,000cr QIP. Separation also gives electronics its own margin and valuation identity — 2.8% EBITDA when ILJIN was bought in 2018 on INR300cr revenue, 6.9% FY25, 8.8% FY26, 10.8% in Q4 FY26, 26% ROCE, guidance of 40% FY27 growth at 9.5-10% and a $1bn revenue target at 11.5-12% EBITDA — against a weather-driven RAC business that saw quarters of -30% to -35% and nine bad seasons in 25 years. The outside CCPS holders also need a price: conversion happens 'based on the future multiple and valuation' (auditors provisioned up to ~30% dilution in NCI), which a listing supplies; and their presence already constrains group structuring, since management could not say whether the new Oppo mobile-phone business would sit in ILJIN 'because we have other shareholders also in the IL JIN cap table'. It is being done as a listing of the subsidiary, not a demerger: in April 2026 Amber put another INR296.02cr into an INR328.12cr ILJIN rights issue (89.58% to 89.72%); in July 2026 ILJIN split shares from Rs10 to Rs5, raised authorised capital to Rs250cr, issued a 25:1 bonus, converted from private to public limited, shifted its registered office from Pune to Greater Noida and resolved to explore fund-raising 'including... public issue'; the DRHP was filed on 7 November 2026. In parallel Amber is cleaning up the rest of the portfolio — merging wholly-owned AmberPR Technoplast into itself for compliance/cost reduction and peer benchmarking, and selling Sidwal's entire 49% Shivaliks (Titagarh Firema) JV for a nominal Rs1,09,798.85 after INR112cr of FY26 impairment/JV losses, 'to curtail future losses'.
rationale.evolution: The capex trigger appears first on the Jan 2025 call (Korea Circuit JV awaiting the ECMS scheme, Rs1,000cr+ threshold) and on 19 May 2025, when the funding answer is still vague — 'in touch with various institutions' — alongside an INR3,000cr application plan. By 30 July 2025 it has split into two named routes, an INR2,500cr QIP enabling resolution at Amber and 'private equity funds who are chasing to invest in the electronic division', with the $1bn/11.5-12% electronics ambition and a net-debt-free pledge framing why outside money must sit at ILJIN; on 7 Nov 2025 the INR1,750cr ILJIN raise (CCPS, ChrysCapital INR1,100cr pending CCI) and Amber's INR1,000cr QIP are both announced, and 10 Feb 2026 confirms the full INR1,750cr received with Amber still at 90% until CCPS convert. From there it becomes an exit path for those investors: 18 May 2026 ties conversion to 'future multiple and valuation' (~30% assumed dilution), 20 June 2026 shows the ILJIN cap table already constraining where new businesses can be placed, and the filings then execute mechanically — Mar/Apr 2026 rights issue, 11 July 2026 split, 25:1 bonus, public-limited conversion, registered office to Greater Noida and a 'public issue' resolution, and the DRHP on 7 Nov 2026 — none of it ever discussed on an earnings call.

points.point: The capex need that later drives the separation starts here: the Korea Circuit HDI/substrate JV is on hold pending the ECMS scheme, with a likely Rs1,000cr-plus minimum investment and 70-75% of it only reimbursed later by MeitY and the states.
points.quote: So, on Korea Circuit we are waiting for Government to finalize the incentive scheme.

points.point: With an INR3,000cr PCB application planned and subsidies spread over 5-6 years, management says the Electronics division is itself seeking third-party funding — the first hint of capital being raised at the subsidiary rather than at Amber.
points.quote: So we are already in touch with various institutions for that.

points.point: Two funding routes are named — an INR2,500cr QIP enabling resolution at Amber and private equity money targeted specifically at the electronics arm; the same call sets the constraint that drives it, a board cap of 2x debt/EBITDA and a goal to be net-debt-free by FY27.
points.quote: Second direction is a lot of private equity funds who are chasing to invest in the electronic division.

points.point: The separated entity is given its own standalone ambition and margin identity — $1bn revenue in three years at 11.5-12% EBITDA, versus ILJIN's 2.8% EBITDA on INR300cr when acquired in 2018.
points.quote: With all the add -ups, we intend to take Electronics division to $1 billion by next 3 years with target EBITDA of 11.5% to 12% range.

points.point: The raise happens at two levels simultaneously: INR1,750cr into ILJIN (mostly CCPS; INR370cr in September, INR280cr in October, ChrysCapital's INR1,100cr pending CCI) and a separate INR1,000cr QIP at Amber used mainly to cut debt.
points.quote: We secured funding of INR1,750 crores from marquee investors.

points.quote: But we will not be able to define it right now because we have other shareholders also in the IL JIN cap table .

points.point: The rest of the group is being simplified in the opposite direction: wholly-owned AmberPR Technoplast (cross-flow fans) is merged into Amber — no shares issued, NCLT dispensed with meetings, appointed date moved to 1 April 2026 — for compliance savings, scale synergies and cleaner peer comparison.

points.point: Portfolio pruning runs alongside: the 49% Shivaliks/Titagarh Firema stake is impaired (INR94cr in Q3, INR112cr FY26 including JV losses) and then sold in March 2026 to JP Fincap for a nominal Rs1,09,798.85, ending Italy export ambitions while keeping the Titagarh commercial relationship worth ~INR700cr of visibility.

Amber: retains ~89.7%, frees cash for consumer durables and railway (30-35% growth, 16-17% margins), stays under 2x debt/EBITDA near net-debt-free; CCPS dilution finally priced off a market valuation.

rationale.rationale: The documents supplied contain no separation, demerger, spin-off, slump sale, hive-off or scheme of arrangement for Emmvee Photovoltaic Power Ltd., and management never explains one — so no rationale can be reconstructed from these texts. Across all four calls (Dec 2025, Jan 2026, Apr/May 2026, Jul 2026) the strategic direction stated is the opposite of separation: deeper vertical integration inside one group. Management's stated plan is to add a 6 GW integrated TOPCon cell+module facility at Devanahalli/ITIR Phase 2 (total cost ~INR 5,500 crores, hard costs ~INR 4,600 crores, IREDA term loan sanctioned at INR 3,306 crores at 7.95%/sub-8%), taking capacity to ~16.3 GW modules and 8.9 GW cells by end-FY27, then backward integrate into 9 GW of ingot and wafer in two phases (5 GW in FY29, 4 GW in FY30, ~INR 600-700 crores per GW, largely from internal accruals) 'primarily to protect margins, reduce exposure to upstream supply chain volatility, and strengthen the economics of our domestic cell and module manufacturing operations.' Suhas Manjunatha explicitly argued that standalone module capacity in India 'starts to become irrelevant' and that the future belongs to integrated cell+module and then wafer/ingot players — an argument for combining businesses, not splitting them. The only structural fact disclosed is that the group already operates through two manufacturing entities — the parent Emmvee Photovoltaic Power Ltd. and subsidiary Emmvee Energy — with inter-company order execution and eliminations, but this is described purely as an accounting/execution matter 'all within the group,' with no plan to separate them. The only filing provided is a December 2, 2025 postal ballot notice seeking ratification of ESOS-2025 (35,00,000 options) and extension of ESOS benefits to subsidiary employees; its sole references to demerger are standard ESOP boilerplate on corporate-action adjustments and option treatment, not an announced transaction. No investor, lender, partner or analyst on any call asked for a separation.
rationale.evolution: The idea never surfaces. Dec 2, 2025 (Q2 FY26 call) sets the four-pillar integrated strategy and flags intended backward integration into wafers and ingots timed to ALMM List 3 (June 2028); Jan 16, 2026 (Q3 FY26) repeats that wafer/ingot is 'the next transition' but declines to commit a timeline pending ALMM clarity; Apr 29, 2026 (Q4/FY26) quantifies it at 9 GW in two phases (FY29/FY30) and says 'we will deepen integration'; Jul 16, 2026 (Q1 FY27) restates the same 9 GW plan with commissioning around mid-CY2028 and reiterates margin protection as the purpose. At no point in this 36-month sequence does management, an analyst or a filing raise separating, demerging or divesting any business.

points.point: Management's stated structural direction for FY27 is deeper integration across the value chain, not separation of any business.
points.quote: For Emmvee, the direction is clear: we will deepen integration, scale with discipline, improve technology and efficiency, pro tect balance sheet strength and build resilience across the supply chain.

points.point: Suhas Manjunatha argued the industry is moving toward integrated cell+module (and later wafer/ingot) players, with standalone module manufacturing becoming irrelevant — a case for combining, not separating, businesses.
points.quote: So when look at standalone module manufacturers, I think the roadmap of the industry is quite clear that in the next couple of years the standalone module capacity in India starts to become irrelevant and the focus is going to be completely on integrated module manufacturers.

points.point: The stated purpose of the only structural initiative disclosed — 9 GW of ingot and wafer backward integration in two phases (5 GW FY29, 4 GW FY30) funded largely from internal accruals — is margin protection and supply-chain control, not separation.
points.quote: This backward integration is intended primarily to protect margins, reduce exposure to upstream supply chain volatility, and strengthen the economics of our domestic cell and module manufacturing operations.

points.point: The only group-structure disclosure is that two entities — parent Emmvee Photovoltaic Power Ltd. and subsidiary Emmvee Energy — both manufacture, with cross-entity order execution producing inter-company eliminations, explicitly described as internal to the group.
points.quote: Yeah, yeah, you’re right. I mean, basically, it’s like, you know, we have two , companies basically, one, is the parent and other is a subsidiary where both have manufacturing capacities and one has cell manufacturing capacity.

points.point: Capital allocation for the 6 GW integrated Devanahalli facility is being kept inside the existing company, with land paid for and taken into the company's possession and an IREDA term loan of INR 3,306 crores sanctioned — no separate vehicle or carve-out is mentioned.
points.quote: IREDA has sanctioned our term loan for INR3,306 crores for this facility. We have also completed payment for land allotment at Devanahalli, Bengaluru and the land is now in the company’s possession.

points.point: The December 2, 2025 postal ballot's only references to demerger/reorganisation are generic ESOS-2025 provisions for adjusting options on corporate actions — boilerplate, not an announced separation.
points.quote: RESOLVED FURTHER THAT  in case of any corporate action(s) such as rights issues, bonus issues, merger and sale of division or other re -organization, split  or any other change in the capital structure of the Company, as applicable from time to time, requisite adjustments (which may include adjustments to the number of options in ESOS 2025 ) shall be appropriately made, in a fair and reasonable manner in accordance with ESOS 2025 .

points.point: The same notice contemplates employees being transferred under a scheme of arrangement only as a contingency for option treatment, with no transaction identified, no businesses named and no rationale given.
points.quote: In the event that an employee who has been granted benefits under the Scheme is transferred pursuant to a scheme of arrangement, amalgamation, merger or demerger, or continued in the existing company prior to the vesting or exercise, the treatment of options in such case shall be as specified in such scheme of arrangement, amalgamation, merger or demerger, provided that such treatment shall not be prejudicial to the interest of the employee.

rationale.what_management_expects: Nothing is said about a separation. What management does quantify is from integration: EBITDA margin up to 35% in Q1 FY27 on higher internal cell use, EBITDA per watt of ~INR 2-2.5 (non-DCR module), ~INR 6-6.5 (cell), ~INR 8.5-9 (DCR module), ~INR 2,400 crores EBITDA targeted for FY27, net debt/equity of -0.06x, ROCE 38%, ROE 51%, and ICRA upgrades to A.
rationale.gaps: Everything: the calls and the single filing never mention a separation, so no businesses, numbers, problems solved, requesting parties, timeline or plan changes are explained anywhere.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is Swara Baby Products Limited, Brainbees' diaper/hygiene manufacturing subsidiary, which filed a DRHP on July 02, 2026 for an IPO of up to Rs 10,000 million (Rs 5,000 million fresh issue plus Rs 5,000 million offer for sale), with Brainbees itself selling up to Rs 3,000 million in the OFS (board approval July 01, 2026). Management's stated reason is drift in purpose: Brainbees invested Rs 906.17 million in 2020 for 53.45% (fully diluted) purely as backward integration — "to scale up our home brands within diaper category" with "more control on quality at scale, production timelines and continued innovation in diaper manufacturing" — but Swara then became the largest contract manufacturer by value in Fiscal 2025 in Indian hygiene manufacturing, adding adult diapers and sanitary napkins (similar absorbent raw materials and processes), third-party and multinational customers, and exports via a US subsidiary (Swara Corp, incorporated 08 December 2025). Brainbees' share of Swara's revenue fell from 27.03% in FY24 to 22.64% in FY26, so management says Swara "has charted a very different long term vision as compared to the original alignment with Brainbees," with "different capex and working capital needs" it should "bridge their own capital requirement" rather than draw on Brainbees' cash. On selling into the OFS despite holding cash, management argued "holding cash and holding an investment are two different capital allocation decisions" and that partial monetisation lets it "crystallize value, improve return on investment and maintain flexibility for future strategic opportunities." Control and commercials are explicitly unchanged: Brainbees stays Promoter at 76.59% (raised from 75.92% in a December 2025 swap that moved Solis Hygiene under Swara to put the hygiene vertical "under a single roof"), Swara remains a subsidiary, Brainbees' management has no involvement in running it (Alok Birla and Udit Birla lead; Supam Maheshwari and Gautam Sharma sit as non-executive directors), and "terms of trade" stay at arm's length with "no impact either on supply chain or pricing." Swara contributed Rs 11,639 million revenue in FY26 (Rs 9,004.39 million after eliminating Rs 2,634.61 million of inter-company sales) and Rs 1,445.7 million of adjusted EBITDA into the India multi-channel segment. No lender, partner or investor is named as having demanded it; analysts had only pushed on a separate asset, GlobalBees, where Supam said in August 2025 that "the most probable outcome for Globalbees... will be listing" given its separate board, management and investors (Premji, Lightspeed, Chiratae).
rationale.evolution: The idea first surfaced as an analyst question about a different unit: on the Aug 2025 call (Aug 13, 2025) Sachin Dixit asked whether FirstCry investors could expect liquidity from GlobalBees "getting demerged, having its own IPO," and Supam said listing was the most probable outcome over a few years; on the Feb 2026 call (Feb 13, 2026) Ajay Agarwal asked for GlobalBees listing timelines and got no answer. Meanwhile the hygiene business was quietly being tidied for separation — a December 26, 2025 intra-group restructuring put Solis Hygiene under Swara Baby to bring the whole hygiene vertical under one roof, lifting Brainbees' Swara stake to 76.59%. Neither the Feb 2026 nor the Jun 2026 call (May 26, 2026) mentioned Swara or any separation at all; on Jun 2026 Supam even said buybacks and similar capital actions had not been discussed internally or at board level. The plan then appeared fully formed in filings only — board approval of OFS participation on July 01, 2026, DRHP plus a management Q&A on July 02, 2026 — followed by a related narrowing at GlobalBees, whose non-core brand rationalisation culminated in the October 07, 2026 sale of its entire 51.54% in Mush Textile.

points.point: Asked by JM Financial's Sachin Dixit whether FirstCry shareholders could get liquidity from GlobalBees being demerged or separately IPO'd, Supam framed listing as the likely eventual route and Brainbees' monetisation path over a few years.
points.quote: Having said this, the most probable outcome for Globalbees as an outcome will be listing, which company and its shareholders will decide over a period of time, is when Brainbees also will find a monetization opportunity over a period of a few years.

points.point: The structural argument for separability given for GlobalBees was that it already runs independently of Brainbees, with its own CEO, board and outside shareholders including Premji, Lightspeed and Chiratae.
points.quote: The company has a separate management team, which is run separately and also it has its separate board, and also it has a separate set of investors as well, apart from Brainbees as well, which includes Premji, Lightspeed, and Chiratae, and so on and so forth.

points.point: Garima Mishra pressed on the CCPS infusion into GlobalBees; Gautam said it funded working capital, and that all three investor-directors who had stepped off the GlobalBees board participated in that round — the capital-need theme that later justifies Swara funding itself.
points.quote: This is largely for taking care of their working capital requirement, Garima

points.point: Ajay Agarwal again asked directly for a GlobalBees listing timeline; the reply covered only Flipkart's revenue-recognition impact and GlobalBees' EBITDA growth (c.150% YoY in Q3, c.50% in 9M), with no timeline given.
points.quote: And again on Globalbees, any plans on listing of Globalbees? Can you share the tentative timelines or any sense on the same?

points.point: Five weeks before the Swara DRHP, asked about the low valuation, takeover risk and buybacks, Supam said no such capital action had been discussed internally or by the board — and said nothing about any separation.
points.quote: Yes, we have sufficient cash on the company, but we haven't discussed any of these buybacks and stuff like that so far, in our internal discussions or even board discussions.

points.point: The July 02, 2026 DRHP filing states the original purpose of the 2020 Rs 906.17 million investment for 53.45%: backward integration to scale FirstCry's own diaper home brands with control over quality, timelines and innovation.
points.quote: We wanted to scale up our home brands within diaper category and wanted to do backward integration to get more control on quality at scale, production timelines and continued innovation in diaper manufacturing.

points.point: Core rationale: Swara outgrew the FirstCry ecosystem — multiple third-party and multinational customers, adult diapers and feminine hygiene, exports and a US subsidiary, with Brainbees' share of its revenue down from 27.03% (FY24) to 22.64% (FY26).
points.quote: With Swara Baby's diversification across product lines, more channels, expansion into International geographies, the business has charted a very different long term vision as compared to the original alignment with Brainbees.

points.point: Why not just fund Swara off Brainbees' balance sheet: its capex and working-capital profile differs, so it should raise its own money while Brainbees keeps supply and arm's-length pricing unchanged.
points.quote: With this expansive and global vision in contract manufacturing of disposable hygiene products with different capex and working capital needs, we decided to initiate the process of separately listing this business so that they can follow their independent journey and bridge their own capital requirement.

points.point: Why Brainbees sells up to Rs 3,000 million into the OFS despite ample cash: capital-allocation discipline and value crystallisation, while Swara stays a 76.59% subsidiary and Brainbees' management stays out of its operations.
points.quote: Partial monetization of a successful investment allows us to crystallize value, improve return on investment and maintain flexibility for future strategic opportunities.

points.point: Preparatory step on December 26, 2025: Swara Baby acquired 100% of Solis Hygiene (FY25 turnover Rs 240.73 crore, 3% of consolidated), with Brainbees swapping its 79.34% Solis stake for 56,26,738 Swara shares, lifting its Swara holding from 75.92% to 76.59%.
points.quote: In order to bring the complete Hygiene vertical under a single roof, the restructuring is being done.

points.point: The parallel pruning at GlobalBees: on October 07, 2026 it signed an MOU to sell its entire 51.54% in Mush Textile (brands Mush and BePlush, Rs 11.34 crore or 0.13% of FY26 turnover) for Rs 5,68,93,940 to Nihar Gosalia and Vaishvik Brahmbhatt.
points.quote: Upon completion of the aforesaid transaction, Mush will cease to be a Subsidiary of GlobalBees and, accordingly, will also cease to be a Step-down Subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: The GlobalBees brand-rationalisation logic that frames the Mush exit: loss-making, slow-growing non-core brands were being exited, with core categories at 30% growth and 4.9% adjusted EBITDA versus 2% consolidated.
points.quote: As you're aware, over the last few quarters, we've been speaking about rationalizing certain brands because they were delivering a relatively lower revenue growth as well as incurring losses.

rationale.what_management_expects: Swara funds its own capex/working capital from the Rs 5,000 million fresh issue and pursues an independent global contract-manufacturing path; Brainbees crystallizes value, improves ROI and gains flexibility via up to Rs 3,000 million OFS cash, while keeping 76.59% control, Promoter status, consolidation of Swara's Rs 9,004 million revenue and Rs 1,445.7 million adjusted EBITDA, and unchanged arm's-length supply and pricing.
rationale.gaps: No earnings call ever mentions the Swara IPO, its valuation, or use of OFS proceeds; GlobalBees listing timeline never answered; Mush sale pricing and loss unexplained.

judge.what_is_spun: Nothing is spun off — listed subsidiary Shiva Cement is amalgamated into parent JSW Cement
judge.reason: Create a single unified cement platform unlocking operational, financial and management synergies; backward integration of clinker, cheaper funding, simplified structure, and greater liquidity for Shiva's public shareholders.
judge.insiders: JSW Cement holds 66.23% of Shiva's equity and all its OCCRPS; promoter group of JSW Cement goes 72.02% to 71.39% post-merger; no consideration/benefit to promoters stated.
judge.hidden_value: Shiva's 1.32 mtpa Sundargarh clinker unit plus FY26-commissioned 1.0 MTPA Sambalpur grinding unit come in with negative net worth (INR -30.08 crore) and INR 133.92 crore accumulated losses written off against securities premium.
judge.selling_pressure_why: Only 1.21 crore new shares on 137.55 crore base (~0.9%); same industry, same promoter, larger and more liquid entity.
judge.listing_timeline: No new listing; Shiva Cement "shall cease to exist upon effectiveness of the Scheme without being wound up" and the transaction "is expected to be completed within 12-14 months" (said September 29, 2026 and repeated October 27, 2026)
judge.read_next: The Regulation 37 Scheme filing with the valuation report and fairness opinions behind the 5:41 share exchange ratio.
judge.quote: This consolidation creates a single unified cement platform to unlock operational, financial, and management synergies.

listing.text: IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2025-11-17; date not fixed — No new listing; Shiva Cement "shall cease to exist upon effectiveness of the Scheme without being wound up" and the transaction "is expected to be completed within 12-14 months" (said September 29, 2026 and repeated October 27, 2026)

rationale.rationale: The premise needs one correction: across these texts JSW Cement is not separating a business — the only scheme of arrangement on record (Boards of 29 September 2026) is the opposite, an amalgamation of its listed 66.23%-owned subsidiary Shiva Cement Limited into JSW Cement under Sections 230-232 read with Sections 52 and 66, appointed date 1 April 2026, expected to close in 12-14 months. Management's stated reasons are: (i) business synergies from pooling financial, managerial, technical, distribution and marketing resources, giving cost reduction and streamlined day-to-day running of the units; (ii) backward integration into Shiva's 1.32 MTPA clinker plant at Sundargarh, Odisha, so clinker — 'a key raw material in manufacturing of cement' — is available internally instead of bought from third parties with mark-ups; (iii) financial synergies, i.e. raising funds 'within a single entity on more favorable terms' and eliminating inter-company guarantees — relevant because Shiva standalone had negative net worth of INR (30.08) crore at 31 March 2026 on turnover of only INR 435.17 crore, against JSW Cement's INR 7,029.47 crore net worth and INR 5,995.28 crore turnover; (iv) ending the cost of running two listed entities — duplicated administration, multiple record-keeping, double compliance and group-consolidation effort; (v) giving Shiva's 33.50% public float shares in a far more liquid, institutionally-held stock (consideration is 5 JSW Cement shares of FV INR 10 for every 41 Shiva shares of FV INR 2, no cash, taking JSW Cement to 1,37,55,13,537 shares and diluting promoters from 72.02% to 71.39%); and (vi) 'right sizing' both balance sheets — Shiva's accumulated losses set against its securities premium (leaving retained earnings at INR (133.92) crore and SPA nil) and the Amalgamation Adjustment Deficit Account set against JSW Cement's premium, which ends at INR 4,335.67 crore. The genuine separations in these texts are divestments, not demergers: the 17 November 2025 Securities Purchase Agreement selling 100% of Algebra Endeavour Private Limited / Vadraj Energy Gujarat Ltd (a Gujarat power plant) to Nuvoco Vistas for INR 191.63 crore, a unit that contributed nothing to turnover or net worth, and the 13 August 2026 Board approval to sell up to INR 123 crore of JSW One Platforms shares as Promoter Selling Shareholder in JOPL's IPO. Valuation was done by PwC Business Consulting Services and BDO Valuation Advisory, with fairness opinions from SBI Capital Markets (for JSW Cement) and DAM Capital (for Shiva), JM Financial as exclusive financial advisor.
rationale.evolution: The Shiva merger never appears in any earnings call in the window — not Sep 2025 (Q1 FY26), not Feb 2026, not the 21 May 2026 Q4 FY26 call; the Nov 2025 call transcript is an unextractable scanned PDF, so it cannot be checked. What the calls do show is investors pushing on the group's other unconsolidated structure: on 3 September 2025 Kamlesh Bagmar argued holding the Fujairah clinker capacity through a JV 'don't make much sense for the shareholders' and Narinder Singh replied the financial investors would exit and it would become a full subsidiary; on 21 May 2026 Raghav Maheshwari asked directly about merging that JV in and was told 'not as of now', maybe in two to three years once the financial investor is given an exit. The Shiva amalgamation then arrives fully formed in the 29 September 2026 Board outcome, press release and Regulation 30 annexure, and is restated as a 'Key Business Update' in the 27 October 2026 Q2 FY27 press release with the 12-14 month timeline unchanged.

points.point: The 29 September 2026 Board approved amalgamating listed subsidiary Shiva Cement into JSW Cement, framed as building one consolidated platform rather than splitting anything off.
points.quote: This consolidation creates a single unified cement platform to unlock operational, financial, and management synergies.

points.point: The core industrial logic is securing clinker internally: Shiva's 1.32 mtpa Sundargarh, Odisha kiln becomes an in-house raw-material source rather than a related-party supplier.
points.quote: The proposed amalgamation will result in backward integration of clinker manufacturing with the Transferee Company's cement manufacturing business. The internal availability of clinker is expected to reduce dependence on external procurement, improve supply-chain efficiency, and result in cost savings by avoiding third-party purchases and associated mark-ups.

points.point: Funding is an explicit driver — one borrower instead of two, and the inter-company guarantees JSW Cement had been giving for Shiva fall away.
points.quote: The proposed amalgamation will lead to greater ability of the consolidated entity to access and raise funds within a single entity on more favorable terms, leading to elimination of inter company guarantees and facilitate more efficient funding arrangements.

points.point: Shiva's 33.50% public float (9,88,24,292 shares) is moved into a much larger, more liquid stock; this is the benefit management offers minorities in place of cash.
points.quote: The public shareholders of the Transferor Company would become shareholders in the Transferee Company, which has a higher traded equity share base, greater market liquidity, and a diversified institutional investor base, thereby providing shareholders with enhanced liquidity, broader market participation, and improved opportunities for value realization.

points.point: Running two listed cement companies in the same group was itself the problem — duplicated administration, double compliance and group consolidation effort.
points.quote: The proposed amalgamation will result in a simplification of the existing corporate structure and eliminate administrative functions and duplications, reducing regulatory and legal compliances of two listed entities, eliminating multiple record keeping and reducing time and efforts for consolidation of financials at the group level, consequently reducing the administrative costs of maintaining separate companies, while reducing the multiple legal and regulatory compliances.

points.point: Shiva was a loss-making, negative-net-worth entity (net worth INR (30.08) crore at 31 March 2026 on INR 435.17 crore FY26 turnover), so the Scheme writes its accumulated losses off against its securities premium, leaving retained earnings at INR (133.92) crore and SPA nil; JSW Cement's premium absorbs the Amalgamation Adjustment Deficit and ends at INR 4,335.67 crore.
points.quote: The reorganization of reserves shall result in the right sizing of the financial statement of the Transferor Company which will reflect its true and fair financial position.

points.point: Consideration is all-paper at 5-for-41 with no cash, taking JSW Cement from 1,36,33,64,936 to 1,37,55,13,537 shares and promoters from 72.02% to 71.39%; JSW Cement's own 66.23% stake and Shiva's entire INR 100 crore of 1% OCCRPS held by JSW Cement are cancelled.
points.quote: The Transferee Company shall, without any further application, act or deed, issue and allot to the equity shareholder(s) of the Transferor Company (except the Transferee Company) whose names are recorded in the register of members as a member of the Transferor Company on the Record Date 5 (Five) Equity Shares of the face value of INR 10 (Indian Rupees Ten only) each fully paid-up, for every 41 (Forty One) equity shares of the face value of INR 2 (Indian Rupees Two only) each fully paid-up held by such member in the Transferor Company.

points.point: CEO Nilesh Narwekar's own framing on 29 September 2026 puts integration, synergies, structural simplicity and minority liquidity in one sentence.
points.quote: The proposed merger is a strategic step towards creating a more integrated and efficient business. It will unlock operational and financial synergies, strengthen backward integration, and simplify our corporate structure. Importantly, it will enable Shiva Cement's public shareholders to participate directly in the growth of a larger and more liquid listed entity.

points.point: Strategic ambition beyond cost: a single platform is presented as the vehicle for scale and share, with closing dependent on exchanges, SEBI, NCLT Mumbai, Odisha IDCO, shareholders and creditors over 12-14 months.
points.quote: Unified Cement Platform: Creating a consolidated cement platform supports Transferee Company's strategy, enabling category leadership, increased competitiveness, enhanced market share and efficient resource utilization.

points.point: On 21 May 2026 an investor (Raghav Maheshwari, Equirus) asked whether the unconsolidated UAE Fujairah clinker JV would be folded in; management deferred, citing the need to exit a financial investor first — the only consolidation question asked on any call in the window, and it was about the JV, not Shiva.
points.quote: Not as of now. Probably going forward in next 2-3 years, we will have a look because there is a financial investor sitting there, we'll have to provide exit to him.

points.point: The structural-simplification pressure came from investors as early as 3 September 2025, when Kamlesh Bagmar (Lotus Asset Managers) argued that holding Fujairah clinker through a JV 'don't make much sense for the shareholders'.
points.quote: So, Kamlesh, as I mentioned earlier, the other stakeholders in the Fujairah entity are financial investors. So, over a period of time, definitely they will be taking the exit, and this becomes a full subsidiary.

points.point: The genuine disposals are non-core asset sales, not demergers: the Q3 FY26 deck disclosed the sale of the Gujarat power-plant entity to Nuvoco (the 17 November 2025 SPA covers 100% of Algebra Endeavour Private Limited, a unit the filing says contributes nothing to turnover or net worth).
points.quote: Entered into a Share Purchase Agreement with Nuvoco Vistas Corp. Ltd. for the transfer of Vadraj Energy Gujarat Ltd. (owning a power plant in Gujarat), for a consideration of Rs. 191.63 crore

rationale.what_management_expects: JSW Cement: one unified platform with category leadership, higher share and efficient resource use; cost reduction from pooled resources; in-house clinker from Shiva's 1.32 mtpa Sundargarh kiln avoiding third-party mark-ups; cheaper funding in a single entity, inter-company guarantees gone; right-sized statements (SPA INR 4,335.67 crore). Shiva holders: direct economics plus liquidity in a bigger, institutionally-held stock.
rationale.gaps: No quantified synergy, clinker-saving or cost figure; no call commentary, Q&A or analyst pushback on the merger; Nov 2025 transcript unreadable; Fujairah JV consolidation still unresolved.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is NTPC's captive coal mining business — nine coal blocks with 92 MMTPA peak rated capacity — hived off out of NTPC standalone into NTPC Mining Limited (NML), a wholly owned subsidiary, under a Business Transfer Agreement "at an estimated value of 10,503 crore" (amended BTA dated 17 September 2025), executed in tranches (Chatti Bariatu and Badam first, per the 28 Aug / 1 Oct / 1 Dec 2025 and 1 Feb 2026 disclosures) and completed with the final tranche — Pakri Barwadih mine plus the Coal Mining Head Quarter at Ranchi — effective 1 April 2026, on which date Pakri Barwadih North West was also declared commercial. Management's stated case rests first on scale and fuel security: captive production rose from 35.64 MT (FY24) to 45.82 MT in FY25 (+29%) to 47.88–48.66 MT in FY26 (+8.5%), cumulative mining capex climbed INR12,380 crore (FY25) → INR13,300 crore (Sep-25) → INR14,136 crore (Dec-25), captive coal now meets 18% of requirement and is targeted at 25% by FY30 (CMD: 25% "in next 3 to 4 years"), and in FY26 no coal was imported at all. Second, economics: Director (Finance) repeatedly framed mining capex as "long-term equity deployment under the cost-plus framework and supporting a stable return on equity," and standalone regulated equity is reported as a single pool "for conventional power and mining business" (INR94,631 crore at 31 March 2026), while Aug 2025 he said the "more preponderant thing is fuel security," not cheaper coal than Coal India. Third — and this is the only explicit reason given for needing a separate company — CMD stressed the entity's name: "it is not Coal Mining Limited, it is a Mining Limited," because "we are trying to have some other mines also into that," and NML is the vehicle to pursue "all kind of possibilities within or outside," naming the Government's ~INR37,000 crore coal-gasification programme (coal-to-SNG, pilot 0.4 MTPA at Talaipalli with EIL, potentially feeding NTPC's idle gas plants at peak) and, under the SHANTI Act, fuel processing in the nuclear chain. Structurally it repeats the pattern of NGEL (renewables plus green chemicals; listed 27 November 2024), NPUNL (advanced nuclear, incorporated Jan 2025) and the ASHVINI JV with NPCIL — each business in a dedicated entity carrying its own capex inside a programme of INR17 lakh crore to FY37 and 41% of future capacity sitting in JVs/subsidiaries, with Government of India having raised the investment-approval limit for renewable subsidiaries to INR20,000 crore. Critically, no lender, partner or investor was named as having asked for the mining hive-off, and management never attached a tax, tariff, valuation or monetisation rationale to it; the only "unlocking value" language in three years of calls came in response to an investor question (Apoorva Bahadur, 23 May 2026) about press reports of listing THDC, NEEPCO and Hindustan Urvarak, where DF said there are "no definitive plans," it is "one of the options," and as a JV with the UP government it must be "dealt at the fairly senior policy level."
rationale.evolution: Through the 25 Jan 2025, 24 May 2025 and 18 Aug 2025 meetings there is no mention of NML at all — the separation story is NGEL's 27 Nov 2024 listing, NPUNL's incorporation, and mining described only as capex "contributing to Regulated Equity growth" and a fuel-security play. The hive-off surfaces in the 30 Oct 2025 (Q2 FY26) call as a done deal already signed: BTA for INR10,503 crore, Chatti Bariatu and Badam transferred, "we expect to complete transfer of all the remaining mines to NML in the current fiscal." The 30 Jan 2026 call reports only progress metrics (INR14,136 crore mining capex, Pakri Barwadih NW dispatch, Badam mine-opening clearance), the 23 May 2026 call announces completion on 1 April 2026, and only at the 27 July 2026 annual meet did management explain the logic — DF: "we have now carved it out as a separate company"; CMD: the name is Mining, not Coal Mining, so other mines can come in, with coal gasification and nuclear-fuel processing flagged as the adjacent prizes.

points.point: The template for carve-outs is set: NGEL, the renewables vehicle, was listed on 27 November 2024 and presented as the way to position the clean-energy business separately.
points.quote: The successful listing of NTPC Green Energy Limited (NGEL) during the quarter marks a significant milestone in NTPC's journey towards sustainable energy leadership.

points.point: Before any hive-off is mentioned, mining is justified inside NTPC purely as regulated-equity-accretive capex — INR12,380 crore invested on a standalone basis — plus captive production up 29% to 45.82 MT.
points.quote: We have invested 12,380 crore in developing our coal mines on standalone basis, contributing to Regulated Equity growth and resulting in additional revenue stream for the Company.

points.point: Asked by Ramesh Bhojwani whether captive coal is cheaper than Coal India's, DF declined the cost argument and named fuel security as the dominant purpose of owning mines, noting new mines carry higher stripping ratios and capital cost.
points.quote: See, the primary idea of NTPC getting into its own captive mines is, the more preponderant thing is fuel security.

points.point: On an investor question about where new businesses will sit, CMD confirmed the group's entity-per-business design — green chemicals and hydrogen derivatives go into NTPC Green, not the parent.
points.quote: You have already said, the green chemicals will be part of the NTPC Green.

points.point: First disclosure of the separation in a call: the Business Transfer Agreement for hiving off coal mining to NTPC Mining Limited was signed at an estimated value of INR10,503 crore, with Chatti Bariatu and Badam already transferred.
points.quote: We expect to complete transfer of all the remaining mines to NML in the current fiscal.

points.point: Mid-transfer, the economics are restated as cost-plus: cumulative mining capex of INR14,136 crore at 31 December 2025 is presented as equity earning a regulated, stable return — the same framework that will travel with the business into NML.
points.quote: The cumulative capital expenditure in coal mining stood at INR14,136 crores as on 31st December 2025, providing a long-term equity deployment under the cost-plus framework and supporting a stable return on equity.

points.point: Completion announced: with Pakri Barwadih moving on 1 April 2026 the whole mining business now sits in a wholly owned subsidiary; captive coal (18% of requirement, 47.88 MT, +8.5%) is cited as why fuel security is "more assured than ever before."
points.quote: With the transfer of Pakri Barwadih coal mines on 1st of April 2026, the transfer of NTPC's mining business to NTPC Mining Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, has been fully completed under the business transfer agreement.

points.point: The only investor-initiated separation question in three years: Apoorva Bahadur (IIFL) raised press reports of listing THDC, NEEPCO and Hindustan Urvarak; DF said there are no definitive plans, that THDC is a JV with the UP government needing a senior policy mandate.
points.quote: As a group, we keep exploring all these avenues as a part of our financial strategies and unlocking value.

points.point: DF formally characterises the step as a carve-out of the mining business — nine mines, 92 MMTPA peak capacity, FY26 production 48.66 MT — with all existing NTPC mining assets transferred.
points.quote: And we have now carved it out as a separate company, as you all know, this is the NTPC Mining Limited.

points.point: CMD gives the clearest reason for a separate vehicle: the subsidiary was deliberately named "Mining," not "Coal Mining," so that non-coal mines can be brought into it.
points.quote: And take a note that it is not Coal Mining Limited, it is a Mining Limited.

points.point: NML is positioned as the platform for adjacent fuel businesses — the Government's ~INR37,000 crore coal gasification programme (coal-to-SNG, a serious contender) and, under the SHANTI Act, nuclear fuel processing.
points.quote: But as I was mentioning that this is the NTPC Mining Limited, so we are exploring all kind of possibilities within or outside, whatever it is.

points.point: The quantified payoff management attaches to the mining business: captive share of coal requirement rising from 18% to 25% by FY30 (CMD: within 3-4 years), with no coal imported at all in FY26.
points.quote: Presently, 18% of our coal requirement is met through our captive coal mines, which would go up to 25% fulfilment through captive mining by FY30, thus enhancing the fuel security and supply reliability.

points.point: Filing of 1 April 2026 records the final tranche — Pakri Barwadih mine plus the Coal Mining Head Quarter at Ranchi — under the amended BTA dated 17 September 2025, with COD of Pakri Barwadih North West declared the same day.
points.quote: With this, the hiving-off of the Coal Mining Business has been completed in all respects, and all coal mining units stand transferred to NTPC Mining Limited.

rationale.what_management_expects: For NML: fuel security — captive coal from 18% of requirement to 25% by FY30, nine mines/92 MMTPA, mining capex (INR14,136 crore) as cost-plus regulated equity earning stable ROE, plus a platform for non-coal minerals, coal gasification and fuel processing. For NTPC: an unchanged cost-plus core. No margin, valuation or listing target was given.
rationale.gaps: No stated tax, tariff or regulated-equity consequence; no NML standalone financials, funding or listing plan; no named initiator; no employee-transfer or consideration mechanics beyond the INR10,503 crore valuation.

rationale.rationale: These texts do not describe Orkla India separating, demerging or spinning off any business — on the evidence here the company is moving the other way, having merged Eastern with MTR Foods into a single listed entity (Feb 2026: 'Post-the merger of Eastern with MTR Foods and the creation of Orkla India'), merged the two export books into one international business of ~21% of sales across 45 countries, and named M&A a 'major priority' for acquiring, not divesting. The only 'separation' management discusses is operational and internal: a re-architecting of brand Eastern's legacy direct-to-retail distribution system in Kerala, which Orkla left untouched from the 2021 acquisition until FY26. Management says Eastern runs on 'one system for all' with a 200-SKU range, and that this legacy route-to-market has 'sub-optimal market coverage, lack of customer focus in tune with the trade evolution', and 'ineffective focus on convenience food'. The fix is to split the channel into separate units — one dedicated to spices, one to convenience foods — plus a dedicated standalone modern-trade structure, further digitisation of the retailing framework and better trade-marketing effectiveness. The stated problems it solves: Eastern is 'very heavily indexed on spices and more so pure spices' and carries lower EBITDA margin than MTR, so convenience food needs its own feet-on-street; and numeric reach in Kerala is only 70% despite being 2x the nearest competitor, so coverage can still be extended. The cited cost is real: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 6.2% versus 7.8% excluding Kerala, domestic growth 6.5% versus 8.9% ex-Kerala, spices 6.1% versus 11.1% ex-Kerala (6.5% volume), and Kerala category share fell 50bps MAT March '26 (Kerala also hit by a HoReCa LPG crisis). No investor, lender or partner is said to have asked for it; the nearest external push is Ravi Purohit (May 2026) pressing on why Orkla earns ~16% EBITDA versus MDH/Everest at 20-25%, to which management tied Eastern's margin catch-up to this restructuring and the convenience-food shift.
rationale.evolution: Nov 13, 2025 (first post-listing call): disclosed as a modest efficiency project — Eastern's direct-to-retail Kerala model untouched since acquisition, now to be improved via three changes, the first being splitting the 200-SKU channel into separate spices and convenience-food units. Feb 11, 2026: the project is not mentioned at all; the call instead covers deflation, GST 2.0, MTR Prakriti and M&A ambitions. May 19, 2026: it reappears much larger and renamed an 'internal sales restructuring project'/'re-architecting' of the distribution model, kicked off early in Q4 FY26, now with three phases (one done, second by end-May, third over two more quarters), a dedicated modern-trade structure added, and quantified Kerala damage plus completion by Jan 1, 2027. The July 25, 2026 filing is only the AGM notice (ESOP/MSOP ratification) and contains no scheme of arrangement.

points.point: First disclosure: Eastern's Kerala distribution is a non-standard direct-to-retail system that Orkla deliberately left unchanged since the 2021 acquisition, and is only now being made more efficient.
points.quote: Post acquisition of Eastern, we have not made any changes to this distribution model.

points.point: The only literal 'separation' in these texts — the Eastern sales channel is split into two dedicated units because one force cannot carry a 200-product range across both spices and convenience foods.
points.quote: We have a very large range of 200 products. So, we have split the channel into two separate units. One that will focus only on spices and one that will focus on the convenience foods range.

points.point: Direction of travel is consolidation, not separation: the two companies and two cultures have been merged into one entity, Orkla India, with a single integrated international business.
points.quote: Post-the merger of Eastern with MTR Foods and the creation of Orkla India, this was the first engagement survey that we conducted.

points.point: Asked about portfolio moves, management flags buying businesses in new states, not separating any — and the Kerala restructuring is never mentioned on this call.
points.quote: Yes, so as far as M&A is concerned, I think it's an important strategy for our growth to go beyond our local agenda.

points.point: Re-framed as a structural re-architecting; the diagnosis is that a single undifferentiated distribution system caps what the company can capture by category and channel.
points.quote: Today, our distributions for Eastern operates on a "one system for all" approach, which limits our ability to fully capture the potential across categories and channels.

points.point: A third dedicated structure is added for standalone modern trade, alongside deeper spices coverage and a sharper convenience-food engine.
points.quote: Third, we are creating a dedicated structure for standalone modern trade, enabling us to capture growth more effectively and strengthen our market shares.

points.point: The quantified cost: Kerala dragged Q4 growth to 6.2% (7.8% ex-Kerala), spices to 6.1% (11.1% ex-Kerala, 6.5% volume), domestic to 6.5% (8.9% ex-Kerala), with Kerala share down 50bps; execution is district-by-district in three phases, complete by Jan 1, 2027, with impact for about two more quarters.
points.quote: While this transition has led to some near-term disruption in Kerala market, these steps are structural in nature and are aimed at building a stronger, more scalable distribution engine.

points.point: Answering an investor comparison with MDH/Everest at 20-25% margins versus Orkla's ~16%, the CFO ties the restructuring to lifting Eastern's margin by de-indexing it from pure spices toward convenience foods.
points.quote: Eastern today is very heavily indexed on spices and more so pure spices, and by shifting and accelerating the growth of convenience foods, we expect that margins in Eastern will also improve.

points.point: No scheme of arrangement, demerger, slump sale or spin-off document exists in these texts; the single filing supplied is the 30th AGM notice (Aug 19, 2026), whose only special business is ratification of ESOP 2025 (27,39,784 options, 2% of capital) and MSOP 2025 (4,70,000 options, 0.34%) and their extension to subsidiary and holding-company employees.
points.quote: To receive, consider and adopt the Audited Financial Statements (both Standalone and Consolidated Financial Statements) of the Company for the Financial Year ended March 31, 2026, together with the reports of the Board of Directors and Auditors thereon.

rationale.what_management_expects: No separate entities are created, so no per-entity economics are given. For the restructured Kerala/Eastern business: segmented, agile, scalable distribution; wider numeric reach beyond today's 70%; faster convenience-food, modern-trade and open-format-outlet growth; Eastern's EBITDA margin converging toward MTR's as the mix de-indexes from pure spices; positive momentum across all lines once complete by January 1, 2027; disruption for roughly two more quarters.
rationale.gaps: Everything about an actual separation: no demerger, entity, scheme, record date, capital structure, valuation, lender or partner consent, or margin/capital split is discussed anywhere in these texts.

rationale.rationale: The premise cannot be supported from these texts: across the three transcripts supplied (Investor & Analyst Day of 25 March 2026, Q4/FY26 call of 12 May 2026, Q1 FY27 call of 21 July 2026) and the two filings supplied (the 29 May 2026 postal ballot notice and the 28 January 2026 Q3 FY26 press release), Sagility Ltd. never announces, proposes, or discusses separating, demerging, spinning off, hiving off, or divesting any business, and there is no scheme of arrangement, NCLT filing, record date, share-entitlement ratio, or appointed-date language anywhere in the material. The strategic direction management actually articulates is the opposite of separation: consolidation and bolt-on acquisition. They bought BroadPath (closed January 2025, bringing roughly 30 mostly mid-market payer clients and onshore, open-enrolment-heavy delivery) and CareSeed (closed 11 June 2026, Kansas City, founded 2012, CY2025 revenue 5.1 million dollars, 95 percent recurring, 31.4 percent EBITDA margin, 30 clients of which 26 new, 14 staff, platforms Forecast and Harvest), and Ramesh Gopalan says BroadPath is now fully integrated to the point that revenue cannot be split out, with Srinivas Mattapalli giving only an approximate 13.5 to 13.6 million dollars for BroadPath clients in Q1 FY27. The two reporting segments an investor might expect to be split, Payer (89.6 percent of Q1 FY27 revenue) and Provider (10.4 percent), are both explicitly described as businesses the company intends to keep and grow, including doubling down on provider-side RCM with an agentic AI layer. Capital allocation is framed as full debt repayment during FY27 (net debt 1,110 million rupees, 0.06x adjusted EBITDA), cash of 9,674 million rupees retained for M&A and AI investment, and a small final dividend of 0.10 rupees per share, with no mention of unlocking value through a separation. The only separation-like event referenced anywhere is historical and appears solely in a press-release footnote: the earlier carve-out of the healthcare business from HGS, cited as the origin of intangible amortisation now adjusted out of Adjusted PAT. The only corporate action actually put to shareholders in the filings is the Sagility Limited Employee Stock Options and Performance Stock Units Scheme 2026 (up to 3,09,10,845 options and 12,36,43,222 PSUs, exercisable into up to 15,45,54,067 shares, run through the Sagility ESOP Trust with an interest-free loan capped at 5 percent of paid-up capital and free reserves).
rationale.evolution: The idea does not surface at all. At the Investor & Analyst Day on 25 March 2026 the plan presented is capability expansion (managed services, Synchrony, MLR-reduction, clinical) plus capability-led M&A, and Ramesh Gopalan rules out even moving outside healthcare. On the 12 May 2026 Q4/FY26 call the forward agenda is FY27 debt extinguishment, retained cash for acquisitions in both payer and provider, and a possible dividend review. By the 21 July 2026 Q1 FY27 call the company has added CareSeed and is scouting further clinical, provider and healthcare-technology targets, so the trajectory over the three calls is consolidation, not separation.

rationale.rationale: These texts do not describe Indus Towers separating, demerging, spinning off or hiving down any business, so no separation rationale can be reconstructed from them — the premise is not supported by the supplied material. Across all seven transcripts (Nov 2023 through May 2026) and the one filing (Q1 FY27 results, July 27, 2026), management discusses the opposite direction: consolidation and bolt-on expansion of a single tower business. The only structural actions named are (a) the acquisition of about 12,600 towers (including lean) from Bharti Airtel, completed in the last week of March 2025 for roughly INR 18-20 billion of consideration (Rs. 1,800 crore line item in cash flow; Rs. 18 billion booked to common control reserves; Rs. 1.7 billion of restated opex/depreciation from 19 Nov 2024), and (b) the creation of a new Africa holding structure — wholly owned subsidiaries in UAE plus Zambia, Uganda and Nigeria entities, and Indus Towers Global Ventures IFSC Limited (incorporated 28 April 2026) — which management repeatedly frames as greenfield organic growth of the same core tower business, not a carve-out of an existing one. The only 'separation' language anywhere is operational, not corporate: the EV-charging pilot was to be run by a 'separate business unit, separate team' (Jan 2025), and by May 2025 that pilot was still being evaluated and might be held back so 'focus will remain on the towers.' The filing's single reference to a 'scheme of arrangement' is a legacy depreciation-to-general-reserve adjustment (Rs. 185 million in Q1 FY27, Rs. 795 million in FY26), not a new separation, and both standalone and consolidated results state the company 'has a single reportable segment.' Capital-structure debate in these calls is about dividends versus leverage (INR 14 per share final dividend for FY26, about INR 37-38 billion, roughly 100% of FY26 free cash flow of INR 37.6 billion) — not about separating anything. No investor, lender or partner on any of these calls asks for a separation.
rationale.evolution: The idea never surfaces. Nov 2023 through May 2025 the structural theme is consolidation (Airtel's 12,600 towers, 'aggressively pursuing market share through both organic and inorganic routes'); Jan 2025 adds an EV-charging pilot as a 'separate business unit,' which by May 2025 is merely 'evaluating that pilot' and may be dropped in favour of towers. Oct 2025 announces Africa (Nigeria, Uganda, Zambia) explicitly as the same tower business, not diversification; Feb 2026 adds the UAE/local-country holding structure and possible GIFT City debt funding, and the July 2026 filing lists ten subsidiaries plus Indus Towers Global Ventures IFSC Limited (28 April 2026). May 2026 closes on Zambia licence in hand, Uganda/Nigeria approvals pending, and a resumed dividend — with no separation mentioned on any call.
