rationale.rationale: These texts contain no separation, demerger, spin-off, slump sale out, hive-off or scheme of arrangement by KRN — there is no Scheme document among the ten filings, no shareholder resolution for one (the 15 April 2026 EGM covers only promoter re-appointments, an ESOP plan of 6,00,000 options and a ₹500 crore QIP), and no call question or management answer about separating any business. The only going-concern business transfer in the record runs inward, not outward: on 6 October 2025 wholly-owned subsidiary KRN HVAC Products Pvt Ltd signed a Business Transfer Agreement with Sphere Refrigeration Systems Pvt Ltd to acquire its bus air-conditioning division, which management framed as buying technology, know-how, the three ex-Subros/'Sparrows Motherson' professionals, their 12–13 years of experience, employees, assets and store, with the price 'not much' and never disclosed — Sphere Refrigeration's own top line was only ₹2–3 crore, while the related Sphere Thermal did ₹40–50 crore and had been sold six months earlier to a third party wanting railway HVAC entry. The separation visible in that deal is the counterparty's: Sphere's founders sold Sphere Thermal and 'bought back' the bus AC business into Sphere Refrigeration, which KRN then acquired. KRN's own structure is deliberately multi-entity rather than separating: the new 600,000 sq ft Neemrana plant sits in KRN HVAC because it carries the 15% concessional tax rate, the ₹141.72 crore white-goods PLI sanctioned by IFCI (5%, then 4%, over three years) and Rajasthan RIPS at ~1.56% of top line for 10 years, while the listed parent runs at the old tax rate and full capacity; Thermotech Research Laboratory Pvt Ltd was incorporated as a 100% subsidiary with a separate plot, separate building, separate investment and a name 'not linked to KRN' precisely so it can act as an independent AHRI-accredited third-party lab. Two filings point the other way from separation: on 12 January 2026 the parent amended its 15 April 2023 loan agreement (₹100 crore limit, ₹99.94 crore outstanding) to make the loan convertible into KRN HVAC equity at the lender's discretion, and granted Thermotech a ₹10 crore unsecured loan at 12% — deeper consolidation of ownership, not a split. Nobody asked for a separation: no investor on any of the seven calls raised it, lenders appear only via the CRISIL A-/Stable rating and the ₹350 crore QIP allotted 1 June 2026 at ₹1,060 (to ValueQuest, Ashoka WhiteOak, ADIA, Bank of India funds, Subhkam and others), and partners/customers appear only as OEM approvals. The 9 June 2026 promoter sale of 10,00,000 shares (1.52%, Santosh Kumar Yadav and Anju Devi 5,00,000 each, taking the group from 67.22% to 65.69%) is an open-market OFS of shares, not a separation of any business.
rationale.evolution: No separation idea surfaces in any call. The nearest structural events are: 15 May 2025 and 1 August 2025, when Thermotech Research Laboratory is described as deliberately kept 'separate' in identity, plot, building and name so it can serve as an AHRI third-party lab; 6 November 2025, when the inbound Sphere bus-AC Business Transfer Agreement is announced alongside the CRISIL A-/Stable rating and management says both 'have not contributed to the H1 FY26 performance' but 'set the stage for the next leg of growth'; 9 February 2026, when the acquisition cost is refused ('cost of course we cannot disclose… it's not much'), gross margin is said to beat existing products and the ₹1,000 crore-plus Indian bus AC market growing 20–25% is targeted at 15% share; and 15 May 2026, when bus AC has delivered ~₹10 crore in FY26 against a ₹150 crore presentation figure, with 12 January 2026 and 1 June 2026 filings adding loan-to-equity convertibility in KRN HVAC and the ₹350 crore QIP.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is M&M's Mahindra Truck & Bus Division (MTBD), which the board on 29 July 2026 approved selling as a going concern on a slump-sale basis to SML Mahindra Limited (formerly SML Isuzu), M&M's own listed subsidiary, for Rs 525 crore subject to working-capital adjustment, priced off a valuation report from GT Valuation Advisors Private Limited. Management's stated reason is structural, not financial distress: M&M had two separate truck-and-bus businesses after buying 58.97% of SML from Sumitomo Corporation and Isuzu Motors on 1 August 2025 plus the mandatory open offer, and the filings call the MTBD transfer 'a natural next step in creating a simplified operating model with sharper market focus, enhanced scale and improved competitiveness.' The problem it solves is fragmentation and subscale presence — MTBD covers light, intermediate and heavy trucks and buses, SML is a market leader in ILCV buses, and combining them is meant to produce one entity across the whole >3.5T CV segment with 'enhanced scale, broader market coverage, a strengthened product portfolio and improved operational efficiencies.' The sizing shows how small the business is inside M&M: MTBD generated total income of Rs 2,989 crore in FY2025-26, about 2.02% of M&M's total income from operations, and M&M's investment in it was ~Rs 481 crore, about 0.65% of net worth — small enough that M&M states it does not even qualify as an 'undertaking' under Section 180(1)(a), so no shareholder vote and no Regulation 37A process. SML's own scale was Rs 2,837.92 crore revenue in FY2025-26 (Rs 2,398.99 crore FY2024-25, Rs 2,195.93 crore FY2023-24) on a net worth of only Rs 519.34 crore, which is why the combined entity needs funding: SML's board approved a rights issue of up to Rs 1,450 crore on 6 November 2026, with M&M committing ~Rs 855 crore for its entitlement plus up to ~Rs 595 crore for any unsubscribed portion — i.e. M&M is prepared to fund the entire raise. Operational continuity is preserved because M&M will keep making Mahindra-branded trucks and buses for SML under a contract manufacturing arrangement, and both brands' heritage and positioning are to be retained. No investor, lender or partner is named as having asked for the separation; it is presented as a group-level capital-allocation and structure decision, consistent with the parallel exits (Erkunt Foundry, Blue Planet) and the Mauritius holding-company merger aimed at a streamlined group structure.
rationale.evolution: There are no earnings-call transcripts on file, so the idea can only be traced through filings: the enabling step was M&M's purchase of 58.97% of SML Isuzu from Sumitomo and Isuzu on 1 August 2025 followed by the open offer, which left the group with two overlapping truck-and-bus businesses. On 29 July 2026 the M&M board approved the MTBD slump sale to SML for Rs 525 crore, with the BTA to be executed by 7 August 2026 and closing on or before 31 January 2027 (FY2027), plus a contract-manufacturing arrangement so M&M keeps building Mahindra-branded trucks and buses. One day later, on 30 July 2026, the board approved absorbing Mahindra Investment Company (Mauritius) Limited to rationalise overseas entities, part of the same simplification push that also included the 10 April 2026 exit from Erkunt Foundry 'in line with capital allocation framework' and the 2 March 2026 exit from Blue Planet. The plan's funding leg appeared last: on 6 November 2026 SML approved a rights issue of up to Rs 1,450 crore and M&M committed ~Rs 855 crore of entitlement plus up to ~Rs 595 crore of any unsubscribed shares, with no change of control envisaged.

points.point: Board approval of the slump sale of the Truck & Bus Division — employees, assets, IP, licences, contracts and liabilities — to listed subsidiary SML Mahindra for Rs 525 crore under a Business Transfer Agreement.
points.quote: We hereby inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held today, i.e. 29th July 2026, accorded its approval for the sale, transfer, and disposal of the Company's Truck & Bus Division together with its employees, assets, intellectual property, licenses, permits, insurance policies, contracts, interests, rights, and liabilities ("MTBD Business Undertaking"), as a going concern on a slump sale basis, as per Section 2(103) and other applicable provisions of the Income-tax Act, 2025, to SML Mahindra Limited, a listed subsidiary of the Company, under a Business Transfer Agreement ("BTA"), for a consideration of Rs. 525 crore, subject to working capital adjustments as set out in BTA.

points.point: The stated rationale: one unified Mahindra Group truck-and-bus business spanning light, intermediate and heavy CVs plus buses.
points.quote: The combination of MTBD Business Undertaking and SML is a strategic step towards creating a unified Truck & Bus business in Mahindra Group with a comprehensive presence across light, intermediate and heavy commercial vehicles, as well as buses.

points.point: Expected benefits are scale, coverage, portfolio and efficiency, producing a 'future-ready' organisation.
points.quote: The combined business is expected to benefit from enhanced scale, broader market coverage, a strengthened product portfolio and improved operational efficiencies.

points.point: The move is framed as the sequel to M&M's August 2025 acquisition of control of SML Isuzu from Sumitomo and Isuzu.
points.quote: Following M&M's acquisition of a 58.97% stake in SML Mahindra Limited (formerly SML Isuzu Limited) from Sumitomo Corporation and Isuzu Motors Limited on August 1, 2025, and the subsequent mandatory open offer, the proposed transfer of MTBD to SML is a natural next step in creating a simplified operating model with sharper market focus, enhanced scale and improved competitiveness.

points.point: Group CEO Anish Shah frames it as simplifying the group's CV structure into a single focused entity aimed at CV leadership.
points.quote: The transaction simplifies Mahindra Group's commercial vehicle business structure by consolidating truck and bus operations under SML Mahindra, creating a single focused entity dedicated to growth and leadership in the commercial vehicle sector.

points.point: Auto & Farm CEO Rajesh Jejurikar points to synergies across operations, technology and customer-facing domains while keeping both brands distinct.
points.quote: By combining strengths of SML and Mahindra Truck & Bus, we can drive meaningful synergies across operations, technology and customer-facing domains while preserving the unique heritage and market positioning of both brands.

points.point: SML Executive Chairman Vinod Sahay positions it as a single unified CV platform with greater scale and 'significant commercial and operational synergies'.
points.quote: By bringing together SML and Mahindra Truck & Business under one unified commercial vehicle platform, we are creating a stronger business with greater scale, broader market coverage and a more comprehensive product portfolio.

points.point: MTBD's smallness inside M&M is quantified — Rs 2,989 crore total income, ~2.02% of income; investment of ~Rs 481 crore, ~0.65% of net worth.
points.quote: The MTBD Business Undertaking generated a total income of Rs. 2,989 crore during the financial year ended 31st March 2026, representing approximately 2.02% of the Company's total income from operations for the said year.

points.point: Because MTBD is not an 'undertaking' under Section 180(1)(a), the sale avoids Regulation 37A and the shareholder-approval route, though it is a related-party transaction done at arm's length and priced on an external valuation.
points.quote: The provisions of Regulation 37A of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 are not applicable to this transaction, as MTBD Business Undertaking which is being transferred by the Company through a slump sale does not qualify as an "undertaking" within the meaning of Section 180(1)(a) of the Companies Act, 2013.

points.point: M&M retains the factories: it will keep manufacturing Mahindra-branded trucks and buses for SML under contract.
points.quote: Manufacturing of Mahindra branded trucks and buses will continue to be undertaken by M&M under a contract manufacturing arrangement, ensuring continuity of supply and operational stability.

points.point: Timing and shareholding: closing on or before 31 January 2027 (during FY2027), with no change to M&M's shareholding pattern.
points.quote: Slump Sale of MTBD Business Undertaking is proposed to be consummated on or before 31st January 2027, or such later date as may be mutually agreed upon by the parties, subject to satisfactory fulfilment of the conditions precedent, including obtaining all requisite approvals and completion of such procedures as may be required, in accordance with the terms of the BTA.

points.point: Funding leg (6 November 2026): M&M backstops SML's Rs 1,450 crore rights issue in full — ~Rs 855 crore entitlement plus up to ~Rs 595 crore of any unsubscribed shares — with no change of control.
points.quote: Subscription to additional equity shares and/or any portion of the rights issue that remains unsubscribed, if any, beyond the Company's entitlement, aggregating ~Rs. 595 crore.

points.point: SML's receiving-end scale and thin net worth: revenue of Rs 2,837.92 crore in FY2025-26 against net worth of only Rs 519.34 crore, with market leadership in ILCV buses.
points.quote: For the financial year ended 31st March 2026, SML's revenue from operations stood at Rs. 2,837.92 crore, and its net worth as of 31st March 2026 was Rs. 519.34 crore.

points.point: Parallel portfolio pruning: the Erkunt Foundry exit (10 April 2026) is justified purely on capital allocation, after infusing ~Rs 256 crore to extinguish debt and selling for Turkish Lira 1,00,000.
points.quote: The exit of the foundry business is in line with capital allocation framework of the Company.

points.point: Parallel structural simplification: the 30 July 2026 absorption of Mahindra Investment Company (Mauritius) to cut overseas entities and compliance cost.
points.quote: Ensure a streamlined group structure by reducing and rationalizing the number of overseas entities in the group structure;

points.point: Defence/aerospace is being partnered rather than retained wholly: Embraer takes 51% of newly incorporated Novavayu Aerospace for ~Rs 5,10,000, turning it from a step-down WOS into an associate.
points.quote: MDSL will receive aggregate consideration of approximately Rs. 5,10,000 for the sale of its 51% equity stake in NAL to Embraer S.A.

rationale.what_management_expects: For SML: enhanced scale, broader market coverage, a strengthened product portfolio, improved operational efficiencies and competitiveness in a consolidating CV market, funded by up to Rs 1,450 crore of rights equity M&M will largely supply. For M&M: a simplified CV structure, sharper market focus, retained factory utilisation via contract manufacturing, Rs 525 crore of proceeds, and capital freed per its allocation framework. No margin, synergy or valuation targets were quantified.
rationale.gaps: No earnings-call transcripts exist here, so no management Q&A, no quantified synergies, margin, ROCE or valuation targets, no post-rights M&M stake, and no contract-manufacturing economics.

rationale.rationale: What is being 'separated' is not a demerger or spin-off: it is a 40% minority dilution of Nippon Life India AIF Management Limited (NAIF), NAM India's wholly owned alternatives (AIF) subsidiary, to DWS Group GmbH & Co. KGaA via a fresh issue of 3,40,000 equity shares (face value INR 10) at INR 21,569 per share for INR 733,34,60,000 (~INR 733.35 crore), after which NAIF 'will cease to be a wholly owned subsidiary' but 'continue to remain as a subsidiary' — so NAM India keeps control and consolidation, and the filing states 'No impact' on management or control of the listed entity. The stated purpose in the Scheme documents is 'to jointly develop and build a leading alternative investment funds franchise in India along with DWS'; management's own explanation on the calls is purely about distribution reach, not about fixing a problem inside the business. Sikka's logic, repeated across three calls, is that NAM India is strong domestically and has 'very strong Japanese access' through parent Nippon Life Insurance, but 'Europe access was lower', and DWS — described by him as 'the largest asset manager of Europe' (EUR 1,085 bn AUM at Dec 31, 2025, ~5,000 employees per the filing) — is the channel to bring European money into India, 'especially the alternate and the infrastructure side.' The collaboration is explicitly wider than the JV: the Nov 13, 2025 board authorisation says NAM India and DWS 'will also work closely in other areas including passive investment products and global distribution,' and Sikka added it will help the mutual fund business on 'capability of international funds, ETFs, and also offshore money.' Scale context given: NAIF's cumulative AIF commitments were INR 95.8 bn (Q1 FY27, +18% YoY), up from INR 74.1 bn at Q4 FY25; NAIF contributed INR 101.96 crore of turnover (4.6%) and INR 102.18 crore of net worth (3.1%) in the last financial year; non-MF products are ~8% of gross revenue and MF was 91% of FY26 revenue; and Parag confirmed the AIF entity is already 'a profitable company. It's a profitable franchise.' The background pressure visible in the calls is the persistent failure of the offshore/international engine to scale — offshore AUM went from INR 172 bn (Sep-2024) to INR 161 bn (Sep-2025) to INR 139 bn (Mar-2026), and Sikka conceded 'we would have expected offshore contribution to be higher… it is a little binary' — so the DWS tie-up reads as the fix for foreign-inflow access rather than for anything in the domestic MF franchise. Nobody — no investor, lender or regulator — is said to have asked for it; the counterparty link is related-party-adjacent only in that promoter Nippon Life Insurance 'presently holds 5.00% stake in DWS,' and DWS had already been listed in Apr 2025 as one of the Nippon Life network entities through which offshore business was being sourced. The deal is conditional on SEBI and CCI approvals plus consent of NAIF's AIF investors, with a 12-month long-stop date, and the SHA gives DWS board and senior-management appointment rights, reserved matters requiring its consent, a put option, exit rights, non-compete, transfer restrictions and lock-in.
rationale.evolution: Through Jul 2024 and Oct 2024 AIF is only flagged as 'an important focus area' with senior hiring and seed capital, and in Apr 2025 DWS appears merely as one of several Nippon Life network entities (with GENKAI, BBLAM, Cathay) through which offshore money already trickles in, while Nov 2025 shows management conceding offshore is 'a small part of our overall business, but the ambition is to grow bigger.' The idea surfaces formally at the Feb 2026 call (Q3 FY26, held Jan 29, 2026), which discloses the Nov 13, 2025 board authorisation of a strategic collaboration with DWS taking 'up to 40%' of NAIF plus cooperation in passives and global distribution — still only a non-binding agreement, with Sikka declining detail beyond 'the idea will be to get more global flow into India.' By the Apr 2026 call it is called a JV and justified as access to overseas money 'especially the alternate and the infrastructure side' plus spillover to the MF business; the Mar 14, 2026 filings then harden it into signed SHA/SSA with a fixed 40%, INR 733.35 crore price and SEBI/CCI conditions. At the Jul 2026 call the stake is confirmed as 40%, approvals are still awaited, the Japan-plus-Europe positioning is sharpened ('one side it will be Europe and one side it will be Japan'), and unit economics are declined as 'too early.'

points.point: Pre-history: DWS is already named as one of the Nippon Life group entities through which NAM India's offshore business is sourced, alongside Japan, Thailand and Taiwan affiliates.
points.quote: Till now, if you see where most of our business that is coming, international business is coming – you can look at slide in the presentation, whether it is coming through DWS, whether it is from the GENKAI which is Japan, BBLAM which is Bangkok Life Asset Management and Cathay, which is Taiwan.

points.point: Context for the deal: the non-MF businesses (AIF subsidiary, offshore subsidiary) are tiny in the mix but are the stated growth ambition; yields on these products range 60–120 bps versus ~36 bps blended MF yield.
points.quote: Currently, it's a small part of our overall business, but the ambition is to grow bigger.

points.point: First disclosure of the separation: the Nov 13, 2025 board authorisation of DWS acquiring up to 40% of the AIF subsidiary via fresh equity, plus a wider collaboration on passives and global distribution.
points.quote: Our Board of Directors at their meeting on November 13, 2025, authorised the Company to enter into a strategic collaboration with DWS Group (a leading European Asset Manager), wherein DWS intends to acquire a minority stake of up to 40% in Nippon Life India AIF Management Limited by subscribing to fresh issuance of equity shares.

points.point: Management's one-line rationale at first disclosure, delivered in the same breath as the admission that offshore inflows have disappointed and are 'binary'.
points.quote: As I mentioned in my speech earlier, our AIF is getting into a JV with DWS. Again, the idea will be to get more global flow into India.

points.point: The problem the tie-up is meant to address: offshore contribution has undershot management's own expectations for years, partly on USD-INR, and is lumpy institutional-mandate driven rather than predictable like SIPs.
points.quote: I have mentioned in past also - clearly we would have expected offshore contribution to be higher. It has taken a little more time; it is a little binary.

points.point: Purpose restated as sourcing overseas capital specifically for alternates and infrastructure, still under a non-binding agreement at that date.
points.quote: The idea is we clearly see an opportunity to get a lot of overseas money and especially the alternate and the infrastructure side.

points.point: The JV is explicitly not ring-fenced to AIF — management expects collateral capability transfer into the mutual fund business (international funds, ETFs, offshore money).
points.quote: Also, as far as the JV is concerned, it will also help in collaboration not only in the AIF where it will be a JV, but also with the mutual fund business, you know, to as in whether from a capability of international funds, ETFs, and also offshore money.

points.point: The strategic gap being closed is geographic: Japan access was already strong via the parent; Europe was the missing leg.
points.quote: The idea is to keep getting ready as India keeps, you know, getting stronger. More foreign money will come into India and I think building capabilities access, we were always very strong in Japan. So now this JV gives us an access to Europe.

points.point: Management also flags DWS's passive/ETF strength as a reason the partnership could extend to product launches in India if investor demand appears.
points.quote: And to your earlier question, having DWS with us, you know, and DWS is one of the largest international players both in not also in ETF space, but also passives, you know.

points.point: The signed deal (Mar 14, 2026): SHA with the Company, NAIF and DWS plus an SSA, with the stated object of jointly building an India alternatives franchise and DWS taking 40%.
points.quote: To jointly develop and build a leading alternative investment funds franchise in India along with DWS and in pursuance thereof DWS has agreed to acquire a minority stake of 40 percent in NAIF.

points.point: Price and mechanics: INR 733.35 crore of primary capital into NAIF for 3,40,000 fresh shares at INR 21,569 each — money goes into the subsidiary, not to the listed parent as sale proceeds.
points.quote: DWS has agreed to pay a sum of INR 733,34,60,000/- (Indian Rupees Seven Hundred Thirty-Three Crores Thirty-Four Lakhs Sixty Thousand only) as consideration for acquiring 40% equity stake in NAIF by subscribing to 3,40,000 equity shares [having a face value of INR 10/- (Indian Rupees Ten) per share], to be issued by NAIF by way of preferential allotment.

points.point: Scale of what is being diluted: NAIF is ~4.6% of turnover and ~3.1% of net worth — i.e. the separation touches a small slice of the group.
points.quote: During the last financial year, NAIF contributed INR 101.96 crore to the Turnover (4.6%) and INR 102.18 crore to the Net Worth (3.1%) of the Company.

points.point: It is a dilution, not a disposal — NAM India retains consolidation and, per the filing, control of the listed entity is unaffected.
points.quote: After the said issuance of equity shares, NAIF will cease to be a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company and it would continue to remain as a subsidiary.

points.point: Governance price of the deal: DWS gets board and senior-management appointment rights, veto matters, a put option and exit rights, with non-compete, transfer and lock-in restrictions on NAM India.
points.quote: The SHA provides few customarily required covenants which includes inter alia, provisions w.r.t. board composition, senior management appointment, reserved matters requiring DWS's consent, put-option, exit rights granted to DWS, governance related matters, information-sharing obligations, provisions with respect to non-compete, transfer restrictions and lock-in provisions.

points.point: Conditionality and timeline: SEBI and CCI approvals plus consent of NAIF's AIF investors, within a 12-month long-stop date.
points.quote: The proposed transaction is expected to be completed within 12 months from the execution of the Agreement Date ("Long Stop Date") or such other date mutually agreed between the Parties, subject to receipt of regulatory approvals from SEBI and Competition Commission of India and requisite consent of investors of the AIFs managed by NAIF and upon fulfilment of other conditions precedent stipulated in the SSA.

points.point: The counterparty is not formally related, but promoter Nippon Life Insurance already owns 5% of DWS — the plausible origin of the relationship.
points.quote: DWS is not related to the Company in any manner, however, Nippon Life Insurance Company (i.e. the promoter of the Company) presently holds 5.00% stake in DWS.

points.point: Post-signing framing: DWS as Europe's largest asset manager is the whole point of the JV, with approvals still pending.
points.quote: But specifically, and I'd like to touch upon the JV with DWS, we believe from Europe a lot more money can come to India and DWS is the largest asset manager of Europe and the JV has been done with that in mind.

points.point: The competitive-positioning argument: a dual Europe-plus-Japan access channel is claimed as a unique edge for capturing foreign money into India.
points.quote: We have very strong Japanese access. But Europe access was lower -- and we will become one of the unique asset management companies in India where on one side it will be Europe and one side it will be Japan.

points.point: Management refuses to quantify the economics of the deal — no yields, no AUM or revenue contribution.
points.quote: I think it would be too early. We see a very big opportunity there.

points.point: The entity being part-sold is already profitable on its own, and the AIF book stands at INR 95.8 bn of cumulative commitments, up 18% YoY, with fundraising live across listed equity, private credit and direct VC.
points.quote: Yeah, so it's a profitable company. It's a profitable franchise.

rationale.what_management_expects: For NAIF: European capital into Indian alternates and infrastructure, INR 733.35 crore of fresh primary capital inside the subsidiary, DWS board/veto/put rights, and a jointly built 'leading' India AIF franchise that stays a consolidated, already-profitable subsidiary. For NAM India: Europe access added to its Japan access, spillover capability in international funds, ETFs, passives and global distribution. No margin, capital-release or valuation benefit was ever quantified.
rationale.gaps: No margin, valuation, capital-use or AUM targets; why 40%; how the INR 733 cr is deployed; NAIF standalone P&L; put/exit pricing; dilution impact on consolidated EPS; no investor or lender demand cited.

rationale.rationale: These texts do not describe Power Mech Projects separating, demerging or spinning off any business — there is no scheme of arrangement, no NCLT filing, no record date, no share-entitlement ratio, and no management discussion of hiving off a division on any of the six calls (May 2025 through May 2026) or in either filing (postal ballot of 10 November 2025 and AGM notice of 8 August 2026). The only occurrences of the words 'merger/demerger, sale of division/undertaking' are inside the standard corporate-action adjustment clause of the proposed 'Power Mech Projects Limited -Employee Stock Option Plan -2026' (10,00,000 options, of which up to 2,00,000 for subsidiary employees, 3.16%–3.19% of capital on a fully diluted basis), which merely says options would be re-priced fairly if such an action ever occurred; it is boilerplate, not a plan. What the texts actually show is the opposite of separation — consolidation and the use of subsidiaries/SPVs inside one listed entity: the Transmission/Electrical division was wound down and its portfolio 'shifted' into the Civil business while a new BOP EPC vertical was added (May 2026); a 100% subsidiary, PM Green, was incorporated for the 250 MW / 1,000 MWh West Bengal BESS BOO project (INR 800 crore capex, INR 103 crore/year over 15 years, INR 1,563 crore, 51% Power Mech-led consortium, 16–18% equity IRR) which was later cancelled by the West Bengal State Electricity department; MDO assets sit in SPVs (Tasra SPV carrying INR 400 crore of coal-handling-plant and railway-siding capex, KBP raising a INR 256 crore term loan, the INR 690–700 crore washery built in Power Mech's own books) and riverbed-mineral/sand mines sit in LLPs taxed at 35% versus 25% at company level, lifting the consolidated effective tax rate to 28–29%. Portfolio pruning that did happen was order-book, not corporate: INR 4,264 crore of non-moving Adani FGD orders (Kawai, Tiroda, Mundra) were removed by mutual agreement, leaving only the INR 936 crore Udupi job, and management said it is 'not showing interest' in new water projects, with the UP Jal Jeevan Mission book run down to about INR 900 crore pending central funding. Management's stated strategic direction is to concentrate the same listed company on power, O&M, BOP EPC and MDO (visibility to FY30, 12.3% FY26 EBITDA rising toward 14% by FY30) — not to separate anything. If a separation exists, it is documented somewhere outside the material supplied here.
rationale.evolution: The idea never surfaces: across CALL Feb 2025, CALL May 2025, CALL Aug 2025, CALL Nov 2025, CALL Feb 2026 and CALL May 2026 no analyst asks about a demerger and no manager raises one; the only corporate-structure questions concern succession (Rohit Sajja's induction to the Board, May 2025) and fund-raising (QIP of INR 240 crore, borrowing limit raised from INR 5,000 crore to INR 7,500 crore in the November 2025 postal ballot). The two filings in the window are an ESOP-2026 postal ballot (10 November 2025, voting 21 November–20 December 2025, with a 1%-of-capital grant resolution) and the 27th AGM notice (8 August 2026, meeting 17 September 2026) re-tabling the same ESOP plus a INR 1.50 dividend, independent-director appointment and director remuneration — none of which mention a separation. The nearest thing to a structural change evolves as consolidation: PM Green is created for BESS (disclosed CALL Feb 2026), the BESS order is then cancelled (CALL May 2026), and the Electrical/Transmission division is declared 'over' and merged into Civil while BOP EPC is created as the new vertical (CALL Nov 2025 signalling, confirmed CALL May 2026).

points.point: The closest actual restructuring is internal consolidation, not separation: the Transmission/Electrical segment was discontinued and absorbed into the Civil division, with BOP EPC created as the replacement reporting vertical.
points.quote: No, it is a different business because, actually, earlier the Transmission division used to do the transmission erection of the lines and other things. That business is over now.

points.point: Management explicitly folded the electrical/T&D portfolio into civil rather than separating it, and added BOP EPC as a new line of activity.
points.quote: So, now we shifted that entire portfolio to the civil business, and we added a new line of activity of BOP EPC business.

points.quote: So , we have incorporated a 100% subsidiary as a PM Green for this, and this is a small attempt we to see where the renewable segment fits into the Power Mech's vision of sustained growth and margins.

points.point: MDO assets are held in SPVs within the consolidated group, with capex split between the Tasra SPV and Power Mech standalone - a financing structure, not a separation.
points.quote: And in TASRA SPV, INR 400 crores of Capex Tasra Coal Handling Plant and railway siding is added.

points.point: Riverbed-mineral/sand-mine operations run through LLP entities taxed at 35% versus 25% at company level, lifting the consolidated tax rate to 28-29% - the only structure-driven economic friction management quantified.
points.quote: The exceptional revenue generat ed from the Riverbed Minerals business was booked through L LP. Where applicable tax rate is 35%, compared to 25% at the company level .

points.point: Portfolio pruning that did occur was contractual, not corporate: INR 4,264 crore of non-moving Adani FGD orders were removed from the order book by mutual agreement, leaving only the INR 936 crore Udupi package.
points.quote: So, we have taken a djustment of non moving FGD orders – after discussion and negotiations with the client.

points.point: The only 'demerger / sale of division' language in the filings is the standard option-adjustment clause of the proposed PMPL ESOP-2026 (10,00,000 options, up to 2,00,000 for subsidiary employees), appearing identically in both the 10 November 2025 postal ballot and the 8 August 2026 AGM notice; it is contingent boilerplate, not an announced transaction.

Management's expectations are for the single consolidated entity: FY27 revenue growth of 21% on INR 6,107 crore, EBITDA rising from 12.3% to about 12.5% and toward 14% by FY30 as O&M (15-16%) and MDO (15% to 20-21% at peak rated capacity) outweigh sub-10% construction margins, with operating cash flow of INR 430 crore and debt/equity of 0.32x funding capex internally.

rationale.rationale: These texts contain no business separation, demerger, spin-off, slump sale or scheme of arrangement by Triveni Turbine Ltd. — the premise cannot be supported from the material supplied, and the corporate-structure actions disclosed all run in the opposite direction, toward consolidation. The only scheme-type filing is the April 2026 South African merger in which TSE Engineering (Pty) Ltd was merged INTO Triveni Turbines Africa (Pty) Ltd — both step-down wholly owned subsidiaries held via Triveni Turbines DMCC, UAE — approved by the CIPC on April 14, 2026 and effective April 1, 2026, with TSE dissolved; FY25 turnover was ₹119 Cr (ZAR 257 million) for TTAPL and ₹50 Cr (ZAR 109 million) for TSE, with no cash consideration, no share-exchange ratio and no change in TTL's shareholding pattern. The stated rationale is simplification, not separation: to simplify the Group's South African corporate structure, gain operational and administrative efficiencies, and consolidate into a single unified legal entity for improved governance and streamlined reporting. This followed the Q3 FY26 buy-in of the remaining 30% of TSE for ZAR 10.97 million (₹56 million), which management framed on the Nov 2025 call as consolidating ownership, strengthening operational control, simplifying the group structure, improving decision-making and agility and realising operational synergies and cost efficiencies through unified management — and on the Feb 2026 call as 'unifying our operations in the South African market' while widening scope from SADC to Sub-Saharan Africa. The only other structural items are a Ind AS 19/wage-code exceptional charge of ₹157 million (not structural at all) and the NCLT-approved reduction of share capital of wholly owned Triveni Energy Solutions Limited, which produced a ₹360 million standalone exceptional gain in Q3 FY25 — a capital reduction within a wholly owned subsidiary, not a business separation. The sole separation anywhere in the texts is historical and concerns the parent, not TTL's own businesses: the About-the-Company boilerplate in the November 21, 2025 press release notes TTL 'was demerged from its parent Company, Triveni Engineering and Industries Limited (TEIL) in 2010', with TEIL holding 21.85% until it fully divested on September 21, 2022 — no rationale, numbers or requesting party is given for that 2010 demerger. Consistent with this, both standalone and consolidated results state the company operates in a single reportable segment, 'Power Generating Equipment and Solutions', with no reportable segments under Ind AS 108, and Nikhil Sawhney told the May 2026 call the company is 'still pretty much a steam turbine company' — i.e. no separable second business is even presented, and no investor, lender or partner is recorded as asking for one.

Instead: Aug 2025 and May 2025 discuss investing in and absorbing losses at the US and South African subsidiaries; Nov 12, 2025 announces buying TSE's remaining 30% for ZAR 10.97 million to consolidate ownership and simplify group structure; Feb 4, 2026 says 100% control allows 'unifying our operations' and widening scope from SADC to Sub-Saharan Africa; the April 15, 2026 filing completes that by merging TSE into Triveni Turbines Africa effective April 1, 2026. rationale.rationale: On the evidence of these transcripts and filings, APSEZ is not separating or demerging a business, and management never explains one, because no separation exists in the record: the only Scheme of Arrangement here runs the other way, folding a subsidiary in. The Scheme is the amalgamation of Adani Harbour Services Limited (AHSL, the wholly-owned harbour/marine-services arm) INTO APSEZ under Sections 230-232 of the Companies Act, 2013 — intimated by the letter of November 4, 2025, sanctioned by the NCLT Ahmedabad Bench on April 1, 2026, and effective April 21, 2026 when the certified order was filed with the RoC Gujarat; no rationale, synergy, cost saving or valuation argument is given in the filing, and no earnings call mentions it. The only transaction that separates economic interest in a business is the Vizhinjam partial sell-down: a Share Purchase and Subscription Agreement dated June 29, 2026 under which Mundi Limited, a subsidiary of Terminal Investment Limited (TiL, the terminal arm of MSC), takes 49% of Adani Vizhinjam Port Private Limited (AVPPL) at a total deal value of USD 2.85bn, of which TiL's 49% share is USD 1.397bn — USD 539mn for the stake and USD 858mn on completion of the Phase 2 expansion by December 2028 (total expansion capex USD 1.75bn, capacity 1.6m to 5.7m TEUs, 3.5x; quay 800m to 2,000m; STS cranes 8 to 29). This is explicitly not a demerger or slump sale (both marked "Not Applicable" in the Regulation 30 disclosure): APSEZ keeps 51%, a majority of board seats, and continues to consolidate AVPPL as a subsidiary, so it is a partner-led monetisation of a minority stake, not a separation of the asset from the group. The problems it is said to solve are commercial, not structural — enhanced volume visibility and ramp-up ahead of plan, a higher share of Bangladesh cargo today routed through competing Southeast Asian transshipment hubs, a stronger position on East Africa trade routes, more relay cargo — plus funding: "Transaction unlocks USD 1.397bn for APSEZ's future growth trajectory" against AVPPL FY26 income of Rs 843.19 crore, share capital of Rs 897.00 crore and net worth of Rs 2,813.98 crore at 31.03.26. Who asked: the counterparty is MSC/TiL, a third strategic partnership after Mundra CT3 (AICTPL, 50:50, 3.2m TEUs in FY26) and Ennore (AECTPL, 51:49, 701K TEUs in FY26); no investor, lender or rating agency in these texts asks for any business to be separated, and investors instead asked for, and got, separate REPORTING lines (international ports, marine, trucking and international freight network) plus capital-allocation detail. Management's stated strategic direction across every call is the opposite of separation — integration and consolidation into one "integrated transport utility" with scale, and the only business they declined to own, shipbuilding, was declined on competency grounds, not separated.
rationale.evolution: The idea of a separation never surfaces in the calls: Oct 2024, Feb 2025, May 2025 (May 1, 2025), Nov 2025 (Nov 4, 2025) and the Apr 30, 2026 Q4 call discuss volumes, margins, ROCE, capex and leverage, with no demerger, spin-off or listing of a vertical mentioned. What did evolve was disclosure and structure: at the May 2025 call management introduced separate reporting lines for international ports, marine services and trucking/IFN "thanks to your feedback"; on November 4, 2025 — the same date as the Q2 FY26 call, where it was not discussed — APSEZ intimated the inward amalgamation of Adani Harbour Services into the parent, sanctioned April 1, 2026 and effective April 21, 2026. Only after the last call in this set does a partial separation of economic interest appear, in the June 29-30, 2026 Vizhinjam agreement with MSC's TiL for 49% of AVPPL, which was never previewed or justified on any call in this record. Across the whole window the narrative runs toward consolidation — Ambition 2031, capex first, strategic M&A second, buyback "the last option" — not toward breaking anything out.

points.point: The only Scheme of Arrangement in the record is an inward amalgamation, not a separation: wholly-owned Adani Harbour Services Limited was merged into APSEZ under Sections 230-232, sanctioned by the NCLT Ahmedabad Bench on April 1, 2026, with no rationale stated in the filing.

points.point: Asked by Pulkit Patni (Goldman Sachs) whether a possible group shipbuilding venture would sit inside Adani Ports or in a separate entity, the CEO refused the business on competency grounds rather than discussing any separate-entity structure.

points.point: Closing remarks frame integration across ports, logistics and marine as the core competitive advantage — the opposite of a separation thesis.

points.point: Even in the quarter when the AHSL amalgamation was intimated (letter of November 4, 2025, the call date), the stated direction of travel was one consolidated global platform, with no mention of the scheme on the call.

points.point: What investors actually asked for and received was segment-level transparency — separate reporting for international ports, marine and trucking/IFN — not legal or structural separation of any business.

points.point: Management repeatedly argued the case for keeping the verticals together, on the grounds that the port network feeds logistics market share — a direct integration argument against carving out logistics.
points.quote: Now what we want to do is use the port's network to increase the market share of our inland logistics and this is where, we are going to focus on capex, on the logistic business

points.point: The founding frame for the period under review is an integrated utility absorbing commodity and geographic risk across one portfolio, which management uses to justify holding the businesses in one entity.
points.quote: During the period, we continued to strengthen our value proposition as an integrated transport utility company with unmatched waterfront to last mile connectivity solutions.

rationale.rationale: These texts do not describe Bajaj Auto separating, demerging or spinning off any business, so no rationale for one can be reconstructed from them — the only structural moves management discusses run in the opposite direction, toward consolidation. In the Jul 2026 call the electric two-wheeler business was folded INTO an existing unit: 'to capture some synergies, we have brought our electric two-wheeler business in the umbrella of the two-wheeler business unit.' On KTM, Bajaj moved from a 49.9% associate stake to control (BAIH BV holding 100% of BAIH AG, which holds ~74.9%–75% of Bajaj Mobility AG), completed 18 November 2025 after the European Commission subsidies approval of 10 November 2025, with line-by-line consolidation from Q4 FY26 at a one-quarter lag — an acquisition, not a separation. KTM is described as being 'run as an independent company' with its own Executive Board, but that is operating autonomy inside the group, not a separation of a Bajaj business; the turnaround workstreams there explicitly include 'simplifying the organization and corporate structure' and resetting fixed costs. The capital-structure action in the filings is a buyback of up to 46,94,000 shares at INR 12,000 (INR 5,632.80 crore, 1.68% of capital, 16.93% of standalone capital+free reserves), combined with a INR 150/share final dividend (INR 4,192 crore) for a 100% payout of FY26 PAT of INR 9,825 crore — justified by surplus cash (INR 18,000 crore at FY26 close, over INR 21,000 crore at June 2026), FY26 free cash flow above INR 8,000 crore, and an expected improvement in EPS and ROE, not by any portfolio separation. Subsidiaries that are already separate legal entities — Bajaj Auto Credit Ltd (AUM ~INR 20,000 crore, PAT INR 227 crore in Q1 FY27, ROE over 25%, CP and NCD listed) and the Brazil subsidiary — are presented as scaling contributors to consolidated results, with the last equity infusion into BACL described as the final one, again with no mention of separating them. The buyback explanatory statement is explicit on the point: the Board confirmed 'there is no pendency of any scheme of amalgamation or compromise or arrangement pursuant to the provisions of the Act, as on date.'
rationale.evolution: Aug 2025 and Nov 2025 track the KTM/Pierer transaction toward control (regulatory approvals, call options on Stefan Pierer's and Pierer Industries' 50% stake, Austrian Takeover Commission clearance 23 October 2025), i.e. combination rather than separation. Feb 2026 and May 2026 report change of control effective 18 November 2025, renaming of Pierer Bajaj AG to Bajaj Auto International Holdings AG and Pierer Mobility AG to Bajaj Mobility AG, and a turnaround plan whose only structural element is simplification of KTM's own organization and corporate structure. May 2026 adds the 100% payout plus buyback as the shareholder-return mechanism, and Jul 2026 reports the buyback's completion (46,94,000 shares extinguished 24 July 2026) alongside the internal folding of the electric two-wheeler business into the two-wheeler BU. At no point across these eleven months does any call or filing announce, foreshadow or explain a separation of a Bajaj Auto business.

points.point: The only portfolio-structure change announced is an internal consolidation — the electric two-wheeler (Chetak) business was moved under the domestic two-wheeler business unit to capture synergies, the opposite of a separation.
points.quote: Domestic two-wheelers, to capture some synergies, we have brought our electric two-wheeler business in the umbrella of the two-wheeler business unit.

points.point: Asked about India-KTM integration, Rakesh Sharma framed KTM's autonomy as governance of an acquired subsidiary run by its own management, not as a separation of a Bajaj business; collaboration and Indian manufacturing for KTM are being expanded.
points.quote: So first of all, I must say that KTM is being run as an independent company.

points.point: The reason given for KTM operating separately is brand/franchise difference, with KTM to be run by its own management on arm's-length competitive benchmarks — a reason for autonomy, not for carving out any Bajaj unit.
points.quote: So, they are going to be run separately.

points.point: The structural event of the period was Bajaj moving from a minority to a controlling stake in KTM, with BMAG and KTM AG becoming step-down subsidiaries consolidated line-by-line with a one-quarter lag — an acquisition and integration, not a demerger.
points.quote: With the transaction completed on 18th of November, Bajaj moved from being a minority position to a controlling stake and BMAG and KTM are now step -down subsidiaries of the group.

points.point: The KTM 360-degree turnaround plan's structural workstream is simplification of KTM's own organization and corporate structure plus cost reset and Bajaj-KTM synergies — internal restructuring inside the group, with no separation of any business.
points.quote: This broadly will encompass sharpening the product portfolio across the 3 bands of KTM, Husqvarna and GASGAS, reworking the target operating model for go -to-market and looking for synergies between the Bajaj and the KTM system, resetting the fixed cost base across all lines, simplifying the organization and corporate structure.

points.point: Pierer Mobility AG was renamed Bajaj Mobility AG and kept listed in Zurich and Vienna with Bajaj appointees replacing Pierer nominees on both boards — a change of control and rebranding of an acquired listed entity, not a separation.
points.quote: In terms of next steps, an extraordinary general meeting has been called for and will be convened on 19th of November at which the name of the company will be changed, it is proposed to be changed from P ierer Mobility AG to Bajaj Mobility AG.

rationale.rationale: On the evidence of these four transcripts and four filings, Bank of Baroda is not separating or demerging an existing business, and management never offered a separation rationale — no scheme of arrangement, demerger, carve-out listing or hive-off is discussed anywhere, and the word 'spin-off' never appears. What the texts do show is the opposite direction of travel: building new businesses *outside* the standalone bank as fresh subsidiaries rather than splitting existing ones out. On the May 2026 (8 May) call Dr. Debadatta Chand said the bank 'made one of the subsidiary operating from 1st April' — BOB Securities and Giltedge Limited, a standalone primary dealer company that will also do DCM and act as market maker in debt instruments, with committed capital of ₹2,000 crore of which only ₹500 crore had been availed; the stated logic was that the bank 'having a large investment book internally... as a group we can do well on the debt market segment', i.e. sitting the PD/DCM activity in a separate regulated vehicle alongside BOBCAP (equity), insurance, mutual fund, the card business and Baroda Sun Technology (the tech company formalised the prior year). The second new entity is a pension fund: the bank had only received the sponsor appointment letter, with PFRDA and other approvals pending and a 6–9 month timeline. The only genuine *reductions* in the group perimeter are not management-initiated strategy: the Government of India gazette notification CG-DL-E-07042025-262329 dated 05.04.2025 amalgamated Regional Rural Banks one-per-state from 01.05.2025, under which Baroda Rajasthan Kshetriya Gramin Bank passed to State Bank of India as sponsor (consolidated P&L debited ₹1,307.14 crore on reversal of carrying value versus the ₹108.27 crore capital redemption received, while ₹2,466.38 crore of excess equity over cost went to reserves, and the bank subscribed ₹35.99 crore and ₹341.43 crore for 35% of Gujarat Gramin Bank and Uttar Pradesh Gramin Bank); the Malaysia joint venture India International Bank (Malaysia) Berhad was placed under liquidation on 06.11.2025 with capital repatriated; BOB (UK) Ltd repatriated GBP 75 million by capital reduction on 27.03.2026; and the 08.09.2026 filing discloses an offer-for-sale of up to 76,90,375 NSE shares — 35% of the bank's holding — into the NSE IPO, which is minority stake monetisation, not separation of a business. No investor, lender, rating agency or partner is recorded anywhere as asking for any separation; CARE Ratings' 07.10.2026 rationale is standalone and discusses only GoI ownership, capital, asset quality and the ₹5,680 crore NMC settlement.
rationale.evolution: Oct 2024 (25 Oct) contains nothing on group structure at all. The Feb 2026 call (30 Jan 2026) is silent too, with the RRB sponsorship transfer and the Malaysia JV liquidation appearing only in the notes to the Q3 results filed the same day. The idea surfaces as additive subsidiary-building on the May 2026 call (8 May), where BOB Securities and Giltedge Limited is announced as operational from 1 April 2026 and the pension fund sponsor appointment as announced 'yesterday', with Chand closing the topic — 'my current plan of getting into other businesses outside the standalone Bank, I think we're done with that' — and then the Jul 2026 call (24 Jul) returns to zero mentions, while the 8 September 2026 filing adds the NSE offer-for-sale.

points.point: The only new business moved outside the standalone bank is the primary dealer/DCM activity, incorporated as BOB Securities and Giltedge Limited and made operational from 1 April 2026.
points.quote: At the same time, we announced that we have made one of the subsidiary operating from 1st April, that is we created a primary dealer business in terms of creating a BOB's Securities and Giltedge Limited.

points.point: The PD entity is funded with ₹2,000 crore committed capital of which only ₹500 crore had been drawn, and is expected to be a market maker in debt instruments leveraging the bank's own large investment book.
points.quote: We have committed a capital of Rs. 2,000 crores for this, the PD business. And currently they have only availed Rs. 500 crores.

points.point: Chand framed the subsidiary set as complete and complementary — BOBCAP for equity, the new entity for PD plus DCM, pension fund next, plus insurance, mutual fund, cards and Baroda Sun Technology — with no further structural moves planned.
points.quote: So, I think with this, my current plan of getting into other businesses outside the standalone Bank, I think we're done with that.

points.point: The pension fund subsidiary was only at appointment-letter stage, with PFRDA and other regulatory approvals pending and a 6-to-9-month setup estimate; the PD company was already live and needed to be scaled from a standing start.
points.quote: So, as I said, on the pension fund 6 to 9 months, whereas the standalone PD, the PD is already operational from 1st April 2026.

points.point: Filing 08.09.2026: the bank will sell 35% of its National Stock Exchange holding — up to 76,90,375 shares — through the offer-for-sale in NSE's IPO; FY2025-26 dividend from NSE was ₹76,90,37,500. This is stake monetisation, with no business or division separated.
points.quote: we advise that the Bank of Baroda is proposing to divest upto 76,90,375 equity shares, being equivalent to 35% of the shares held by the Bank in National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE), by way of Offer for Sale through Initial Public Offering, subject to all regulatory approvals.

points.point: Filing 30.01.2026 (Q3 notes): the RRB exit was imposed by government gazette, not chosen — one RRB per state from 01.05.2025, moving Baroda Rajasthan Kshetriya Gramin Bank's sponsorship to State Bank of India while BOB took 35% of the merged Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh entities.
points.quote: The Government of India, vide gazette notification CG-DL-E-07042025-262329 dated 05.04.2025, has provided for the amalgamation of Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) into a single Regional Rural Bank (RRB) in different states effective from 01.05.2025.

points.point: Filing 30.01.2026: the Rajasthan RRB exit cost ₹1,307.14 crore through the consolidated P&L against a ₹108.27 crore capital redemption, with ₹2,466.38 crore of excess equity over cost taken to reserves — the only quantified structural impact in the documents.
points.quote: In case of Baroda Rajasthan Kshetriya Gramin Bank, the Bank has debited its consolidated profit and loss account by ₹ 130714 lakhs towards reversal of difference between the carrying value of investments and the proceeds received for capital redemption.

points.point: Other perimeter reductions are wind-downs and capital repatriation rather than separations: the Malaysia joint venture went into voluntary liquidation on 06.11.2025, and BOB (UK) Ltd returned GBP 75 million by capital reduction on 27.03.2026.
points.quote: During the quarter, India International Bank (Malaysia) Berhad, a joint venture of Bank of Baroda, was placed under liquidation on November 06, 2025.

points.quote: It allows us to close a legacy matter and focus on our customer, stakeholder and long-term sustainable growth.

rationale.what_management_expects: Nothing was said about margins, capital release or re-rating from any separation. For the new subsidiaries management expects only scale-up: the PD/DCM entity to become a debt-market maker leveraging the group's large investment book from ₹500 crore of ₹2,000 crore committed capital, the pension fund to be built after PFRDA approval, and existing subsidiaries to be stabilised and strengthened before anything further.

rationale.rationale: No separation, demerger, spin-off, slump sale or scheme of arrangement is disclosed anywhere in these three years of calls or in the eight filings provided — so the premise cannot be sourced from these texts, and I will not reconstruct a rationale that management never gave. The eight filings are all ANDA approval press releases from Caplin Steriles Limited (Foscarnet Sodium, Calcium Gluconate, Potassium Phosphates, Desmopressin Acetate, Sodium Phosphates, Methylprednisolone Acetate, Linezolid, Acetaminophen); none is a scheme, record-date, valuation report, NCLT or restructuring intimation. What management actually describes is the opposite direction of travel: tighter integration of an already-subsidiarised group — Caplin Point (LatAm/RoW parent), Caplin Steriles Limited (CSL, US/regulated injectables), Caplin Steriles USA (CSU, own-label front end), Caplin One Labs (COL, oncology), the Vizag API unit and Amaris Clinical — funded entirely from internal accruals, zero debt, INR 1,471 crore cash and INR 2,726 crore liquid assets at FY26, with roughly INR 1,000–1,100 crore of capex of which about INR 510 crore remains. The only de-coupling management explains with numbers is commercial, not corporate: CSL stopped signing exclusive B2B deals with upfront milestones and launched its own US label, because B2B partners squeezed manufacturer prices and took 50% of profit — 'that 50% that we've been sharing over the last few years, it accrues directly back to us now' (Feb 2025) — producing nearly INR 100 crore / ~$11mn of own-label revenue in FY26 with 30 products launched, CSL FY26 EBITDA of INR 142 crore (30%, vs INR 102 crore / 27.9%), and no degrowth in B2B. The only equity-structure questions raised by investors were (a) Sachin Kasera asking in Feb 2025 whether CSL's minority investors would be taken out via a listing or buyback, which the Chairman said had never been discussed, and (b) a top-10 PE fund in Nov 2025 offering ~$300mn to co-fund a ~$200mn US target, which would have diluted the family's ~71% holding — management declined it as 'not a meaningful fit'. Nobody — no investor, lender or partner — asked for a business to be separated in any of these six calls, and no lender pressure exists to create one, the group being virtually debt-free with no finance cost.
rationale.evolution: The idea never surfaces. The nearest equity-structure moment is Feb 05, 2025, when an investor asks about listing or buying out CSL's minority holders and the Chairman says it was never discussed; and Nov 06, 2025, when a PE fund's ~$300mn offer that would have diluted the promoters' ~71% stake is rejected as not complementary. By Feb 05, 2026 and May 14, 2026 the discussion has moved entirely to 17 injectable lines, INR 510 crore residual capex, ANDA buyouts and a possible LatAm distribution acquisition — i.e. consolidation inside one group, with Feb 2026 explicitly describing the aim as 'a vertically integrated company like any other big company'.

points.point: The only question about separating out an entity was whether CSL's outside investors would exit via listing or buyback; the Chairman said the subject had never even been raised internally or by them.
points.quote: Yes. That, of course, we haven't discussed, and they are also happy.

points.point: The real de-coupling management explains is from B2B front-end partners, not a corporate separation: CSL stopped exclusive deals and milestone/royalty upfronts so the 50% profit share previously given away accrues to Caplin.
points.quote: Now, why I say mid - to long term is that over the mid - to long term, that 50% that we've been sharing over the last few years, it accrues directly back to us now.

points.point: The stated reason for taking the US front end in-house was partner behaviour — cheaper CMOs undercutting on price and B2B partners protecting their own margins by squeezing manufacturers.
points.quote: Number 2, with the amount of competition our B2B partners being the size that they are, they are always going to ensure that their margins are not affected.

points.point: The only structural equity event discussed was a top-10 PE fund's ~$300mn investment into a ~$200mn US target that would have diluted the family's ~71% stake; it was turned down as not complementary to existing lines of growth.
points.quote: See, as a family, we own around 71%.

points.point: Asked directly for a material update on inorganic plans, management said there was nothing at a late stage — and described the end-state as one vertically integrated company, not separated businesses.
points.quote: Nothing to report at this point, please.

points.point: The FY26 close is framed as scaling an integrated group — 60 ANDAs, 17 injectable lines planned, INR 510 crore residual capex, INR 1,471 crore cash, zero leverage — with acquisitions sought only if 'meaningful'; no separation is mentioned.
points.quote: I would say that in summary, our US business is transitioning from a phase of foundation building to one that is scaling and growing in depth.

rationale.rationale: On the evidence supplied, the "separation" is not a demerger or business carve-out at all: it is a sequence of minority listings of Coal India's wholly-owned mining and planning subsidiaries, each done purely as an Offer for Sale of CIL-held shares, and management never explained a rationale for it on any of the three calls. The filings show the trigger was the owner, not the market: Ministry of Coal Office Memorandum I/37811/2025 dated 16.12.2025 "advised CIL to take concrete steps to ensure further listing of subsidiaries namely MCL and SECL in the upcoming financial year," after which the CIL Board gave in-principle approval by circular resolution on 23.12.2025 for onward submission to DIPAM — i.e. a government disinvestment instruction routed through the administrative ministry, with no investor, lender or JV-partner request cited anywhere. Executed so far: Bharat Coking Coal (BCCL) sold 465,700,000 shares of ₹10 face value at ₹23, listed 19.01.2026, cutting CIL from 100% to 90% (4,657,000,000 to 4,191,300,000 shares); Central Mine Planning & Design Institute (CMPDIL) sold 107,100,000 shares of ₹2 face value at ₹172, listed 30.03.2026, cutting CIL from 100% to 85% (714,000,000 to 606,900,000 shares). In the pipeline: MCL DRHP dated 01.09.2026 for an OFS of up to 661,836,300 shares (₹2 face value) and SECL DRHP dated 01.11.2026 for up to 668,056,100 shares (₹2 face value), both "held by Coal India Limited" and subject to approvals and market conditions. Each filing states the subsidiary "ceases to be a wholly-owned subsidiary… However, it continues to remain a subsidiary," so control, consolidation and sale proceeds all stay with CIL and no fresh capital reaches the units. The only separation question ever asked on a call — Feb 2024, on housing the renewable/alternative-energy verticals as a demerged entity — was refused by management, who said existing subsidiaries and JVs already covered it and "It is not in our discussion right now." The calls do, however, describe the businesses now being listed: BCCL as an all-coking-coal producer (~41 mt target FY24; ~3.7 mt supplied to steel, 2.4–2.7 mt washed) constrained by washing capacity and monetising assets (2 mt Durga washery won by JSW Steel); SECL as the chronic underperformer (197 mt target vs 162 mt, slipping 8–9 mt on land and heavy rainfall); MCL as the low-cost, low-stripping-ratio, low-manpower unit (89.4 mt with 21,523 employees); and CMPDIL as the in-house planning/design arm building CIL's own e-auction platform.
rationale.evolution: Across all three calls in the window (21 Nov 2023, 19 Feb 2024, 14 May 2025) there is no mention of listing or separating any subsidiary; discussion is confined to volumes, e-auction premiums, FMC/railway evacuation, capex of ~₹80,000 crore over five years, employee cost and diversification into solar, gasification and critical minerals. The idea surfaced only once on a call, on 19 Feb 2024, when an investor asked whether the energy/alternative-energy verticals would be a "separate demerged entity" — and management rejected it outright. The actual separation then appears without any call-side preparation in the filings: Ministry of Coal OM of 16.12.2025, CIL Board in-principle approval for MCL and SECL on 23.12.2025, BCCL RHP 02.01.2026 and listing 19.01.2026, CMPDIL RHP 12.03.2026 and listing 30.03.2026, MCL DRHP 02.09.2026 and SECL DRHP 02.11.2026. The sequencing shifted in practice — the two subsidiaries the ministry named (MCL, SECL) were overtaken by BCCL and CMPDIL, which listed first, while MCL and SECL are still only at DRHP stage a year after the directive.

rationale.what_management_expects: Nothing stated. Across all three calls management gave no expectation for any separation — no margin, capital-allocation, valuation-unlocking or focus argument, and on 19 Feb 2024 it denied any such plan. The filings are bare Regulation 30 disclosures citing only approvals and market conditions; being pure Offers for Sale, they raise no capital for BCCL, CMPDIL, MCL or SECL, and CIL retains 90% and 85% control respectively.
rationale.gaps: Everything: no call discusses the IPOs, rationale, valuation, proceeds use, or subsidiary autonomy. No call after May 2025 is provided, so the Dec 2025 directive onward is unexplained by management.

rationale.rationale: These texts contain no demerger or spin-off of an operating division — there is no scheme of arrangement for a split, no share-entitlement ratio, and the only court scheme in the filings runs the other way (wholly-owned Godawari Energy Limited amalgamated INTO GPIL, NCLT order 10.03.2026, effective 23.03.2026, appointed date 01.04.2025) — so the separation management actually explains is portfolio and group-structure separation in three parts. First, GPIL exited its entire 37.85% associate stake in Ardent Steel, a merchant iron ore pellet plant, for about INR 91 crores, framed in Feb 2026 as 'part of the company's ongoing efforts to simplify and streamline group structure'; the economics management gave for that kind of asset is that merchant pellet players 'solely dependent on market for purchase of iron ore' face 'a squeeze in margins' (May 2026) and that 'buying fines in the market and investing in pellet plant, I don't see a business proposition there' (Feb 2025) — while GPIL's own pellet book is captive-ore backed, 2.7 to 4.7 mt with Ari Dongri going 2.35 to 6 mt. The accounting they walked through: INR 91 crore dividend plus ~INR 73 crore book profit standalone (standalone PAT +19%), but under equity method only INR 17 crore gain consolidated, netted against a ~INR 36-37 crore write-off of erstwhile Godawari Energy's thermal power preoperative cost, 'dropped during the year on account of shifting to Solar power', leaving a net INR 17-18 crore consolidated exceptional loss. Second, the non-ferrous recycling arm Jammu Pigments — acquired in FY25 for INR 255 crore on a ~INR 500 crore post-money valuation for 51%, diluted to 43.96% when promoters converted loans — was first declared operationally stand-alone and self-funded ('Jammu Pigments will run independently... We have no intention of investing any further money', Feb 2026), then partly sold back to JPL's own promoters/affiliates in July 2026: 16,75,000 shares at an independent-valuer price of Rs 298.45, Rs 49.99 crores, cutting GPIL from 85,69,762 (43.96%) to 68,94,762 (35.36%); that filing sizes JPL at only 1.92% of FY26 consolidated profit/income (Rs 1,536.21 lakhs) and 4.68% of net worth (Rs 27,381.90 lakhs). Third, the new low-margin, high-volume businesses are deliberately kept outside the steel entity from inception: the BESS plant (10 GW announced Aug/Nov 2025, scaled to a single-line 20 GW with Rs 1,025 crore capex by Feb 2026) sits in wholly-owned Godawari New Energy Private Limited at AURIC/Bidkin on 112 acres, funded '40% from GPIL and balance... by the debt in the SPV', with GPIL's sanctioned investment raised from Rs 500 crore to Rs 700 crore in May 2026, and the contracting layer put into a second wholly-owned Maharashtra company, Godawari Energy Solutions Private Limited, incorporated 17.10.2026 for BESS/renewables EPC; the residential school likewise sits in 81%-held Godawari Education and Research Foundation, funded by an enabling Rs 150 crore loan at 12% and expected to 'separately go for the loan from the other sources'. The problem this structure solves, on management's own numbers, is margin and capital dilution of the steel franchise: BESS at 7-8% and CRM at 8-10% EBITDA against GPIL's FY26 consolidated 23% EBITDA / 15% PAT, which is why the 2031 vision shows ~Rs 3,000 crore PAT on a much larger top line, and why debt for the new verticals is raised at SPV level with prepayment options rather than loaded on GPIL, management having said explicitly they 'don't want to go back into the same debt cycle, which we had entered last 10 years back'. Nobody is recorded as demanding the separations — not lenders, not partners (EVE, Shanghai Shenyi Roche, FIMER, GAIL contract at the project/subsidiary level) — but analysts repeatedly pressed on exactly this (Vikash Singh on capital allocation and 'Jammu Pigments hasn't done anything yet', Sahil Sanghvi on 'we are getting into low profitable businesses', Divya Agarwal on the 10% PAT margin), and the same pruning instinct earlier killed the 2 mt greenfield steel plant and the OPVC pipe project (Feb 2025).
rationale.evolution: The pruning starts Feb 2025, when the 2 million-ton greenfield steel plant and the OPVC pipe venture are both dropped (capex mis-estimation from ~INR 6,000 crore to INR 8,000 crore-plus, and loss of first-mover advantage) only months after the Dec 2024 call pitched Jammu Pigments as diversification; by Aug 2025 the new verticals are explicitly ring-fenced, BESS placed in 100% subsidiary Godawari New Energy Private Limited with 40% GPIL equity and SPV-level debt, confirmed with land and INR 175 crore equity in Nov 2025. Feb 2026 is the turning point for exits: the Board approves disinvestment of the whole 37.85% Ardent Steel stake for ~INR 91 crores expressly to 'simplify and streamline group structure', and management simultaneously declares Jammu Pigments will run independently with no further GPIL money. May 2026 reports it done — stake de-recognised, INR 91 crore dividend plus ~INR 73 crore standalone gain, INR 17 crore consolidated gain against the INR 36-37 crore Godawari Energy thermal write-off — alongside the GEL merger into GPIL (effective 23.03.2026) and a raise of GNEPL funding to INR 700 crore; then July 2026 extends the sell-down logic to Jammu Pigments (16.75 lakh shares, Rs 298.45, Rs 49.99 crores, 43.96% to 35.36%) and Oct 2026 adds a further carve-out, Godawari Energy Solutions Private Limited, for BESS/renewables EPC.
