rationale.rationale: The business being separated is Greaves Electric Mobility Limited (GEML) — the Ampere/ELE/Greaves 3-Wheelers electric 2W and L5 3W business, with step-downs MLR Auto and Bestway Agencies — which management reclassified under its GREAVES.NEXT strategy (Nov 2025) as an 'investee business' alongside Greaves Finance (ev.fin), as distinct from the 'core' B2B engineering company of Energy, Mobility and Industrial Solutions. Management's stated reasons were: (1) GEML needs growth capital the core cannot and should not fund — the DRHP (filed 23 Dec 2024) sought a ₹1,000 crore primary issue plus a smaller OFS, for technology development, the technology centre, in-house battery assembly, expanding subsidiaries' manufacturing capacity, raising stake in one subsidiary, digitisation/IT, inorganic growth and general corporate purposes, while the core's own ₹500–700 crore capex is funded internally; (2) GEML's losses dilute consolidated profitability — Q2 FY26 EV loss of ~₹50 crore against >₹100 crore EBIT in the other segments, FY26 EV segment result of −₹182.01 crore, GEML consolidated FY26 net loss of ₹204.51 crore, EBITDA improving only from −30% to −20%; (3) capital locked in the investees wrecks returns — of ₹1,619 crore net worth a large part sits in GEML/GFL plus ₹500+ crore cash, roughly ₹900 crore that Manish Poddar took out of the ROCE calculation to leave ~₹700 crore of core capital employed earning 'healthy returns'; (4) the two have different maturity curves, different paths to profitability and different orientation (B2B engineering vs consumer), so they must be managed, measured and valued separately, with GEML's employee cost and investment ahead of revenue not comparable to GCL's; (5) partner Abdul Latif Jameel (then ~36%) did not want to be a promoter after a public listing and so was forced to dilute toward 20%, as set out in the DRHP; and (6) investors repeatedly pressed that the two are worth more apart — Zaki Nasser said Greaves and Greaves EV 'will be worth much more separately' and that against Ola/Bajaj/Ather valuations and a re-rating Kirloskar Oil the combined entity is 'caught somewhere in between', while Krisha Kansara wanted the market 'valuing both our businesses separately'. Post-IPO GCL intended to drop below 51% while remaining the largest shareholder, after which consolidation of EV losses and the parent's financial support would cease — which Parag Satpute confirmed as 'a fair understanding'.
rationale.evolution: The idea surfaced from investors first: on the Nov 2024 call shareholders asked about an IPO or demerger of EV and 'unlocking' value via a separate listing, and Akhila Balachandar would only say the board was 'cognizant'; by the Jan 2025 call the DRHP had been filed (23 Dec 2024) with its use of proceeds, and on the May 2025 call the chairman disclosed SEBI's observations and ALJ's forced dilution from 36% toward 20% because it would not be a promoter post-listing. Through Aug 2025 and Nov 2025 the IPO stayed in 'active conversations' and the separation was formalised conceptually as 'core' versus 'investee' businesses under GREAVES.NEXT, with management saying GCL would fall below 51% but stay the largest shareholder; by Feb 2026 the ₹1,000 crore primary was spelled out, Akhila said there was no plan B, and Saket Kapoor got agreement that the EV drag on parent profits would end. On the May 2026 call the plan had slipped — SEBI extended the observation letter's validity to 30 Sep 2026 and the IPO committee would act only when it could get 'a proper valuation' — and the DRHP gag left management unable to answer breakeven questions at all. The plan then changed materially in the filings: on 9 Jul 2026 the board approved subscribing ₹331.12 crore to a GEML rights issue, on 31 Jul 2026 GEML told SEBI it would not avail the extension so the Offer lapsed, the ₹530 crore rights issue was fully subscribed on 2 Aug 2026 (GCL ₹331.12 crore, ALJ ₹198.87 crore) leaving GCL at an unchanged 62.48%, and the Oct 2026 results wrote off ₹12.66 crore of IPO costs as exceptional — separation deferred to 'an appropriate time'.

points.point: Investors, not management, raised separation first — asking directly whether an IPO or demerger of the EV business would improve focus and growth parameters; management gave no commitment.
points.quote: Second, are we considering an IPO or a demerger of the EV mobility business?

points.point: Asked about value unlocking and listing the segments separately within two-three years, the CFO said only that the board was aware of the option.
points.quote: Any decisions on unlocking of value, capital raise, this is something that the board is cognizant of, and we will come back to you as and when the board gives a different decision.

points.point: GEML's DRHP was filed with SEBI on 23 December 2024, and the use of proceeds was laid out — technology, battery assembly, subsidiary capacity, stake increase, digitisation and inorganic growth, i.e. capital the core would otherwise have to supply.
points.quote: We propose to utilize the proceeds for investments in technology development, enhancing capabilities at our technology center, development of in-house battery assembly, funding expansion of manufacturing capacities of our subsidiaries, increasing the stake in one of the subsidiaries, increasing digitization and deployment of information technology infrastructure, funding inorganic growth opportunities and general corporate purposes.

points.point: A partner requirement drove part of the structure: ALJ, then holding 36%, refused promoter status after listing and therefore had to dilute toward 20%, as reflected in the DRHP.
points.quote: And I think I said in my speech that ALJ did not want to be a promoter post a public listing.

points.point: Shareholders framed the separation as a valuation problem — the engineering business had begun a strong growth trajectory and they wanted the market to price the two businesses independently.
points.quote: I wanted to understand if there is a demand in the market for us to successfully launch this IPO because as investors of Greaves Cotton, it is also very crucial for us that the market starts seeing and valuing both our businesses separately.

points.point: Management made the timing conditional from the outset — SEBI's final observations were in hand but the launch depended on markets, readiness and 'strategic considerations'.
points.quote: The actual IPO launch, however, will be subject to prevailing market conditions, internal preparedness, and other strategic considerations.

points.point: GREAVES.NEXT formalised the split: GCL core is a B2B engineering company (Energy, Mobility, Industrial Solutions) while Greaves Electric and Greaves Finance are consumer-facing 'investee' businesses to be managed differently, with core growth of 16–20% CAGR and ₹500–700 crore capex ring-fenced to the core.
points.quote: While our investee companies of Greaves Electric and Greaves Finance will continue to pursue their growth ambitions, the core of Greaves Cotton Limited will remain centered on building a trusted future-ready engineering company.

points.point: An investor quantified the drag the separation is meant to remove — a ₹50 crore quarterly EV loss against more than ₹100 crore of EBIT in the rest of the group, with consolidated EBIT margin of 17% ex-EV.
points.quote: This quarter also, EV reported Rs. 50 crore loss, while the other segments reported more than Rs. 100 crore of EBIT?

points.point: Management stated the intended end-state ownership: GCL would go below 51% after the IPO (deconsolidating control) but stay a large shareholder.
points.quote: But yes, that is the strategic thinking that post the IPO, we will be below 51% but we will continue to remain significant large shareholders in the company.

points.point: The funding purpose was restated with numbers — a ₹1,000 crore primary issue flowing directly into GEML (plus a smaller OFS to GCL and ALJ), which the CFO identified as the very point of the IPO when asked how long the loss-making business could be sustained.
points.quote: And if you have read through the documents, we will be raising approximately a primary of 1,000 crores, which will be utilized for funding the growth aspirations of Greaves Electric Mobility.

points.point: Management confirmed an investor's reading that after the raise the parent's financial support to, and consolidation drag from, the mobility business would cease, leaving a clean view of core operations — Parag Satpute replied 'That's a fair understanding.'
points.quote: So that is the only fair understanding investors can keep in mind that by May, we should expect that this depleting of the profitability for the parent company because of consolidation and its financial support to the mobility franchise will cease and we will have fair understanding of the core operations of the company.

points.point: Pressed on the nine-month delay since SEBI's May 2025 observations and on alternatives if the IPO did not happen, the CFO said there was no plan B.
points.quote: The plan A is to go for the IPO and we are working on that.

points.point: Timing slipped again: SEBI's April 2026 circular extended observation-letter validity to 30 September 2026, and the IPO committee would wait for a favourable market and 'a proper valuation'.
points.quote: This allows us more time therefore to get into a favorable market scenario and then the investment committee and the IPO committee to take an appropriate call on timing for the IPO.

points.point: An investor pressed that the combined structure was being penalised in the market relative to loss-making EV peers whose capitalisation was rising and to core peer Kirloskar Oil at highs.
points.quote: But the path is there to separate the two, right, sir?

points.point: The return-on-capital case: of ₹1,619 crore net worth, the investee stakes plus ₹500+ crore cash — roughly ₹900 crore — must be stripped out, leaving ~₹700 crore of core capital employed earning healthy returns, with normalisation expected in 2–3 years.
points.quote: I think overall, if you see the net worth at INR 1,619 crores, a big portion of that is into the invest ee businesses, the Greaves Electric Mobility and Greaves Finance Limited.

points.point: The 13–15% EBITDA and 16–18% growth guidance applies only to the core (standalone plus Excel and Greaves Technologies); GEML and GFL are explicitly excluded as being on a different path to profitability.
points.quote: Grea ves Electric Mobility and Greaves Finance Limited are part of our invest ee businesses.

points.point: A cost of the unfinished separation: the live DRHP barred management from giving GEML breakeven, loss-reduction or topline guidance to its own shareholders, repeatedly, through FY26.
points.quote: Sorry to interrupt, but we are held back by the statutory compliances and therefore kindly appreciate our limitations to answer this question.

points.point: On 9 July 2026 the GCL board approved subscribing its full entitlement — about ₹331.12 crore — in a GEML rights issue, and authorised the Risk, Strategy and Investment Committee to take up any unsubscribed shares: funding GEML from the parent instead of from the public market.
points.quote: (a) Subscription to the equity shares proposed to be issued by Greaves Electric Mobility Limited, a material subsidiary of the Company, pursuant to its rights issue, to the full extent of the Company's rights entitlement, aggregating up to approximately ₹331.12 crore; and

points.point: On 31 July 2026 the BRLMs told SEBI that because of the rights issue and SEBI ICDR restrictions on further issuances, GEML would not use the extension, so the final observations lapsed and the IPO was abandoned.
points.quote: Consequently, the Company will not be proceeding with the Offer.

points.point: The ₹530 crore rights issue was fully subscribed on 2 August 2026 by GCL (~₹331 crore) and ALJ (₹198.87 crore) pro rata, so GCL's holding stayed at 62.48% and GEML remained a consolidated material subsidiary — no separation occurred.
points.quote: The Company's shareholding in GEML remains unchanged at 62.48%, and GEML continues to be a material subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: The listing was deferred rather than cancelled, with the stated purpose of the capital being next-generation products, battery management systems, powertrains and new-age technology.
points.quote: While GEML has presently decided not to avail itself of the SEBI extension for the proposed Offer , it remains committed to pursuing a public listing at an appropriate time, subject to market conditions, regulatory approvals and other relevant considerations.

points.point: The abandoned separation was written off in H1 FY27 — ₹12.66 crore consolidated (₹1.72 crore standalone) of IPO costs as an exceptional item, alongside ₹20.09 crore of Bestway goodwill/brand impairment and accelerated depreciation of ₹7.75 crore on discontinued 2W tooling and ₹19.55 crore on a 3W brand.
points.quote: Consequentl y, IPO­ refated expenses of Rs. 12.66 crore have been recognized in the Statement of Profit and Loss and disclosed as an exceptional item.

points.point: Separation also showed up in reporting structure: from H1 FY27 Cables & Control Levers was merged into Engines and Engineering Products and vehicle finance was carved out as its own reported segment.
points.quote: During the period ended September 30, 2026, the Group has reorganised its segments by (a) merging Cables & Control levers segment as part of Engines and Engineering Products and (b) Separately reporting the vehicle finance business.

rationale.what_management_expects: GEML: ₹1,000 crore primary for technology, in-house battery assembly, subsidiary capacity, digitisation, inorganic growth, and its own market valuation. GCL core: 16–18% organic growth, 13–15% EBITDA, ₹500–700 crore internally funded capex, no further consolidation drag on profits, improved ROCE once the ~₹900 crore tied up in investees and cash is deployed; GCL below 51% yet largest shareholder.
rationale.gaps: No GEML breakeven date or volume, no valuation, no post-listing accounting treatment, no reason rights replaced the IPO beyond market conditions, no cap on further GCL funding.

rationale.rationale: The separation is of HFCL's defence & aerospace business, which is being consolidated out of the listed parent into subsidiary HFCL Advance Systems Private Limited (HASPL), with a Board Restructuring Committee (formed April 30, 2026, advised by Ernst & Young from the July 2026 call) simultaneously studying whether to go further and demerge HFCL's other verticals — optical fibre/OFC, telecom products, and the EPC/turnkey business. Management's stated problem is that the three businesses need entirely different people and execution capability: 'Defense requires different capability, different set of people. EPC needs a different set of people, and fiber business needs a different set of people.' The binding constraint Nahata named twice on the April 30, 2026 call was partner capital: HFCL had received offers from strategic partners, but 'any strategic partner cannot come into such a mix of products where defense, EPC and cable and telecom all are mixed up,' and when asked how the ~₹230 crore Andhra Pradesh ammunition plant would be funded he said equity partnership 'cannot be done when you are a mix of a telecom, defense and fiber-optic. That's why this restructuring committee.' The second driver was an acquisition HFCL could not do organically: the Defsys aerostructures business carries certifications and a confirmed export-oriented order book of ~₹1,930 crore (₹1,890 crore in the June 3, 2026 filings), and Nahata said building it in-house 'would not have been possible for next five to seven years' because aerostructure component approvals take five to seven years. HASPL became the vehicle: on June 3, 2026 HFCL subscribed ₹89.25 crore of a ₹175 crore round (HFCL left at 51.02%, Anant Nahata 6.50%, the Gupta/DMG group 9.50% with two of six board seats and veto rights, ITI Holdings 14.99%, BAS Engineering 3%, and a 14.99% employee ESOP trust), bought 80% of Raddef for ₹75 crore, slump-sold its thermal weapon sight business (FY26 revenue ₹0.66 crore, net worth ₹21.24 crore) in for ₹50 crore, and had HASPL buy HFCL Defence Systems (ex-Spiral EHL, FY26 turnover ₹166.21 crore) for ₹25 crore plus the Defsys aerostructure business for ₹25 crore. The quantitative prize management attached to it: defence order book rising from ~₹300 crore to ~₹2,230 crore, FY27 defence revenue of ~₹500 crore, and an aspiration of ₹3,000 crore-plus by FY29 and ₹5,000 crore the year after — against a group order book of ₹21,200 crore at FY26 and ₹26,665 crore by Q1 FY27 — in a business management says could eventually be 'nearly comparable in scale to HFCL's current overall business.' The stated objectives are to simplify the group structure, sharpen execution focus, improve capital efficiency and unlock long-term shareholder value, bounded by three principles: long-term shareholder value, operational effectiveness and financial discipline.
rationale.evolution: The idea was put to management by an analyst, not volunteered: on the Oct 17, 2025 call Abhishek Jain (Arihant) asked whether three segments — telecom products, EPC, defence — made a case for value unlocking via demerger, and Nahata replied they had 'not really thought about any such thing at this point of time'; the Feb 3, 2026 call carried no restructuring discussion at all (the capital question there was the ₹550 crore QIP). By the Apr 30, 2026 (Q4 FY26) call the March 25, 2026 Board had already approved consolidating defence under HASPL and a Strategic Restructuring Committee was formed 'today itself,' with Nahata framing it as what to merge and what to demerge, driven by differing capabilities and by strategic-partner offers that cannot enter a mixed entity, while refusing the word 'demerger' for defence ('We are currently trying to consolidate it under one roof'). The June 3, 2026 filings executed the first leg — share subscription and shareholders' agreement for HASPL, 80% of Raddef, the TWS slump sale, and the Defsys aerostructure/HDSPL acquisitions — taking HFCL to 51.02% of the defence platform. On the Jul 22, 2026 call the scope widened and slowed: Ernst & Young was appointed strategic advisor, 'various alternatives' were still under evaluation with no specific outcome commented on, and Nahata clarified the carve-out is partial — ammunition and electronic fuzes 'are still remaining in HFCL.'

points.point: An analyst first raised demerger as a value-unlocking route given three distinct segments (telecom products, EPC, defence); management said it had not considered it.
points.quote: is there any compelling case for value unlocking via demerger or any other opportunity for us?

points.point: Nahata explicitly declined the idea at that stage, promising to revert if it was ever taken up — the baseline against which the later reversal should be read.
points.quote: We have not really thought about any such thing at this point of time. If we think about it, we'll come back to you.

points.point: Opening remarks disclosed the March 25, 2026 Board approval to consolidate complementary defence capabilities under subsidiary HASPL as a dedicated defence and aerospace platform.
points.quote: The core objective of this proposed transaction is to create a focused and scalable and future ready defence and aer ospace platform by consolidating complementary defence capabilities under our subsidiary, HFCL Advance Systems Private Limited.

points.point: Management's stated structural problem: each vertical needs a different skill set and execution model, which is why a Restructuring Committee was constituted to decide what to merge and what to demerge.
points.quote: Defense requires different capability, different set of people. EPC needs a diff erent set of people, and fiber business needs a different set of people.

points.point: The trigger named was inbound strategic-partner interest that cannot be accommodated inside a conglomerate entity mixing defence, EPC, cable and telecom.
points.quote: Now, any strategic partner cannot come into such a mix of products where defense, EPC and cable and telecom all are mixed up.

points.point: Asked how the 1,000-acre Andhra ammunition plant would be funded, Nahata tied the impossibility of an equity partnership directly to the mixed structure — the clearest statement of the capital-raising motive.
points.quote: There's no plan of any partnership at this point of time because partnership -- equity partnership cannot be done when you are a mix of a telecom, defense and fiber-optic. That's why this restructuring committee.

points.point: Management distinguished the defence step (consolidation under one roof) from a demerger, saying the committee formed that day would study whether demerging into specialised entities is more efficient and would enable strategic tie-ups.
points.quote: But a restructuring committee has been formed precisely to look into such aspects, whether it is efficient to demerge the businesses into the specialized areas so that some strategic tie-up or even if that kind of thing is required, can be done.

points.point: The stated benefits of the HASPL structure for the defence vertical were execution focus, capital efficiency and sustainable growth.
points.quote: We believe that the proposed structure will sharpen execution focus, improve capital efficiency and drive sustainable growth from defence vertical.

points.point: The acquired aerospace/aerostructure business brings certifications and a confirmed export order book of ~₹1,930 crore, lifting the defence order book from ~₹300 crore to ~₹2,230 crore.
points.quote: Importantly, this business comes with established capability base, certifications, long-standing customer relationships and a confirmed export -orien ted order book of approximately INR 1,930 crore, providing immediate revenue visibility.

points.point: Buy-versus-build rationale: aerostructure approvals take five to seven years per component, so entering greenfield was not feasible — hence acquisition into a dedicated platform.
points.quote: If we had tried ourselves, it would not have been possible for next five to seven years with an order book and with certified products and with possibility to get more orders.

points.point: The mandate was restated as group-wide simplification and value unlocking, and Ernst & Young was appointed strategic advisor, with no specific outcome disclosed.
points.quote: As communicated earlier, our Board had constituted a Restructuring Committee to evaluate strategic alternat ives aimed at simplifying the Group structure, enhancing operational efficiency and unlocking long -term shareholder value.

points.point: Three governing principles were set out for any restructuring outcome, with management declining to comment on specifics at that stage.
points.quote: While it would not be appropriate t o comment on specific outcomes at this stage, I would like to assure our shareholders that every decision will be guided by three fundamental principles creating long -term shareholder value, strengthening operational effectiveness and preserving financial discipline.

points.point: The carve-out is partial: ammunition and electronic fuzes stay in listed HFCL, and the wider restructuring design is still being worked out with E&Y.
points.quote: It's not the ent ire ammunition business, Electronic Fuzes, those are still remaining in HFCL and we are not -- how we would restructure the entire business.

points.point: A shareholder challenged HFCL being left with only ~51% of the defence platform; Nahata rejected the dilution framing because the same step brought in an acquired business with a >₹2,000 crore order book.
points.quote: Wait, wait. You are not realizing one thing. We have not diluted. We have acquired business also.

points.point: The June 3, 2026 board outcome states the purpose: a focused, scalable platform strengthening existing defence and adding aerostructures, with immediate access to a ~₹1,890 crore export order book and consolidation of aerostructures, radar/surveillance and thermal weapon sights.
points.quote: The aforesaid transaction is intended to establish a focused and scalable platform to strengthen HFCL's existing defence business and expand its presence in the aerostructures segment through HASPL.

points.point: Rationale given for slump-selling HFCL's thermal weapon sight business (FY26 revenue ₹0.66 crore, 0.01% of consolidated revenue; net worth ₹21.24 crore) into HASPL for ₹50 crore.
points.quote: The transfer is aimed at achieving focused management , improved operational efficiencies, optimal resource allocation, and enhanced synergies within the defence vertical, while enabling the Company to strengthen its overall strategic positioning and effectively capitalise on growth opportunities in the sector, in line with its long -term business objectives.

points.point: The structure is explicitly designed to keep control while admitting outside investors — HFCL at 51.02%, DMG group 9.50% with 2 of 6 board seats and veto rights, ITI Holdings 14.99%, and a 14.99% employee ESOP trust, out of a ₹175 crore round.
points.quote: Post completion of th is transaction, HASPL will continue to remain a subsidiary of the Company , ensuring continued control while benefiting from participation by other investors.

points.point: The May 1, 2026 EGM clarification shows HFCL funds only ₹90 crore of the ₹175 crore needed for the four HASPL-level acquisitions, with the balance ₹85 crore raised by HASPL itself — the practical point of a separate vehicle.
points.quote: Accordingly, the balance amount of ₹85 crore shall be arranged by HFCL Advance Systems Private Limited from other permissible sources, in accordance with applicable laws.

rationale.what_management_expects: For defence/aerospace (HASPL): sharpened execution focus, improved capital efficiency, access to strategic-partner and outside equity impossible inside the mixed parent, ESOP-led talent incentives, order book from ~₹300 to ~₹2,230 crore, ~₹500 crore FY27 revenue scaling to ₹3,000–5,000 crore, margins a couple of points above group. For HFCL: a simpler group, each business realising full growth potential, and unlocked long-term shareholder value.
rationale.gaps: No demerger decision, timeline, listing or swap ratio; no valuation of any vertical; no E&Y recommendation; no reason ammunition and fuzes stay in HFCL.

rationale.rationale: There is no separation, demerger or spin-off of a business by ICICI Bank in these texts — the question's premise is not supported by the transcripts or the filing, and the dominant direction of travel is the opposite: consolidation of group entities into the Bank. The nearest things management actually described are four entity-level reorganizations. (1) Pension funds: the Board on July 19, 2025 approved acquiring 100% of ICICI Prudential Pension Funds Management Company Limited from ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, moving it from a step-down subsidiary of ICICI Life to a direct wholly owned subsidiary of the Bank; the share purchase agreement was executed January 12, 2026, and on the Jan 2026 media call Sandeep Batra said the rationale was that 'the synergy with the Bank will be better and the business will be able to expand in a much better fashion,' i.e. 'synergising with the banking set of customers'; ICICI Life booked a Rs. 1.1 billion gain on the sale, which was part of why its FY2026 PAT rose 34.6% to Rs. 16.00 billion (25.0% excluding the sale). (2) ICICI Venture's private equity, venture capital and real estate fund management business was approved in principle on May 8, 2025 for transfer to ICICI Prudential AMC, completed with ICICI Prudential AMC managing the transferred funds effective April 1, 2026; the stated purpose was 'offering of an integrated full range of investment asset classes, including private equity,' while ICICI Venture keeps only 'certain advisory activities' and 'certain residual funds' — ICICI Venture's PAT jumped to Rs. 1.5 billion in FY2026 from Rs. 0.2 billion in FY2025. (3) A small divestment of the Bank's entire stake in the NIIT Institute of Finance and Banking JV (set up around 2006), which Batra on Apr 2025 called 'a very small amount' done to 'rationalise and simplify our own portfolio where we want to remain focused on.' (4) Closure of the Offshore Banking Unit in the SEEPZ, Mumbai, for which RBI gave a no-objection letter in May 2026 (a prior OBU closure had already pushed Rs. 3.40 billion of negative foreign currency translation reserve into the Q4-FY2024 P&L). Against these, the Bank was pulling businesses in, not pushing them out: ICICI Securities was delisted on March 24, 2025 and became wholly owned (56 million ICICI Bank shares issued at a 67:100 swap, which Anindya Banerjee cited as the main reason net worth rose about Rs. 20,000 crore sequentially, 'while it's capital neutral'); the Bank bought ~2% more of ICICI Prudential AMC and ~2% more of ICICI Life, explicitly 'towards maintaining the Bank's majority shareholding' against stock-based compensation dilution; it infused Rs. 5.0 billion (including Rs. 500 crore in Q3-FY2026) into ICICI Home Finance, which Batra justified as meeting 'the regulatory requirement and expansion that is required from their business point of view'; and it acquired the remaining equity of I-Process Services. The only genuine ownership separations described are at the partner/JV level, not the Bank's: ICICI Prudential AMC listed on BSE and NSE effective December 19, 2025 following Prudential Corporation Holdings' February 2025 announcement of a 'potential listing and partial divestment of its stake,' and after PCHL agreed on May 17, 2026 to buy 75% of Bharti Life, ICICI Life applied to IRDAI to reclassify PCHL from 'promoter' to 'investor' and to rename itself 'ICICI Life Insurance Limited' (IRDAI approved the name change August 7, 2026).
rationale.evolution: No separation idea ever surfaces as such: on Apr 2025 (call of April 19, 2025) the only disposal discussed is the small NIIT Institute JV stake sale, framed as portfolio simplification, in the same quarter ICICI Securities was delisted into the Bank (March 24, 2025). The ICICI Venture PE/VC/real-estate fund management transfer was approved in principle on May 8, 2025 and the pension-fund acquisition on July 19, 2025 — the same day as the Jul 2025 call, where neither was mentioned and no analyst asked. By Jan 2026 (call of January 17, 2026) Batra confirmed the pension step-down subsidiary had been brought under the Bank, noting 'we explained this, I think, about two quarters back when we made the decision,' and the Oct 2025 transcript is unreadable so any interim discussion is unverifiable; the Apr 2026 call (April 18, 2026) contains no mention of any of it, and only the September 18, 2026 Annual Securities Report records the ICICI Venture transfer as effective April 1, 2026 and the PCHL promoter-to-investor reclassification.

points.point: Batra confirmed the Bank had taken over the pension fund business from ICICI Life, explaining it was a step-down subsidiary and that the decision had been disclosed about two quarters earlier.
points.quote: It was a step-down subsidiary. We explained this, I think, about two quarters back when we made the decision.

points.point: The stated rationale for moving the pension fund manager under the Bank was synergy with the Bank's customer base and faster expansion, not value unlocking or capital release.
points.quote: We do believe that the synergy with the Bank will be better and the business will be able to expand in a much better fashion.

points.point: Asked directly whether the pension business had been acquired from the subsidiary, Batra confirmed it in one word; no numbers, consideration or targets were given on the call.
points.quote: Yes, we have.

points.point: The only outright exit discussed on any call — the entire stake in the NIIT Institute of Finance and Banking JV set up around 2006 — was framed as immaterial portfolio simplification, with no consideration disclosed.
points.quote: And over the period, we are just wanting to rationalise and simplify our own portfolio where we want to remain focused on.

points.point: The one real carve-out of a business line in the texts: ICICI Venture's private equity, venture capital and real estate fund management business was approved for transfer to ICICI Prudential AMC on May 8, 2025, with ICICI Prudential AMC managing those funds from April 1, 2026.
points.quote: On May 8, 2025, ICICI Venture Funds Management Company Limited's Board of Directors and ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited's Board of Directors, in their respective meetings, approved, in principle, a proposal to transfer the private equity, venture capital and real estate fund management business of ICICI Venture Funds Management Company Limited to ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited.

points.point: The purpose of that transfer was to give ICICI Prudential AMC a complete asset-class platform, leaving ICICI Venture with only advisory work and residual funds.
points.quote: The transaction enabled the offering of an integrated full range of investment asset classes, including private equity, by ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited.

points.point: The pension transaction was a Board-approved intra-group purchase to convert a step-down subsidiary into a direct wholly owned subsidiary, conditional on RBI and PFRDA approvals; the SPA was executed January 12, 2026.

judge.what_is_spun: Nothing separated; documents describe merger by absorption of REC Limited into Power Finance Corporation Limited
judge.reason: Union Budget proposal to restructure PFC and REC "to achieve scale and improve efficiency in the Public Sector NBFCs"; create a single focused institution for power sector financing
judge.insiders: PFC holds 52.63% of REC since 2019; Government of India to retain control and merged entity's "Government Company" status, possibly via capital infusion; GoI stake would fall to 41%-42% on plain swap
judge.hidden_value: Swap of 88 PFC shares per 100 REC shares; consolidated loan book INR 11.64 lakh crore, consolidated PAT INR 33,625 crore, net NPA 0.13%, leverage 7.7x-7.8x; group borrowing exposure limit drops from 25% to 20%
judge.selling_pressure_why: Documents state REC dissolves and its shareholders receive PFC shares, but say nothing about index exclusion or shareholder flows
judge.listing_timeline: No new listing; REC is to be "dissolved without being wound up" and PFC issues Consideration Shares; management said on May 13, 2026 "We are targeting for the merged entity to come into existence by 1st of April 2027"; NSE observation letter dated October 19, 2026 valid six months for filing with NCLT
judge.read_next: The draft Scheme's valuation report and Para 25(1) pre-conditions in the NCLT shareholder notice
judge.quote: We are targeting for the merged entity to come into existence by 1st of April 2027.

listing.text: IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2026-06-28; date not fixed — No new listing; REC is to be "dissolved without being wound up" and PFC issues Consideration Shares; management said on May 13, 2026 "We are targeting for the merged entity to come into existence by 1st of April 2027"; NSE observation letter dated October 19, 2026 valid six months for filing with NCLT

rationale.rationale: These documents describe no separation at all: the only restructuring in them is the opposite — a merger by absorption of REC Limited (a 52.63% PFC subsidiary since the 2019 acquisition) into PFC, announced by the Hon'ble Finance Minister in the Union Budget of 1 February 2026 "to achieve scale and improve efficiency in the Public Sector NBFCs, as a first step", and given in-principle board approval at both companies on 6 February 2026. Management's stated reasoning is that funding the power sector toward "Viksit Bharat 2047" needs one institution rather than two near-identical lenders: CMD Parminder Chopra said a unified institution unlocks "better scale, strong capital efficiency, faster decision-making, deeper sector reach and larger financing capabilities" and will be "a single window financing partner for India's power sector", adding that integration is easy because both have very similar business models, regulatory frameworks, and already-aligned lending, pricing, accounting and operational policies. The scale cited on the May 2026 call: consolidated loan book ~INR 11.64 lakh crore (largest NBFC book in India), renewable book INR 1.65 lakh crore, consolidated PAT INR 33,625 crore, consolidated net NPA ~0.13%; PFC standalone FY26 PAT INR 20,051 crore (+16%), net worth past INR 1 lakh crore, CRAR 23.44% with Tier-1 21.93%, standalone book ~INR 5.8 lakh crore growing only 7% against 10-11% guidance because banks aggressively refinanced commissioned assets — and the 12 February 2026 filing says the merged entity "would be positioned as the largest power sector financer in India" with better balance-sheet strength, capital efficiencies and operational synergies, plus stronger technical capability for green hydrogen, CCUS, small modular nuclear reactors and storage. The problems named: two lean teams duplicating work ("we are just 520 and so is the number for the REC", ~1,000 combined, with two people looking at the same account, to be redeployed into monitoring, relationship management, compliance, GIFT City and REC's regional offices); the hold-co discount and an underpriced stock, raised by an investor in May 2024; and the unfinished "logical conclusion" of the 2019 acquisition. It was asked for by the Government of India as majority shareholder — through the Budget, with cabinet and presidential approval required under PFC's Articles — and earlier pressed by minority investors on valuation grounds; lenders and partners are not cited as requesters. Management openly conceded two costs: bank borrowing capacity shrinks because the exposure cap moves from the 25% group limit (itself down from 20%+20% pre-2019) to a 20% single-entity limit, which they argue is manageable given the top-ten banks' aggregate Tier-1 of ~INR 18 lakh crore and a borrowing mix of ~57% domestic bonds, 25% foreign currency, 18% bank/FI; and a plain share swap takes Government holding to ~41-42%, below the Companies Act 50% line, which the Government has committed to cure — possibly by issuing securities to or infusing capital from the Centre — so the merged entity stays a "Government Company". The only genuine business separations in the record are never discussed on any call: PFC Consulting builds transmission SPVs and sells each to the TBCB-winning bidder (e.g. Jam Khambhaliya REZ at INR 19.22 crore, Kakinada I at INR 20.51 crore, Kurnool IV REZ at INR 20.94 crore), a mandated bid-process-coordinator mechanic, not a strategic de-merger.
rationale.evolution: The idea first surfaced only as an investor complaint at the 15 May 2024 investor meet, where a shareholder asked how the Government could be influenced to consolidate given the hold-co discount, and the CMD replied that the merger had always been the logical conclusion of the 2019 acquisition but was put on the back burner by COVID and other Government priorities, pending the majority shareholder's direction; the Nov 2024, Feb 2025, May 2025 and Nov 2025 calls contain no mention of it at all. It became policy with the Finance Minister's Budget announcement of 1 February 2026, a BSE/NSE clarification on 3 February, in-principle board approvals on 6 February and a detailed synergy/exposure note on 12 February 2026. By the 13 May 2026 call the plan had hardened into a merger (not some other restructuring) with legal, transaction, merchant-banking and valuation advisers appointed, a target vesting date of 1 April 2027, and open questions on valuation, the draft scheme, Government-company status and manpower. Execution then proceeded step by step: the Board reserved the proposal for the President on 16 May 2026, presidential approval came 10 June 2026, the Board approved the scheme and the 88:100 PFC:REC share-exchange ratio on 28 June 2026, RBI's no-objection arrived 15 October 2026 and the BSE/NSE observation letters on 19 October 2026, SEBI's clearance being conditional on the RBI approval and settlement of outstanding dues.

points.point: The restructuring originates in the Union Budget of 1 February 2026 (para 43), where the Finance Minister framed it as a scale-and-efficiency measure for public sector NBFCs, and PFC's board took it on record and gave in-principle approval to a merger on 6 February 2026.
points.quote: In order to achieve scale and improve efficiency in the Public Sector NBFCs, as a first step, it is proposed to restructure the Power Finance Corporation and Rural Electrification Corporation.

points.point: Chopra's core rationale: one institution rather than two for the power sector's capital needs on the road to Viksit Bharat 2047, built on PFC's existing 52.63% REC stake from 2019.
points.quote: A unified institution will help unlock better scale, strong capital efficiency, faster decision-making, deeper sector reach and larger financing capabilities.

points.point: The positioning objective for the combined lender is to be the sector's one-stop financier.
points.quote: The combined entity will be positioned as a single window financing partner for India's power sector.

points.point: Integration risk is downplayed because the two businesses are already near-identical in model, regulation and policy, so the merger is presented as a formality over an existing alignment.
points.quote: Over the last few years, we have aligned many of our policies across lending, pricing, accounting and operational processes.

points.point: Timeline and approval set: vesting targeted for 1 April 2027 subject to MCA, RBI, SEBI, cabinet and presidential approval, with legal, transaction, merchant-banking and valuation advisers already appointed.
points.quote: We are targeting for the merged entity to come into existence by 1st of April 2027.

points.point: Asked by Nomura's Shreya about 600-700 overlapping employees on each side, Chopra said no portfolio-level plan existed yet, and that the ~1,000 combined staff would be redeployed into monitoring, relationship management, compliance, GIFT City and REC's regional offices rather than cut.
points.quote: So, we are just 1000 employees and looking at the portfolio.

points.point: Piran Engineer (CLSA) pressed on the Government-company test: a plain swap takes Government holding to ~41-42%, below the Companies Act 50% line.
points.quote: But the Government has committed that they are going to maintain the status of the merged entity as the government Company.

points.point: The acknowledged cost of merging is a tighter borrowing cap — from a 25% group limit (itself reduced from 20%+20% before the 2019 acquisition) down to a 20% single-entity limit — which Chopra argued is absorbable given rising bank net worth and limited current utilisation.
points.quote: And now if from the two entities the merged entity comes into picture, the borrowing limit is going to reduce from 25% to 20%.

points.point: Scale credentials cited alongside the restructuring: largest NBFC loan book and highest NBFC profit, with very low NPAs after resolving Sinnar Thermal (INR 3,001 crore, 42% principal recovered, ~INR 670 crore write-back) and TRN Energy (INR 1,139 crore, ~INR 160 crore reversal).
points.quote: With this size, balance sheet strength and sector experience, we believe that PFC and REC restructuring will create a financial institution of significant scale and strategic relevance.

points.point: On dividends post-merger, Chopra noted the present leakage — REC's dividend enters PFC's profit and only 30% of that flows out, so investors effectively get ~9% of it — and said the merged entity will declare 30% of merged profit under the DIPAM policy, subject to RBI's NBFC dividend norms.
points.quote: And once the merged entity is there profitability of both the companies are there.

points.point: Shareholder Manoj Chandani asked the Government nominee director to influence the majority shareholder toward consolidation, arguing the largest NBFC was undervalued at ~7x PE and low price-to-book because of cross-holding between two companies.
points.quote: On the consolidation front, yes, there is an issue of hold co discount and how you are seeing that the stock is underpriced.

points.point: Chopra answered on the nominee director's behalf that merger was always the intended end-state of the 2019 REC acquisition, shelved by COVID and other Government priorities, and that PFC was awaiting the majority shareholder's direction — two years before the Budget announcement delivered exactly that.
points.quote: You know, at that time of acquisition, the intent, the logical conclusion for the acquisition was the merger of the two companies.

points.point: The 12 February 2026 clarification quantifies the synergy case and the capital/exposure mechanics: credit-concentration limits will apply to consolidated Tier 1, no borrower-exposure breach is foreseen, and the merged entity targets emerging technologies (green hydrogen, CCUS, small modular nuclear reactors, storage).
points.quote: Based on consolidated metrics, the merged entity would be positioned as the largest power sector financer in India.

points.point: On 28 June 2026 the board approved the scheme under Sections 230-232, fixing consideration and providing for REC's dissolution without winding up.
points.quote: 88 equity shares of PFC of INR 10/- each fully paid up for every 100 equity shares of REC of INR 10/- each fully paid up

points.point: The 16 May 2026 board reserved the proposal for the President of India and allowed for capital infusion/securities issuance to the Centre to preserve Government-company status; presidential approval followed on 10 June 2026.
points.quote: subject to maintaining the merged entity's status as a 'Government Company' (including by way of issuance of necessary securities to I infusion of capital by, the Central Government)

points.point: Regulatory clearances landed in October 2026 — RBI's no-objection on 15 October and BSE/NSE observation letters on 19 October — with SEBI's comment making the letter effective only on receipt of the RBI approval and settlement of outstanding dues.
points.quote: The observation letter issued is conditional upon receipt of approval from the sectoral regulator.

points.point: The only actual business separations in the record are the mandated sales of PFC Consulting's transmission SPVs to competitive-bidding winners (Jam Khambhaliya REZ INR 19.22 crore, Lakadia C INR 19.94 crore, Kakinada I INR 20.51 crore, Kurnool IV REZ INR 20.94 crore, among others), each described as negligible to revenue and not a slump sale; no earnings call mentions them.
points.quote: The SPV has to be transferred to the Successful Bidder selected through International Competitive Bidding Process under Tariff Based Competitive Bidding Guidelines.

rationale.what_management_expects: No separation is expected; the merger is expected to produce one lender with ~INR 11.64 lakh crore book and INR 33,625 crore PAT, the largest power financier, with better scale, capital efficiency, faster decisions, operational synergies, deeper reach for emerging technologies, redeployed manpower, dividends on merged profit, and (per investors) removal of the hold-co discount. Borrowing cap narrows 25%-to-20%.
rationale.gaps: No separation was ever proposed, so no separation rationale exists. Unexplained: valuation basis for 88:100, how Government stake returns above 50%, cost-synergy or ROE quantification, employee restructuring.

segments.measure_notes: No segment reporting exists for REC: PFC's standalone and consolidated accounts state operations comprise only one business segment, so there is no segment revenue or segment result/EBIT/EBITDA disclosure. The only REC-specific profit figure on these pages is REC's share in consolidated profit and loss under the Schedule III disclosure (note 61.2), which is a post-tax profit (PAT) amount before consolidation adjustments/eliminations. No REC revenue or operating-profit line is carried; revenue breakdowns on these pages (note 58.2) are Group-level (PFC consolidated), not REC's own.

rationale.rationale: On these texts alone, Tata Technologies Ltd. is not separating any business of its own — no demerger, spin-off, slump sale, carve-out or segment separation of TATATECH is proposed, discussed or filed in the three years of calls or in the filing. The only separation documented is at its parent: the filing of 2026-01-16 records that Tata Motors Limited (now Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited), 'the Holding Company of Tata Technologies Ltd', approved at its board meeting of August 1, 2024 a Composite Scheme of Arrangement demerging its Commercial Vehicle business undertaking into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited and merging erstwhile Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited into the listed TML, 'thereby resulting in two separate listed companies for the CV and Passenger Vehicle businesses'; the NCLT Mumbai Bench approved it and it took effect October 1, 2025, after which Tata Motors Passenger Vehicle Limited became TATATECH's holding company. Management's only commentary on it came on the Jan 2026 call in answer to an investor (Venkata Siva Ram) who asked 'how Tata Tech is seeing demerger of Tata Motors?' — Warren Harris said TATATECH was 'very instrumental in enabling the 2 organizations to separate', having been 'responsible at Tata Motors for a lot of their enterprise applications' and having done 'much of the work to enable both companies to stand alone and manage their operations independently'. So TATATECH is the vendor to the separation, not its subject: the rationale, problems solved and requesting parties for the CV/PV split are never explained in these texts, only the fact of it, its effective date and its effect on TATATECH's demand. Harris framed the outcome commercially — prospects for both CV and PV 'are strong', CV 'reinforced by the impending acquisition of Iveco', and 'the impact for us, we expect to be accretive and positive'. Everything TATATECH itself did over these 36 months runs the other way — adding businesses, not separating them: acquiring ES-TEC (€51.4m fixed plus up to €14.6m variable, ~300+ engineers, VW access), scaling the BMW TechWorks JV past 2,000 engineers, and explicitly refusing to diversify or restructure its own Services / Technology Solutions mix ('we're not looking to diversify into other industry verticals', May 2026).
rationale.evolution: Nothing on any TATATECH separation appears in Feb 2025, Apr 2025, Jul 2025 or Oct 2025. The parent's scheme, board-approved August 1, 2024, surfaces in these materials only via the Jan 2026 filing (NCLT-approved, effective October 1, 2025, changing TATATECH's holding company) and, the same day, on the Jan 2026 call, where it is raised by a retail investor rather than by management and answered as a delivery credential plus a demand tailwind (Iveco integration, accretive impact). It is not mentioned again in May 2026 or Jul 2026, where the strategic narrative is the opposite — ES-TEC integration, BMW JV scaling, full-vehicle and Tenneco wins, and an explicit decision to stay in Automotive/IHM/Aerospace.

points.point: The only separation in the record is the parent's: Tata Motors' board approved on August 1, 2024 a Composite Scheme demerging the Commercial Vehicle undertaking into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited and merging erstwhile TMPV into listed TML, creating two separate listed companies for CV and PV. No rationale is given in the filing.

rationale.rationale: On the evidence of these texts alone, Cohance Lifesciences is NOT separating a business: across the nine supplied transcripts (Dec 2024 through May 2026) and the one supplied filing (Board outcome, 27 April 2026) there is no demerger, spin-off, slump sale, scheme of arrangement, carve-out or divestiture of any segment — the corporate action running through this period is the opposite, consolidation. The company merged Cohance into Suven Pharmaceuticals (shareholder approval 99.99%, NCLT hearing 18 Feb 2025, 38.11 crore shares outstanding post-merger, rebranded Cohance in May 2025) and bought capability rather than shedding it: Sapala Organics (oligonucleotides, consolidated from 11 July 2024) and NJ Bio of Princeton NJ (ADCs — 56% stake, ~US$100m pre-money equity value, US$64.4m outlay of which US$49.4m secondary and US$15m primary, on US$32m revenue growing at ~70% CAGR, with call/put on the balance after 5 years), with Himanshu Agarwal stating 'inorganic growth is a core part of our thesis' and Vivek Sharma saying 'our hope is that we don't end at six. We keep adding more.' The only 'separation' management actually describes is organisational, not legal: three distinct business verticals — Pharma CDMO (Yann D'Herve), API+ (Gunjan Singh) and Specialty Chemicals (Amrit Singh) — each given full operational ownership and P&L accountability reporting directly to the Executive Chairman, approved by the Board alongside MD Dr Prasada Raju's resignation and disclosed on the 28 October 2025 update call. The problems that restructuring was said to solve were internal, not structural: a 'multi-business portfolio and expanding global footprint', six formerly family-owned businesses welded into one needing 'greater agility, faster execution, and deeper accountability', and getting to the US$1bn/2030 vision faster; Vivek Sharma explicitly denied there had been any overlap problem at the top ('There was no such thought process that there was an overlap of responsibility'). It was board- and management-driven — no investor, lender or partner is recorded as asking for it; the only investor pressure on record is Varun Bang of Bandhan Life attacking Advent's stewardship ('execution discipline seems to have collapsed') and Chirag Shah of White Pine asking for governance and selective-information-flow fixes, neither of which asked for a separation. The numbers an investor might build a separation case from are disclosed but never framed that way by management: consolidated FY26 EBITDA margin of 21% versus 24.6% standalone (9M FY26: 21% vs 24%; Q3 FY26: 15.5% vs ~19%), i.e. a 4–5% drag Himanshu attributes to first-year NJ Bio consolidation and subsidiary losses in the biotech funding winter, plus INR260 crore of destocking in two large commercial molecules and INR55 crore (INR610 million FY26) lost at the Nacharam formulation site after its OAI and warning letter — and management's answer to all of it is remediation and recovery, with Yann saying NJ Bio needs 'a little bit more than two years to get back to this level', not a sale or demerger.
rationale.evolution: The idea never surfaces: no call in the supplied window raises separating, demerging or selling a segment. The structural idea that does evolve is the opposite — segmentation into three reporting engines (Pharma CDMO, Specialty Chemicals, API+) described as 'engines of growth' from the Feb 2025 and Jun 2025 calls, hardened on 28 October 2025 (filed 1 Nov 2025) into three business-unit CEOs with full P&L authority reporting to Executive Chairman Vivek Sharma plus a platform COO, restated on the 12 November 2025 and 12 February 2026 calls, and then carried into a leadership handover rather than a split: the 27 April 2026 filing records Sharma's resignation effective 30 April 2026 (staying nine months as Special Advisor) and Umang Vohra's appointment as Chairman and Group CEO, who on his first call (12 May 2026) promised only 'a strategic blueprint for growth and sustainable value creation' by fiscal year end — explicitly declining to say whether tough decisions were coming ('I do not know if we are at a point where we will make tough decisions at this stage'). If a separation exists, it is in the six older calls omitted for length or in filings not supplied here.

points.point: On the 28 October 2025 update call (filed 1 Nov 2025), announcing MD Dr Prasada Raju's resignation, Sharma said the Board approved a revised organisational structure — not a corporate separation — citing the multi-business portfolio and the US$1bn vision.
points.quote: In light of this development, the board has approved a revised organizational structure, one that better reflects our multi-business portfolio and expanding global footprint and positions Cohance strongly on its path towards a $1 billion U.S. vision.

points.point: The stated purpose of that restructuring was speed and accountability inside one company, with the three business-unit leaders given full P&L ownership reporting to the Executive Chairman.
points.quote: This new structure is designed to bring greater agility, faster execution, and deeper accountability across our businesses.

points.point: Operational ownership was pushed down to the three vertical CEOs — Yann D'Herve (Pharma CDMO), Gunjan Singh (API+), Amrit Singh (Specialty Chemicals) — with CFO Himanshu Agarwal joining the Board; no entity was carved out.
points.quote: These business unit leaders have full operational ownership and accountability will henceforth report directly to me.

points.point: On the 12 November 2025 Q2 FY26 call Sharma restated the same three-vertical structure as a capability-amplification phase of integration, again with no mention of separating any of them.
points.quote: Over the past year, we had established three distinct business verticals, each led by highly experienced and accomplished industry leaders who bring deep expertise and proven track record in their respective domains and each has full operational ownership and accountability.

points.point: The underlying complexity management was managing is the merger of six separate businesses into one platform — an integration problem, which Sharma answered with cultural and leadership change rather than any split.
points.quote: Somebody started saying we are a combination of six family-owned businesses that have now become part of who we are today, right?

points.point: The one fact pattern that could support a separation thesis is the subsidiary drag Himanshu quantifies — consolidated versus standalone margin — but he frames it as timing and first-year NJ Bio consolidation, not a reason to separate.
points.quote: Adjusted EBITDA for nine-month FY '26 has declined by 43% to INR348 crore , with adjusted EBITDA margins at 21%. For context, stand-alone adjusted EBITDA margins stood at 24%, highlighting the impact of subsidiary consolidation and muted operating leverage.

points.point: FY26 repeats the same standalone-versus-consolidated gap (24.6% vs 21%), and when Ashish of UTI asked directly about Sapala and NJ Bio dragging margins, the answer was a turnaround plan and a $10m Princeton expansion — not a disposal.
points.quote: The adjusted EBITDA stood at INR 4.77 billion. EBITDA margin stood at 21%, while our standalone adjusted EBITDA margin were at 24.6%.

points.point: Management's declared capital-allocation philosophy over the window is acquisitive consolidation, treating organic and inorganic as one capital-allocation decision — the opposite of a separation rationale.
points.quote: So, for us, inorganic growth is a core part of our thesis.

points.point: Asked about M&A direction on the 28 October 2025 call, Sharma described buying differentiated niche-tech capability (ADC, oligo) across East and West — adding businesses, including unwanted assets inside bundles, rather than divesting.
points.quote: So, idea is to look for capabilities, not capacities.

points.point: The only supplied filing is a Board outcome covering Vivek Sharma's resignation as Executive Chairman effective 30 April 2026 (continuing nine months as Special Advisor), Umang Vohra's appointment as Chairman and Group CEO, and a new ESOP 2026 of 25,918,613 options (6.25% fully diluted, floor price INR 325). It contains no scheme of arrangement, demerger or separation.
points.quote: the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting held today i.e., April 27, 2026 inter-alia considered and approved the following: 1. Taking note of the resignation of the Executive Chairman and Director

rationale.what_management_expects: Nothing — no separation benefits are claimed anywhere in these texts. For the three-vertical reorganisation they claimed only agility, faster execution, deeper accountability, full P&L ownership per CEO, and faster progress toward US$1bn revenue by 2030 with mid-30s EBITDA margins. Margin recovery is pledged via volume, mix and operating leverage within the single consolidated platform, not via separation.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is not a manufacturing division but a non-core software unit: on 23 June 2026 Endurance Overseas SpA, Italy (a wholly-owned subsidiary) signed a Share Purchase Agreement to sell 100% of Veicoli Srl, Italy — a step-down wholly-owned subsidiary 'engaged in the business of providing software platforms to companies operating in fleet management sector' — to Banyan Software UK Limited, an unrelated buyer, with completion expected 1 July 2026. The single reason management put on record is portfolio/resource focus: the decision was taken 'considering the Endurance Group's strategic focus on allocating resources towards the continued growth and development of its core auto components business.' The unit is immaterial to the group: FY2025-26 total income of Rs 32.58 crore, 0.22% of consolidated total income (consolidated FY26 total income was Rs 14,720 crore), and net worth of Rs 3.15 crore at 31 March 2026, 0.48% of consolidated net worth. Consideration is an upfront fixed €2.2 million, deferred fixed €0.3 million, and an earn-out linked to the first three years' financial results capped at €5.0 million, subject to cash and debt adjustments; the filing states the disposal is outside any scheme of arrangement and that 'there is no corporate restructuring or any other event where a scheme of arrangement needs to be filed.' The competing claim on resources is visible in the calls: India capex of roughly Rs 800 crores in FY26 versus Rs 600 crores in FY25 with FY27 'similar', four greenfield plants (AURIC Shendra castings, AURIC Bidkin alloy wheels, the Talegaon battery-pack plant, the Chennai brakes plant), a 12 lakh-unit ABS line addition on top of 6.4 lakh, a fifth aluminium forging press, plus €38 million paid for 60% of Stöferle and about €38 million of Europe capex in FY26. Management's own stated capital rule on 13 February 2026 was that M&A would be 'mainly in our existing areas' and that 'our investments will be in profitable growth products, mainly' — a fleet-management software platform fits neither. The direction of travel in Europe over the same period was consolidation of the auto entities rather than diversification: Endurance Engineering Srl and Endurance SpA were merged into Endurance Castings SpA effective 1 January 2026 (appointed date 1 April 2025), with the surviving company renamed Endurance SpA. No problem, lender, partner or investor request was named anywhere — no analyst asked about Veicoli in any of the seven transcripts, and the only problem the separation is said to solve is where the group's resources go.
rationale.evolution: The separation never surfaced on any earnings call in the window — Nov 2024 through 15 May 2026 transcripts contain no mention of Veicoli, fleet-management software, or any divestment. The only visible precursor is the European entity simplification intimated 31 July 2025 and completed effective 1 January 2026 (Endurance Engineering Srl and Endurance SpA merged into Endurance Castings SpA), alongside the 13 February 2026 call where Jain framed all M&A as 'mainly in our existing areas' and capex as going to 'profitable growth products'. The 15 May 2026 call, five weeks before signing, gave no hint; the SPA was signed 23 June 2026 and disclosed 24 June 2026 as a Regulation 30 sale, expressly outside a scheme of arrangement.

points.point: The divested entity is identified as a fleet-management software business held two levels down under Endurance Overseas SpA, Italy — i.e. outside the auto-component product range described in every call.
points.quote: Veicoli is a step-down wholly-owned subsidiary of EOSpA and is engaged in the business of providing software platforms to companies operating in fleet management sector.

points.point: The stated rationale is entirely resource allocation toward the core auto components business; no operational problem, loss, dispute or third-party demand is cited.
points.quote: Considering the Endurance Group's strategic focus on allocating resources towards the continued growth and development of its core auto components business, it has been decided to divest the Group's investment in Veicoli.

points.point: Materiality disclosed is tiny — 0.22% of consolidated total income and 0.48% of consolidated net worth — against FY26 consolidated total income of Rs 14,720 crores reported on the May 2026 call.
points.quote: Total income of Veicoli Srl for the financial year 2025-26 is Rs. 32.58 crore, which is 0.22% of consolidated total income of the Company.

points.point: Price is mostly contingent: €2.2 million upfront, €0.3 million deferred, and up to €5.0 million of earn-out over three post-completion years, subject to cash and debt adjustments; buyer is Banyan Software UK Limited, not a related party.
points.quote: Earn out consideration linked to financial results for the first three years after completion, subject to a cap of € 5.0 million.

points.point: The company expressly denies this is a corporate restructuring — it is a straight share sale, not a demerger or court-approved scheme, and not a slump sale.
points.quote: Yes. There is no corporate restructuring or any other event where a scheme of arrangement needs to be filed.

points.point: In parallel the Italian auto entities were being consolidated, not diversified: two step-down subsidiaries merged into one, renamed Endurance SpA, with retrospective appointed date.
points.quote: Effective Date of the merger is 1st January, 2026 with appointed date being 1st April, 2025.

points.point: Jain defined the group's M&A and capital-deployment boundary as existing product areas with higher margins and a clear target market — the implicit test Veicoli fails.
points.quote: See, firstly the M&A strategy will be mainly in our existing areas - like we have done, for example in the solar business.

points.point: On the FY27 capex plan Jain said investment would be steered to profitable growth products, citing that over two-thirds of the Rs 930 crores order win was 4W castings and solar dampers at 'much higher margin'.
points.quote: Our investments will be in profitable growth products, mainly.

points.point: The scale of the competing capital programme — four greenfield plants, ABS expansion, forging press, battery packs — was quantified as roughly Rs 800 crores of India capex in FY26 with FY27 similar.
points.quote: Our India capex in FY 26 was approximately 800 crores compared to 600 crores in the previous year, and was driven by new plants and investments in new growth areas.

rationale.rationale: These texts describe no separation, demerger, spin-off, slump sale or scheme of arrangement of any GESHIP business — the premise is not supported by the record supplied. The only corporate actions disclosed are (a) a ₹900 crore open-market buyback of up to an indicative 58,82,352 equity shares (4.12% of paid-up capital) at a maximum ₹1,530/share, approved by the Board on August 27, 2026, opened September 4, 2026, with 20,63,954 shares repurchased by October 7, 2026, and (b) the December 22, 2025 NCLT dissolution of Greatship Oilfield Services Limited, a dormant wholly-owned subsidiary of Greatship (India) Limited with nil revenue and net worth of ₹17.73 lakhs — a shell clean-up, not a business separation. The buyback public announcement affirmatively states there are no pending schemes of amalgamation, compromise or arrangement involving the Company, and that the buyback 'will not result in a change in control or otherwise affect the existing management structure.' The stated reasons for the buyback are capital-allocation, not structural: effectively utilizing available cash (net cash of about $500 million standalone / ₹7,000 crore consolidated, versus ship prices management repeatedly called too high to buy), lifting EPS, book value per share and return on equity by shrinking the equity base, and giving non-promoter shareholders a cash exit option while promoters (30.07%) are barred from participating. Throughout the calls the two businesses — shipping (40 vessels, 3.24 mn dwt) and offshore oilfield services through Greatship (India) Limited (19 vessels, 4 jack-up rigs) — are discussed as continuing parts of one group, with the parent still funding GIL (₹425 crore and ₹65 crore loans, ₹392 crore outstanding at March 31, 2026, plus ₹272 crore of parent-subscribed preference shares being redeemed over four years). Investors on the calls pressed on the 25%-40% discount to NAV and on unlocking value, but management's answer was dividends, buybacks and patience on asset prices — never a separation; it also said it was 'not currently looking to buy any companies and diversify.'
rationale.evolution: No separation idea surfaced in any call. What did evolve is the buyback: Jan 28, 2025 — 'we always evaluate whether we should go for ships or do a buyback... in the immediate future we have no plan'; May 12 and Aug 1, 2025 — 'no discussion around buyback at the board level'; Nov 10, 2025 and Jan 30, 2026 — dividends preferred because they reach every shareholder and buyback tax treatment was 'somewhat unviable'; May 15, 2026 — 'one of the biggest impediments has been removed,' now 'a function of the price'; then the Aug 24/27, 2026 board intimation and approval, Sept 3-4, 2026 commencement, and daily buyback reports through Oct 7, 2026. Separately, the only entity removed from the group was the dormant GOSL (approved April 30, 2025; NCLT dissolution reported December 22, 2025).

points.point: The buyback public announcement (Aug 29, 2026) expressly confirms no scheme of arrangement, amalgamation or compromise involving the Company is pending — i.e. no separation is underway.

rationale.rationale: On the record available here, GODREJIND's "separation" is the carve-out of its financial services arm, Godrej Capital Limited (GCL) — an NBFC-Core Investment Company (exempt from registration), incorporated September 6, 2019 — out from under the listed company and beneath a newly created, wholly owned intermediate holding company, Godrej Investment Limited (GINVL), incorporated January 5, 2026. GIL transferred its entire 91.11% equity stake in GCL to GINVL on January 28, 2026 for cash consideration of ₹3,862,69,28,016 (≈₹3,862.69 crore), funding GINVL by fully subscribing a rights issue of 3,89,775 equity shares of ₹10 each; GINVL "will carry on the business of financial services" as GCL's holding company. The effect stated in the filings is purely structural: GCL "ceased to be a direct subsidiary (Material Unlisted Subsidiary)" and became a step-down subsidiary, with GINVL as immediate holding company. The scale being ring-fenced is material — in FY25 GCL contributed ₹1,553.80 crore, or 7.90%, of consolidated turnover/revenue/income and ₹3,321.07 crore, or 32.71%, of consolidated net worth. The filings explicitly state the transfer was done outside any scheme: "The transaction is not in accordance with any Scheme of Arrangement. Thus, compliance with Regulation 37A is not applicable," and that it is a related-party transaction on an arm's-length basis with approvals obtained — shareholder approval having been taken by postal ballot (results September 29, 2025) following board approval on August 13, 2025. Separately, GIL continues to monetise its GCPL holding, selling 0.50% in the open market on September 24, 2026 for ₹450.12 crore and retaining 23.23% of an associate that contributes nil consolidated turnover but 35.69% (₹3,989.08 crore) of consolidated net worth. Critically, no management reasoning is present in these documents: no transcripts were supplied ("no transcripts on file"), and the three filings are Regulation 30 intimations that disclose mechanics, dates and amounts only — they state no strategic purpose, no problem being solved, no investor, lender or partner request, and no demerger or listing of the financial services business.
rationale.evolution: The only visible sequence is procedural and comes from cross-references inside the January 28, 2026 filings: the GIL board approved the step on August 13, 2025; shareholders approved it by postal ballot with results declared September 29, 2025; the vehicle GINVL was incorporated January 5, 2026 and intimated to the exchanges on January 6, 2026; and the stake transfer plus the ₹3,862.69 crore rights-issue funding completed on January 28, 2026. The later filing of September 24, 2026 is not a change to that plan but a parallel treasury action — a 0.50% GCPL open-market sale for ₹450.12 crore, taking GIL to 23.23%. Because no earnings call transcripts were provided, there is no call-by-call record of how the idea surfaced, was questioned or was revised; nothing in the supplied texts shows the plan changing from its August 2025 board approval.

rationale.rationale: These texts do not contain any separation, demerger, spin-off or scheme of arrangement by HCL Technologies — the word 'carve-out' appears only on the buy side, where HCLTech is the acquirer of businesses other companies are separating. The two filings provided (both dated 12 January 2026) are the Q3 FY26 un-audited results and the dividend record-date intimation; their only structural notes are Note 4, a definitive agreement signed 18 December 2025 to 'carve-out and acquire' HPE's Telco Solutions Business for ₹1,438 crores ($160 million), including a ₹135 crore ($15 million) performance incentive, to gain IP, product engineering and R&D talent and CSP relationships; and Note 5, a definitive agreement signed 22 December 2025 to carve-out and acquire Jaspersoft from Cloud Software Group for ₹2,157 crores ($240 million) for an embedded analytics/pixel-perfect reporting platform and its developer community. Management framed both as additive — Telco Solutions building on the 2024 HPE CTG acquisition ('which is now growing nicely') to deepen telecom IP, and Jaspersoft/Wobby/Zeenea completing the Actian data-intelligence stack with the missing 'visualize layer' (Jaspersoft closed in early July 2026, guided at $10–15 million revenue per quarter). The only separations discussed as HCLTech's own doing are internal restructuring (a people-and-non-people program costing ~40–50 bps of FY26 margin, 62 bps in Q1 FY27, intended to give 'structural agility' in the AI era), the creation of new subsidiaries rather than divestments (HCLTech Public Sector Solutions in the US, April 2025), discontinuation of some HCL Software products, and walking away from deals worth '$1 billion more' of TCV. Separation appears as a demand theme, not a corporate action: in Oct 2025 CVK cited 'carveout related separation work' at Retail/CPG clients as a revenue pocket. HCLSoftware is described as structurally distinct — 'a dedicated products and platform organization that operates largely independent of the Services business with its own GTM and R&D investments', reported as its own segment with its own ROIC (21.6% in Q1 FY27) and ARR ($1.063 billion) — but no call or filing proposes separating it, and no lender, partner or investor is recorded asking for any separation. The nearest new-entity decision is the July 2026 AI datacenter business: up to ₹3,500 crores, scaling toward 50 MW, possibly funded with partners, equity and debt — but it is described as a new growth vector inside HCLTech, not a carve-out.
rationale.evolution: Jan 2025 (Q3 FY25) is the first structural note: HPE's CTG assets closed 2 December 2024 and HCLSoftware is described as operating 'largely independent' of Services, with no separation proposed. Apr 2025 adds a new subsidiary (HCLTech Public Sector Solutions) and Jul 2025 announces a restructuring program, while Oct 2025 cites clients' own 'carveout related separation work' as a demand pocket. Jan 2026 and the 12 January 2026 filing record HCLTech as the buyer of two carve-outs (HPE Telco Solutions, $160M; Jaspersoft, $240M), Apr 2026 flags both as delayed by US government approvals, and Jul 2026 confirms Jaspersoft closed and CTG-follow-on still pending — never once a separation of HCLTech's own business.
