rationale.rationale: The separation is the June 8, 2026 carve-out of Purple Fabric (purplefabric.ai), Intellect's Open Business Impact AI platform, out of the consolidated product organisation into an independent Line of Business under a new CEO, Deepak Dastrala, reporting directly to Arun Jain, who stays as mentor; Dastrala also joins the Intellect Management Council as Senior Management Personnel. Management's stated reason is DNA, not portfolio pruning: Intellect curated two parallel architectural disruptions over two years — eMACH.ai (the composable banking foundation, 700 microservices, ~₹1,667 Cr license-linked revenue, Wholesale ₹1,500 Cr+, Consumer ₹1,000 Cr+, Wealth/Insurance ₹500 Cr+) and Purple Fabric (the cognitive/AI layer) — and concluded 'the intrinsic DNA of eMACH.ai and Purple Fabric are completely different,' so sharing one structure was holding Purple Fabric back. The timing argument is a market inflection from AI experimentation to scaled enterprise-wide deployment, which management says makes this 'the optimal time' to give Purple Fabric an independent identity with dedicated resources, freedom and agility to 'curate its own destiny.' Purple Fabric's own traction justifies standalone status: 45+ clients live, a 95%+ accuracy SLA, an 18-layer architecture, 550 domain-aware agents, ~₹160 Cr FY26 AI revenue off ₹92 Cr of FY26 investment (against a ₹130 Cr plan), a $50mn+ AI order book booked in FY26, and two large enterprise-AI platform deals in India plus three-four outside. The problems it solves are structural: a licence/implementation banking business and a consumption-priced AI platform have opposite economics (Purple Fabric deals start at a quarter-to-half-million dollars and scale in years 2-3 toward a $3-5mn platform target, versus $5-7mn banking licences), opposite operating cadence (Jain's answer to the pricing question was the Salesforce-to-Bajaj analogy), and opposite talent model — the LoB is designed as an organisation 'in flow' with a networked 'Leadership Circle,' micro-teams and people wearing multiple hats instead of hierarchy. Nobody external forced it: Intellect is zero-debt with ₹1,257 Cr cash, so there are no lenders in the story; the pressure came from management's own AI thesis and from SI/partner demand (one large global system integrator plus 14 value-discovery partners signed, a target of ~100 partners), while investors had been pushing for separate Purple Fabric numbers and ROI visibility for four straight calls and were repeatedly refused.
rationale.evolution: Purple Fabric was first framed to investors as a ₹1,000-5,000 Cr opportunity in the December 19, 2024 session and the Feb 2025 call, where Jain said adoption, not revenue, was the objective and declined to split it out of the ₹10,000 Cr funnel. At the Jun 2025 (FY25) call he explicitly ruled separation out — 'We are not separating the company, but we will keep the costs separate' — while committing ₹100-130 Cr of non-capitalisable P&L spend; by Aug 2025 it had its own Business Head (John Turner), by Nov 2025 its own ₹25 Cr/quarter investment line (costing 3-3.25% of EBITDA), its own AI Labs in the new 7.25 lakh sq ft Siruseri facility, and Jain was rebuking the 'cannibalisation' question with 'It's a completely different line of business.' In Feb 2026 it was formally relabelled the 'fourth growth engine,' and the same call exposed the reporting problem — an investor computed only ~₹19 Cr of segmented Purple Fabric revenue against the ₹200 Cr claim, answered with 'Purple Fabric is embedded across the businesses.' After the May 2026 FY26 call disclosed ₹160 Cr AI revenue, a $50mn order book and product-wise Purple Fabric go-to-market (Trade, Lending, Wealth, Risk & Governance, Onboarding), the June 8, 2026 release completed the reversal and granted independent LoB status.

points.point: The core stated rationale is that the two platforms have fundamentally different natures, so independent LoB status buys Purple Fabric freedom and dedicated resources rather than divesting anything.
points.quote: However, because their intrinsic DNAs are entirely unique, granting Purple Fabric independent LoB status gives it the freedom and dedicated resources to accelerate its growth.

points.point: Timing is justified by the market shifting from AI pilots to scaled enterprise deployment, making this the moment for a separate identity to capture it.
points.quote: As the market approaches an inflection point, moving rapidly from AI experimentation to scaled, enterprise-wide deployment, Intellect has determined that it is the optimal time to give Purple Fabric its independent identity.

points.point: The division of labour is explicit: eMACH.ai remains the foundational architecture while Purple Fabric supplies the cognitive intelligence layer; the LoB is built on a networked 'Leadership Circle' with micro-team DNA, backed by 45+ live clients, a 95%+ accuracy SLA, 18-layer architecture and 550 domain-aware agents.
points.quote: If eMACH.ai forms our foundational architecture, Purple Fabric provides the critical cognitive intelligence enterprises need to operationalize AI with complete confidence.

points.point: In May 2025 Arun Jain explicitly rejected separating the business, committing only to ring-fencing the ₹100-130 Cr Purple Fabric cost inside the consolidated P&L — the position the June 2026 carve-out reverses.
points.quote: We are not separating the company, but we will keep the costs separate.

points.point: From the start Purple Fabric was run on a different scorecard from the banking products — platform adoption rather than revenue or margin — foreshadowing the DNA argument.
points.quote: Revenue number is not an objective for Purple Fabric but adoption is.

points.point: Asked whether Purple Fabric was a top-up or cannibalised existing products, Jain rejected the framing outright and insisted it was a distinct line of business — the same logic later used for the carve-out; the quarter carried ₹25 Cr of Purple Fabric spend, costing 3-3.25% of EBITDA margin.
points.quote: It's a completely different line of business.

points.point: Purple Fabric was formally reclassified as a standalone fourth growth engine alongside Wholesale (₹1,400 Cr), Consumer (₹1,000 Cr) and IntellectAI (₹500 Cr), a structural step before the LoB carve-out.
points.quote: From 2024 onwards, we have begun building a fourth growth engine Purple Fabric, our Open Business Impact AI Platform.

points.point: Investors pressed on the disclosure problem — only ~₹19 Cr of segmented Purple Fabric revenue was visible against the ₹200 Cr full-year claim — because the platform was buried inside wealth, insurance and the other businesses.
points.quote: Am I correct in understanding that Purple Fabric in the last 12 months has contributed only ₹19 Crs.

points.point: By FY26 Purple Fabric had its own commercial engine — ₹160 Cr revenue, a $50mn+ AI order book off ₹92 Cr invested, platform revenue up 141% to ₹580 Cr, and a product-by-product go-to-market (Trade, Lending, Wealth, Risk & Governance, Onboarding) — plus two India and three-four overseas platform deals.
points.quote: We have signed two large enterprise AI platform deals in India and three or four platform deals outside India, and our pipeline is growing well.

points.point: The technical moat behind the 95%+ accuracy SLA is Jain's accuracy-multiplication argument (85% x 95% x 95% = 76.7%, unusable for core banking processes), solved with ~15 patents filed in six months out of 125 filed overall — research management treats as a distinct discipline from banking product engineering.
points.quote: For a financial institution's core processes, we need at least 95% as a benchmark to make it usable for production-grade AI, which I call production-grade AI or enterprise AI.

points.point: Purple Fabric's economics were incompatible with the banking P&L from launch — the entire ₹130 Cr was non-capitalisable expense — and Jain positioned it in a different competitive set (Palantir, C3.ai) with its own revenue model (pilot, implementation, transaction/outcome, core-based platform licence).
points.quote: All of it will be in the P&L. In the market, we cannot capitalise on any of this investment.

points.point: The go-to-market also diverged: Purple Fabric is sold through system integrators and value-discovery partners (target ~100 globally, 14 signed by Q3, plus one large global SI) rather than Intellect's direct banking salesforce, and separate AI Labs were funded in the new 7.25 lakh sq ft Siruseri campus.
points.quote: So, we are one of the three options available to SI to take to the market.

rationale.what_management_expects: Purple Fabric: dedicated resources, freedom, agility and micro-team speed to accelerate growth and 'curate its own destiny' in Business Impact AI; scale a platform/consumption model from $0.25-0.5mn entry deals toward $3-5mn, against a ₹1,000-5,000 Cr TAM. eMACH.ai remains the foundational architecture. Jain calls it 'a massive long-term opportunity for value creation.' No per-entity margin, capital or valuation target was given.
rationale.gaps: No legal structure, demerger, separate entity, shareholding or external funding; no standalone P&L, margin, capital or headcount disclosure; no asset/IP transfer terms; no timeline; no eMACH.ai impact.

judge.quote: Upon completion of the transaction, the Company's shareholding in Freshbus Private Limited shall stand reduced from 25.66% to 8.27% of its paid up share capital, resulting in Freshbus Private Limited ceasing to be an associate company of Le Travenues Technology Limited.

listing.text: NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

rationale.rationale: On the documents supplied, ixigo (Le Travenues Technology Ltd.) is not separating, demerging or spinning off any business of its own — there is no scheme of arrangement in the filings, and the one filing tagged 'Diversification/Disinvestment' (August 13, 2026) is expressly marked 'Not applicable' against the question of whether the disposal sits outside a Scheme of Arrangement or needs Regulation 37A compliance. The only actual separation disclosed is the unwinding of ixigo's minority holding in Freshbus Private Limited, the electric intercity bus operator it first backed under an Investment and Shareholders' Agreement dated October 28, 2022 (68,258 CCPS plus 1 equity share at ₹2,344 per share). Under a Share Purchase Agreement dated August 13, 2026 with Twelve Stone LLP and Freshbus, ixigo sells 46,264 CCPS at ₹7,911 per share for cash of ₹365,994,504 (~₹36.6 crore), being 17.39% of Freshbus' paid-up capital, cutting its stake from 25.66% to 8.27% and ending Freshbus' status as an associate company; completion is set for on or before August 30, 2026. The buyer is Twelve Stone LLP, whose designated partners are Sudhakar Reddy Chirra, Freshbus' Founder and Managing Director, and Sasya Chirra — i.e. a founder-side vehicle buying ixigo out — and the filing states it is not a related-party transaction and that ixigo has no identifiable promoter group with an interest in it. The economics ixigo discloses are the only 'problem' the documents attach to the holding: Freshbus was a persistent drag on consolidated profit, with share of associate losses of ₹11.22 crore in FY26, ₹9.1 crore in FY25 versus ₹5.9 crore in FY24, and quarterly call-outs of ₹2.0 crore (Q1 FY25), ₹1.93 crore (Q2 FY25), ₹1.9 crore (Q3 FY25), ₹3.29 crore (Q4 FY25), ₹2.34 crore (Q1 FY26), ₹1.47 crore (Q2 FY26), ₹2.9 crore (Q3 FY26) and ₹45.59 million (Q4 FY26), against a carrying value of just ₹18.87 crore, or 0.96% of consolidated net worth. The exit price of ₹7,911 versus a ₹2,344 entry is roughly 3.4x, so the disclosed facts support a profitable exit from a loss-making, immaterial, non-core associate rather than a structural separation. Management never discusses the sale on any call — the latest call (May 21, 2026) predates the SPA — and in the same period the group is moving the other way, consolidating rather than separating: a ₹1,296 crore Prosus preferential issue (46,270,092 shares at ₹280, allotted November 12, 2025), a new wholly owned Singapore subsidiary IXIGO PTE. LTD., and a 60% upfront acquisition of Spain's Online Travel Solutions S.L. ('Trenes') for €11.70 million through that subsidiary. The only 'separation' management itself describes is organisational, not legal: the 'NewCo inside the old co' AI team built inside ixigo, which has no separate entity, capital or shareholding attached to it.
rationale.evolution: Freshbus enters the story as a deconsolidation, not a separation: on the Aug 2024 call (Q1 FY25, August 1, 2024) management explains it was a subsidiary until September 13, 2023 and became an associate after a primary round diluted ixigo, so its losses moved below EBITDA. Through May 2025 (May 14, 2025), Jul 2025 (July 16, 2025), Nov 2025 (October 29, 2025), Jan 2026 (January 22, 2026) and May 2026 (May 21, 2026) it appears only as a recurring one-off call-out of rising associate losses, never as a candidate for exit, and no analyst asks about it. Separately, on Nov 2025 Rajnish Kumar introduces the 'new co inside the old co' idea for AI self-disruption, which by May 2026 has become 'NewCo inside ixigo' and ixigo NEXT — an internal team, explicitly not a carve-out. The actual disposal surfaces only in the August 13, 2026 filing, after the last transcript, with no management narrative attached.

points.point: The August 13, 2026 filing is a straight share sale of a minority stake, not a demerger: ixigo sells 46,264 CCPS of Freshbus to Twelve Stone LLP at ₹7,911 per share (17.39% of paid-up capital), and the filing marks the Scheme-of-Arrangement / Regulation 37A question 'Not applicable'.
points.quote: Pursuant to the said agreement, the Company has agreed to sell 46,264 Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares of Freshbus Private Limited to Twelve Stone LLP at a price of ₹7,911 per share, constituting 17.39% stake of the paid up share capital in Freshbus Private Limited.

points.point: The consequence is loss of associate status: the holding drops from 25.66% to 8.27%, so Freshbus stops being equity-accounted, but ixigo keeps a residual 8.27% rather than exiting fully.
points.quote: Upon completion of the transaction, the Company's shareholding in Freshbus Private Limited shall stand reduced from 25.66% to 8.27% of its paid up share capital, resulting in Freshbus Private Limited ceasing to be an associate company of Le Travenues Technology Limited.

points.point: The only quantified case in the filing is that the holding was loss-making and immaterial: ₹11.22 crore of associate losses in FY26 against a ₹18.87 crore carrying value, under 1% of consolidated net worth.
points.quote: Net worth: It contributes ₹18.87 crore as investment in associate accounted for in consolidated financial statements constituting 0.96% of the net worth as per the audited consolidated financial statements as on March 31, 2026 .

points.point: The buyer is a founder-side vehicle — Twelve Stone LLP, whose designated partners are Freshbus' own Founder and Managing Director and Sasya Chirra — and the exit price of ₹7,911 compares with a ₹2,344 entry price under the October 28, 2022 Investment and Shareholders' Agreement, roughly 3.4x.
points.quote: The Company had invested in Freshbus Private Limited pursuant to an Investment and Shareholders' Agreement dated October 28, 2022, under which it acquired 68,258 Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares and 1 Equity Share at a price of ₹2,344 per share.

points.point: Freshbus had already been separated once — by dilution, not by design: it was consolidated as a subsidiary until September 13, 2023, after which a primary round reduced ixigo's ownership and pushed its losses below the EBITDA line.
points.quote: Last year, our investment company FreshBus was a subsidiary until 13 September 2023, and therefore in Q1 FY'24 a loss of Rs.1.46 crores was incorporated in our EBITDA.

points.point: Full-year disclosure shows the drag widening — associate losses up over 50% year on year — while the earlier revaluation gains shrank from ₹29.7 crore to ₹5.8 crore.
points.quote: Share of loss of Fresh Bus increased from INR 5.9 crores in FY '24 to INR 9.1 crores in FY '25.

points.point: In the last call before the SPA, Freshbus appears only as a quarterly one-off call-out of ₹45.59 million of associate losses, with no mention of a sale, review or strategic rethink of the stake.
points.quote: The call-outs for Q4 FY '26 include share of loss from Fresh Bus and associate company of INR45.59 million, tax benefits amounting to INR82.5 million

points.point: The only 'separation' management itself articulates is organisational self-disruption — a 'new co' inside the existing company that uses the parent's data and resources, with no separate entity, capital or shareholders.
points.quote: We call this building a new co inside the old co.

points.point: By the latest call that NewCo has become ixigo NEXT, described as an internal AI-native rebuild of the organisation and product, reinforcing that it is a team and operating layer rather than a business being carved out.
points.quote: So over the past year, we created what we internally called NewCo inside ixigo.

points.point: Over the same period the group is consolidating, not separating: ₹1,296 crore raised from Prosus with 25% earmarked for inorganic growth, an investment committee constituted, and a Singapore subsidiary set up as the channel for overseas investment — later used to buy 60% of Spain's Trenes for €11.70 million.
points.quote: On the AI investments Rajnish talked about, I want to reiterate that when we raised the preferential issue last quarter, we had earmarked 25% of the proceeds for inorganic growth opportunities and 25% for organic growth initiatives.

rationale.what_management_expects: Nothing is stated. No call or filing sets out expected effects on margins, capital, valuation or focus from the Freshbus exit; the filing gives only cash of ₹365,994,504, cessation of associate accounting (removing ₹11.22 crore of FY26 share-of-loss), and a retained 8.27%. For ixigo overall, management frames Prosus capital, the Singapore vehicle and Trenes as TAM expansion, not separation.
rationale.gaps: No stated reason for exiting Freshbus, no buyer-selection or valuation rationale, no mention on any call, no lender, partner or investor request, and no demerger of any ixigo business.

The only Freshbus-specific lines are related-party transactions of the Group with it (advertisement revenue from Freshbus: 0.21 in FY24, 0.56 in FY25, 3.60 in FY26; ticketing revenue from Freshbus: 4.94 in FY24, 7.90 in FY25, 17.63 in FY26) and trade payables (1.02 / 0.51 / 1.12) — these are ixigo's income from Freshbus, not Freshbus's own revenue. The consolidated segment tables report Flight/Train/Bus/Others, where 'Bus' is ixigo's OTA bus-ticketing LOB (segment result = contribution margin: segment revenue less direct expenses, net of discount, external), NOT Freshbus. The P&L line 'Share of loss of an associate, net of tax' (59.07 FY24, 90.97 FY25, 112.22 FY26) is ixigo's equity-method share of associate loss, not disclosed as Freshbus-only (a second associate, Sqaas, exists from FY26), so it is not usable as Freshbus's PAT. rationale.rationale: The supplied record does not contain any statement of why JPPOWER is separating a business, because it contains no earnings call transcripts at all ("no transcripts on file") and no scheme of arrangement, demerger, slump sale or composite scheme document. The only two filings provided are distress/insolvency disclosures, neither of which mentions a separation, a resulting company, a share entitlement ratio, or any business being carved out. The 27th February 2026 filing discloses that National Asset Reconstruction Company Limited, as Trustee of NARCL Trust, acting through its power of attorney holder India Debt Resolution Company Limited, filed a Section 7 IBC application before the NCLT Allahabad Bench at Prayagraj against JPPOWER itself, alleging default of Rs. 511,72,82,207 plus interest and charges, arising from a corporate guarantee JPPOWER extended for Jaiprakash Associates Limited (under IBC); the same dispute was already before the Hon'ble DRT-III, Delhi (disclosed 27th October 2025). The 17th March 2026 filing discloses the NCLT Allahabad Bench's oral order under Section 31 IBC approving Adani Enterprises Limited's resolution plan dated 14th October 2025 (with email clarifications of 5th November 2025) for promoter Jaiprakash Associates Limited, under which JAL's securities will be delisted, shareholders receive NIL consideration because the liquidation value is insufficient to satisfy even secured creditors in full, and all pre-CIRP share capital, convertible instruments, warrants and rights will be entirely cancelled and extinguished for zero consideration on an Effective Date no later than 90 days from NCLT approval. These documents describe a change of control at the promoter level and a creditor-initiated insolvency threat at JPPOWER on a guarantee obligation — not a voluntary business separation. No management named any businesses to be separated (e.g. thermal power, hydro, cement grinding), cited no segment numbers, identified no investor, lender or partner who asked for it, and set out no problems a separation would solve. Any rationale would therefore have to be supplied from outside these texts, which the instructions forbid.
rationale.evolution: The idea does not surface anywhere in the provided record: there are zero earnings calls on file, so there is no call-by-call progression to trace. The only datable developments are the JAL insolvency track — resolution plan filed with NCLT per JAL's 27th November 2025 disclosure, NCLT approval of Adani Enterprises Limited's plan orally pronounced 17th March 2026 (JPPOWER's related disclosure chain beginning 3rd June 2024) — and the guarantee default track, moving from the DRT-III Delhi dispute disclosed 27th October 2025 to NARCL's Section 7 CIRP application against JPPOWER disclosed 27th February 2026. Neither track is presented as, or linked to, a separation of a business.
rationale.what_management_expects: Not stated. The record contains no management commentary on a separation and therefore no expectations for margins, capital structure, valuation re-rating, or business focus at any entity. The only forward-looking content is JAL's delisting, NIL exit price for its shareholders, and extinguishment of its pre-CIRP share capital within 90 days of NCLT approval.
rationale.gaps: Everything: no transcripts supplied, no scheme document, no businesses named, no segment financials, no demerger rationale, ratio, timeline, or requesting stakeholder.

rationale.rationale: On the evidence of these texts, Jubilant FoodWorks is not separating a business in any demerger, spin-off or scheme sense — none of the seven earnings calls contains a single word about separating, demerging, hiving off or listing any business, and no scheme of arrangement is filed. The only separation document present is the Regulation 30 intimation dated December 29, 2025, under which the Company executed a Share Purchase Agreement with Mr. Karan Chechani, one of the founders of Hashtag Loyalty Private Limited, to sell its entire 31.66% stake, after which Hashtag ceases to be an associate; the filing itself answers 'Not Applicable' to whether the disposal sits outside a Scheme of Arrangement. The stated reason is prior discontinuance of Hashtag's business operations, and the numbers management disclosed make the exit economically trivial: Hashtag's FY2024-25 total income was Rs. 27.47 million and its net worth as on March 31, 2025 was Rs. 1.22 million, each contributing 'Nil' to JFL's consolidated financials, the investment was already fully impaired during FY2024-25, and total consideration is Rs. 6,415.94 — a token sum returning the stake to a founder who is explicitly not part of the promoter or promoter group, in a transaction that is not a related-party transaction, with completion expected on or before February 12, 2026. The nearest thing to a portfolio-separation narrative on the calls is pruning, not separation: management repeatedly described curtailing or stopping expansion of Dunkin' and Hong's to concentrate on Domino's and Popeyes, quantifying the emerging-brands EBITDA drag at roughly 200 bps (FY24 base, Nov 2025) and 230-250 bps (Feb 2026), and targeting at least halving it within 12-18 months as part of the 200 bps margin-improvement commitment to FY28. Separately, the Turkey (DP Eurasia) acquisition debt of about EUR 110 million sitting in the Netherlands entity was de-linked from India cash flows — serviced entirely from Turkish internal cash flows and dividends for three quarters by Feb 2026 — but management framed this as refinancing and self-funding, never as a separation of the entity. No investor, lender, brand partner (Domino's International, RBI, Inspire Brands) or aggregator is recorded anywhere in these texts as asking for a business to be separated. The only shareholder-driven structural question was Vivek M.'s May 2025 query about the group's HCCB transaction, which Hari Bhartia answered by reaffirming that focus stays at Jubilant FoodWorks and that funding was already arranged.
rationale.evolution: The idea never surfaces as a separation on any call: Nov 2024 through May 2026 contain only portfolio pruning — Nov 13, 2024 (no expansion for Hong's and Dunkin' until store economics work), May 14, 2025 (expansion in both formally curtailed mid-year to focus on Popeyes; drag to halve), Aug 13, 2025 (expansion 'down to a trickle or stopped', drag halving in 12-18 months), Nov 13, 2025 and Feb 10, 2026 (drag quantified at ~200 bps on FY24 and 230-250 bps, to halve), and May 20, 2026 (drag reduction 'ahead of the plan'). Hashtag Loyalty is never mentioned on any of the seven calls; it appears only in the December 29, 2025 filing, which itself refers back to 'various disclosures made' earlier about discontinuance of Hashtag's operations — disclosures not included in this pack. The plan therefore did not visibly evolve in these texts; a dormant, fully impaired 31.66% associate stake was simply sold back to a founder for Rs. 6,415.94, with completion due on or before February 12, 2026.

points.point: Immateriality is the explicit justification: Hashtag's FY25 total income of Rs. 27.47 million and net worth of Rs. 1.22 million each contribute 'Nil' to JFL consolidated, and the entire stake fetches Rs. 6,415.94, with Hashtag ceasing to be an associate on completion by February 12, 2026.
points.quote: Post completion of the transaction, Hashtag will cease to be an associate of the Company.

points.point: The closest the calls come to separating businesses is pruning the emerging brands: Khetarpal said JFL had decided mid-year to stop expanding Dunkin' and Hong's and concentrate on Popeyes, expecting the drag between Domino's 14.5% margin and the 11.8% standalone quarterly margin to halve.
points.quote: And as you would see, we have already taken the stance of curtailing any or not doing any expansion in Dunkin' and Hong's.

points.point: Hegde confirmed expansion of Dunkin' and Hong's had effectively ceased and that the ~200 bps FY25 drag from emerging formats would be at least halved in 12 to 18 months by fixing unit economics rather than by any corporate separation.
points.quote: Expansion, as you can well see in the numbers we have come out with, have almost come down to a trickle or stopped, right?

points.point: Hegde quantified the emerging-brands drag at roughly 230-250 bps as disclosed, to be halved on the path to the 200 bps EBITDA improvement over FY24 by FY28 — framed as margin repair inside the listed entity, not as carving anything out.
points.quote: And the reduction of the drag on the EBUs, at the point in time that we had disclosed our numbers, the drag was of Popeyes, Dunkin and Hong's was approximately about 230 bps, 250 bps.

points.point: The only de-linking management described was financial, not structural: the roughly EUR 110 million Netherlands-held acquisition debt for DP Eurasia is now serviced wholly from Turkish cash flows and dividends, with no remittance from India for three quarters.
points.quote: We are pleased to share that Turkey is now servicing its acquisition-related debt entirely through internal cash flows.

points.point: In the most recent call the emerging brands are still described as a drag being managed inside JFL and running ahead of plan — confirming no separation of Popeyes, Hong's or Dunkin' is contemplated in these texts.
points.quote: Just to remind you, there is a drag of new businesses like Popeyes, Hong's and Dunkin.

points.point: The one structural question from an investor concerned the promoter group's HCCB transaction and whether JFL resources would be used; Hari Bhartia said focus stays with JFL and funding was already arranged, and nobody asked for a business to be separated.

For the retained portfolio they expect the Popeyes/Dunkin'/Hong's drag of roughly 230-250 bps to halve, EBITDA margin up at least 200 bps over FY24 by FY28, Domino's India about 15% revenue growth and about 15% pre-Ind AS margin, and Turkey to self-fund its EUR 110 million acquisition debt.

listing.text: NOT YET — scheme at 'nclt_sanction' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

rationale.rationale: These texts describe no spin-off, demerger or separation of a business by Max Healthcare Institute Ltd. (MAXHEALTH) — the direction of travel across all eleven disclosures is the opposite: consolidation of subsidiaries into fewer entities, acquisitions (Jaypee Healthcare/Max Noida, Kalinga Hospital Bhubaneswar at ~INR 298 crore for 58.28% rising to 66.34%, Yerawada Properties Pvt. Ltd.) and brownfield/greenfield bed addition (~20% brownfield capacity commissioned in FY26, 500-bed Gurgaon Sector-56, 700-712 beds at Shaheed Path Lucknow for ~INR 1,400 crore). The only business genuinely separated out is small: the Chitta and Anoopshahr hospitals, divested for INR 40 crore under a binding term sheet announced on the Aug 2025 (Q1 FY26) call and completed in September 2025. Management's stated reason was strategic fit and sub-scale economics, not value unlocking: the two came in as part of the Jaypee Healthcare acquisition and 'had limited strategic alignment' with a strategy 'to focus on super-specialty care in selected geographies'; only Chitta was operational, at ~INR 5 crore revenue and an INR 1 crore EBITDA loss in Q1 FY26, running 26% occupancy on 100 of 200 capacity beds, with no plan to spend on opening the balance 100 beds. On the Nov 2024 call Abhay Soi said of Anoopshahr/Bulandshahr that they were 'not meaningful enough', that no value had been attributed to them in the Jaypee price, and that the choice was between spending CSR time and money on them or wrapping them up. The second, larger strand is internal simplification rather than separation: merger of wholly-owned subsidiaries Alps Hospital Limited with Max Hospitals & Allied Services Limited, and of Crosslay Remedies Limited (CRL) with Jaypee Healthcare Limited (JHL), which management said would 'simplify the holding structure, improve governance and optimize cash flows' and 'reduce our outflow on the acquisition by INR 200-225 crore'; the CRL-JHL amalgamation (NCLT Chandigarh, appointed date October 5, 2024, effective December 15, 2025) produced a one-time tax gain of INR 149 crore in Q2 FY26 (~INR 142 crore net after a ~INR 7 crore Q4 FY26 reversal) against a INR 14 crore stamp-duty provision inside the INR 55 crore of Q3 FY26 exceptional items. Alongside this, step-down subsidiary ET Planners Private Limited was voluntarily liquidated with its entire undertaking transferred to Alps Hospital Limited on a going-concern basis (dissolved March 25, 2026), and MHC Global Healthcare (Nigeria) Ltd — nil revenue, negative net worth of INR 70.89 lakh, -0.0076% of consolidated net worth — was put into voluntary liquidation from January 29, 2026. No investor, lender or partner is recorded in these texts as asking for a separation; no scheme of arrangement for a demerger appears in the filings (the only MOA change put to shareholders, approved October 19, 2026, widens the objects clause to add medical colleges, pharmaceuticals/cyclotron radiopharmaceuticals and food & beverage services — an expansion of scope, not a carve-out). The one business repeatedly discussed as structurally separate — the Partner Healthcare Facility societies (Balaji, Devki Devi, GM Modi, Nirogi, Vikrant) — is being drawn closer, not separated: cash is moved between societies or upstreamed into MHIL via revised medical service fees (e.g. ~INR 25 crore a year at Balaji) because, as Yogesh Sareen explained, 'there is no dividend that can be declared for any society' and upstreaming costs ~25% tax.
rationale.evolution: The idea surfaced on the Nov 7, 2024 call, where Abhay Soi called the Bulandshahr/Anoopshahr units 'not meaningful enough', said no value was attributed to them in the INR 1,660 crore Jaypee enterprise value, and was weighing whether to keep them or 'wrap it up'; on the May 21, 2025 (Q4 FY25) call the same assets were disclosed as sub-scale (Chitta 26% occupancy, only 100 of 200 beds opened, no plan to open the rest) while a parallel 'simplify the holding structure' programme was announced — Alps/MHASL merger concluded and a CRL-JHL merger filed with NCLT to cut acquisition outflow by INR 200-225 crore. It hardened into a transaction on the Aug 14, 2025 (Q1 FY26) call with a binding term sheet to divest Chitta and Anoopshahr for INR 40 crore, and was reported complete on the Nov 17, 2025 (Q2 FY26) call under the heading of streamlining the corporate structure, together with NCLT approval of the subsidiary merger and its INR 149 crore one-time benefit. Thereafter the thread is only tidying-up — stamp duty inside Q3 FY26's INR 55 crore exceptional items (Feb 6, 2026 call), liquidation of MHC Nigeria (Jan 29, 2026) and ET Planners (dissolved March 25, 2026) — and by the May 22, 2026 and later disclosures the narrative is entirely acquisition and capacity addition (Kalinga/Bhubaneswar, Pune, Lucknow Shaheed Path), with no separation plan of any kind.

points.point: First signal: asked whether the Bulandshahr/Anoopshahr units attached to the Jaypee deal mattered, Soi said no value had been ascribed to them and the company was deciding between supporting them or exiting.
points.quote: No, they're not meaningful enough. And we did not even attribute any value to it. We are trying to determine whether we should focus and spend CSR time and money on this or just wrap it up.

points.point: Simplification of the group structure — not separation — is framed as the corporate-action agenda, tied to governance (IiAS 'Next Leaders' recognition) and cash flows; Alps/MHASL merger done, CRL-JHL merger filed with NCLT.
points.quote: On that note, we would like to highlight that we continue to undertake corporate actions to simplify the holding structure, improve governance and optimize cash flows.

points.point: The cash rationale for the CRL-JHL merger is quantified: it reduces the cash outflow on the Jaypee acquisition by INR 200-225 crore.
points.quote: We have also filed an application with the NCLT for merger of Crosslay Remedies Limited and Jaypee Healthcare Limited, which will, in effect, reduce our outflow on the acquisition by INR 200-225 crore.

points.point: Chitta is shown as sub-scale and capital-starved — 100 of 200 beds opened, 26% occupancy on those, and no intention to spend on the rest — the operating backdrop to the divestment decision.
points.quote: Similarly, Chitta Hospital is a 200-bed hospital, but only 100 beds have been opened. And on those 100 beds, we have only 26% occupancy. So, there is no plan to open the balance 100 beds because that will also require some spend.

points.point: The only actual business separation: a binding term sheet to divest Chitta and Anoopshahr for INR 40 crore, justified by strategic focus on super-specialty care in selected geographies, with only Chitta operational at ~INR 5 crore revenue and INR 1 crore EBITDA loss in Q1 FY26.
points.quote: As part of our strategy to focus on super-specialty care in selected geographies, we have executed a binding term sheet to divest Chitta and Anoopshahr hospitals for Rs. 40 crores, with completion expected by September '25.

points.point: The problem the divestment solves is stated as fit, not funding or valuation: the assets arrived with the Jaypee Healthcare acquisition and did not fit the network strategy.
points.quote: These assets were part of the overall Jaypee Healthcare acquisition and had limited strategic alignment.

points.point: Completion is reported under the banner of corporate streamlining, together with NCLT Chandigarh approval of the two-subsidiary merger (appointed date October 5, 2024) and its INR 149 crore one-time benefit.
points.quote: Alongside our expansion efforts, we also streamlined our corporate structure. Divestment of hospitals in Chitta and Anoopshahr was completed in September 2025.

points.point: The cost side of the restructuring: Q3 FY26 carried INR 55 crore of exceptional items, part of it stamp duty on the subsidiary merger (INR 14 crore per the FY26 earnings update, with INR 41 crore for the Code on Wages).
points.quote: During the quarter, there were exceptional items aggregating to INR 55 crore relating to impact of the Code on Wages, 2019 and provision for stamp duty on the merger of two of our subsidiaries.

points.point: The structurally separate Partner Healthcare Facility societies are explicitly being kept inside the network and their cash upstreamed or moved between societies rather than separated, because societies cannot pay dividends and upstreaming costs ~25% tax; Balaji's fee revision alone adds ~INR 25 crore a year to MHIL.
points.quote: No, there is no dividend that can be declared for any society.

points.point: Filing of May 21, 2026 (FY26 earnings update): the subsidiary amalgamation was completed, with the merged entity retaining the Crosslay Remedies name — a consolidation of two legal entities into one, the opposite of a carve-out.
points.quote: Post approval of Scheme of Amalgamation, two WoS i.e., CRL and JHL, have amalgamated effective December 15, 2025 and the name of amalgamated entity has been changed to Crosslay Remedies Limited

points.point: NCLT order of March 25, 2026 dissolving step-down wholly-owned subsidiary ET Planners Private Limited: its whole undertaking was moved up to parent Alps Hospital Limited on a going-concern basis, removing a legal entity rather than separating a business.
points.quote: The entire business undertaking of the company which comprises of all assets, all liabilities, customers and suppliers contracts, service agreements, lease and licenses, employees etc. on a going concern basis will be distributed to its shareholder i.e. Alps Hospital Limited.

points.point: Filing of January 29, 2026: voluntary liquidation of MHC Global Healthcare (Nigeria) Ltd, a non-material subsidiary with nil revenue and negative net worth of INR 70.89 lakh (-0.0076% of consolidated net worth), explicitly with no business or financial consequence.
points.quote: The voluntary liquidation of MHC Nigeria will neither affect any business nor impact materially the consolidated financials of the Company.

points.point: The only structural item put to shareholders (postal ballot results declared October 19, 2026) widens the company's objects into medical colleges, pharmaceuticals/radiopharmaceuticals and food & beverage — evidence that no demerger scheme was placed before members in this period.
points.quote: Alteration of the Main Objects Clause of the Memorandum of Association of the Company

rationale.what_management_expects: No separation economics were given, because no separation was announced. For the divested Chitta/Anoopshahr units: INR 40 crore proceeds and exit of a strategically misaligned, loss-making asset (INR 1 crore EBITDA loss). For MHIL: a simpler holding structure, better governance, optimized cash flows, INR 200-225 crore lower Jaypee outflow and a ~INR 142 crore net one-time tax gain, against INR 14 crore stamp duty.
rationale.gaps: No demerger, spin-off, listed-entity separation, buyer identity, Anoopshahr financials, or any investor, lender or partner request for a separation is explained anywhere in these texts.

rationale.rationale: These texts do not contain a business separation by Minda Corporation — no demerger, no spin-off, no slump sale of a division, and no Scheme of Arrangement document is present. Across the eight calls (Aug 2024 to May 2026) management describes the opposite direction: buying 49% of Flash Electronics for INR 1,372 crore cash on a INR 3,100 crore valuation (completed Jan 2025), a 60:40 switches JV with Toyodenso of Japan (~INR 150 crore, SOP Q4 FY27), a 50:50 sunroof/power-tailgate JV with HCMF of Taiwan (~INR 80-100 crore, INR 350 crore lifetime order), a TLA with Sanco of China for high-voltage connectors, a Turntide (UK) EV-powertrain JV formed in March 2026, and — announced on the May 22, 2026 call — consolidating associate Minda VAST (~INR 500 crore revenue, ~7% EBITDA margin, >90% passenger vehicle) into Minda Corporation from FY27 to lift PV mix from 14% toward the 25% Vision-2030 target. The single separation event anywhere in the record is a one-line board approval of September 24, 2026 to sell the investment in EVQ Point Solutions Private Limited, a step-down associate in which wholly-owned subsidiary Spark Minda Green Mobility Systems Private Limited holds a 29.5% equity stake. The filing gives no reason at all: buyer 'Will be intimated once finalised', consideration 'shall be intimated at the time of execution', completion date 'Will be intimated in due course of time', not a related-party transaction, and the Regulation 37A / Scheme of Arrangement row is marked 'Not Applicable'. The only quantification attached to it is the FY2025-26 consolidated share of profit of Rs. 3,95,197 — and on the May 2026 call the CFO's associate-profit breakdown (Flash ~INR 70 crore, Furukawa ~INR 8 crore, Minda VAST ~INR 5 crore) records that 'EVQ did not contribute', i.e. an immaterial, non-earning minority stake rather than a business being carved out. No investor, lender, OEM or JV partner is recorded in any call or filing as having asked for a separation; the only balance-sheet asks management responds to are deleveraging (gross debt ~INR 1,100 crore, INR 70 crore repaid in 9M FY26, INR 104-105 crore of promoter warrant money applied to debt repayment, stated intent to move 0.5x debt/equity to 0.2x) and ROCE discipline (22% to 25% by 2030) — funded by promoter warrants and a same-day board approval for up to INR 500 crore of NCDs, not by divesting an operating business.
rationale.evolution: EVQ is never named as a separation candidate in any of the eight calls; it surfaces only once, in Ajay Agarwal's associate-profit breakdown on the May 22, 2026 Q4 FY26 call, where he notes it contributed nothing to PAT. The decision then appears without warning as item 3 of the Board Meeting outcome filed September 24, 2026, alongside unrelated items (INR 500 crore NCD enabling approval, a new wholly-owned subsidiary in China, two senior appointments). Nothing between those two dates — including the Feb 5, 2026 and May 22, 2026 calls, which both discuss capital allocation, debt and Vision 2030 at length — flags it, and the plan has not changed since because no terms have yet been disclosed. Over the same 36 months the only structural change management actually explained was in the other direction: bringing Minda VAST on-balance-sheet from FY27 after a shareholder-agreement change with the JV partner.

points.point: The only separation approved in the record: the Sept 24, 2026 board approved selling the 29.5% stake in EVQ Point Solutions, held via wholly-owned subsidiary Spark Minda Green Mobility Systems, with no rationale stated.
points.quote: The Board has approved the sale of investment held in EVQ Point Solutions Private Limited  through Spark Minda Green Mobility Systems Private Limited (Wholly Owned Subsidiary of the Company).

judge.reason: CCEA gave in-principle approval for strategic disinvestment of the NISP unit, then for demerger of NISP from NMDC and strategic disinvestment of the resulting entity by selling the entire Government of India stake.
judge.insiders: GoI to divest its 50.79% shareholding in NSL with management control to a strategic buyer; GoI shall offer 10% of NSL to NMDC Limited after the buyer is identified. Management incentives not stated.
judge.hidden_value: A standalone, leveraged single-plant steel business: borrowings Rs 5,056.15 Cr, net worth Rs 13,228.35 Cr, rating cut AAA to BBB+/A- post-demerger, FY25 loss Rs 2,373.78 Cr turning to Rs 50.51 Cr profit in Q1 FY27 as interest resets 12.45% to 8.40%.
judge.selling_pressure_why: Documents state only that GoI will divest 50.79% to a strategic buyer; no index, distribution or float detail given.
judge.listing_timeline: Not stated as a date; already listed and filing as of 14.08.2026 with BSE (Scrip Code 543768), NSE (Security ID NSLNISP) and Calcutta Stock Exchange (Scrip ID 74920), with demerger referred to in the past ('Subsequent to demerger', 'pre-demerger period')
judge.read_next: The Preliminary Information Memorandum / Request for Expression of Interest for GoI's 50.79% strategic sale.
judge.quote: As per the Preliminary Information Memorandum and Request for Expression of Interest invited, GOI had decided to divest its 50.79% shareholding in Resulting Company ("NMDC Steel Limited" or "NSL") along with management control to strategic buyer.

listing.text: NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

rationale.rationale: On the record supplied, the "separation" is not a new divestiture announced by NMDC Steel Limited (NSL, scrip NSLNISP / BSE 543768 / CSE 74920) — it is the already-completed demerger of the NISP business (NMDC Iron & Steel Plant, Nagarnar, Dist. Bastar, Chhattisgarh, a 3 MTPA-class greenfield integrated plant) out of NMDC Ltd., the iron-ore mining parent, into NSL as the "Resulting Company" (CIN L27310CT2015GOI001618). The stated reason is entirely a Government of India privatisation mechanic, not an operating or synergy argument: the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs gave in-principle approval on 27 October 2016 for strategic disinvestment of several CPSEs including the NISP unit of NMDC Ltd., and then on 14 October 2020 approved the demerger of NISP from NMDC together with strategic disinvestment of the resulting entity by selling the entire GoI stake. In other words, the carve-out exists so that the steel plant could be made a separately listed, separately saleable entity, leaving NMDC Ltd. as a pure mining company; the asker is the sovereign owner through CCEA, not investors, lenders or a JV partner. The transaction terms set out in the Preliminary Information Memorandum and the Request for Expression of Interest are that GoI divests 50.79% of NSL along with management control to a strategic buyer, and will additionally offer 10% of NSL to NMDC Ltd. once the strategic buyer has been identified through the bidding process. The scheme also allocated legacy exposure to the parent: the Rs 111.19 Cr GST input-credit dispute for July 2017–March 2021 (Rs 8.45 Cr paid, Rs 45.90 Cr dropped, Rs 56.40 Cr in abeyance before the Bilaspur High Court, Rs 0.35 Cr under appeal) is pre-demerger, so NMDC Ltd. files the appeals "as per the demerger scheme." Nothing in the filings claims the separation improves margins, capital allocation or valuation; the only measurable consequence disclosed is that standing alone cost NSL its parent's credit umbrella — rating fell from AAA to A- on demerger (NCD coupon 7.30% to 8.80% from 16.02.2023), then to BBB+ (9.05% from 5 June 2024), with the Rs 523.80 Cr NCDs rated "ICRA BBB+ Rating Watch with Developing Implications" and Ind A-/Negative until redemption on 28.08.2025, and the SBI rupee term loan of Rs 4,476.20 Cr (drawn Rs 4,475.81 Cr) repricing off external rating from 7.1% to 12.45% w.e.f. 01.03.2025 before being repositioned at NSL's request to 8.70% (12.04.2025), 8.45% (12.10.2025) and 8.40% (12.01.2026). Financially the standalone entity moved from a FY25 loss before tax of Rs 3,321.72 Cr on revenue of Rs 8,503.05 Cr (PAT Rs -2,373.78 Cr, EPS -8.10) to FY26 revenue of Rs 13,641.81 Cr with PBT Rs 75.78 Cr and PAT Rs 58.72 Cr, and Q1 FY27 (quarter ended 30.06.2026) revenue Rs 3,661.84 Cr with PBT Rs 73.95 Cr, PAT Rs 50.51 Cr, borrowings Rs 5,056.15 Cr and net worth Rs 13,228.35 Cr — i.e. the asset was handed to the market loss-making and has only just crossed into profit as the sale process remains open.
rationale.evolution: There are no earnings-call transcripts on file, so the only visible evolution is the repetition of the same two-step CCEA history — 27 October 2016 (in-principle strategic disinvestment of the NISP unit) and 14 October 2020 (demerger of NISP from NMDC plus sale of the entire GoI stake in the resulting entity) — carried verbatim as a note in each of the three filings dated 3 February 2026, 29 May 2026 and 14/15 August 2026, with the PIM/EoI terms (50.79% plus control to a strategic buyer, 10% offered to NMDC Ltd. afterwards) unchanged throughout. What changes across the three is the aftermath rather than the plan: by the 3 February 2026 filing the Rs 523.80 Cr NCDs had been redeemed on 28.08.2025 (principal plus Rs 42.98 Cr interest, net of Rs 4.42 Cr TDS), ending the "Rating Watch with Developing Implications" overhang, and the SBI term loan had been stepped down from the 12.45% post-DCCO reset to 8.45%. By the 14 August 2026 filing the rate is 8.40% (from 12.01.2026), term-loan outstanding is Rs 3,177.27 Cr after Rs 1,298.54 Cr repaid, and the entity is profitable (Q1 FY27 PAT Rs 50.51 Cr) — but no filing records any new stage of the sale, bidder shortlist or revised structure. No fresh separation is announced by NSL in this window; the company reports a single segment and no subsidiaries, JVs or associates.

points.point: Filings of 03.02.2026, 29.05.2026 and 14.08.2026 all trace the separation to CCEA's 27 October 2016 in-principle approval for strategic disinvestment of CPSEs including the NISP unit of NMDC Ltd. — i.e. the sale decision predates the carve-out.
points.quote: Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs ("CCEA"), in its meeting dated October 27, 2016, gave in-principle approval for strategic disinvestment ("Strategic Disinvestment") of several CPSEs including the NISP unit of NMDC Ltd.

judge.what_is_spun: Paytm Payments Bank Limited, an associate company, separating from the Company via voluntary winding up
judge.reason: In view of cancellation of its banking licence by the RBI w.e.f. April 24, 2026, PPBL's Board and Shareholders approved resolutions to enable winding-up, as instructed by the RBI, or voluntarily with RBI permission.
judge.insiders: Not stated for any new entity; filings state One 97 Communications Limited 'is a professionally managed company and does not have any identified promoter.'
judge.hidden_value: PPBL contributed Nil turnover, revenue, income and net worth last financial year, and the Company has no exposure or material business arrangements with it — so the separation removes a regulatory overhang without giving up earnings; all Paytm services continue uninterrupted.
judge.selling_pressure_why: No shares distributed or listed — PPBL is being wound up and contributed nil revenue and net worth; no index exclusion arises.
judge.listing_timeline: not stated; the April 25, 2026 filing says only that the expected date of completion is 'Not determinable at this stage, as the winding-up process is subject to applicable regulatory and legal proceedings.'
judge.read_next: The winding-up order of the appropriate court or authority, which determines any consideration receivable by the Company.
judge.quote: The Company wishes to assure its shareholders and investors that the winding-up of PPBL and the consequential cessation of the associate relationship are not expected to have any material impact on the business, operations, or financial condition of the Company.

listing.text: NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is One 97 Communications' (OCL) Offline Merchant Payments business — the device-led acquiring franchise (soundbox, card soundbox/EDC card machines, QR) — which has been carved out of the listed parent and transferred as a going concern, on a slump-sale basis, to Paytm Payments Services Limited (PPSL), OCL's wholly owned subsidiary that holds the online payment-aggregator licence. The stated reason in the Business Transfer Agreement filing is regulatory: "The transfer is being undertaken to take steps to comply with the Reserve Bank of India's Master Directions on Regulation of Payment Aggregators dated September 15, 2025"; the filing additionally characterises it as "an internal restructuring intended to consolidate the related business within a dedicated wholly owned subsidiary, in alignment with applicable regulatory requirements and to achieve operational efficiency." Mechanics and numbers: shareholder approval on November 23, 2025, BTA executed November 28, 2025, effective from midnight of November 30, 2025, for a lump-sum cash consideration equal to the book value of the transferred undertaking at the effective date, with approximately INR 960 crore cited as the March 31, 2025 reference book value; Mr. Ripunjai Gaur (COO – Offline Payments) and Mr. Deependra Singh Rathore (CTO – Payments) transferred to PPSL and ceased as OCL Senior Management Personnel. Because it is a parent-to-wholly-owned-subsidiary transfer at book value, the filing stresses "there is no change in the ultimate beneficial ownership or control, and the entire economic interest in the Transferred Undertaking will continue to vest with the holding company." On the calls, the problem management says this solves is legal-entity fragmentation: online and offline acquiring sat in separate legal entities, so omnichannel merchants "could have not onboarded" — and online merchant onboarding had been paused/under embargo since 2021-22. With licences and entities combined, Vijay Shekhar Sharma says Paytm can "formally" do omni-channel, give a merchant a single dashboard, and layer value-added services — spend analytics, settlement, payout — so "per payment, we make more bps"; he also took over as CEO of PPSL (disclosed on the Jan 30, 2026 call) and called online "literally a new line of business" that will be "materially sizable," carrying platform fees plus EMI and card initiatives and feeding payment processing margin (guided above 4 bps, with net payment margin ~9 bps in Q4 FY26). Who asked for it: the RBI, via the September 15, 2025 Payment Aggregator Master Directions, with OCL shareholders approving the slump sale on November 23, 2025 — no investor, lender or commercial partner demand is cited anywhere in these texts. Critically for a special-situation investor, this is not a demerger to shareholders: there is no scheme of arrangement (the filing marks the Regulation 37A/scheme questions "Not Applicable"), no separate listing and no value-unlock event — the separation is purely intra-group consolidation into the licensed entity.
rationale.evolution: On the July 22, 2025 call there is no mention of any carve-out at all — payments is discussed as one full-stack business ("We own the machine, we own the customer") operating at breakeven. The plan surfaces in the Oct 15 and Nov 24, 2025 disclosures referenced by the BTA filing, and on the November 5, 2025 call Vijay Shekhar Sharma confirms the rationale for the first time — the regulator "made both licenses and one license together," so "now formally, we can do omni-channel," plus new VAS revenue per payment; the BTA is then executed November 28, 2025, effective November 30, 2025. By the January 30, 2026 call the framing has shifted from compliance to offence: VSS discloses he has become CEO of PPSL, says "now we can acquire both in the same entity," and calls online a new, materially sizable line of business paused since 2021. On May 7, 2026 Madhur Deora describes online as a tailwind that "obviously has a full license now" and "a very meaningful double digits" of GMV, and by July 21, 2026 the subject disappears into broad-based growth commentary (GMV +31%, embargo described as past).

points.point: The BTA filing of November 28, 2025 states the sole purpose of transferring the Offline Merchant Payments business to wholly owned subsidiary PPSL is compliance with the RBI's September 15, 2025 Payment Aggregator Master Directions.
points.quote: The transfer is being undertaken to take steps to comply with the Reserve Bank of India's Master Directions on Regulation of Payment Aggregators dated September 15, 2025.

points.point: The company frames it as intra-group consolidation at book value — not a value-unlock demerger — with the related-party/arm's-length answer spelling out the consolidation and efficiency logic.
points.quote: Yes, the transfer is proposed to be carried out at book value, given that it forms part of an internal restructuring intended to consolidate the related business within a dedicated wholly owned subsidiary, in alignment with applicable regulatory requirements and to achieve operational efficiency.

points.point: Consideration is lump-sum cash based on book value at the November 30, 2025 effective date; the only number given is the prior-year reference book value of the transferred undertaking.
points.quote: For reference, the book value of the Transferred Undertaking as on March 31, 2025 is approximately INR 960 Crores (Indian Rupees Nine Hundred Sixty Crores).

points.point: Because it is a parent-to-WOS slump sale, OCL argues there is no economic change for shareholders — no scheme of arrangement, no listing, no dilution.
points.quote: As the transaction is between the holding company and its wholly owned subsidiary, there is no change in the ultimate beneficial ownership or control, and the entire economic interest in the Transferred Undertaking will continue to vest with the holding company.

points.point: Two Senior Management Personnel — Ripunjai Gaur, COO Offline Payments, and Deependra Singh Rathore, CTO Payments — moved with the undertaking and ceased to be OCL SMPs from midnight of November 30, 2025, after shareholder approval on November 23, 2025.
points.quote: Further Mr. Ripunjai Gaur, COO - Offline Payments and Mr. Deependra Singh Rathore, CTO - Payments, both designated as Senior Management Personnel (SMPs) of the Company, will also be transferred to PPSL w.e.f. midnight of November 30, 2025 and upon such transfer they will cease as SMPs of the Company.

points.point: Baseline before the carve-out: payments is presented as a single full-stack, breakeven business with no mention of any entity transfer, and VSS insists Paytm owns both the device and the merchant relationship (the assets that later move to PPSL).
points.quote: We own the machine, we own the customer. We are in that business.

points.point: First call-level rationale, three weeks before the BTA: VSS says the regulator collapsed the two licences into one, which finally lets Paytm serve a merchant omnichannel from one entity with a single dashboard.
points.quote: And now formally, we can do omni-channel. I mean, you can imagine that a single company will be able to see their single dashboard, et cetera, et cetera. So we are very happy about it. The regulator has also made both licenses and one license together.

points.point: Asked directly by Vijit Jain (Citi) whether combining online and offline payment aggregation is what enables omnichannel, VSS names the constraint explicitly — the offline business sitting in a different legal entity blocked onboarding of omnichannel merchants.
points.quote: So all these businesses, we couldn't have onboarded and just because there's an offline entity was a different company, a legal entity could have not onboarded.

points.point: The commercial payoff claimed is incremental bps per payment from value-added services that only a combined entity can sell.
points.quote: Yes, not just this element, but there are other VAS elements like spend analytics, like settlement, like payout. All those things start to show up as new value-add items. So per payment, we make more bps or more money than we will make standalone and offline or standalone and online.

points.point: Management links the restructuring to margin mix: newly onboardable online merchants carry higher MDR and net margin, supporting the payment processing margin improvement reported that quarter.
points.quote: Sachin, another thing that we now have is the privilege of onboarding online merchants. Online merchants eventually are high MDR plus high net margin.

points.point: Post-transfer, VSS discloses he has personally taken over as CEO of PPSL, the entity now holding both online and offline merchant payments.
points.quote: You may have noticed that I've become the CEO of the PPSL company. So online business will start generating more upside in payments and financial services.

points.point: He reframes the carve-out as creating a new revenue line — online acquiring, effectively paused since 2021 — boosted by both the licence permission and the new entity structure, with enterprise sales hiring behind it.
points.quote: I mean, it's an important thing to note that the payment business will get boosted because of permission and the structure that we are doing.

points.point: The single-entity point is stated as the operational unlock: offline and online merchants can now be acquired by the same company.
points.quote: And because we are championing offline, we were championing online. Now we can acquire both in the same entity.

points.point: Madhur Deora attributes FY27 revenue acceleration partly to online merchants now operating under a full licence, after a year in which they could not onboard new customers for about half the year.

points.quote: We are a very significant player in online merchants, despite the fact that until last year, we were not really adding new customers for more than three years, right?

points.point: A year after the transfer the separation itself is no longer discussed; online is simply one of several accelerating payment businesses, with the prior constraint described in the past tense.
points.quote: As you know, online business was also under embargo. So that is obviously a headwind. Now, the increase in growth has come in all of those businesses, including the consumer side, as you mentioned.

rationale.what_management_expects: One licensed entity for all merchant acquiring: formal omnichannel, a single merchant dashboard, VAS (spend analytics, settlement, payout) and more bps per payment; online — higher-MDR, platform-fee, EMI/card-led — becomes a materially sizable new revenue line lifting payment processing margin past 4 bps. OCL receives book-value cash; no change in beneficial ownership or economic interest.

rationale.rationale: There are no earnings-call transcripts on file, so the only stated reasoning is in the Regulation 30 filings, where management frames the separation as an internal group restructuring that splits the AI/technology business from the VFX/post-production services business. The entity being separated is Prime Focus Technologies Limited — renamed Brahma AI Services India Limited — together with the Metaphysic assets (Metaphysic Limited renamed Brahma AI Services UK Limited, DAX Cloud ULC renamed Brahma AI Canada Inc., DNEG Creative Private Limited renamed Brahma AI India Technologies Private Limited); the stated purpose of the March 30, 2026 steps is "internal restructuring and consolidation of the AI / Technology business under the Company's vertical 'Brahma'", which the company says "is expected to leverage the brand value and provide additional revenue streams", and the April 1, 2026 steps are to "streamline the business operations". Mechanically the separation runs both ways: pure software/IP moves up into Brahma (proprietary software assigned from Brahma India to Brahma AI ME Ltd for INR 75.2 Crores, and from Prime Focus Technologies Inc. for USD 3.44 Million), while the people-and-services tails move back into DNEG — the TCS business and Restoration business sold as a going concern by slump sale to DNEG India Media Services Limited for INR 26.5 Crores (FY25 turnover INR 102.62 Crores, 2.85% of consolidated turnover; net worth INR 23.86 Crores, 2.38%), and all of Prime Focus Technologies Inc. (the US services arm, revenue sliding from USD 13,459,863 in FY23 to USD 10,589,160 in FY25) sold by Brahma India to DNEG S.a.r.l. for about USD 21 Million. The holding structure is then re-pointed: DNEG S.a.r.l. sells 100% of Brahma India (its own 92.23% plus the residual 7.77% from other holders) to Brahma AI Holdings Limited, Jersey, for USD 90.09 Million, so the AI business sits under a separate Jersey holdco that is 90.20% held by Double Negative Holdings Limited — i.e. roughly 9.8% outside equity already sits at the Brahma level, which is the only structural hint at third-party participation. Management stresses this is not a divestment and not a court scheme: "the sale is outside the scheme of arrangement. Regulation 37A is not applicable", and "PFT US and Brahma India will continue to be part of the group and will continue to be step-down subsidiaries of the Company". It is also explicitly cashless at the parent: the conversion of Brahma India's inter-company loan and optionally convertible redeemable preference shares in PFT US into equity "does not involve any fresh infusion of capital by the Company or Brahma India". By the time shareholders ratified both transfers as material related-party transactions at the September 30, 2026 AGM, the same notice also carried an increase in authorised capital from 85 Crore to 100 Crore shares and an enabling resolution to raise up to Rs 3,000 Crore via QIP/ADR-GDR/preferential/rights issue — the clearest signal of what the cleaned-up structure is meant to be used for. No filing names any investor, lender or partner as having asked for the separation.
rationale.evolution: The groundwork predates the Brahma language: in the June 2024 quarter Prime Focus Limited sold its entire shareholding in Prime Focus Technologies to step-down subsidiary DNEG S.a.r.l. for Rs 69,302.55 Lakhs, booking an exceptional gain of Rs 21,621.18 Lakhs (shareholder approval June 6, 2024), and on February 14, 2025 the group acquired Metaphysic Inc. for USD 130 Million settled in subsidiary shares (goodwill Rs 96,942.67 Lakhs, later topped up by Rs 6,399.09 Lakhs), while FY25 also carried Rs 38,017.71 Lakhs of exceptional impairments including Rs 17,574.77 Lakhs of decommissioned intangibles. The July 3, 2025 preferential issue of 46,26,69,444 shares at Rs 120 (Rs 5,55,203.33 Lakhs, mostly a 2,561-for-100 swap of DNEG shares, allotted September 17 and 23, 2025) pulled DNEG up into the listed entity and cut non-controlling interest from Rs 1,28,432.26 Lakhs to Rs 45,713.96 Lakhs — a precondition for cleanly re-sorting the subsidiaries. The split itself then arrives in two board/audit-committee steps: March 30, 2026 (software assignments to Brahma AI ME Ltd plus the TCS and Restoration slump sale to DNEG India) and April 1, 2026 (PFT US to DNEG S.a.r.l.; Brahma India to Brahma AI Holdings Limited, Jersey), with the Prime Focus Technologies → Brahma AI Services India renaming confirmed in the May 28, 2026 results. Approval was completed at the September 30, 2026 AGM (resolutions 4 and 5), alongside the capital increase, the Rs 3,000 Crore fund-raise enabling resolution, and Namit Malhotra's move from Non-Executive Director to Whole-time Director effective August 7, 2026.

points.point: Filing of March 30, 2026: the stated reason for assigning proprietary software out of Brahma India and PFT USA into Brahma AI ME Ltd (INR 75.2 Crores and USD 3.44 Million respectively) is consolidation of the AI/technology business under the 'Brahma' vertical, justified on brand value and new revenue streams.
points.quote: The said software assignment forms a part of internal restructuring and consolidation of the AI / Technology business under the Company's vertical "Brahma". This is expected to leverage the brand value and provide additional revenue streams.

points.point: Same filing: the TCS business and Restoration business are sold as a going concern by slump sale from Brahma India to DNEG India Media Services Limited for INR 26.5 Crores, on the identical Brahma-consolidation rationale — i.e. services work is deliberately moved out of the AI entity and into the VFX entity.
points.quote: The said slump sale by Brahma India to DNEG India forms a part of internal restructuring and consolidation of the AI / Technology business under vertical "Brahma". This is expected to leverage the brand value and provide additional revenue streams.

points.point: The March 30, 2026 filing draws the dividing line between the two businesses explicitly: Brahma India is the cloud software platform, DNEG India is the post-production services operation.
points.quote: Brahma India: Provides a cloud-based technology platform for content, workflow, supply chain, and production management for the media and entertainment industry.

points.point: Filing of April 1, 2026: the two share transfers — 100% of PFT US from Brahma India to DNEG S.a.r.l. (about USD 21 Million) and 100% of Brahma India from DNEG S.a.r.l. to Brahma AI Holdings Limited, Jersey (USD 90.09 Million) — are presented only as streamlining of operations, with no financial target attached.
points.quote: the following mentioned subsidiaries of Prime Focus Limited (the "Company" or "PFL") have proposed to undertake certain steps for internal restructuring within the group to streamline the business operations

points.point: Management is emphatic that nothing leaves the group and that this is not a demerger or court-sanctioned scheme requiring Regulation 37A compliance.
points.quote: Upon completion of the aforementioned transfers, PFT US and Brahma India will continue to be part of the group and will continue to be step‑down subsidiaries of the Company.

points.point: The restructuring is funded by converting existing intra-group exposure, not new money: Brahma India's inter-company loan and optionally convertible redeemable preference shares in PFT US convert to equity before PFT US is handed to DNEG.
points.quote: It is important to note that the issuance of additional equity shares does not involve any fresh infusion of capital by the Company or Brahma India.

points.point: AGM of September 30, 2026 (Annexure A): the separated AI entity is sized for shareholders — Brahma India FY2025-26 consolidated turnover INR 328.72 Crores (7.03% of group) and net worth INR 278.63 Crores (10.95% of group), versus PFT US turnover INR 99.74 Crores (2.13%) and net worth of just INR 1.04 Crores (0.04%).
points.quote: Consolidated Turnover of Brahma India for FY 2025 -26: INR 328.72 Crores

points.point: The same AGM that ratified both transfers as material related-party transactions also raised authorised capital from 85 Crore to 100 Crore shares and approved an enabling resolution for up to Rs 3,000 Crore of fresh capital, linking the clean-up to a funding event rather than to any disposal.
points.quote: To consider, evaluate and approve the proposal to raise funds of an amount not exceeding Rs.3,000 Crore (Rupees Three Thousand Crore Only) or its equivalent in any other currency through one or more permissible mechanism as may be deemed appropriate by the Board of Directors of the Company ("Board"), by way of issuance of equity shares and/ or debt securities or non -convertible securities and/or other securities including share warrants and/ or any other equity linked securities.

points.point: Audited results of May 28, 2026 undercut any claim that the two businesses are already reported separately — despite the Brahma/DNEG split the group still reports a single operating segment and still describes itself as one integrated setup.
points.quote: The Group is mainly engaged in operating as integrated post-production setup.

points.point: Context for the timing: the FY26 results carry an emphasis of matter on the admitted-then-stayed Section 7 insolvency petition by Raspalfa (formerly Reliance Alpha) for Rs 35,379.75 Lakhs, with the full amount deposited with the Registrar, NCLAT; the underlying Bombay High Court suit was recorded as settled and withdrawn on August 4, 2026, and the group refinanced USD 500 Million of foreign-subsidiary debt to June 2029.
points.quote: Subsequent to year end, the Group has refinanced its debt facilities of USD 500 Mn in its foreign subsidiary tills June 2029

rationale.what_management_expects: Only two stated effects: consolidating all AI/technology under the Brahma vertical to "leverage the brand value and provide additional revenue streams", and streamlined operations. Structurally, Brahma AI Holdings (Jersey, 90.20% held) gathers the platform and Metaphysic IP; DNEG takes back PFT US, TCS and Restoration services. No margin, capital-allocation or valuation claim is made anywhere in the filings.
rationale.gaps: No earnings-call transcripts on file. Filings give no margin, valuation or synergy numbers, no listing/demerger plan for Brahma, no segment financials, and name no investor, lender or partner as requesting it.

judge.insiders: Promoter/promoter group/group companies have no interest in Buildnext; buyer JSW One is not promoter group. Consideration is JSW One shares to PVPL; "our shareholding will be insignificant in JSW One."
