Ajai Kumar : It is difficult to give timeline right now because we are working to see at what time we can maximize our value Kabir : Okay. Okay. Now my second question is with Dr. Ajai. So there have been rumors about CVC exit. And everyone expects them to exist some time. So just wanti

which we will be addressing in the next few quarters with our new investor, and we will keep you definitely updated on. Sakshi Pratap: Understood. And would you be able to provide the percentage contribution by international patients to our revenue? Raj Gore: Around 3-4% of revenue is from international. Moderator: Next question is from the line of Umang Gada from Avener Capital. Healthcare Global Enterprises Limited May 26, 202 5 Page 15 of 15 Umang Gada: My question was more on the Milann side of the business. That business has evidently continued to struggle to grow. So, I just wanted an update from the management side that what are the strategies over there even maybe are we looking to spin off in the future or any strategies over there? B.S. Ajaikumar: Yes. I can answer that. You're absolutely right. Milann have been through quite a tough time, particularly with our former partner self -starting units near our center. We have addressed this issue internally. We were just waiting for the new investor also to come. We have also discussed with them. So, we are definitely putting a proposal to divest. And hopefully, this will happen definitely this fiscal year, and we'll keep you updated. Umang Gada: Yes, yes. I was, the answer was audible. Moderator: Ladies and gentlemen, that was the last question. I would now like to hand the conference over to the management for closing comments.

rationale.rationale: Management presents this as an exit from fertility to concentrate capital and management bandwidth on oncology. The business separated is Milann, HCG's fertility/IVF chain held through BACC Health Care Private Limited — a majority stake taken in 2013 and a fully-owned subsidiary from 2020 — sold to Inviga Healthcare Fund I at an enterprise valuation of INR 63 crore, with equity consideration of INR 37.6 crore for 100% including certain transition services support, 75% received upfront at closing and 25% over 18 months (filings specify INR 28.23 crore at closing and INR 9.41 crore deferred, not contingent). The problems cited: Milann's operating footprint had steadily declined, centres falling from 9 to 6; the business ran at a low EBITDA margin and was only marginally above break-even on a post-rent basis; and reviving and scaling it would need significant management bandwidth plus primary capital infusion, both outside HCG's focus on building the core oncology network. Filings add that BACC is not a material subsidiary and that fertility is not a core business activity — FY26 revenue of INR 60.45 crore (4.45% of HCG standalone revenue) and net worth of INR 17.53 crore (1.09%). The root cause of the decline was named earlier: Milann's original founder/partner exited, her non-compete lapsed, and she opened her own centres very close to HCG's, denting revenue at Kumara Park and J.P. Nagar. The buyer was described as better positioned to infuse growth capital, scale the business independently and carry forward the Milann legacy, and was chosen through a comprehensive, competitive sale process focused on maximizing valuation, transaction certainty and a smooth transition for Milann's employees, with Audit Committee and Board approval and an independent third-party valuation. Crucially, the buyer is a related party: Inviga Healthcare Fund I is sponsored and controlled by Dr. B.S. Ajaikumar, HCG's promoter and Non-Executive Chairman. The push came repeatedly from analysts (Avener Capital, ChrysCapital, Sameeksha, Ambit, Pratap Securities) rather than lenders or partners, and the exit was explicitly held back until the incoming majority shareholder arrived — Ajaikumar said HCG was waiting for the new investor and had discussed it with them.
rationale.evolution: The idea surfaced on the Nov 2023 call, where Ajaikumar said post-COVID Milann had been through a tough time, a Delhi centre had been closed, and HCG was looking at divesting with no firm timeline; on the Mar 2025 call (Feb 27, 2025) he named the cause — the founder's non-compete expiring and her new centres next to HCG's — and said the timing of a divestment was still being decided. By May 2025 it hardened into intent: HCG was definitely putting a proposal to divest, hopefully within that fiscal year, having waited for and consulted the new investor (KKR/Hector). At the Dec 4, 2025 investor meet the new CEO Manish Mattoo said operations had been stabilised but the focus would be cancer care, with several strategic options under evaluation and divestment of the vertical named as one; Feb 2026 carried no update though revenue was already reported excluding fertility. It completed on May 19-20, 2026 — SPA signed May 19, board approval and pricing disclosed, closing guided to Q1 FY27 — and filings confirm BACC ceased to be a subsidiary from June 30, 2026.

points.point: First flagged: Milann had suffered post-COVID, a Delhi centre was closed for efficiency, and divestment was on the table with no timeline given.
points.quote: It has come, it is coming up the ladder, and we are looking at it in the future for divesting, but we cannot give any firm timeline for it.

points.point: Ajaikumar named the competitive cause of Milann's revenue dip — the founder's exit, expiry of her non-compete, and her new centres opening next to HCG's Kumara Park and J.P. Nagar units — while saying divestment timing was still being weighed.
points.quote: In view of that, she has started her own few centers very close to our center. So because of that, particularly in Kumara Park and J.P. Nagar, we have seen a dip in the revenue.

points.point: Divestment was framed as a decision of timing, not of principle, with Milann's turnaround (including a new andrology focus) pursued in parallel.
points.quote: But at the same time, there is a decision where we want to see what time to divest it, we will be looking at that also as we move forward.

points.point: Asked by Umang Gada (Avener Capital) whether HCG would spin off Milann, Ajaikumar said a divestment proposal was being put forward, and that HCG had deliberately waited for the incoming investor (KKR) and discussed it with them.
points.quote: We have addressed this issue internally. We were just waiting for the new investor also to come. We have also discussed with them. So, we are definitely putting a proposal to divest. And hopefully, this will happen definitely this fiscal year, and we will keep you updated.

points.point: At the investor and analyst meet the new CEO reset the rationale around single-specialty focus: Milann operations had been stabilised, but future focus would be cancer care, with strategic options under evaluation. Milann was also lumped into the new international cluster rather than given its own segment.
points.quote: But going forward, our focus will be on cancer care. And hence, we are evaluating several strategic options on the way ahead for Milann.

points.point: Pressed by Rajas Joshi (ChrysCapital) on what options existed, Mattoo named divestment explicitly but stopped short of commitment.
points.quote: I think one of the options, while we are still evaluating, could be divestment of this vertical.

points.point: No divestment update was given, but management had already begun reporting the core business excluding fertility (Q3 FY26 revenue INR 633 crore total versus INR 618 crore ex-fertility), effectively pre-separating Milann in disclosure while the review ran.
points.quote: Excluding the fertility business, HCG delivered revenues of INR 618 crore, supported by healthy patient volume growth of 8% year-on-year, underscoring resilient demand for oncology care across the network.

points.point: Announced: board approved the sale of Milann to Inviga Healthcare Fund, signed the previous day, closing expected within Q1 FY27 — presented as a strategic decision to sharpen oncology focus.
points.quote: Finally, we have taken a strategic decision to sharpen our focus on oncology. In line with this, the board has approved the sale of Milann, our fertility business, to Inviga Healthcare Fund.

points.point: Terms: enterprise valuation INR 63 crore; equity consideration INR 37.6 crore for 100% including certain transition services support, 75% upfront at closing and 25% over 18 months.
points.quote: The equity consideration for 100% of the business, including certain transition services support is INR37.6 crore, of which 75% will be received upfront at closing and the balance 25% over 18 months.

points.point: The operational problem quantified for Pranav Chawla (Ambit): 13 years inside HCG, centres down from 9 to 6, low EBITDA margin and barely above break-even after rent.
points.quote: The number of centers has come down from 9 to 6 and today the business operates at a low EBITDA margin and remains only marginally above break-even on a post-rent basis.

points.point: The core why: fixing Milann would consume management bandwidth and require primary equity capital, both of which HCG wants aimed at the oncology network instead.
points.quote: So, reviving and scaling the platform would require significant management bandwidth and primary capital infusion, both of which are outside HCGs current strategic focus because we are focused on developing the primary oncology network, core oncology network.

points.point: The buyer rationale: an owner better able to fund and scale fertility independently and preserve the Milann brand legacy.
points.quote: So, HCG then decided to exit this non-core business and transfer it to a buyer who was better positioned to infuse growth capital, scale the business independently, and carry for/ward the Milann legacy.

points.point: Process described as a competitive sale with Inviga shortlisted as preferred buyer, optimising for valuation, deal certainty and employee transition, cleared by Board and Audit Committee.
points.quote: See, we initiated a comprehensive sale process, a competitive sale process where HCG shortlisted Inviga as the preferred buyer and the focus was on maximizing valuation and ensuring that the transaction, you know, was done with certainty and it facilitated a smooth transition for Milann's employees as well.

points.point: Abdulkader Puranwala (ICICI Securities) linked the divestment and the INR 425 crore rights issue to leverage; management said net debt/EBITDA had fallen from 2.2-2.3x to 1.4x against an internal ceiling of 2.5x, giving headroom for brownfield capacity (200+ beds, INR 90-100 crore) and the 1,000-bed FY30 plan.
points.quote: So the net debt to EBITDA ratio has, come down favourably. Earlier it was 2.2 x, 2.3x. It is come down to 1.4 x as of today and this gives us enough headroom to invest in capacity addition, expansion, brownfield, technology additions and all.

points.point: Filing (May 19, 2026) confirms it is a share sale of BACC Health Care Private Limited, not a scheme of arrangement or demerger (the LODR question on disposal outside a Scheme of Arrangement is answered Not Applicable), and states fertility is non-core.
points.quote: BACC is not a material subsidiary of the Company and is engaged in the business of fertility and reproductive healthcare services, which is not a core business activity of the Company.

points.point: Filing states the capital-allocation purpose: greater operational focus and redeployment of capital into high-growth areas and cancer services.
points.quote: The Proposed Transaction is aligned with the Company's broader strategic and capital allocation objectives and is expected to facilitate greater operational focus and business alignment, allowing the Company to reinvest capital in high growth areas and cancer services.

points.point: Materiality quantified: BACC FY26 revenue INR 60.45 crore (4.45% of HCG standalone revenue) and net worth INR 17.53 crore (1.09%); consideration split INR 28.23 crore at closing and INR 9.41 crore deferred within 18 months, with the deferred piece explicitly not contingent.
points.quote: The deferred consideration referenced above is not a conditional or contingent payment.

points.point: The buyer is promoter-controlled: the transaction is a related party transaction done on an arm's length basis, based on an independent third-party valuation and a competitive process.
points.quote: Dr. B.S. Ajaikumar, Promoter and Non-Executive Chairman of the Board of the Company is the Sponsor of the Inviga Healthcare Fund I (Fund) and also the Promoter of Inviga Investment Advisors Private Limited, the Investment Manager of the Fund. Accordingly, the Fund is controlled by Dr. B S Ajaikumar.

points.point: The exit was value-destructive on the books: on reclassification as held for sale, HCG recognised a standalone impairment of INR 37.52 crore and a consolidated goodwill impairment of INR 31.91 crore as FY26 exceptional items, against the fair value of the consideration receivable.
points.quote: Accordingly, the investment was measured at the lower of its carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell. Accordingly, an impairment loss of Rs. 3,752 lakhs was recognised as an exceptional item during the previous year ended 31 March 2026 based on the fair value of the consideration receivable, net of related expenses.

points.point: Completion confirmed in the Q1 FY27 results: sale closed June 29, 2026 for INR 37.64 crore (INR 28.23 crore received upfront, INR 9.41 crore receivable within 18 months), BACC deconsolidated from June 30, 2026, with a INR 2.96 crore gain booked in consolidated other income.
points.quote: Consequent to completion of the transaction, BACC ceased to be a subsidiary of the Company with effect from 30 June 2026.

points.point: A separate, earlier internal separation: the Triesta lab and Cyclotron (FDG production) businesses were slump-sold into a wholly-owned subsidiary so oncology sat in one company and the scalable diagnostics business could grow outside the HCG network with greater freedom; management said the restructuring under the Triesta brand was completed by the Mar 2025 call.
points.quote: So this is more on account of business realignment where onco comes under one company and the expandable business, which we can look at expanding beyond our own network, which is the lab and the Cyclotron business can move to a separate entity. It also allows greater freedom with a separate entity structure.

rationale.what_management_expects: For HCG: management bandwidth and capital freed for the core oncology network (brownfield/greenfield, 1,000 beds by FY30), sharper single-specialty focus, modest cash (INR 37.6 crore, 75% upfront) on an already de-levered balance sheet (net debt/EBITDA 1.4x after the INR 425 crore rights issue). For Milann: a new owner able to infuse growth capital, scale it independently and carry its legacy forward. No margin or valuation uplift was quantified.
rationale.gaps: No Milann EBITDA figure, competing bids, or why a Chairman-controlled fund won; no reconciliation of INR 63 crore EV with the INR 37.5 crore impairment; no use of proceeds.

segments.measure_notes: No Ind AS 108 segment disclosure exists — HCG reports a single operating segment, 'Medical and Healthcare Services', in both standalone and consolidated accounts (AR2024 p237/p312, AR2025 p257/p340, AR2026 p277/p364). The only fertility-specific figures are in investor presentations: business-level total revenue and reported EBITDA (basis pre/post Ind AS 116 not stated; no inter-segment split, no PAT). Quarterly/half-year only: Q1 FY27 revenue ₹169 Mn and EBITDA ₹23 Mn (Presentation Aug 2026 p6); Milann revenue Q2FY26 ₹148 Mn, Q2FY25 ₹158 Mn, H1FY26 ₹297 Mn, H1FY25 ₹302 Mn (Presentation Nov 2025 p14). rationale.rationale: The texts do not support the premise: in the three years of calls and the one filing provided, KSB Ltd. announces no demerger, spin-off, slump sale or scheme of arrangement of any operating business, and management never gives a separation rationale. The only separation of any entity is administrative — the 28 Sep 2026 filing says Pofran Sales and Agency Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary incorporated on 7 January 2005, has applied for voluntary strike-off with the Registrar of Companies, Pune, and will cease to be a subsidiary on completion. The stated reason is simply dormancy: Pofran 'was not operating for past seven years' and 'has been inoperative since last 7 years.' The Annexure A disclosure confirms there is no economics to it — turnover/revenue/income and net worth contributed are 'Not applicable,' as are the sale agreement date, consideration, buyer details, related-party and arm's-length questions, and the regulation 37A / scheme-of-arrangement item; the only timeline given is 'according to the prescribed guidelines of voluntary strike off under Companies Act 2013.' No investor, lender or JV partner is said to have asked for it, and no cost, capital, focus or valuation benefit is claimed. The nearest portfolio decisions management does discuss run the other way or are exits, not separations: in Mar 2026 Rajeev Jain says of the BP&CL reciprocating-pump business that 'initially, we thought to sell it off, luckily we did not and we decided to build it ourselves,' and in Mar 2025 he describes having exited cast-iron foundry work (about 1,100 patterns and 3,000 metric tonnes) by handing it to third-party foundries, while FGD business 'suddenly overnight has vanished' because of a change in government regulation. Throughout, the strategy presented is consolidation and range-completion within one listed entity — nuclear (₹1,300 crore order book), solar (₹245 crore CY25 to 300+ crore CY26), valves, SupremeServ at ~15-17% of sales, firefighting, mining, exports at 17% — not separation of any of it.
rationale.evolution: The idea never surfaces in the calls: Mar 2024, Mar 2025, Sep 2025, Nov 2025 and Mar 2026 all discuss capacity additions (Shirwal and Sinnar sheds to be commissioned by March 2026), new segments and the group's willingness to localise more products, with no question or answer about demerging, hiving off or listing any division separately. Over this period the only direction of travel discussed is inward: BP&CL technology (acquired 2023) being built up rather than sold, and openness to further acquisitions ('if such opportunities occur in future, we are definitely exploring it', Sep 2025). The single separation event appears only in the 28 Sep 2026 filing, as the voluntary strike-off of the dormant shell Pofran Sales and Agency Limited. The plan therefore has no evolution to trace — one administrative cessation announced once, with no prior or subsequent discussion in the transcripts supplied.

points.point: The only separation disclosed is a voluntary strike-off application for the wholly owned subsidiary Pofran Sales and Agency Limited, filed with the Registrar of Companies, Pune; on completion Pofran ceases to be a subsidiary.

points.point: The entire stated reason is dormancy — the entity, incorporated 7 January 2005, has not traded for seven years. No strategic, capital or valuation rationale is offered.

points.quote: Pofran has been inoperative since last 7 years.

points.point: There is no buyer, no consideration, no sale agreement and no related-party or arm's-length question, and the scheme-of-arrangement / regulation 37A item is 'Not applicable' — i.e. this is a dissolution, not a demerger or slump sale.

points.point: The only timeline given is the statutory strike-off process under the Companies Act 2013, not a board-approved scheme with record dates or share entitlement ratios.

points.point: Management explicitly rejected divesting a business: the BP&CL reciprocating-pump line was considered for sale after the 2023 acquisition and deliberately retained and developed in-house, with an NPCIL-approved prototype.
points.quote: Reciprocating pump business we acquired from BP&CL and it was good acquisition. Initially, we thought to sell it off, luckily we did not and we decided to build it ourselves.

points.point: The closest real exit discussed is the step-by-step closure of the captive cast-iron foundry business, roughly 1,100 patterns and 3,000 metric tonnes, outsourced to third-party foundries — framed as supply-chain simplification, not as a separation of a business unit.
points.quote: You know that our foundry also for cast iron, we have closed it step by step. We have come out of the cast iron business and almost 1,100 patents and the 3,000 metric tons of business. We have given it to other foundries here, and we did not have any issues.

points.point: Asked directly what worries him and what the parent provides, Jain names no portfolio restructuring — only the pace of nuclear project implementation — and describes royalty, IT and service charges to the parent, with no entity reorganisation.

points.point: Management frames the multi-segment structure as the deliberate hedge that makes separation unnecessary — mixed margins across nuclear, valves, SupremeServ, solar and firefighting are pooled to hold a 13-14% EBITDA band.
points.quote: So, that's why overall, I would say, the return which we always target is that EBITDA level what we have.

points.point: On the same logic, segment volatility is presented as internally absorbed — FGD vanishing overnight was offset by the L&T supercritical win — rather than as a reason to carve any segment out.
points.quote: But something else, this is KSB's strength that we have all segments and today we got this L&T supercritical and we are expecting much, much more with the next five years what is being invested.

rationale.what_management_expects: Nothing is claimed. The filing states only that Pofran ceases to be a subsidiary on completion; it attributes no revenue, income or net worth to it, names no consideration, and asserts no benefit to margins, capital, focus or valuation for KSB or for the struck-off entity. Management's stated goals stay unchanged: double-digit topline growth, 13-14% EBITDA, rising dividend.
rationale.gaps: Everything: no demerger exists in these texts. Unexplained why Pofran was dormant seven years before strike-off, and why no earlier call mentioned it.

In Mar 2026, Director Finance Rakesh Tumane explicitly minimises the ferroalloy unit rather than proposing to separate it: capacity 12,000 tons per year, "it's not going to have any impact" and "not something impactful thing here." The only corporate-structure actions discussed are additive and outward: proposed joint ventures (GMDC in Gujarat at 51% MOIL / 49% GMDC on a 9.5 million-ton resource, MP State Mining Corporation for Bhudkum and Selva blocks, CMDC for 218 sq km in Nilkanthpur/Balrampur, Chhattisgarh), DIPAM and NITI Aayog approvals for JV formation, INR275 crore earmarked for overseas acquisition within a INR600 crore FY26 capex target, and a possible third-party beneficiation plant near the mines if MOIL can commit ~3 lakh tons per annum of low-grade ore. rationale.rationale: The texts describe two separate things that both fall under 'separation', and neither is a classic demerger of a listed business into a new listed entity. First, Nestlé India carved out businesses by slump sale: the Nutraceutical Business was transferred to Dr. Reddy's and Nestlé Health Science Limited — a 49:51 joint venture (Nestlé India 49%, Dr. Reddy's 51%) that 'came together only in July of last year' (July 2024) — and the Nestlé Business Services Division was transferred to Nestlé Business Services India Private Limited (formerly Purina PetCare India Private Limited), a Nestlé affiliate; the gains on both appear as exceptional items of Rs 2,908.2 million standalone and Rs 1,834.2 million consolidated for the nine months to 31 December 2024 and FY ended 31 March 2025. The only rationale management gave, in the 4 February 2025 analyst meet, was capability complementarity rather than any problem with the parent: Nestlé India is 'a consumer product company with a more limited health care exposure as compared to Dr. Reddy's which is a health care company', so the JV 'combin[es] the synergies of product portfolio and distribution reach' to attack an addressable health-science/nutrition opportunity management sized at 'INR 24,000 Crores', with Nestlé Health Science products to be 'by and large manufactured locally' using Nestlé's R&D base (INR 1.8 billion R&D spend in CY2023, 4,000+ employees, 23 sites). Suresh Narayanan reported the integration as 'successful', the teams 'working well together', 'double digit growth', and new launches on the anvil from both the Nestlé Health Science and Dr. Reddy's portfolios; he sits on the JV board. Second, and legally distinct, a Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by the NCLT New Delhi Bench on 15 September 2023 and effective 19 October 2023 reclassified Rs 8,374.3 million from General Reserve to Retained Earnings — a balance-sheet/distributable-reserve action, out of which Rs 964.2 million was capitalised for the 1:1 bonus issue in August 2025 and the residual Rs 7,410.1 million funds the Rs 2 per share Special Dividend 2026 (Rs 3,856.6 million). Post-separation, the JV is accounted for as an associate, not consolidated, and Nestlé India's consolidated accounts carry a charge for its share of the associate's result (Rs 164.4 million in Q1 FY2026-27, Rs 423.1 million for 9M FY2025-26 and Rs 455.2 million for FY2025-26), so the carved-out business is currently a drag on consolidated versus standalone earnings. Nowhere in these texts did management cite investor, lender or regulatory pressure as the reason; no analyst on the 4 February 2025 call asked a single question about the slump sales or the Scheme.
rationale.evolution: Only one earnings call falls in the window, and the separation was already largely done by then: the Scheme of Arrangement was sanctioned on 15 September 2023 and became effective 19 October 2023, and the Dr. Reddy's JV 'came together only in July of last year', i.e. July 2024, with the slump-sale gains booked in the nine months to 31 December 2024 and FY ended 31 March 2025. At the 4 February 2025 analyst and institutional investors meet, Narayanan presented the JV twice — once as a 'rising health consciousness' growth platform with an INR 24,000 crore opportunity and once under 'Partnerships' as 'the first of its kind in India for Nestlé' — reporting successful integration and double-digit growth, but gave no rationale for the Scheme itself and no financials for the transferred businesses. In every filing after that (30 January 2026 results, 3 July 2026 dividend intimation, 22 July 2026 Q1 results) the Scheme appears only mechanically, as the source of the reclassified Rs 8,374.3 million used for the August 2025 1:1 bonus and the Rs 2 per share Special Dividend 2026; the only new structural step disclosed is the 30 January 2026 in-principle approval of 26% stakes in two captive renewable SPVs with Adani Green Energy and Radiance Renewables, which is not a business separation.

judge.reason: Documents call it the completion of the final tranche of the strategic divestment of 12 assets announced January 2024; monetised cash earmarked for fund-based HAM, solar/BESS equity.
judge.insiders: Buyer does not belong to promoter/promoter group/group companies; no promoter or management stake in Vertis stated. Shareholders approved by special resolution dated 28 September 2024.
judge.hidden_value: Sale is for cash, not a listed spin: Rs 683.84 crore EV on an SPV contributing 1.30% of consolidated revenue and 2.42% of net worth; consolidated cash Rs 2,856 crore, Rs 1,100 crore of it inside PNC Infra Holdings.
judge.selling_pressure_why: No new listed security or share distribution; assets transferred to an InvIT for cash, parent remains sole listed entity.
judge.listing_timeline: not stated — documents say only that equity shares were transferred on March 27, 2026 and all other steps completed March 27, 2026 (filing dated 27.03.2026); no listing of any demerged entity is mentioned

judge.quote: This transaction marked the completion of the final tranche of the strategic divestment of 12 assets announced in January 2024.

rationale.rationale: There is no demerger or spin-off scheme in these texts: the 'separation' PNC Infratech describes is a staged, 100% equity divestment of a ring-fenced road-concession portfolio — 12 SPVs comprising 11 National Highway HAM projects plus 1 State Highway BOT-Toll project, spanning about 3,800 lane-km — to KKR-backed Highways Infrastructure Trust (later renamed Vertis Infrastructure Trust), under definitive agreements/SPA dated 15 January 2024, approved by shareholders by special resolution on 28 September 2024 and executed explicitly 'outside Scheme of Arrangement' (Reg 37A), completing on 27 March 2026 with PNC Challakere (Karnataka) Highways. Management's stated purpose was capital recycling and de-leveraging: the 12 SPVs carried Rs 6,480 crore of project debt, and after tranche 1 consolidated debt fell from Rs 9,345 crore to about Rs 4,300 crore, taking net debt/equity from 1.56x to 0.72x (0.76x by FY26). The realization was pitched at roughly 1.67x equity invested at SPA signing — tranche 1 (10 HAM SPVs, closed 22 May 2025) fetched Rs 1,827.6 crore equity consideration against Rs 1,371 crore invested, plus about Rs 200 crore of back-to-back receivables and Rs 624 crore of change-of-scope works (Rs 584 crore received); Bareilly-Nainital BOT-Toll closed 31 July 2025 at Rs 716.2 crore enterprise value (Rs 153.48 crore equity, Rs 239.35 crore unsecured loan, Rs 80 crore further receivables); Challakere closed at Rs 683.84 crore EV (Rs 80.48 crore equity, Rs 134.94 crore unsecured loans) against Rs 114 crore equity invested, having contributed only 1.30% of FY25 consolidated revenue (Rs 164.03 crore) and 2.42% of consolidated net worth. Gains were booked in the holding subsidiary PNC Infra Holdings (about Rs 460 crore pre-tax, Rs 400 crore post-tax), with no gain in standalone, and roughly Rs 2,200 crore net of debt was collected across 11 assets, leaving Rs 1,100–1,300 crore of cash in PNC Infra Holdings. That cash was explicitly 'earmarked' for fund-based project equity — Rs 1,744 crore of HAM equity commitments (Rs 663 crore, later Rs 542 crore, still to be infused) and about Rs 400 crore for the NHPC solar-plus-BESS SPV — and a buyback was explicitly ruled out. Management also tied the lighter balance sheet to bidding power: with cash and investing capacity it could bid large HAM and BOT-Toll projects directly, where competition is 'moderate' versus 'cutthroat' EPC. The counterparty, not investors or lenders, drove the deal; lenders and the authority were only consent-givers (NOCs from 34 lenders across 11 projects, NHAI in-principle change-of-control approvals obtained asset by asset).
rationale.evolution: The programme was announced with the 15 January 2024 definitive agreements and was tracked purely as execution thereafter: by Nov 2024 management split it into 10 assets (equity value Rs 1,490 crore, enterprise value ~Rs 7,690 crore) for FY25 and 2 assets for FY26, and said the MoRTH debarment did not disturb it. Feb 2025 was about consents — 34 lender NOCs for 11 projects and NHAI in-principle approvals for 8 of 11 — with the target raised to 11 assets by March 2025; Jun 2025 reported tranche 1 of 10 HAM SPVs closed 22 May 2025 at Rs 1,827.6 crore (after a negative Rs 378 crore descoping adjustment that explained the slip from the Rs 2,900 crore headline) and consolidated debt down to ~Rs 4,300 crore. Aug 2025 added Bareilly-Nainital (11 of 12 done), Nov 2025 confirmed the last change-of-control approval and Rs 2,200 crore received net of debt, and Feb 2026 showed the proceeds landing in cash (standalone cash jumping to Rs 1,299 crore 'includes the proceeds received from the KKR') while a second-round divestment of the newer HAM assets was only 'evaluating all the options' with investors approaching. The 27 March 2026 filing and the May 2026 call closed the loop: all twelve SPVs transferred, described as the final tranche of the strategic divestment announced in January 2024, with the next monetisation framework still undecided.

points.point: The 27 March 2026 filing records the transfer of PNC Challakere (Karnataka) Highways to Vertis Infrastructure Trust at Rs 683.84 crore enterprise value (Rs 80.48 crore equity, Rs 134.94 crore unsecured loans), completing all twelve SPVs under the 15 January 2024 SPA; it is a sale outside any scheme of arrangement, shareholder-approved by special resolution on 28 September 2024, and the asset was only 1.30% of FY25 consolidated revenue and 2.42% of consolidated net worth.
points.quote: Now, the Company has completed transfer of all the twelve identified Special Purpose Vehicles ("SPVs") pursuant to the Share Purchase Agreement ("SPA') dated January 15,2024 (as amended from time to time).

points.point: Management described the perimeter of the separation: 12 road assets, 11 NH HAM plus 1 state BOT-Toll, about 3,800 lane-km, sold to KKR-backed Highways Infrastructure Trust in two tranches under January 2024 definitive agreements.
points.quote: Earlier, in January 2024, the Company had signed definitive agreements with HIT to divest a total of 12 road assets, comprising 11 National Highway HAM projects and 1 State Highway BOT – Toll project spanning approximately 3,800 lane -km, to be transacted in two tranches.

points.point: The de-leveraging effect was quantified immediately after tranche 1: consolidated debt fell from Rs 9,345 crore to about Rs 4,300 crore and net debt/equity from 1.56x to 0.72x.
points.quote: After completion of monetization of the 10 assets, as on date the debt got reduced to Rs. 4300.00 crores, which translates net debt to equity of 0.72 times as against 1.56 times.

points.point: Tranche 1 economics: Rs 1,827.6 crore equity consideration for 10 HAM SPVs against Rs 1,371 crore of equity invested, plus about Rs 200 crore of back-to-back receivables and Rs 624 crore of change-of-scope works executed (Rs 546–584 crore already received).
points.quote: Tranche 1 comprised of 10 HAM assets concluded for an equity consideration of Rs. 1,827.6 Crore, after adjustments on account of certain items of works descoped in these 10 projects.

points.point: Asked what they would do with the surplus, management said the proceeds would go into new fund-based PPP mandates in HAM, selectively BOT-Toll, and other central-agency fund-based projects (solar, battery storage, smart metering), judiciously and after due diligence.
points.quote: Yes, we are pursuing quite a few fund-based projects on a PPP mode l, both in the sectors where we are very much active in roads, highway sector, like HAM projects and very judiciously we will do look at the BOT toll projects also.

points.point: Sizing of the two tranches and the enterprise value being taken off the consolidated balance sheet: 10 assets at Rs 1,490 crore equity value out of Rs 1,739 crore for all 12, against roughly Rs 7,690 crore enterprise value and Rs 6,480 crore of SPV debt.
points.quote: The 10 assets equity value is INR1,490 crores as against the INR1,739 crores of 12 assets, and enterprise value will be around INR7,690 crores.

points.point: The separation was gated on third-party consents rather than on any investor demand: NOCs from 34 lenders across 11 projects and NHAI in-principle change-of-control approvals (8 of 11 received, 3 pending).
points.quote: So, there are NOCs required from lenders as well as from the authority and out of the 12 assets, we have already received the NOCs of 11 projects from 34 lenders as of date.

points.point: The valuation yardstick management had guided to was about 1.67x the equity invested, measured at the time of signing the share purchase agreement.
points.quote: Earlier we have given in our note, about 1.67 times of the equity invested at the time of signing of the share purchase agreement.

points.point: Bareilly Nainital, the single BOT-Toll state highway asset, closed on 31 July 2025 at Rs 716.2 crore enterprise value (Rs 153.48 crore equity, Rs 239.35 crore unsecured loan, Rs 80 crore further receivables), taking the count to 11 of 12.
points.quote: With the successful transfer of PNC Bareilly Nainital Highways Private Limited, the Company has now completed the 100% equity divestment in 11 out of the 12 assets under the definitive agreement executed for the equity sale last year.

points.point: Management stated the proceeds are reserved for equity in fund-based projects — Rs 663 crore of HAM equity and about Rs 400 crore for the solar-cum-BESS SPV, funded from PNC Infra Holdings cash plus internal accruals, with no debt funding of equity and a buyback explicitly rejected.
points.quote: We will be basically, for the fund -based projects, we have earmark ed this money.

points.point: Shareholder return was explicitly not the use of proceeds; large-value HAM bids and TBCB transmission/solar/BESS projects were named as the destination instead.
points.quote: No. As of now, we are not considering the buyback of this thing.

points.point: Final asset economics disclosed: Rs 114 crore equity invested in the last HAM SPV against about Rs 630 crore enterprise value with Rs 394 crore of original debt, and Rs 2,200 crore net of debt already received for the 11 closed assets (Rs 200 crore holdback, Rs 38–42 crore received so far).
points.quote: For the 11 asset, the net receivable net of debt was Rs. 2,200 crore , which we have received.

points.point: A second round of divestment of the HAM assets still under implementation was under consideration but undecided, with buyers approaching the company; the priority was first getting PCOD on four projects.
points.quote: Regarding the divestment of HAM assets whi ch are under implementation , so we are evaluating all the option s. Investors are approaching us and we are looking at other options also.

points.point: The cash effect showed up in the standalone balance sheet, where cash and current investments jumped from about Rs 373 crore to Rs 1,299 crore on receipt of the KKR/Vertis proceeds, with consolidated cash at Rs 2,745 crore described as wholly own funds.
points.quote: In last quarter, actually, this amount includes the proceeds received from the KKR.

points.point: Management closed out the programme: the March 2026 Challakere sale to Vertis Infrastructure Trust was the final tranche of the 12-asset strategic divestment announced in January 2024, with the entire consideration received.
points.quote: This transaction marked the completion of the final tranche of the strategic divestment of 12 assets announced in January 2024.

points.point: The strategic payoff cited was bidding capacity: a clean balance sheet (standalone net surplus Rs 327 crore, consolidated net debt/equity 0.76x) lets PNC bid large HAM and BOT-Toll projects directly, where competition is lighter than in cutthroat EPC — it won two UP HAM projects of Rs 3,483 crore combined bid cost.
points.quote: So, since we are in a position to invest into these projects, either it Is a HAM or BOT Toll with our healthy balance sheet and our investing capacity, so we look forward to have a lesser competition in the HAM projects, That too, particularly the larger size HAM projects.

points.point: No framework had yet been set for monetising the next generation of assets; only 5 of the 14 HAM projects had reached PCOD/COD and management called a second deal premature.
points.quote: So, we certainly will let you know once we reach out to any kind of framework mechanism on how to monetize these projects.

rationale.what_management_expects: For PNC: consolidated debt down (Rs 9,345 crore to ~Rs 4,300 crore, 1.56x to 0.72x), ~Rs 2,200 crore cash net of debt realised at ~1.67x equity invested, held in PNC Infra Holdings and earmarked for Rs 1,744 crore HAM equity plus ~Rs 400 crore solar/BESS equity, no debt-funded equity, no buyback; a balance sheet that supports direct bidding for large HAM/BOT-Toll with less competition. For the buyer-trust: operating concessions transferred with their debt.
rationale.gaps: No stated hurdle IRR or valuation method, no transaction costs/tax detail, no InvIT-unit or sponsor-stake option, no framework or timing for monetising the remaining 14 assets.

segments.segment_name: Toll & Annuity (BOT projects/OMT/Maintenance of Narela industrial park) — consolidated reportable segment; the documents carry NO separate financials for the divested portfolio itself (12 road assets / SPVs sold to Vertis Infrastructure Trust, formerly Highways Infrastructure Trust)
segments.measure_notes: Revenue = 'Segment Revenue — Toll Annuity' from consolidated Operating Segment Information; segment revenue includes sales and other income directly identifiable/allocable to the segment including inter-segment revenue, though reported inter-segment revenue is nil, so the figure equals net revenue from operations for the segment. Operating_profit = 'Segment Results' for Toll Annuity, i.e. segment result after directly allocable expenses but before unallocable expenditure (which includes most finance cost), unallocable income and tax — closer to EBIT than EBITDA, and NOT PBT. PAT is not disclosed segment-wise. This is the Group's whole toll/annuity segment, not the carved-out entity: it mixes the divested HAM/toll SPVs with retained assets (Gwalior-Bhind, Rae Bareli-Jaunpur, Narela), and FY2026 figures already reflect part-year ownership of the assets sold during FY2026.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is Texmaco's EPC arm — the 'Infra – Rail & Green Energy' segment (the erstwhile Kalindee business plus Hydromechanical & Bridge works) — which the Board decided to transfer as a going concern on a slump-exchange basis into a 100% subsidiary of Texmaco Rail (a participant on the Feb 2025 call called the transferee 'BEL'; Belgharia Engineering Udyog Pvt Ltd appears as a wholly owned subsidiary in the filings). Management's stated reason is that this EPC vertical was the one persistent loss-maker dragging a profitable wagon/foundry company: Q1 FY25 segment EBIT loss of Rs 10.1 crores, FY25 segment revenue of only Rs 438 crores with 'infra business did not make much profit' (versus Freight Car Rs 4,300 crores and Bright Power electrification at Rs 368 crores revenue, 16% EBITDA, Rs 44 crores PBIT), and in FY26 a segment loss of Rs 27.4 crores on Rs 348 crores of revenue — all attributed to a handful of 'legacy contracts' they were trying to complete or short-close, against which large unrealised claims from government customers were pending. The separation was framed as a way to ring-fence those legacy liabilities and claims, give the EPC business its own focused management and revive it, 'unlock value, enhance organizational focus and streamline business operations across key verticals,' while repositioning it away from conventional EPC towards niche rail infra, systems and solutions, signalling, ballastless track, auto-fare collection and safety — where the Union Budget outlay (Rs 2.5 lakh crore in FY26, a record Rs 2.93 lakh crore in FY27) is concentrated. It also sits inside a broader restructuring: wagon assets were consolidated (Texmaco West Rail amalgamated into the parent, effective 1 April 2025), while non-core activities were pushed out or into separate vehicles — a freed 12-acre prime land parcel in Kolkata became a separate Real Estate division because 'the competency requirement for development of land is totally different from making wagons', defence was put into Texmaco Defence Technologies Ltd (Rs 200 crores committed, later diluted to 70% with Calculus/Vagus taking 30%), and the Touax leasing JV stake went from 50% to 34% with TrinityRail joining. Nobody outside demanded the hive-off: investors (UTI Mutual Fund, Nuvama, Dalal & Broacha) repeatedly pressed on the infra drag and the weak consolidated margin versus Titagarh/Jupiter, and the lenders were an obstacle rather than a requester — banks withheld clearances and wanted a counter/corporate guarantee from the parent, which management said 'doesn't make much sense to us'. Management insisted it was not a sale or monetisation: 'We want to continue with this business. We see tremendous future for the EPC business.' By FY27 the segment had turned positive (Q1 FY27 segment result +Rs 0.82 crores) and management said the legacy aberrations would be over, which is the outcome they said the separation was meant to produce.
rationale.evolution: The idea was already live and stalled by the Aug 2024 call (14 Aug 2024): exchange no-objection obtained, but held up by bank clearances, corporate-guarantee demands and the unsettled strategy for the new company, with an NCLT timeline of 9-12 months and shareholders' interest cited as the reason it stayed 'work in progress'. By Oct 2024 (28 Oct 2024) management said approval was received and it was 'committed for the separation of that wing', pushed by an investor calling the segment 'a drag on our profitability'. The structure was fixed at the Feb 2025 call (3 Feb 2025) — a slump-exchange transfer of the EPC group as a going concern into a 100% subsidiary, 12-15 months to complete — and by May 2025 (17 May 2025) the scheme had been filed with the stock exchanges, queries answered, NOCs in progress and final approval expected January 2026, now justified as 'unlocking value' and a repositioning into niche rail infra and signalling. After that the scheme largely drops out: Nov 2025 reports only the opposite-direction Texmaco West amalgamation plus the 12 acres of land freed by 'restructuring', Feb 2026 and May 2026 (13 May 2026) speak only of the legacy contracts winding down, a new Real Estate division, Texmaco 2.0 and defence being carved into a subsidiary.

points.point: The demerger was already under way but stuck on lenders: exchanges had given no-objection, while banks had not cleared it and were seeking a counter/corporate guarantee from the parent, which management rejected as illogical; NCLT alone was expected to take 9-12 months.
points.quote: In the meanwhile, we also have to discuss and finalize the arrangement with the banks because currently we don't have the clearances from them with a counter guarantee, corporate guarantee, which doesn't make much sense to us.

points.point: CFO quantified the problem being separated — the Infra-Rail & Green Energy segment (Kalindee, Hydromechanical and Bridge) posted an EBIT loss of Rs 10.1 crores in Q1 FY25, driven by a few legacy contracts management wanted to complete or short-close.
points.quote: They had reported a loss of INR10.1 crores over EBIT. The main reason of it is that yes, there are a few legacy contracts which are being continued, which management has full focus on how do we close this contract, either close and complete or how can we short-close this contract.

points.point: Vice Chairman added that these same legacy EPC contracts carry large unrealised claims against government customers that take years to recover — the overhang the separation was meant to isolate.
points.quote: I'd like to add Hemant on to your comments by saying that most of these contracts there are a huge amount of potential claims, which we have not yet got paid.

points.point: An institutional investor (UTI Mutual Fund) framed the segment as a drag on group profitability and asked for the demerger status; the MD confirmed approval was in hand and the company was committed to separating the wing, declining to promise FY25 completion because of statutory processes.
points.quote: So Nikhil, we have received the approval, and you know that these things require a kind of a process.

points.point: The structure was disclosed: the EPC group would be transferred as an ongoing business on a slump-exchange basis into a 100% subsidiary of Texmaco Rail, expected to take 12-15 months, alongside the inward merger of Texmaco West Rail.
points.quote: Additionally, as part of our business organization, we also decided to transfer the Infra -Rail and Green Energy, which is our EPC group primarily, as an ongoing business on a slump exchange basis into a 100% subsidiary of Texmaco Rail.

points.point: Asked directly whether the EPC business would be monetised after the slump exchange, management said no — it is being separated to be grown and made profitable like the wagon business, given budget focus on track-laying and signalling.
points.quote: We want to continue with this business.

points.point: In closing remarks the Vice Chairman tied the separation to risk control and a careful, blip-free move into new areas (passenger mobility via the Saira interiors acquisition), explicitly naming the demerged business.
points.quote: That's the reason we have decided to demerge the EPC business, which is the Infra -Rail & Green Energy business.

points.point: Opening remarks gave the formal rationale for both restructuring legs — the West Rail merger and the Infra-Rail & Green business transfer — as value unlocking, organisational focus and streamlining.
points.quote: The proposed merger of Texmaco West Rail Limited, which was erstwhile Jindal Rail Manufacturing Company and business transfer of Infra-Rail and Green are expected to unlock value, enhance organizational focus and streamline business operations across key verticals.

points.point: CFO gave the procedural status and the only completion date ever put on record: the scheme had been filed with the stock exchanges, exchange queries answered, NOCs being worked on, with final approval expected in January 2026.
points.quote: We are working with the NOCs , and we are expecting final approval in January 26.

points.point: The MD said the act of taking up the demerger had itself already reduced losses, and that the purpose was a focused approach to revive the business and reposition it from conventional EPC into niche rail infra, systems, solutions and signalling, domestically and on select international projects.
points.quote: But this was the whole purpose that we have a very focused approach to revive that when we have huge positive traction so far the orders progress in the market and the government push to improve the infrastructure.

points.point: The Vice Chairman noted the consolidated FY25 margin of 10.3% was achieved despite the infra segment making almost no profit — the arithmetic case for ring-fencing it (Infra-Rail & Green Energy FY25 revenue Rs 438 crores versus Freight Car Rs 4,300 crores and Bright Power Rs 368 crores at 16% EBITDA, Rs 44 crores PBIT).
points.quote: This is, I think, in spite of the fact that our infra business did not make much profit.

points.point: The restructuring of the non-wagon businesses (hydromechanical power station equipment, bridges) freed a 12-acre land parcel in Kolkata, which management decided to develop rather than sell in a distressed sale, adding a land-unlocking motive to the reorganisation.
points.quote: By restructuring all this, we have seen that we have a land parcel.

points.point: Management said the infra green energy part was turning around with the remaining drag purely from legacy contracts — one delayed by geopolitical reasons — and would start contributing positively by the next financial year; rail infra order book was Rs 511 crores against Bright Power's Rs 1,800 crores.
points.quote: So whatever aberrations we were seeing, it is from the legacy contracts.

points.point: The reorganisation produced a further carve-out: prime land released by restructuring became a separate Real Estate business division, justified on a competency-mismatch argument rather than cash need, and described as a finite, non-continuing division.
points.quote: And the competency requirement for development of land is totally different from making wagons.

points.point: The separations are now part of 'Texmaco 2.0' — reducing dependence on the cyclical wagon business while a Rs 700 crore contingency provision was taken against free reserves for unforeseen risks on large contracts and pending project claims.
points.quote: We are reducing on to the risk of cyclical type of busi ness.

points.point: The filings show the subsequent pattern of pushing new verticals into separate entities rather than running them inside the parent: Texmaco Defence Technologies Ltd got a Rs 200 crore commitment and then a Share Subscription & Shareholders' Agreement (14 Aug 2026) under which Vagus Def Tech & Aerospace Fund-1 ('Calculus') takes 30%, cutting Texmaco's holding to 70%; the Touax Texmaco Railcar Leasing JV was likewise diluted from 50% to 34% to admit TrinityRail Global Inc.
points.quote: Upon completion of the proposed subscription, Calculus shall hold 30% of the equity share capital of TDTL, and TDTL shall  accordingly cease to be a wholly -owned subsidiary and shall become a subsidiary of the Company.

rationale.what_management_expects: For the EPC/Infra-Rail & Green Energy entity: focused management, revival from losses, exit from legacy contracts, a shift to niche rail infra, signalling and systems with higher margins. For the parent: a streamlined structure, operational efficiency, value unlocking, margins moving from ~10% toward mid-teens and 'beyond mid-teens', and freed prime land monetised through a separate real estate division.
rationale.gaps: No valuation, consideration, debt/guarantee allocation, capital structure or listing plan for the transferee; no quantified value unlock; and no confirmation the scheme actually completed after the January 2026 target.

segments.segment_name: Defence business — not a reported segment. Segment notes carry only Freight Car Division, Infra – Rail & Green Energy, Infra – Electrical and (FY26) Real Estate. The only defence-labelled disclosures are entity-level Schedule III lines: 'Texmaco Defence Electrication Ltd.' (shown as 'Texmaco Rail Electrification Ltd.' in earlier years) and associate 'Texmaco Defence Systems Pvt. Ltd.'

The only numbers available are entity-level 'Share in Profit or (Loss)' amounts from the Schedule III consolidation note (net profit/loss after tax as consolidated), not segment data; revenue and operating profit for that entity are not disclosed. These Schedule III / segment tables are OCR-garbled with visibly shifted year columns (e.g. AR2024 p.219 shows 11,269.01 as parent profit, which AR2025 reports as FY2024-25), so the year attribution of even these entity figures is uncertain.

rationale.rationale: These texts do not describe TSF Investments separating, demerging or spinning off any business — nothing in the six filings proposes a separation, and no earnings-call transcripts are on file, so no management rationale for a separation exists in this record. What the filings actually show is the opposite direction of travel: consolidation of the group's holdings. On 19 August 2026 the Board and Audit Committee approved subscribing to a preferential private-placement issue by associate Wheels India Limited (WIL) — initially 10,57,827 shares at ₹1,418 (premium ₹1,408), aggregating not more than ₹150 Crores — stating the objective as 'To consolidate the shareholdings in Wheels India Ltd (associate company)'; TSF already held 61,09,914 shares, or 25.007%, of WIL. Management's stated reasoning was that TSF, as an Exempted Core Investment Company, was 'looking at better investment opportunities to optimize returns on investments and also consolidating its shareholdings in its Group Companies', and that the capital infusion would let WIL 'repay or reduce its Debt thereby enhancing the leverage position, narrowing the gap to the peer averages and ensuring adequate headroom for sustained growth'; funds at WIL were earmarked for 'Debt Reduction' and TSF's source of funds was 'Internal accruals'. Scale numbers cited: WIL FY2025-26 standalone turnover ₹5,124.40 Cr, PAT ₹138.56 Cr, net worth ₹974.53 Cr (turnover ₹4,424.86 Cr in 2024-25, ₹4,619.03 Cr in 2023-24); TSF's own FY2025-26 consolidated turnover ₹985 Cr, making the materiality threshold ₹98.50 Cr, so the deal (15.23% of TSF turnover, 2.74% of WIL turnover) needed shareholder approval as a material related-party transaction under Reg. 23(4). The second structural item is also a combination, not a separation: the NCLT, Chennai, by order dated 27 August 2026 (uploaded 8 September 2026), sanctioned the amalgamation of wholly-owned subsidiary Forge 2000 Private Limited into subsidiary Axles India Limited; no reasons for that merger are given in these filings. The only parties shown asking for a change were the exchange and the regulator — NSE advised WIL to reprice the issue — not investors, lenders or partners seeking a separation.
rationale.evolution: No separation idea surfaces anywhere in this record, and there are no earnings calls to trace it through. The consolidation plan appears on 19 August 2026 (Board/Audit Committee approval of the ₹150 Cr WIL preferential subscription) and is put to shareholders by Postal Ballot Notice dated 19 August 2026, dispatched 20 August 2026 with e-voting from 22 August to 20 September 2026. It changed once: a corrigendum dated 3 September 2026, after NSE advised WIL to reprice under Chapter V of SEBI ICDR, cut TSF's allotment from 10,57,827 shares at ₹1,418 to 10,26,694 shares at ₹1,461 with the ₹150 Cr total unchanged; the resolution passed with 99.29% of votes in favour on 21 September 2026, while separately the NCLT sanctioned the Forge 2000 into Axles India merger on 27 August 2026.

points.point: The only scheme in the record is a merger, not a separation: Forge 2000 Private Limited (wholly-owned subsidiary) was amalgamated into Axles India Limited (subsidiary), sanctioned by NCLT Chennai on 27 August 2026 and uploaded to the NCLT portal on 8 September 2026. No rationale for it is stated anywhere in the filings.
points.quote: We wish to inform you that the National Company Law Tribunal, Division Bench Court – II, Chennai, has, vide Order dated 27th August 2026 has sanctioned the scheme of amalgamation between Forge 2000 Private Limited (wholly-owned subsidiary) ('Transferor Company') and Axles India Limited (Subsidiary) ('Transferee Company') and uploaded the order in NCLT portal on 08th September 2026.

points.point: The Board's stated object for the ₹150 Cr WIL subscription is consolidation of group shareholdings — the opposite of a separation. TSF proposed 10,57,827 shares at ₹1,418 (premium ₹1,408), to complete on or before 30 September 2026 subject to shareholder approval.
points.quote: To consolidate the shareholdings in Wheels India Ltd (associate company)

points.point: Management framed the investment as part of TSF's role as an Exempted Core Investment Company optimising returns and consolidating group stakes, with TSF already holding 61,09,914 shares (25.007%) of WIL.

points.point: The purpose at the investee level was deleveraging: WIL would use the money for debt reduction, closing its leverage gap to peer averages; TSF funded it from internal accruals with no borrowing.
points.quote: The proposed capital infusion will enable your Associate Company to repay or reduce its Debt thereby enhancing the leverage position, narrowing the gap to the peer averages and ensuring adequate headroom for sustained growth.

points.point: Materiality was driven by TSF's own small revenue base: FY2025-26 consolidated turnover of ₹985 Cr set a ₹98.50 Cr threshold, so the ₹150 Cr deal (15.23% of turnover) required prior shareholder approval by ordinary resolution under Reg. 23(4).
points.quote: The annual consolidated turnover of the Company for the year ended 31st March 2026 was ₹985 Crores and therefore any transaction in excess of ₹98.50 Crores (i.e. 10% of the annual consolidated turnover of the Company) with a related party will be deemed to be a material related party transaction and shall require prior approval of the shareholders of the Company by way of an Ordinary Resolution.

points.point: Promoter-group members subscribed alongside TSF — Srivats Ram (WIL's Chairman & Managing Director) ₹15.00 Cr / 1,05,782 shares, Gita Ram ₹7.50 Cr, Nivedita Ram ₹7.50 Cr — and related parties were barred from voting.

points.point: The plan changed on exchange instruction, not investor pressure: NSE told WIL to reprice under Chapter V of SEBI ICDR, raising the price to ₹1,461 and cutting TSF's allotment to 10,26,694 shares with the ₹150 Cr aggregate unchanged.

rationale.rationale: The texts provided do not describe any separation, demerger, spin-off or hive-off of a Vikram Solar business — no such transaction, business, rationale or scheme is mentioned anywhere in the four earnings calls or the two filings, so no separation rationale can be reconstructed from these documents alone. What management actually describes is the opposite of separation: a consolidation of the whole PV value chain inside one listed entity through backward integration, staged as "modules first, then cell, then wafer and ingot" (May 8, 2026), taking the company from 9.5 GW of modules to 15.5 GW, to a 9 GW TOPCon cell plant (first cell December 2026, ~70% backward integration) plus 3 GW in FY28, and a 12 GW wafer-ingot plant whose first 6 GW phase (~INR 3,700 crores, commissioning FY29) was board-approved the day before that call. The explicit logic given is integration, not disaggregation: the 6 GW wafer-ingot addition "turns Gangaikondan into a single integrated solar manufacturing campus - ingot to module with zero transport cost between fabs, zero transit damages, and nil inventory buffers," and the cell/wafer mandates (ALMM List-II from June 2026, draft ALMM List-III from June 1, 2028) are cited as a "coherent industrial framework" rewarding integrated players. The second new business, battery energy storage (target 15 GWh by FY30; 5 GWh cell-to-pack by March 2027, INR ~150 crores assembly, 7.5 GWh cell phase FY29 and second phase FY30; capex quoted at INR 4,300 crores on 65:35 debt:equity in the Jan 20, 2026 call), is also described as being built inside Vikram Solar — "This completes our energy platform and it takes us from a product company to a complete energy solution provider" — not carved out. Asked directly about structural moves on May 8, 2026, the CEO said the company is "not thinking anything beyond" backward integration and BESS. The only things scaled back or dropped were capacity plans, not legal entities: the 2 GW Falta module expansion was held back (17.5 GW guidance cut to 15.5 GW) and the 3 GW US module plan was shelved because of US traceability-to-quartz requirements and skilled-manpower constraints. The two filings on record are insolvency matters, not a scheme of arrangement: an NCLT Kolkata order of June 12, 2026 admitting an Isitva Steels Section 9 petition (claim INR 9,44,12,332 incl. 14% interest; principal held at INR 5,22,25,343), set aside by NCLAT on June 29, 2026 because the admitted dues of INR 91,98,556 were below the INR 1 crore threshold.
rationale.evolution: No separation idea surfaces in any of the four calls — Sep 10, 2025, Oct 17, 2025, Jan 20, 2026 or May 8, 2026 — so there is nothing to trace. What does evolve is integration and diversification within the single entity: on Sep 10, 2025 management framed 17.5 GW of modules plus a 12 GW captive cell line by FY27 and a 1-5 GWh BESS plan; on Oct 17, 2025 it added a 186-acre Gangaikondan campus (6 GW module, 12 GW cell, INR 6,100-6,200 crores) and said wafer capex was only being "actively evaluated" pending ALMM-III; on Jan 20, 2026 module guidance was trimmed to 15.5 GW (Falta 2 GW deferred), 9.5 GW of modules were commissioned and BESS was sized at INR 4,300 crores; and on May 8, 2026 the board approved the first 6 GW of wafer-ingot (INR 3,700 crores) to make Gangaikondan an ingot-to-module campus, with the US module plan dropped. The June 19 and June 30, 2026 filings are IBC proceedings, unrelated to any restructuring of businesses.

points.point: Asked directly whether the company would pursue further vertical or horizontal moves like peers, the CEO ruled out anything beyond backward integration and BESS — no structural separation was contemplated.
points.quote: At this point of time, we are completely focused on backward integration on the module and expanding into BESS. At this point of time, we are not thinking anything beyond.

points.point: The stated strategic logic is to pull the value chain into one site and one entity (6 GW wafer-ingot approved at ~INR 3,700 crores, commissioning FY29), explicitly for cost and quality gains from co-location — the opposite of separating a business.
points.quote: This addition turns Gangaikondan into a single integrated solar manufacturing campus - ingot to module with zero transport cost between fabs, zero transit damages, and nil inventory buffers between stages of the value chain.

points.point: BESS (target 15 GWh by FY30) is positioned as completing Vikram Solar's own platform rather than as a separable unit.
points.quote: This completes our energy platform and it takes us from a product company to a complete energy solution provider, delivering solar plus storage as dispatchable power .

points.point: The only capacity 'removed' was the 2 GW Falta module expansion — deferred, not divested, pending ALMM-II cell mandates; module guidance was cut from 17.5 GW to 15.5 GW.
points.quote: No, we have not cancelled that. So, we have retained it at 15.5 for the time being to ensure 75% backward integration with the 12 GW capacities planned.

points.point: Cells were always framed as captive inputs for Vikram Solar's own modules (1:1 cell-to-module ratio against 12 GW cell vs 17.5 GW modules), not as a standalone cell business.
points.quote: So, we would be looking at captively consuming the solar cells for our modules.

points.point: The US module capacity (3 GW) was abandoned on operating grounds — traceability and manpower — with capital and management bandwidth redirected to India, again with no entity separation involved.
points.quote: Which is why we are focusing all of the capital as well as management bandwidth on scaling our existing business in India and backward integrating.

points.point: No scheme of arrangement is on record. The two filings are an NCLT Kolkata order of June 12, 2026 admitting an Isitva Steels Section 9 IBC petition and an NCLAT order of June 29, 2026 setting it aside because the admitted dues were below the INR 1 crore threshold.
points.quote: since it is admitted case that the due amount was less than Rs. 1 crore ; the admission order dated 12.06.2026,  stands  set aside.

rationale.what_management_expects: Nothing is said about a separation. For the integrated company management expects margin gains: non-DCR EBITDA of INR 1.75-2/Wp in FY27 rising to about INR 5/Wp in FY28 post cell integration, FY27 EBITDA of INR 1,500-1,600 crores (up ~74%), module utilisation 65-70% and cell 70-75%, with net-debt/equity held below 1.5 and coverage above 2.5x at peak drawdown.
rationale.gaps: Everything about a separation: there is no demerger, no entity to be separated, no stated rationale, no requester, no valuation or capital logic, and no scheme document.

judge.what_is_spun: IIFL's housing finance and microfinance subsidiaries — IIFL Home Finance and IIFL Samasta Finance — into three separate entities
judge.reason: Private equity investor ADIA in IIFL Home Finance needs an exit; demerger is the most elegant way to list it separately, and demerging also releases parent capital adequacy.
judge.insiders: Not stated in stake terms; listed-company shareholders would get subsidiary shares in the same economic ratio. Nirmal Jain is founder, promoter and Managing Director.
judge.hidden_value: Subsidiaries are valued at cost in the parent, a disadvantage when computing parent capital adequacy; HFC capital adequacy 41.7%, net gearing 2.6-2.7x, only single-digit ROE; Samasta 24.9%.
judge.selling_pressure_why: No scheme, ratio or record date announced; management says it is a Board call with no decision at this point in time.
judge.listing_timeline: Not stated: on April 29, 2026 management said "I don't think we can t give you any time line this is not something -- the Board has to decide" and "it will happen sometime, but maybe I can't give a time line for that"; on July 22, 2026 they said they are "looking at a strategic divestment partly or listing of microfinance".

judge.what_is_spun: Nothing is spun off; SteriScience's Poland and Baroda injectable facilities would be absorbed into listed OneSource
judge.reason: Acquisition of SteriScience's Poland fill-finish and Baroda carbapenem facilities into OneSource, raising FY28 revenue outlook to $500m+; the separate Singapore amalgamation was to simplify corporate hierarchy, enhance operational efficiency and eliminate redundant administrative, compliance and legal costs.
judge.insiders: Steriscience is a related party "which the family owns along with TPG"; Steriscience owns 51% of listed Brooks. Arun Kumar is Founder/Non-Executive Chairperson; swap would add ~2.5 crore shares, raising promoter shareholding.
judge.hidden_value: Incoming Poland and Brooks assets delivered H1FY26 combined revenue $29m and EBITDA $11m (38% margin), targeting $40m EBITDA; transferors carry accumulated losses to be set off against OneSource's securities premium. Listed Brooks' price fell below the ~INR2,200/share intended valuation.
judge.selling_pressure_why: No new entity is listed or distributed; the scheme issues shares to promoters, and the Board dropped it on May 13, 2026.
judge.listing_timeline: not stated — no demerged entity lists. On Jan 24, 2026 management said "We anticipate, us to be able to get the final all regulatory approvals in place by third quarter of FY27"; on May 13, 2026 the Board decided not to pursue the transaction and to "revisit it following successful delivery of respective companies' FY28 guidance"
judge.read_next: The explanatory statement items SEBI demanded: transferors' accumulated losses and the reserves impact on OneSource pre- and post-scheme.
judge.quote: The Board of Directors at their meeting held today deliberated the proposed transaction and in the best interest of all stakeholders decided to not pursue the transaction in the current form and revisit it following successful delivery of respective companies' FY28 guidance.

judge.reason: Business synergy, consolidation and pooling of resources into a single entity; valuable addition to technology stack, additional product portfolio, diversifying revenue and expediting global expansion, thereby adding value to shareholders
judge.insiders: "will not result in change in management and Promoter/ Promoter Group"; Silverleaf ESOS options swapped 500:1 into SISL ESOS-II at Rs 2 exercise price; 3,80,500 options granted, 1,41,500 vested
judge.hidden_value: Silverleaf is tiny but tech-rich: 8,804 shares, FY25 revenue Rs 31.62 cr with Rs 41.41 lakh pre-tax loss (Rs 6.69 cr PBT in FY24), merged into a Rs 2,655 cr net-worth parent; management guided Silverleaf top line of Rs 50-60 cr
judge.selling_pressure_why: Only 44,02,000 shares allotted versus 22,32,27,530 outstanding; same financial-services industry; fractional entitlements alone sold by trust within 90 days
judge.option_pricing_date: 18th March, 2024 (date of approval of the Scheme by the Board of Directors, when 754 outstanding ESOS options at Rs 10 each are stated); new SISL ESOS-II grant priced at Rs 2 per option by NRC resolution passed by circulation on November 04, 2026
judge.listing_timeline: No separate listing; per the Scheme the New Equity Shares "shall be listed on all the Stock Exchanges on which the Equity Shares of the Transferee Company are listed as on the Effective Date" and "will remain frozen in the depositories system till listing/trading permission is given by the Designated Stock Exchange" (BSE as Designated Stock Exchange). Scheme effective November 03, 2026; 44,02,000 equity shares allotted November 04, 2026. No date given for trading approval.
judge.read_next: Listing/trading permission filing for the 44,02,000 new shares; then Ace Alpha valuation report and 863:1,000 exchange ratio
judge.quote: The Scheme of Amalgamation will not result in change in management and Promoter/ Promoter Group of the listed Transferee Company.

judge.selling_pressure_why: Sapphire promoters, including SFML's ~18.5%+ stake, move to public category in DIL; SFML and Arctic may still pursue a secondary sale.

confidence: the judge read the complete documents: nothing is separated — subsidiaries or another company are amalgamated

judge.what_is_spun: No business is spun off; aluminium products business consolidated into one wholly owned subsidiary via internal amalgamation
demerged_business_names: Sunbeam Lightweighting Solutions Limited (formerly Sunbeam Lightweighting Solutions Private Limited) (Amalgamated Company)
DR Axion India Limited (formerly DR Axion India Private Limited) (Amalgamating Company 3)
judge.reason: Aluminium business and expansion land are fragmented across entities; consolidation under a single focused operating entity gives a stronger balance sheet, unified asset ownership, simplified structure, better managerial focus and efficiency
judge.insiders: Promoter/CMD Srinivasan Ravi sold 5,25,000 shares (2.01%) on 23 June 2026, holding falling 40.15% to 38.14%; no promoter shares issued in the merged subsidiary
judge.hidden_value: Aluminium is now the largest segment (H1 FY27 revenue Rs 3,29,879 lakhs) but lowest-margin; DR Axion turnover Rs 1,298.52 cr on net worth Rs 511.34 cr versus Sunbeam Rs 1,237.46 cr on Rs 107.43 cr; consolidated borrowings Rs 3,61,860 lakhs
judge.selling_pressure_why: No shares distributed to listed shareholders; Company not a party and its shareholding pattern is unaffected
judge.listing_timeline: not stated — on 11 March 2026 the Company said "Not applicable. The Company is not a party to the proposed Scheme, and the shareholding pattern of the Company will not be affected by the proposed Scheme."
judge.read_next: Draft Composite Scheme filed with NCLT, plus Aluminium Products segment EBIT margin in the next quarterly results
judge.quote: This opportunity can be better capitalized by consolidating the Aluminium business under a single focused operating entity having a stronger balance sheet, a broader product and manufacturing base, unified asset ownership, and a streamlined organizational structure.

judge.hidden_value: KEC Investment Holdings earned Rs.1,325 Crore income (6.06% of consolidated revenue) but held Rs.953.77 Crore net worth (17.84% of consolidated net worth), valued at not less than USD 118.30 Million; SAE revenue INR1,800 crores, double-digit margins
judge.selling_pressure_why: No shares distributed to shareholders; documents state no change in shareholding pattern and no change in ultimate ownership
judge.listing_timeline: not stated; the January 30, 2026 filing gives only an expected completion of the share sale: "On April 1, 2026, subject to requisite approvals, or such other date as may be mutually agreed by the parties"
judge.read_next: The registered valuer / SEBI merchant banker valuation supporting the USD 118.30 Million KEC Investment Holdings transfer price
judge.quote: This will result in a unified holding-cum-operating structure, housing all the international tower manufacturing facilities under KEC Towers LLC, without any change in ultimate ownership of the Company over the subsidiaries.

judge.insiders: PFC, the promoter-holder, holds 52.63% of REC on fully diluted basis; Government of India continues to retain majority voting rights and control; merged entity must stay a 'Government Company'. No incentive terms stated.
judge.hidden_value: Swap of 88 PFC shares per 100 REC shares values REC below PFC per share; REC standalone net worth ₹84,290 crore and turnover ₹59,140 crore folds into a combined loan book of over INR 11 lakh crore, India's largest power financier
judge.selling_pressure_why: Documents state REC equity will be cancelled and PFC shares issued, but say nothing about index exclusion, flows or holder size
judge.listing_timeline: not stated — no new entity lists; REC stands dissolved and, per the June 28, 2026 press release, PFC Consideration Shares go to REC shareholders "as existing on a record date to be determined by the Boards of PFC and REC (as may be applicable) at a future date"
judge.read_next: The NCLT/shareholder notice disclosures: basis of the 88:100 swap ratio, Para 25(1) pre-conditions, and post-merger balance sheet
judge.quote: The Share Exchange Ratio for the Proposed Merger of REC into PFC shall be 88 equity shares of PFC of INR 10/- each fully paid up for every 100 equity shares of REC of INR 10/- each fully paid up.

judge.what_is_spun: Nothing is spun off; four wholly-owned subsidiaries merge by absorption into Fortis Hospitals Limited, an intra-group consolidation
judge.reason: "Rationalisation of operational efficiencies and reduction of administrative and managerial overhead, which will help in achieving rationalization of cost by simplification of management structure and financial reporting."
judge.insiders: All five entities are direct/indirect wholly-owned subsidiaries; no shares or cash issued. Promoter IHH (via NTK) holds 31.17% of Fortis and plans to raise it to 51%; ESOP 2026 excludes promoters.
judge.hidden_value: No new entity or value unlocked: FHsL's shares in the transferor companies are cancelled, listed-entity shareholding unchanged. Reveals legacy multi-entity RHT-era structure being simplified, cutting compliance cost and the asset-owner/operator split.
judge.selling_pressure_why: No shares issued, no cash payout, and "Brief details of the change in shareholding pattern (if any) of the listed entity: Not Applicable."

judge.what_is_spun: Nothing separated: listed 72.67% subsidiary Dr. Agarwal's Eye Hospital Limited amalgamated into parent Dr. Agarwal's Health Care Limited
demerged_business_names: Dr. Agarwal's Health Care Limited (AHCL / Transferee Company) is the surviving entity
judge.reason: Merger brings together significant complementarities, consolidating both businesses into a single entity for operational and financial efficiencies, unified capital allocation, stronger balance sheet and simplified legal, regulatory and governance framework; EPS accretive from first year.
judge.insiders: Promoters of the Transferee Company continue as promoters of the merged entity; AHCL promoter group 32.34% pre-merger, diluted approximately 1.48% to 30.86% post; AHCL-granted stock options to AEHL employees continue unchanged.
judge.hidden_value: AEHL is the mature, high-margin half: FY25 revenue INR 397.15cr with PAT INR 54.65cr, versus AHCL standalone INR 1,043.89cr revenue and PAT INR 21.93cr, because AHCL is in an aggressive growth phase. Valuers put AEHL at INR 4,942/share vs AHCL INR 429.
judge.selling_pressure_why: AEHL's 27.33% public holders (13,20,829 shares) receive about 1.52 crore new AHCL shares with no lock-in; AEHL dissolves and ceases to trade.
judge.listing_timeline: No new listing: AEHL 'shall stand dissolved without being wound-up'. Per the October 20, 2026 board intimation, the Scheme 'shall become effective and operative from November 01, 2026 (Effective Date), with the Appointed Date being April 01, 2026', and November 18, 2026 was fixed as the Record Date for allotting consideration shares.
judge.read_next: Annexure XII, AEHL's FY26 audited results, to test the 23:2 ratio against its standalone earnings.
judge.quote: AEHL operates a mature, well -established portfolio of facilities, driving strong and consistent profitability.

judge.read_next: The full Scheme of Amalgamation / NCLT Mumbai petition — appointed date and accounting treatment of the Rs.2,253.90 crore MIPL net worth
judge.quote: The proposed amalgamation is intended to simplify the group structure, improve operational efficiencies, optimize resource utilization and reduce administrative and compliance costs.

judge.read_next: MCA second-motion/Confirmation Petition order and HSCC standalone profit, to size margin added to NBCC PMC segment
judge.quote: There would be no change in the issued, subscribed and paid -up share capital, shareholding pattern, voting rights, promoter shareholding or public shareholding of NBCC pursuant to the Scheme.

demerged_business_names: KIA Biopharma Technologies Private Limited (name prior to January 2022)
judge.reason: "Proposed merger of Kia with the Company will ensure operational synergies" — business synergy, pooling of resources, economies of a larger centralized company, and significant reduction in multiplicity of legal and regulatory compliances
judge.insiders: Promoter and promoter group hold 98,828,360 of 165,531,908 shares and voted 100% in favour; no shares issued, no consideration, no change in shareholding or voting rights
judge.hidden_value: Kia had net worth ₹815.80 lakh and nil revenue at March 31, 2025, and is setting up a plant at Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar/Aurangabad; merger "will augment and diversify the manufacturing footprint" and transfers accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation to Rubicon
judge.selling_pressure_why: No shares issued, no new listed entity, no change in shareholding pattern or index membership
judge.listing_timeline: not stated — no entity lists; the Scheme (filed with exchanges July 22, 2026) says the Transferor Company "shall stand dissolved without being wound-up" on the Effective Date, Appointed Date April 1, 2026
judge.read_next: Regional Director's sanction order / Effective Date filing with Registrar of Companies, and Kia's plant capex and carried-forward losses
judge.quote: On the Scheme becoming effective, the Transferor Company shall without any further act, instrument or deed shall stand dissolved without being wound-up.

judge.what_is_spun: Nothing spun off; the scheme amalgamates Kurlon Enterprise Limited and five other entities into Sheela Foam Limited
judge.reason: "The synergies and integration benefits realised through this acquisition have created a meaningful value for the company"; merger opened opportunities to supplement growth and shareholder value
judge.insiders: not stated
judge.hidden_value: Integration reveals improved economics: core EBITDA crossed INR414 crores (10.8%), first-ever dividend (20%), net debt cut INR156 crores, plus a 34.53%-43% Furlenco stake with possible IPO
judge.selling_pressure_why: Only 4,88,146 new shares allotted to KEL holders versus 10.92 crore existing shares; fractional entitlements sold by Trust
judge.listing_timeline: Per the 22 April 2026 filing, listing and trading approval received from BSE and NSE; "These shares are available for trading effective April 22, 2026"
judge.read_next: The NCLT-approved Composite Scheme (order dated September 17, 2025) and post-allotment shareholding pattern
judge.quote: These shares shall rank pari-passu in all respects with the existing equity shares of the Company.
